author: yyhhyyyyyy
body:
## Summary

The `session.collaboration` namespace gains `session.collaboration.cancel {sessionId, branchId?, memberSessionId}`: a client attached to a leader Session stops a member's current turn and learns whether anything was running. It answers `{"status": "cancelled"}` when the leader's branch held an open request to that member and `{"status": "idle"}` when it did not; `idle` writes nothing anywhere, not even the `stop/interrupt` that `session.stop` always appends. `branchId` defaults to `main`, as it does for `session.stop`.

The member Session id is the only address. The Team relation keyed by that id names the member's Agent and its leader, so the client sends no `agentId`, another Team's member and an unknown id both answer `team_member_not_found`, and a member Session calling the method answers `invalid_params` with the tool's role wording. An unknown or ended branch answers its own Session error and a closed one `session_closed`; none of them is `idle`. A member that is closed or cannot be acquired is `member_closed`.

No `collaboration/cancel` fact is written: that record names the `agent` tool call's turn, request and call ids, and a client call has none. The effect is recorded by facts a client already reads: the member's own `stop/interrupt` and `turn/end`, and the leader's `collaboration/result` and its report input, which the running case asserts.

The design is `docs/design/plugins/Collaboration.md` section 6.7 (method, reply, errors and the boundary with `session.stop`), with the zh mirror; `docs/design/contracts/session-boundary.md` A.1 now lists `session.collaboration` and names `approval.respond` as a built-in method rather than a part registration, with the zh mirror. Files: `crates/dim-app-server/src/collaboration.rs` (the handler, its params, the refusal-to-RPC mapping, and the factored Team-relation check shared with the `agent` tool), `crates/dim-app-server/src/collaboration/approvals.rs` (the namespace declaration and dispatch), `crates/dim-agent-capabilities/src/agent_loop.rs` (`AgentLoop::stop_turn`), `docs/architecture/rust-agent/plugins/Loop.md`, `crates/dim-app-server/tests/transport_flow/collaboration.rs`, `crates/dim-agent-capabilities/tests/interrupt_flow.rs`, and the regenerated architecture graphs.

## Design rule checklist

- [x] Scope: the method is registered by Collaboration's Session part, which owns the Team relation and the delegation's lifetime; no new part, plugin or wiring module is added.
- [x] Commands and results: the stop is the member Loop's turn-scoped `AgentLoop::stop_turn`, naming the turn that consumed the request's input, so a turn that has ended writes nothing; the member's Timeline records `stop/interrupt` and `turn/end`, and the leader's records `collaboration/result`, which a client already reads. An idle cancel changes nothing and its reply says so.
- [x] Handover: n/a. No handover point is added.
- [x] Timeline `before` callbacks: n/a.
- [x] Infrastructure (Timeline, Dispatcher, event envelope, assembly and lifecycle, Session and branch facades): unchanged. One method declaration joins an existing Session namespace.
- [x] Core mechanisms and consumers gain no plugin-specific handling: the method lives in the Collaboration capability and reaches the member through its typed branch services, the way it already reaches InputQueue.
- [x] Batch: n/a.
- [x] Context: n/a. Nothing enters model context.
- [x] No reading another plugin's internal state or deciding for it: the method reads Collaboration's own Team relation and its own open-request set, and asks the member's Loop to stop the turn it names; Loop decides under its own turn lock whether that turn is still open.
- [x] Business configuration stays out of loader rows; contracts are language-neutral: one JSON method, no configuration.
- [x] Missing mechanism capabilities: one, added in its owner. The Session's `stop` carries no turn identity, so Loop gains `AgentLoop::stop_turn`, decided under the lock that opens and closes turns; everything else uses Session methods and the facts Collaboration already reads and writes.
- [x] Timeline holds only facts later decisions use: no event is added, because the effect is already recorded by facts later decisions use; the idle reply is not a fact.

## Documentation

- [x] No accepted ADR is modified or deleted.
- [x] Loop's design gains one sentence for `AgentLoop::stop_turn` in `docs/architecture/rust-agent/plugins/Loop.md`, which has no zh mirror. No other module's design is changed. Collaboration states the method and its boundary with `session.stop`; the session boundary page lists the namespace. Both have zh mirrors, and both are updated.
- [x] No delivery status is added to an ADR, index or roadmap.

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo clippy --locked -p dim-agent-capabilities -p dim-app-server --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test --locked -p dim-agent-capabilities --test interrupt_flow stop_turn`: naming the open turn stops it and cancels its model call; another id and a turn that has ended write nothing.
- `cargo test --locked -p dim-app-server --test transport_flow collaboration`: the collaboration flows, including the interleaving for both the immediate stop and the detached wait: turn A consumes the request's input, A ends, a client submit starts turn B, and the old cancel's stop lands afterwards; B completes and no `stop/interrupt` lands on it.
- `cargo test -p dim-app-server --test transport_flow a_client_cancel`: a running member is cancelled and the member records `stop/interrupt` and a cancelled `turn/end` while the leader receives `collaboration/result` and the report; a second cancel of the settled request answers `idle` and adds no `stop/interrupt`; another Team's member, an unknown id and a member Session are refused with `team_member_not_found`, `team_member_not_found` and `invalid_params`.
- `cargo run --locked -p xtask -- check`
- Ablation: with the open-request check removed, the idle call answers `cancelled` instead of `idle`, so the idle assertion fails.
- Ablation: with `AgentLoop::stop_turn` replaced by the branch's `Session::stop`, both interleaving flows fail with a `stop/interrupt` on turn B.

Closes #1226

body:
Reported by the watchman (mellow-weevil) after the same bug turned up in Marshal's port (marshal#168).

**Problem.** `terminal_send::resolve_targets` matched an id or a nickname with `.find()`. Nicknames repeat across restarts: today the ghost row 64a05eda and the live watchman 7195eda2 were both `mellow-weevil`. So `muster-shim tell mellow-weevil` could go to the ghost and still report the message as sent. That's the command `rally digest` uses to reach the watchman.

**Change.** An exact id still names one session. A nickname that matches several sessions is refused, and the error lists their ids: "`mellow-weevil` names 2 sessions (…); use one's id". An ambiguous id prefix was already handled this way.

**Tests.** `a_nickname_two_sessions_share_is_refused_with_their_ids` covers three cases:
- the shared nickname is refused, and the error lists both ids
- either session's id still reaches it
- with only one session on the nickname, it resolves

Clippy passes.

## Theory to implementation
Preserve the **system's logical behavior** while linearizing only approximate timing/routing. One-pass bounded source probe, conservative affine cost surrogate, exact linear-time Horn-SAT / 2-SAT algorithms, exact source-complete GF(2), fail-closed CaDiCaL fallback.

## Tests
630 random brute-force Horn/2SAT comparisons, 40 generated family selfchecks and late-clause deceptive prefix validation PASSED in GitHub CI build.
114 frozen formulas, 2 repeats and 4 methods = 912 SHA-paired runs; same pinned CaDiCaL binary as R1; 4 shards, final audit.
Current run https://github.com/Frane12/AndroidGameTest/actions/runs/42322926260

## Scientific limits
Source-complete family verification and model witness checking. Cost surrogate is uncalibrated heuristic; its accuracy is not claimed. Synthetic data and reused R1 originals are not blind real holdout. Unverified native UNSAT LRAT proof not supplied. Draft until aggregate audit and deeper review.

author: dwhagar
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"dwhagar"} -->

_Requested by **Boss** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01RuNTFUNB92A8cm5CbojQAi?thread=cmsg_01RuNTFUNB92A8cm5CbojQAiTGcbpCNvpkxtvWhCegzudS)_

## What changes
`config.json` is the file the Settings page (the web user) rewrites. The root scripts used its folder names (`tile_cache.dir`, `jobs.dir`, `log_file`, `log_dir`) to make folders, `chown -R` them to the web user, move or delete files in them, append `update.log`, and write the names into `/etc/logrotate.d`. A web-user compromise could point them at `/etc` or a system log. Now a new standard-library module, `examples/apache/rootpaths.py`, decides first (reached through `deploy-paths.py --check`, and directly from `log-locations.py`).

A path from config.json is used only when it:
- has plain characters only (no space, quote, brace, newline, glob), is absolute and normal;
- sits under `/var/lib`, `/var/cache`, `/var/log`, `/srv`, `/opt`, the checkout, or a folder in root's `PLANETGEN_ROOT_PATH_PARENTS`, and not in a system service's folder or log;
- has no symbolic link on the way or at the end, and only root-owned folders (not writable by the web user) above it;
- if it exists, is already the web user's, left by an earlier run (root with the web group), or empty.

A refused folder is skipped with a plain warning and the install or update carries on. Values from root's own environment (`PLANETGEN_TILE_CACHE_DIR`, `PLANETGEN_JOBS_DIR`, `PLANETGEN_LOG_FILE`, `PLANETGEN_LOG_DIR`) or the script's argument are the operator's and are not checked. `chown -R` on the tile cache is now `-h`.

Wired into: `create-cache-dir.sh` (cache, jobs, move-old-jobs, galaxy-settings removal), `set-permissions.sh` (jobs), `setup-debug-log.sh` and `log-locations.py` (both logs and the rotation files), `scripts/deploy-common.sh` (`update.log`).

Usual defaults pass untouched, so existing installs behave as before; only a custom folder outside the allowed parents is skipped until moved or named in root's environment.

## Tests
`test_deploy_scripts.py`: 123 pass, 20 new (character and parent rules, system folders, links, writable ancestors, existing folders and logs, environment trust, `--check`, and the real scripts run as root against a fake checkout: create-cache-dir leaves an outside jobs folder and a linked cache alone, set-permissions does not chown it, log-locations makes nothing). The three script tests fail without the script changes. The existing jobs test now hands the folder to the web user first, as an earlier run would have.

Also run: apache example, update guard/units/database-step, log shell, version sync, docs index and links, architecture map: pass. Five tests are red on clean main without this change (TEST.661): `test_no_todo_codes_shown`, three in `test_install_python_deps`, and the bash4 check on `deploy-common.sh`.

## Summary
- Upgrade the compatible LangChain 0.3 dependency family, pypdf, and python-dotenv.
- Remove the local unpublished package before dependency auditing so installed dependencies are audited without hiding findings.
- Run pip-audit in strict mode with explicit visibility while the LangChain 1.x migration remains pending.

## Security baseline
- Before: 62 advisory records across 7 packages.
- After: 7 advisory records across 3 packages: langchain, langchain-core, and langchain-text-splitters.
- Resolved packages: langchain-community, langsmith, pypdf, and python-dotenv.
- The remaining findings require a coordinated LangChain 1.x migration and are not ignored.

## Verification
- Ruff check: passed.
- Ruff format check: passed.
- Pytest: 34 passed.
- Coverage: 42.51% with the existing 35% gate.
- Dataset validation: passed.
- Offline BM25 benchmark: 10/10 successful; Recall@5 1.000, MRR@5 0.889, nDCG@5 0.918.
- Package build and installed-wheel resource smoke test: passed.
- Provider/document compatibility imports: passed.
- Dependency audit: executed against the updated environment; 7 unresolved advisories remain.

## Limitations
- The dependency audit remains non-blocking because the baseline is not clean; making it blocking now would fail every CI run without resolving the remaining LangChain migration.
- Optional remote providers and database backends were not live-tested.
- Main branch protection was verified separately: required check `test`, pull requests required, force-push and deletion disabled.

author: castrog
body:
Step 2 of ADR 0025: a function-, block- or `switch`-case-local interface no longer merges with, replaces, or is shadowed by a module-level interface of the same name, and a reference resolves to the nearest enclosing one. Interfaces only; aliases, enums and classes are next.

- `local_depth` and `module_interfaces` are removed. A local interface is keyed `file:Name@f0.b1` (`DeclarationScope::local_key_suffix`), so different scopes are different entries and the same scope still merges. `CollectedInterface` and `FunctionResult` carry their `scope`; the separate `interface_scopes` map from step 1 is gone.
- The resolver tracks where it is reading (`ResolveState.declared_in`, set when reading an interface body, an alias body, or a factory result). `find_declaration` takes the nearest enclosing local interface first, then the module-level one. The `resolve_named` memo key includes the scope.
- A lookup that has no scope finds a local interface only if it is the file's only one of that name and no module-level one exists, so names that do not collide behave as before.
- The `docs/edge-cases.md` entry for local interfaces is updated, and the `switch`-case interface limitation is closed for interfaces.

Known gap, written into `docs/edge-cases.md`: two reads still take no scope, so a local interface that collides with a module-level one of the same name is not found there: a type argument written in a local scope and bound into a module-level generic, and the evaluator's reads other than an indexed access (`keyof`, conditional and mapped types). Threading scope through the roughly 26 `evaluate.rs` call sites is a larger change.

Tests: 12 new tests (extractor and pipeline). Ten fail on main, including module plus function-body interface of one name, two sibling factories, and a local interface extending a local `Base`. Two are guards that pass on main by design. No existing snapshot changed; the cache golden changed with the schema bump (`CACHE_SCHEMA_VERSION` 32).

Against TypeScript's checker (ground-truth harness, uncommitted): the standard generator gives 0 mismatches on valid programs on main and on this branch (seeds 7 and 11, 700 files); 9 new local-interface fixtures (19 props) give 8 mismatches on main and 0 on this branch.

Measured on Chakra with dependencies (`extract --json --load-dependencies --collapse-inherited-props none`, release builds, 9 interleaved runs, medians): cold 291 to 275 ms and 397 to 395 MiB; warm time x0.977, memory x1.004. The Chakra JSON is byte-identical to main apart from `durationMs`.

Checked by the worker: clean-room `cargo nextest` 1296 passed, 1 skipped; `just lint doc-check machete typos` and `just semver` exit 0 (the added public fields are covered by existing pending core changesets; this change adds a patch changeset).

Review round (four findings, all reproduced): a declaration's body was read in the reference site's scope instead of its own. One table test, `a_declaration_body_is_read_in_its_own_scope_by_every_entry_point`, has 10 real-source rows; 7 fail on the earlier tip. The invariant is that the scope in effect while a declaration body resolves is the scope it was declared in, and a type argument keeps the scope it was written in. It is enforced through `ResolveState::enter_declared_in`, now called on three paths that lacked it (direct generic alias expansion, member reads, and factory results through `component_props_type`). Cycle identity in `resolve_props_chain` now includes the reference scope. A fifth case from the same pattern, a local interface passed as a type argument to a module generic, is fixed too. On Chakra (installed corpus) wall time is 0.26 s on both and peak RSS is 411.09 MB on main against 410.98 MB on the branch, with identical JSON apart from durations. Clean-room `cargo nextest` 1298 passed, 1 skipped.

body:
A browser tab that stays open across a Home Assistant restart loads the Noxcast modules again under a new `?v=` cache buster (`panel.py`). Defining `noxcast-panel` (or a card) a second time threw "the name … has already been used with this registry", which the frontend logs. Every module now defines its element only if it is not defined yet, and the two cards add themselves to the card picker only once. The tab keeps the loaded version until it is reloaded, as it did before in effect.

Checked in a browser: every module imported twice under different `?v=` – no error, each card once in `window.customCards`.

## Review
Tier: Frontend and texts.
- A Compatibility: nothing found (no card options or payloads change).
- D Texts: nothing found.
- E Privacy: nothing found.
- F Correctness: nothing found. All 9 `define` calls are guarded; listeners, timers and theme adoption run per element, not at module level; the old panel keeps importing its section modules with its own cache buster, so versions stay consistent within a tab.
- Backtest: not run – no PV model change.

author: romananders90
body:
## Before submitting

- [x] I agree to license this contribution under the terms of [LICENSE.txt](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/LICENSE.txt).
- [x] I ran `pre-commit run` and committed any formatting changes.
- [x] I reviewed the Hard Rules in the `AGENTS.md` for each directory this PR touches (see [root AGENTS.md § Reviewing a PR](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/AGENTS.md#reviewing-a-pr-human-or-agent)) and my changes comply (`python/cudnn/AGENTS.md` Rules 1, 3, 4 and 7 below; the root guide's "Kernel determinism and batch invariance" rules below; no SDPA file is touched, so Rule S2 and the SDPA support-matrix tracker do not apply; Rule 9 does not apply to a direct-call entry -- the graph-API form is a follow-up, as for the fused GDN steps).
- [x] I added GitHub labels: `cat-feature`, `orig-nv-eng`, `mod-cutedsl`, `mod-frost`, `area:frost`, `area:gemm`.

## Affected area

FE OSS kernels or CuTeDSL -- Python only: a new operation family `python/cudnn/moe/` with its FROST backend (`python/cudnn/moe/frost/`), five append-only helpers in `python/cudnn/frost/tile_dsl/`, the lazy `cudnn.SharedExpertDecode` export, tests, goldens and docs. No C++ change, no new dependency, no new environment variable.

## Summary

`cudnn.SharedExpertDecode` (also `cudnn.moe.frost.SharedExpertDecode`) is the bf16 **shared expert** that sits next to a routed MoE, at decode-time token counts, as **two CuTe DSL launches on one stream**:

```text
h    = x @ W_gate_up^T                            W_gate_up [2 I, H] bf16 row-major (gate rows 0 .. I-1, up rows I .. 2I-1)
act  = silu(h[:, :I]) * h[:, I:]                  rounded once to bf16 between the launches
y    = (act @ W_down^T) * sigmoid(x @ W_gate^T)   W_down [H, I] bf16 row-major, W_gate [H] bf16; y [T, H] bf16
```

`x` is `[T, H]` bf16 with `T` in 1 .. 24 (a runtime argument; rows contiguous with any 16-byte-multiple row stride, so a view into a taller slab serves), `y` is written into a caller-owned `[>= T, H]` buffer or the entry's own. The add into the routed output stays with the caller. Served geometries: `Geometry(8192, 256)` (the default: an 8-way tensor-parallel shard of a 2048-wide shared expert) and `Geometry(8192, 128)` (16-way); compute capability 10.x; nvidia-cutlass-dsl >= 4.8.0.

**The pair.** Launch 1 (`gate_up`) is one wave over every SM: 256 CTAs of 256 threads in clusters of eight along K (`K_SPLIT = 8`, 1024-column K slices). Each CTA streams its 32 KB (or 16 KB) slice of `W_gate_up` once by `cp.async.bulk` -- one copy per row, one issuing lane per row -- with the `(gate j, up j)` row pairs resident in the same CTA, so the SiLU-mul sits in its epilogue; the `T` live rows of x's K slice land by one bulk copy each (resident at every T, no ring; rows past T are never loaded). The eight K-slice CTAs of a cluster fold their fp32 partial sums through DSMEM (`st.async.v4`, 16 bytes per lane and tile, completing tx bytes on the leader's mbarrier, which is waited with a cluster-scope acquire) in a fixed rank order; one warp per row-pair group computes its slice of the gate logit `x @ W_gate^T`, folded on the cluster leader the same way. Launch 2 (`down`, 128 CTAs) prefetches its `W_down` rows ahead of `griddepcontrol.wait`, folds the per-group gate partials into `sigmoid` and writes `y`. The math path is `mma.sync.m16n8k16` bf16 -> fp32 in both launches with the tokens on M (zero-padded to 16 or 32 rows); 0 spills in every form (launch 1 at 40-43 / 60 registers for the one- / two-tile forms, launch 2 at 28-40).

**Forms by geometry and part.** The entry compiles once per (geometry, token-tile form, x / y row strides): one 16-token m-tile for `T <= 16`, two for 17 .. 24. The one-wave rule picks the row-pair groups per CTA from the geometry and the part's SM count: at `Geometry(8192, 256)` two groups per CTA (256 CTAs x 32 KB of W, two CTAs per SM at every T -- measured +6..+16 % over the 512-CTA one-group form at 4-6 tokens), at `Geometry(8192, 128)` one group (256 CTAs x 16 KB, four per SM at up to 16 tokens; the two-group grid of 128 CTAs would leave SMs idle). 148- and 152-SM parts pick the same forms. Both forms of the band are resolved and validated at construction, so a config the entry admits never declines at a launch.

**Typed declines**, all before any DSL import: `TypeError` for a dtype or a non-tensor; `ValueError` for a shape, stride, alignment or device mismatch and for a knob combination that no SM100-class part can serve in one wave; `NotImplementedError` for a token count past 24, an unserved geometry, a compute capability outside 10.x (SM90 and SM120 included: no launch-1 form fits a 99 KB per-CTA opt-in), a DSL below 4.8.0 (the message names the installed and the required version, Rule 7), and a part whose SM count cannot hold the pinned one-wave form (the pin never moves to fit a part).

**Numerics and determinism.** fp32 accumulation in a fixed order per output element that is a function of the geometry alone (`K_SPLIT` pinned per geometry, the gate tree's shape by `GATE_CLUSTER_FOLD`), `act` rounded once to bf16 between the launches, `y` once at the end. Against an fp64 reference of the bf16 operands the output sits within the usual bf16 band (rel-L2 2.3e-3 .. 2.6e-3 measured; the harness bound is 2e-2). The pair **replays bitwise** and is **batch-invariant**: a token's bytes alone equal its bytes inside a batch of up to 24, across the one- and two-m-tile forms and the one- and two-group forms (the row-position invariance of the `m16n8k16` datapath, pinned by the batch-invariance cells rather than assumed). There is no determinism switch. Goldens: eight sets under `test/python/determinism_goldens/6451c9d94a2d4210/` -- the default form (`ksplit8`, both geometries x both forms) and the first release's form (`ksplit2` / `ksplit4`, kept as an A/B arm that must reproduce them byte for byte).

**Knobs** (`shared_expert_decode_config.Cfg`, passed as `cfg=`; every knob is a `const_expr` axis of the same two kernel bodies). Bit-neutral: `N_GROUPS` (0 = the one-wave rule), `X_BULK_ROWS` (on; off = the first release's `cp.async` ring), `X_STAGES` (0 = the budget rule; ring form only), `W_PHASES` (1), `ROWS_PER_CTA` (64), `MIN_CTAS_PER_SM` (1), `KRED_SPLIT` (off: the cluster-fold barrier split between the accumulator ships and the gate leaves -- measured, not a win, see below). Rounding-order axes: `K_SPLIT` (8, pinned per geometry) and `GATE_CLUSTER_FOLD` (on). Launch knobs on the entry: `pdl` (launch 1's programmatic-stream-serialization attribute; caller obligation: the immediate stream predecessor must not write `w_gate_up` / `w_gate`, which load before the kernel's `griddepcontrol.wait`), `pdl_pair` (launch 2's; its predecessor is launch 1), `pdl_release` (`griddepcontrol.launch_dependents` at both kernels' entry; measured a loss in every form). All three default off: a knob defaults on only after a measurement with its real predecessor. `v1_cfg(geometry)` is the first release's form (K_SPLIT 2 / 4, 128 CTAs, the x ring, the launch-2 gate fold).

**tile_dsl** (append-only): `barrier.wait_cluster_acquire` (an mbarrier wait with a cluster-scope acquire, for a phase that a peer CTA's `st.async` completes), `tma.ld_shared`, `tma.mapa_u32`, `tma.st_async_f32`, `tma.st_async_v4_f32` (the DSMEM ship helpers). The fused GDN kernels keep their private scalar copies until their next kernel change (their cubins are pinned by md5).

## What changes

26 files, +3,764 / -2, six commits (the kernel pair; the gate partial off the barrier path, the goldens and shared test helpers; the one-wave form; the two-group default and the `ksplit8` goldens; the whole band validated at construction, the pin by geometry alone and the `KRED_SPLIT` arm; a one-tile-only config declined at construction).

- `python/cudnn/moe/__init__.py`, `python/cudnn/moe/frost/__init__.py`, `python/cudnn/moe/frost/kernel/__init__.py` -- the new operation family and its FROST backend (lazy exports

Fixes mac4DSTEM/macTEM#177

SEM brief P4-01. Ports pyEBSDindex 0.3.10.1 to `Sources/TEMCore/SEM/Indexing/`, with its NRL licence named in NOTICE:

- `HoughReflectorLibrary`: the pole families, angle table and triplet table as `tripletlib` builds them, with FCC, BCC and HCP defaults.
- `HoughBandDetector`: the `radon_fast` line plan, LoG kernel, edge fill and convolution; peak finding with sub-pixel fit; and band normals from a Bruker PC.
- `HoughIndexer`: triplet voting, band assignment, QUEST, the confidence metrics, the detector-to-sample frame, the multi-phase pick, and a cancellable parallel `indexMap`.

It runs on the CPU in float64.

## Parity

| Bundle | What it checks | Tolerance |
|---|---|---|
| `m4/hough-library` | families, angle and triplet tables (Ni, BCC, HCP) | indices exact; rtol 1e-7; angles 1e-5° |
| `m4/hough-nickel-block` | Radon transform, convolution, bands, normals, votes and orientations of a 6x6 block | Radon rtol 1e-5; sub-pixel 1e-3 px; fit 2e-3°; misorientation < 0.01° |
| `m4/hough-indexing-nickel-large` (F8) | the full 55x75 map | indexed count within ±1; ≥99 % under 1°; nmatch equal on ≥95 % |

The F8 map test passes on CI.

Apple's float32 sin/cos differ from numpy's in the last ulp. That moves one pixel on 2 Radon lines in one block pattern. The tests allow those lines, and the bands that follow from them, within the brief's 1 px and 1° (see `docs/parity.md`).

The reference fit is an arccos of a float32 dot product near 1, so it carries about 6e-4° of noise.

Decisions:
- D-SEM-70: symmetry variants are compared as families.
- D-SEM-71: results go into `HoughIndexer.Map`.

The CrystalMap conversion is #179. It follows this PR now that #167 has merged.

There is no UI change, so this is unverified on screen. The figure script is `tools/parity/sem/hough_figure.py`.

author: copybara-service[bot]
body:
Only mask the padded last vocab block in chunked XLA linear softmax cross-entropy loss.

cl/1013169187 introduced a vocab-padding mask inside the jax.lax.fori_loop vocab
loop of chunked_xla.py (forward and backward passes). Because v_start was traced,
the dynamic mask evaluation ran across all vocab blocks, which was reported by
ML Compass to regress forward latency from 4.166 ms to 4.790 ms.

This change optimizes the masking logic for both forward and backward passes:
- In Forward: peels the last vocab block out of the vocab loop. The first
  (num_v_blocks - 1) blocks execute through the unmasked loop body with carry
  limited to lse and loss, and only the final block runs with a static mask.
- In Backward: backward stays in one loop to keep dw updated in place, avoiding
  an out-of-loop buffer copy. A static last-block mask is precomputed once
  outside the loop and applied only when j == num_v_blocks - 1. When v_pad == 0,
  masking is completely bypassed.

Measured benchmark results on Misura (TPU v5p):
- unaligned fwd HEAD 4.733 → 3.956 ms (pre-regression unmasked 4.138)
- unaligned fwd+vjp HEAD 11.633 → 10.826 ms (unmasked 10.957)
- aligned fwd HEAD 3.892 → 3.889 ms

Closes #28. Part of #18 (spec §9, §10.2; D8 amendment "Choosing profiled opponents").

## What changes
- **`FullHand::against(pre, post, hero, seed, profile)`**: every bot seat plays the table profile; `FullHand::new` is `against(.., None)`, so reference hands take the exact same code path and RNG draws as before. The deal (hero seat, hole cards) is identical across profiles under one seed.
  - Preflop bots sample `ProfiledBot` (the same transform the build locked for the best-response charts).
  - Postflop the walk is put `against` the profile on the bot's side; bots sample the file's profile strategy on flop/turn and the locked river strategy on the river (new `Walk::actor_strategy`).
  - Hero is graded with `grade_vs` preflop (best-response chart) and `grade_walk` postflop (file / river BR), and every context is filed under the profile (#26 keys).
  - A library without profile data (the installed 245 are reference-only) plays postflop against the reference, graded and filed as reference, and the table says so (`table-hand-profile-fallback`).
- **Storage**: `hands.bot_ids` now holds one entry per seat (`hero` / `reference` / profile id); hands stored before keep `["reference"]` and read as all-reference. Decisions graded against a profile store the `VsProfile` payload under `ev_per_action.vs`. No migration needed (both JSON columns).
- **Review**: `HandReview.seat_profiles` and `ReviewedDecision.vs_profile`; the hand review tags each bot seat, adds a "Table: <profile>" line and shows the exploitative explanation (GTO line, exploit line, EV gap).
- **Desktop**: the opponent picker now also shows in full-hand mode; changing it during a hand applies from the next hand (with a note). Seat tags sit on the pot side of each seat so they cover nothing.
- Spec §10.2 "As built (#28)".

## Acceptance
- [x] Through `App`: a seeded full hand vs "nit" replays identically and grades every hero decision against the nit — `training::tests::full_hands_against_a_profile_replay_and_grade_against_it` (replays the same seed + answers, compares state/end/decisions; records; review returns seat profiles and `vs_profile`; leak buckets are all `nit`). Also `hand::tests::hands_against_a_profile_grade_every_decision_against_it` (reaches flop and river, checks preflop bots only take actions their profile plays) and `same_seed_same_hand_against_a_profile` (maniac).
- [x] Hand review shows the seat profiles (screenshot in the project files: `spikes/hand-review-vs-maniac.png`).
- [x] Reference-table hands behave exactly as today: same path, existing hand tests unchanged and green; `reference_hands_store_every_seat_as_reference`; `a_profile_table_keeps_the_deal_and_changes_the_bots`.

## Review
Independent review (code-review, high) ran on the branch. Fixed: a loose bot holding a combo outside the reference root range used to end the hand as `not-in-range` (blaming hero); it now ends with `bot-off-range` and a message naming the profile (test `a_loose_bot_off_the_library_range_ends_the_hand_with_its_own_reason`). The root cause is a library limitation, tracked in #48 (about 1/3 of station/maniac flops on the fixture). Not changed here: findings on pre-existing code from #25–#27 (leaks opening trainers, reference label in leak buckets, duplicated vs-profile grading in pre/postflop, `Walk::against` by value, river zero-EV with fully blocked bot range, stored format version) and recomputing the preflop transform per bot action (cheap in practice; keeps one source of truth with spot mode).

## Known limits (documented)
- The bot's flop range is the reference range along the line (§9 simplification from #27): see #48.
- Mixed tables (one profile per seat) are the next ticket; `seat_profiles` is already per seat.

## Checks
`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` (incl. desktop with the local xattr patch), `cargo test --workspace --exclude taful-desktop`, `cargo test -p taful-desktop`. Desktop screenshots under Xvfb.

author: katossh
body:
## Summary

- Move the workstation's four `TAG+="uaccess"` rules from `services.udev.extraRules` (`99-local.rules`) to a dedicated `70-workstation-hidraw.rules` provided through `services.udev.packages`.
- Preserve the existing USB vendor/product matches and per-active-seat access model.
- Document why the rules must execute before systemd's `73-seat-late.rules`.

## Root cause

Nixpkgs writes `services.udev.extraRules` to `99-local.rules`. systemd processes the `uaccess` tag in `73-seat-late.rules`, so tags added by the later local file do not receive the expected device ACL. The workstation logs showed the AK620 was detected but `/dev/hidraw7` had only root permissions.

## Validation

- Verified the behavior against the exact locked Nixpkgs revision (`1c89083e451e891152365b799595cf7790a43325`) and its `services.udev.extraRules` / `services.udev.packages` implementation.
- Reviewed the diff; only `hosts/workstation/hardware.nix` and `docs/user-configuration.md` are changed.
- Local Nix formatting, flake evaluation, and build were not run here. The repository's PR workflow should run them.

## Activation

After merging and pulling, apply the system configuration:

```sh
sudo nixos-rebuild test --flake .#workstation
```

Then unplug/reconnect the AK620's internal USB connection (or reboot) so udev reprocesses its device event. Verify:

```sh
getfacl -p /dev/hidraw7
systemctl --user restart deepcool-digital-linux.service
systemctl --user status deepcool-digital-linux.service --no-pager
```

The ACL should contain `user:katossh:rw-` for the active local user. After confirming the cooler display works, make the generation the default with `sudo nixos-rebuild switch --flake .#workstation`.

body:
https://ag-grid.atlassian.net/browse/AG-9003

Fix #AG-9003

Unit 4 of 6 in the AG-9003 stack. It builds on #9009 (`ag-9003/highlighted-item-shadow`) and targets that branch, so the diff is this unit only. Retarget it once #9009 merges.

## What changes

- `glow.gap` is added to `AgGlowOptions` only (a `PixelSize`, validated as a positive number, default unset). Unset, the glow is cast like a shadow, so it shows through an item that is translucent. At `0` the item's own footprint is cut out of the glow, and larger values move the start of the glow outwards.
- The glow is blurred onto a second canvas, sized to the layer and kept per key, and the silhouette dilated by `gap` is erased from it with `destination-out` before it is blitted to the layer. Nothing is erased on the layer or on the shared `kept` canvas.
- The hole is the item's geometry whatever its paint, including the dilated extras (wicks, whiskers), and a fill-less item's stroke.
- Both routes cast it: the engine's mask (`shadowEngine.ts`) and the shape's own cast (`shape/shape.ts`: cutouts, failed root casts). Extents, `planKey` and the silhouette bounds use `gap + spread`.
- `sameShadow` and `matchSignature` keep an unset gap and `0` apart, `glowToShadow` and the HLC and range-area themes carry `gap`, and a `gap` is treated like a `spread` where a path decides the route (`drawsRealPaintWithoutSpread`, `castsShadowFromPrePass`).
- A `Line` has no Path2D to dilate. A shadow root or batch dilates its stroke, so the gap applies. A cutout `Line` casts its glow inline with the stroke, as it does a `spread`, so neither the spread nor the gap applies there.
- The `shadow-root` benchmark gains `glow-gap-bar` and `glow-gap-scatter` cases (gap unset, 0 and 5; load and hover).

With `gap` unset every route is the one it was: no second canvas is acquired and no image snapshot moves.

## Open

- Verified on the skia-canvas mock only. The route has not been run in any browser: not Safari, not Firefox, and not Chromium either.
- Timings are for the benchmark stage; none are quoted here.
- `ag-charts-types:lint` and `ag-charts-core:lint` report warnings in files this PR does not touch.

author: charleslpan
body: ## Summary Agent sends are now one Sentry trace, from the press in the client to the service. That covers Start (and Continue and Fork), a task started with its agent, a steer, and a queued steer (`ADD` and `STEER` queue changes). ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Panel as Panel (renderer / web tab SDK) participant Host as Host (Electron main / tab) participant Service Panel->>Panel: startNewTrace → startSpan("agent.send" …) Panel->>Host: act + sentry-trace/baggage (act-port headers) Host->>Host: SentSendTrace on the call's Effect context Host->>Service: askHosted: sentry-trace + baggage (+ traceparent, same trace) Service->>Service: continueTrace → server span under the press ``` ```diff sendMutation(kind, spanOf) # panel/act-mutations.ts (new) tracedSend(name, trace => sendAct(kind, vars, trace)) # panel/send-traces.ts (new seam) RPCLink headers ← sendTraceHeaders(trace) # panel/app-bridge.ts act-port interceptor # host/act-port/index.ts + sendTraceOf(request.headers) → Context.add(SentSendTrace) askHosted # features/hosted-link.ts - sampled = coin < 0.1 + sampled = press's flag ?? coin; parent = press's span + headers += sentry-trace, baggage procedureTraced / routeFromHttpRouter # service - HttpTraceContext.w3c(headers) + callerTrace(headers): continueTrace(sentry-trace, baggage) ?? traceparent ``` - Span names are one `as const` set, `SENTRY_SEND_SPAN` in `@repo/features/sentry-tracing`: `agent.start`, `task.start`, `agent.send`, `agent.queue`. A sampler can import it. - The shell supplies the seam: `installSendTracer`, over `sentrySendTracer({ startNewTrace, startSpan, getTraceData })`. Until the lazily loaded SDK is ready, a send goes untraced; it never waits for the SDK. - Each send span is the root of its own trace (`startNewTrace`). It's never a child of a page load or navigation, so it's sampled as a send. - No rates change. - The service reads `sentry-trace` through Sentry's own `continueTrace`, and passes on only its trace id, parent span id, and sampled flag, as the Effect external parent. Sentry's Effect tracer continues an external parent from those three alone. So baggage's dynamic sampling context goes over the wire but isn't applied to the service span. - A `sentry-trace` with no sampled flag falls back to `traceparent`. - Effect's router reads only `traceparent`, so for HttpRouter routes the request's `traceparent` is rewritten from `sentry-trace` before the router sees it. - Privacy: a span carries only its name and op. No message text, prompt, file name, or credential is on it. ## Evidence - `packages/service/src/orpc/base.test.ts` turns the existing `traceparent` case into a table. New row: an unsampled `sentry-trace` beside a sampled `traceparent`, with every request traced. The server span takes the Sentry trace id with `sampled: false`. **Before:** fails, because the span takes the `traceparent` trace. **After:** passes. - `packages/features/src/hosted-link.test.ts` gets one new case: an ask under `SentSendTrace`, with a draw that would leave it unsampled, sends the press's `sentry-trace` and `baggage`, and sends `traceparent` flag `01` on the press's trace. **Before:** fails. **After:** passes. - Ran: the two files above, `hosted-call` and `sentry-tracing` tests, the host's `agents-procedures`, `declared-acts`, and `tasks-procedures` tests, the panel's `act`, `use-agents`, `use-agent-queue`, and `use-tasks-tab` tests, typecheck of features, host, panel, service, web, and desktop, biome, oxlint, the anti-slop guards, `discarded-effect`, and `repository-checks.sh`. CI runs the rest. ## Merge Danger **Door:** two-way Measurement only. Reverting brings back today's separate traces. **Blast Radius:** tracing - A send is sampled at the client's rate, `SENTRY_TRACES_SAMPLE_RATE`, which today is the same 1 in 10 as before. - The act port now carries two more headers on sends. - Nothing about the Mac changes beyond the renderer's spans, and no macOS check runs this. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Send actions from the desktop and web apps now carry trace context through the host to the service, making related activity easier to follow across the request path. * Agent starts, messages, queue changes, and eligible task starts are included in send tracing. * Service request traces and logs now use caller trace information when available, preferring Sentry trace context over `traceparent`. * **Bug Fixes** * Sends made before tracing is ready continue to work without trace context.

author: mikejmckinney
body:
The credentials rule from #22 said never to write a key's value anywhere, including a scratch file outside the repository. In practice that blocked every task that needs an API key: an agent can only use a key it has read, and keeping it for the next command means writing it somewhere.

The owner accepts that keys appear in the agent session's own transcript. The rule now draws the line at what other people can read:
- Read only the keys a task needs, from the owner's secrets doc.
- Keep them in one file outside every repository, readable only by the agent (`chmod 600`). Load that file per command and refer to keys by name, not by value.
- Never print a key, and never put one in a repository file, commit, PR, issue, comment, artifact or CI log.
- If a key reaches one of those places, tell the owner which key and where, so it can be rotated.

The credential scan from #22 still blocks a key that reaches a commit.

author: alastor0325
body:
`revue --repo <linked worktree>` treated the linked worktree as the main repo: the default pick skipped it, so another worktree opened, and one repo could be mounted twice under different path spellings.

- Any path inside a repo (main checkout, linked worktree, or a folder in either) resolves to the main worktree (`resolveRepoTarget`). A path in a linked worktree selects that worktree; a worktree name argument wins over it. This also covers an old `defaultRepo` that points at a linked worktree.
- The hub compares repos by `pathKey` (realpath, forward slashes, no trailing slash, lower case on Windows), on add and on `--restart` merge, so one repo is one project.
- Worktree names that would collide (a folder named like the main repo, or `/a/proj-x` and `/b/x`) get a `-N` suffix, so a name always maps to one worktree.
- `revue <name>` and `revue --repo <main> <name>` work as before.
- Release commit bumps to 0.3.2.

Tests (local, macOS): non-UI jest 563 passed, `npm run test:ui` 218 passed. New tests in test/integration.test.js ("--repo at a linked worktree ...") and test/git.test.js (parseWorktreeList name collisions). This repo has no test CI workflow.

author: shatheitguy
body:
## Why

On a Raspberry Pi running 0.8.0, Settings → Software Update showed **"Update to  flopped · The updater stopped before it finished"**, with an empty version and an empty log.

**Root cause:** the 0.7.x updater was killed when install.sh stopped the service, leaving its lock (`update.running`, a bare timestamp with no target or unit). The owner then updated by hand with the one-line installer, which didn't remove the lock. Once 0.8.0 decided the lock was stale, it recorded it as a failed update to an unknown version (`to: ""`) and showed it forever.

## What changed

### Update run / status
- A stale lock is only a failure if its target is newer than the running version. Unknown targets and targets that are already running get cleared quietly.
- Failed results are dropped if they have no target, if their target (or something newer) is already running, or if they're older than the moment the running version first started (`version-seen.json`). Real failures, like a rolled-back update, stay.
- An older version's lock only counts as running while an updater or installer unit is actually active. Before, it counted as running for up to 90 minutes.
- The updater exports `NEEDRESTART_SUSPEND=1`, so package installs can't restart services mid-update.
- install.sh waits up to 2 minutes for NoCapOS to start instead of 30 polls. Slow SD cards could trigger a false rollback.
- install.sh clears leftover locks when run by hand.
- NoCapOS updates and system package jobs refuse to run at the same time.
- Settings never shows a blank version.

### Reconnecting
- `lib/reconnect.ts` probes `/healthz` with a timeout and a backoff of 1s up to 8s, and never gives up.
- It probes again right away when the tab becomes visible or the network comes back.
- A redirect (HTTP→HTTPS, another address) triggers a full page load that follows it.
- The update overlay wraps its status call in a timeout. After 3 minutes it offers a reload (for example when the browser needs to trust the certificate again), and it keeps polling.
- Restart and shut down from the power menu use the same logic.

### Look
- The update overlay and the restart/shut-down screen show `/brand/mark-512.png` with a slow glow.
- Both use a brand-red progress bar with a gradient sweep. While the server is away the bar becomes an indeterminate slide.
- Both honour `prefers-reduced-motion` and the in-app reduce-motion setting.

### System packages (Settings → Software Update)
- Software Update now has two parts: **NoCapOS** and **System packages**.
- System packages lists pending updates. Security fixes are marked: apt suites ending in `-security`, parsed from `apt list --upgradable`. Kernel and Pi firmware updates are flagged too.
- **Check now** and **Install updates** run as audited Packages jobs with live output, using `ActRefresh` and `ActUpgradeAll`.
- Kernel updates leave a restart-needed mark (tied to the boot ID; `/run/reboot-required` also counts), with a **Restart** button.
- A daily background check (added to the existing release check loop) refreshes the lists and sends a notification about new security updates. The same set doesn't notify twice.
- apt "upgrade all" now uses `--with-new-pkgs`, so new kernel packages aren't held back.

### Boot splash
- `deploy/plymouth/`: a script theme "nocapos". The logo sits centred on near-black with a breathing red glow, three loading dots, a progress bar, and a disk-password prompt. Assets are generated from `mark-512.png` and shipped in the bundle (package.sh / package.ps1).
- install.sh installs Plymouth if needed (apt/dnf, not with `--minimal`) and runs `plymouth-set-default-theme -R nocapos`, but only when the theme changed.
- It adds `quiet splash` to `GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX_DEFAULT` and runs update-grub. On a Raspberry Pi it adds `quiet splash plymouth.ignore-serial-consoles` to `/boot/firmware/cmdline.txt` (or `/boot/cmdline.txt`), kept on one line.
- If Plymouth isn't available it skips with a warning. `--no-branding` skips it too.
- uninstall.sh restores the previous theme and removes only the tokens install.sh added.

## Tests
- `update_stale_test.go` covers `versionAhead`, `staleFailure`, the legacy lock being cleared silently (the Pi case), a stale lock for the running version, dropping the bogus result already on disk, and `versionSince`.

author: 0xb1ob
body:
## Verdict: (a) production bug

The intermittent failure in `tests/e2e/dispatch-s29.test.ts` "S29: public validation refuses unavailable routing, effort, skills and inactive jobs" (`timed out … waiting for worker script untouched; last = 0`; main runs 42188730223, 42132325529; PR run 42213088183) came from a real dispatch bug. Test isolation was not the cause.

`assertDispatchable` in `src/dispatch.ts` refused only `closed` jobs. A `deferred` pi job went through lease → branch → checkpoint → deps → brief → **worker spawn → brief sent**, and only then did `Ledger.claim` refuse it with `is deferred`. Dispatch cleanup then killed the worker. The worker's first model request raced that kill; when it reached the mock provider first, it consumed the `worker` script.

Temporary request and run-event logging (removed before commit) showed the deferred job's run log in every logged run: `spawned, checkpoint_captured, deps_prepared, original_task_frozen, routing_resolved, prompt_sent, agent_start, turn_start, message_start, message_end, message_start, message_end, process_exit, job_branch_cleaned`.

## Behaviour (Gherkin)

```gherkin
Feature: cp_dispatch refuses a deferred job before taking anything

  Background:
    Given a ledger job for project "demo" with status "deferred"

  Scenario: dispatching a deferred job is refused up front
    When the parent calls cp_dispatch for that job
    Then the call fails with "<id> is deferred; review its task and authority, then use cp_job update status=open when authorized"
    And no worktree lease is taken and no job branch is created
    And no worker is spawned or prompted, so no "spawned" run event is written
    And no request reaches the worker's model
    And no fleet record is written

  Scenario: previewing a deferred job is refused the same way
    When the parent calls cp_dispatch with dry_run true for that job
    Then the call fails with the same "is deferred" message

  Scenario: a job deferred while its dispatch is in flight is still refused at the claim
    Given an open job whose status turns "deferred" after the up-front checks
    When the dispatch reaches the ledger claim
    Then Ledger.claim refuses it with the same message
    And the spawned worker is shut down and no fleet record survives
```

Pinned by: the first two scenarios by `tests/e2e/dispatch-s29.test.ts` "S29: public validation refuses…" (subtests 6 and 7), the third by `tests/e2e/dispatch-cleanup-s29.test.ts` "a ledger claim refused after spawn leaves no fleet record".

## Fix

- `src/ledger.ts`: `deferredRefusal(id)` holds the one deferred message, and `Ledger.claim` uses it.
- `src/dispatch.ts`: `assertDispatchable` refuses `deferred` with that message before anything is taken. This covers `cp_dispatch` and its `dry_run` preview, and matches script dispatch, which already refuses any non-open job up front. The claim check stays for a job deferred mid-dispatch. The file stays within its grandfathered 960-line structure cap: one duplicated blank line was dropped, and the ceiling is unchanged.
- `docs/contracts.md`: one sentence on that ordering. `changelog.d/cp-s29-root-cause-fc6i.md`.

## Test (kept e2e, every assertion kept)

- **Gherkin:** a `// Scenario:` comment (Given/When/Then) above the e2e test, the repo's convention.
- **Removed the deferred exemption** from the no-spawned-event check. This makes the check stricter.
- **Added a deferred `dry_run` variant**, from a review finding: the docs and changelog claim the dry-run refusal, so a test now pins it.
- **Negative control:** with the up-front check disabled, subtest 6 (deferred dispatch: `no spawned event` timeout) and subtest 7 (deferred dry run: not refused) both fail.
- **Changed the empty-fleet wait** so it treats an absent `fleet.json` as an empty fleet. Before the fix, the deferred dispatch was the only step that created that file. Once nothing writes it, `readFleet` hits ENOENT: the first after-fix loop failed 10/10 on that alone. The assertion still requires zero fleet jobs.
- No change to `defaults/ci-flakes.json` (the S29 seed stays).

## Failure rate, before and after (local loops of `npm run test:one -- tests/e2e/dispatch-s29.test.ts`, whole file)

| | runs | test failures | deferred worker spawned | stray `worker` requests |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| before, plain | 20 | 0 | 13/13 logged runs (logging added from run 8) | 0 captured |
| before, 6-thread CPU stress | 10 | 0 | 10/10 | 0 captured |
| after, plain | 10 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| after, 6-thread CPU stress | 5 | 0 | 0 | 0 |

The CI timeout did not reproduce locally: the kill usually wins the race on this machine. The precondition for it, a worker spawned and prompted by a refusal step, appeared in 100% of logged runs before the fix and 0% after. After the fix no worker exists, so the race cannot happen.

## Checks

- `npm run typecheck`: exit 0.
- `tests/e2e/dispatch-s29.test.ts`: exit 0 (21/21), including the new dry-run variant.
- `tests/structure.test.ts`: exit 0. This was CI's failure on 2f8ab8b: `src/dispatch.ts` was 961 lines against a 960 cap. Fixed in 15bcc81 without raising the cap.
- `tests/e2e/dispatch-cleanup-s29.test.ts`: exit 0. This covers the claim race path.
- `tests/e2e/retired-integration.test.ts`: exit 0. This covers the claim message.
- `tests/contracts-exports.test.ts` passes unchanged. `node scripts/eval.ts --out evals/results/contract.json` left the file unchanged. `npm run eval:contract` and the env-prefixed `CP_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1` form are refused at the tool boundary; no golden changes.
- No pi agent run was needed, so no throwaway agent dir was created. The tests use the harness's own temporary `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR`.

Holding at review pass for the main session's merge bar.

author: yyhhyyyyyy
body:
## Summary

Wakeup records are Scheduler's process state with no Timeline fact, so a client showing them polls `session.wakeup.list`. Now each committed record change is announced as a Session notice: `session.notice` with `source: "Scheduler"`, `kind: "wakeup"` and `data: {branchId, wakeupId, state}`, sent with `session_broadcast::notify` from the Scheduler's own context after the record's write commits.

The send points are: `create`, once the record is stored, with the state it was created with (`scheduled`, or `expired` when the instant is already past the grace); `cancel`, when it settles a `scheduled` record (`cancelled`), while a cancel of a terminal record changes nothing and sends nothing; and the timer pass, with one notice per record it settled (`fired`, `cancelled` for a target that is gone, or `expired`), after the settle write. A `fired` notice follows the `input/message` the pass wrote, because the pass publishes the input, then settles the record, then announces it. Retention pruning changes no readable record and sends nothing.

The notice is not a Timeline event and adds no `hello.features` entry: notifications are not methods, and this is protocol v3 only. Delivery follows the notice contract: a Session that is not loaded, or that no client observes, has no listener and the notice is dropped, and nothing is replayed. A client reads `session.wakeup.list` when it attaches and on every notice; the notice reports that the record changed, and the list is its truth. Because the notice travels on the Session's channel, a client attached to the Session receives it whichever branch the record targets, and `data.branchId` names that branch.

The design is `docs/design/plugins/Scheduler.md` section 11 and 11.1, with the zh mirror. Files: `crates/dim-agent-scheduler/src/methods.rs` (the owner keeps its generation context), `crates/dim-agent-scheduler/src/wakeups.rs` (the notice and its three send points), `crates/dim-agent-scheduler/tests/wakeup_flow.rs`, and the regenerated architecture graphs.

## Design rule checklist

- [x] Scope: Scheduler's process owner holds the wakeup records and sends its own notices; nothing moves scope and no wiring module is added.
- [x] Commands and results: n/a. The notice reports a change the owner already committed to its own store; no other module's state changes.
- [x] Handover: n/a.
- [x] Timeline `before` callbacks: n/a.
- [x] Infrastructure (Timeline, Dispatcher, event envelope, assembly and lifecycle, Session and branch facades): unchanged. The notice uses the existing broadcast channel and the existing `notify` function.
- [x] Core mechanisms and consumers gain no plugin-specific handling: the broadcast and Rpc never interpret `source`, `kind` or `data`, and no core module names Scheduler.
- [x] Batch: n/a. The notice has no sequence and is not a fact.
- [x] Context: n/a. Nothing enters model context.
- [x] No reading another plugin's internal state or deciding for it: the notice is emitted by the owner of the state, from its own context, and clients read what changed through the owner's query.
- [x] Business configuration stays out of loader rows; contracts are language-neutral: one notification with a data object, no configuration.
- [x] Missing mechanism capabilities: none raised. The change uses the existing Session broadcast, which already lets a process-level owner announce committed changes.
- [x] Timeline holds only facts later decisions use: no event is added; the notice reports process-level state and clients recover through `session.wakeup.list`.

## Documentation

- [x] No accepted ADR is modified or deleted.
- [x] No other module's design is changed. The Scheduler page states the notice, its send points and its delivery contract; the zh mirror is updated too.
- [x] No delivery status is added to an ADR, index or roadmap.

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo clippy -p dim-agent-scheduler --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test -p dim-agent-scheduler --test wakeup_flow`, 22 tests. The new ones: an attached client receives `scheduled` on create and `fired` after the wakeup `input/message`; a settling cancel announces `cancelled` and a second cancel of the terminal record announces nothing; a record the pass expires announces `expired`; a second client attached to the same Session receives a notice for a record targeting another branch, with `data.branchId` naming it.
- `cargo run --locked -p xtask -- check`
- Ablation: with the timer pass's notices removed, the `fired` and `expired` expectations time out, and the two tests fail.

Refs #1225

author: semdinsp
body:
## Why
At a restart, the reactivator activates every version, and each one probes its own strike/expiry candidates through `ContractSelector` → trading_hub's `ContractResolver.resolve/4`. Versions on the same underlying probe the same strikes.

On 2026-11-06, about ten XLE versions asked for the same unlisted strikes (62C/59P/57P/62P in Dec/Jan/Feb). trading_hub logged 38 TWS 200 "No security definition" errors between 22:41:07 and 22:41:25. The hub caches hits but not misses, so every repeat was a new `reqContractDetails` to TWS. The trading_hub session reported it.

## What
- New `TradingOptionsSim.ContractListingCache`: a supervised owner of a public ETS table. `cached/1` wraps a resolver function, and both `resolve_via_hub` call sites in `ContractSelector` (single leg and combo) go through it.
- It keeps only definitive misses (`:not_found`, `:ambiguous`), for 1 hour (`:contract_listing_cache_ttl_ms` overrides that). A hub that didn't answer isn't cached, since nothing was learned. Hits are already cached by the hub.
- The key is `{symbol, expiry, strike, right}`, with the strike normalised so 62, 62.0 and Decimal 62.00 match.
- Without the table (the process not started), it calls the resolver unchanged.
- Reactivation is sequential (`Enum.each`), so no in-flight coalescing is needed.

## Tests
- `mix test`: 868 passed.
- `mix compile --warnings-as-errors`: clean.
- New `contract_listing_cache_test.exs`:
  - ten versions probing the same unlisted strike → one hub call for it;
  - `:ambiguous` is cached;
  - transient errors are not cached;
  - strike normalisation;
  - a different expiry or right is a separate key;
  - TTL expiry.

body: ## Summary Every published docs page was downloading the Nibleaf marketing site: the landing page and marketing shell, the blog manifest, and Arabic marketing copy, about **31 KiB gzip** of JavaScript a reader never uses. This PR removes that leak and adds a check so it can't come back. Part of #291. | Build (gzip level 9) | public-docs | public-docs-index | | --- | --- | --- | | main@ed15240e | 383.79 KiB | 382.99 KiB | | this PR | 352.57 KiB | 351.76 KiB | The dashboard also gets lighter on first load (dashboard-home 1270.41 → 1241.41 KiB) because the same modules were eager there too. ## Root cause TanStack Router splits each route's `component` into a lazy chunk, but everything else in a route file (`validateSearch`, `loader`, `head`, and **anything the file exports**) stays in the router's eager chunk, which every page loads. 1. **Exported page components (~30 KiB).** `routes/about.tsx` and `routes/developers.tsx` exported `AboutPage` and `DeveloperResourcesPage` so tests could render them. The code splitter can't drop exports, so `components/cloud-marketing.tsx` came in through them, and with it the blog manifest, its Arabic copy, the privacy-choices dialog and several icons. Rolldown emitted this as a bare `import "./cloud-marketing-*.js"` in the entry chunk. 2. **Arabic marketing head copy (~0.5 KiB).** The `/ar` and `/ar/documentation-platforms` heads read seven long Arabic strings through `siteT`, the reader's own translator, and the Vite `public-site-i18n` group pinned those messages to the reader's eager messages chunk. ## Changes - Move `AboutPage` and `DeveloperResourcesPage` into `components/marketing/about-page.tsx` and `components/marketing/developer-resources-page.tsx`. Route files now export only `Route`. Tests import from the new modules. No copy or design changes. - Load the Arabic head copy from the two routes' loaders (`lib/arabic-marketing-copy.ts`, a lazy import) and pass it to `head` through `loaderData`. SSR output is unchanged; the copy is serialized with the page like any loader data. - Drop those seven keys from `siteT` (typed out of `SiteMessageKey`) and from the `public-site-i18n` Vite group. - **Regression guard** in `scripts/check-bundle-budget.mjs`: - fails when a public profile (which always includes the `__root__` route's preloads) contains `components/cloud-marketing.tsx`, anything under `components/marketing/`, `lib/blog-manifest.ts`, or `marketing_*`/`blog_*` message modules. It uses the module report from `BUNDLE_ANALYZE=true` builds; CI now always builds that way, and the check fails in CI if the report is missing or stale. - fails when marketing or blog copy from the English and Arabic catalogs (201 strings, read at check time so it follows copy edits) appears in any public asset. This one needs no module report, so it also runs locally. - Verified: on the intermediate build where the Arabic messages were still grouped into the reader, the check failed with `includes marketing copy (marketing_arabiclanding_title) in /assets/public-site-i18n-*.js` and the matching module errors. - Lower the public docs budget from 393,000 to 365,000 bytes (~4 KiB above the measured size) and document the import-boundary rules in `BUNDLE_BUDGET.md`. - `turbo.json` lists `.bundle-analysis/**` as a build output and `BUNDLE_ANALYZE` in the build's env, so a cached build restores a report from a build that actually wrote one. Still eager, and small: `lib/marketing-seo.ts`, `lib/blog-seo.ts` and `lib/marketing-faqs.ts` (about 2.5 KiB), because marketing routes' `head` functions use them. The dashboard-route part of #291 (loaders, search schemas, query keys) is a separate PR. ## Test plan - `pnpm --filter @nibleaf/app build` with `BUNDLE_ANALYZE=true`, then `node apps/app/scripts/check-bundle-budget.mjs --check`: passes, numbers above. - `pnpm --filter @nibleaf/app exec vitest run src/routes/-developers.test.tsx src/routes/-marketing-locale.test.tsx author: capi-git
body:
Found by a review of the changes merged since 0.1.171.

**Problem:** #325's new `menu` action walks an app's menu bar from the top, and the first item of every menu bar is the system Apple menu. An agent with consent for any one app could send a path like `["Apple","Sleep"]` (or Lock Screen, Restart…, Shut Down…, Log Out…, Force Quit…) and act on the whole Mac in the background.

**Fix:**
- `hide_system_menu` blanks the menu bar's first item (and any top-level item titled "Apple") before matching, so it can't be chosen and isn't listed in `appState`'s menu names or in "no such item" errors.
- `activate`: once activation is confirmed, a failing window listing no longer turns success into an error; it only leaves out `windowId`.

**Checks:** new unit test; `cargo test --no-default-features --lib` (1,084 passed) and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --no-default-features -D warnings` pass locally. Not tried live against a real app's menu bar.

author: bfs2021
body:
## Problem

Since 0.6.1, a refracting paraxial (thin-lens) surface flips the sign of its power when rays reach it traveling along the surface's local -z, i.e. when the lens is simply rotated (for example `rx=pi`). A positive thin lens then acts as a negative one, so a folded arm that mounts a paraxial focuser backwards stops focusing after upgrading. A thin lens has no front or back, so its power must not depend on the mount orientation.

Fixes #1108

## Root cause

PR #514 rewrote `ThinLensInteractionModel.interact_real_rays` and added `f = self.f * copysign(1, rays.N)` for refracting surfaces. For mirrors hit from behind the mirrored sign convention is intentional, but for refraction it combines with the existing `N = where(rays.N > 0, f2, -f2)` into a double flip: for `rays.N < 0` the outgoing `N` becomes positive (`-f2 = +f*n2`), so transmitted rays reverse their z direction and the lens acts with inverted power. #514's tests only cover unrotated surfaces, where `copysign(1, rays.N)` is a no-op.

## Fix

For refracting surfaces, drop the `copysign` on `f` and keep the unflipped `f1 = f*n1`, `f2 = f*n2`. The transmission-side sign of the outgoing `N` is already handled by `where(rays.N > 0, f2, -f2)`, which is symmetric under `z -> -z`: for `N > 0` nothing changes (bit-identical to before), and for `N < 0` the outgoing direction `(n1*f*L - x, n1*f*M - y, -n2*f)` now aims at the focal point on the transmission side with the on-axis slope preserved. The mirror branch and the `f < 0` negation are untouched.

## Testing

- Added `test_paraxial_surface_refraction_survives_flip` (rx = 0, +pi, -pi): a perfect-imaging optic whose image plane sits at global `z = f` in every orientation. Fails on current `main` for rx = ±pi on both the numpy and torch backends (`rays.y` spread of ~18.7 mm instead of 0), passes with the fix (all 60 tests in `tests/test_thin_lens_interaction_model.py` pass, covering the existing perfect-imaging, mirror, OPD, and plane-refraction cases).
- Issue reproduction: the rx=0 vs rx=pi focus test from #1108 gives a 20 mm spot extent on 0.6.3/`main` and 0.000 mm (focused) with the fix; `optiland==0.6.0` focuses both orientations, matching the regression report.


## Checklist

- [x] If this PR addresses an issue, I claimed it there first and nobody else had.
- [x] I have read the entire diff and can explain every change.
- [x] This PR is one logical change and is as small as it reasonably can be.
- [x] Tests are added or updated, and the relevant ones pass locally (NumPy and PyTorch where applicable).
- [x] Public API is unchanged, or the change was discussed in the linked issue.
- [x] Docs and docstrings are updated where needed.

## AI assistance

- [ ] No AI tools were used.
- [x] AI tools helped (tool: ZCode CLI). I reviewed, ran, and understand all of the output.

author: danielh2018
body:
## What changed, and why

Closes #7506.

An audit of `docs/target-architecture/host/h7-delete-ansible.md` on 2026-11-07 found the *Steps, as PRs* table no longer described the remaining work. `setup_census.py` reports 407 items left on daniel-server, 391 on daniel-pi and 537 on daniel-box, and H7.53's strict census fails while any setup role has a task. No row deleted most of `initial_setup`, `chezmoi_setup`, `github_cli` or `common/tasks/`. The H2 edge on H7.34, H7.35 and H7.48 also held H7.52 and everything after it behind H2.8c, a docs PR that cannot read until about 2026-11-20.

Plan text only. No role, component or test changes.

**One decision for the operator.** H7.58 deletes `Update and upgrade system packages`, because a package cannot run a dist-upgrade. After it, `unattended-upgrades` applies what its origins allow, and every other package update waits for a hand run. The plan marks this **operator-only**: H7.58's PR asks for the ruling.

## What the plan says now

- **H7.58 to H7.60:** the host baseline in canary order, in a `host-hardening` component and `host-tuning`.
- **H7.61 and H7.62:** dev tooling and the worktree holder scan on the two dev hosts, plus `chezmoi_setup` and `github_cli` on daniel-box.
- **H7.63:** the setup-drift check, the collections install and `common/tasks/`, after the deployer's timer.
- **H7.64:** the mirror registries' GC moves to a daniel-box component, because it is the only collector of those stores and D5's operator ruling keeps it a host script.
- **The task-file index:** a new subsection names the row for each of the 67 task files.
- **H7.44 owns `k3s/tasks/server.yml`.** H7.42 merged with those tasks still in place, so old H7.9's fallback named no PR. H7.53 therefore waits on H7.44 and H7.45 as well, or its strict census could not pass.
- **H7.49a and H7.49b:** land.sh's half can run first. monitor-bridge's half merges immediately before H7.52.
- **H7.39:** recorded as landed in #6593, with the uv, Python and prek tasks it never deleted handed to H7.61 and H7.62.
- **H2's status line:** H2.4a and H2.5a are finished inside their CronJob PRs, and H2.6 is dropped to D5.
- **`contracts.md`:** repeats the H7 edges, so its row changes too.

## Why H2.8c constrains none of the three rows

It edits `docs/k3s-etcd-restore.md` and no task file, and it adds no absent arm. Its conditional operator step deletes only old script-made `offbox-*` objects. Native snapshots keep the `offbox-` name, and `scripts/backup/etcd_restore_drill.sh:518` takes the newest `offbox-*` object from the `etcd-snapshots` folder, so the drill finds a snapshot under either outcome.

The narrowed edges come from the file lists of the 21 PRs H2's Status line names. Only these touch the three role directories outside tests and `CLAUDE.md`:

```text
7008  k3s/defaults k3s/files k3s/tasks k3s/templates
5349  k3s/defaults k3s/files k3s/templates
6086  k3s/templates
6105  k3s/defaults k3s/tasks k3s/templates
5753  k8s_host_files/files k8s_host_files/tasks k8s_host_files/templates
5619  k8s_host_files/tasks
5706  k8s_host_files/tasks
5678  k8s_host_files/tasks
7176  k3s/defaults k3s/files k3s/tasks k3s/templates
```

## What I rejected

- **Listing `/usr/local/bin/uv` for deletion with the per-user tooling.** It has readers: `hosts/components/claude-code/`, `hosts/components/loki-route-witness/`, `scripts/backup/etcd_restore_drill.sh`, `k8s/manifests/tasks/release_digest.yml` and setup role templates. H7.61 adds a `/usr/bin/uv` component on the `sops` pattern and repoints them.
- **One PR for H7.49b and H7.52.** Flux and the package apply independently, and `check_gitops_alive` pages on a stale `last_run`, so one PR could not fix the order. Two merges back to back with a live wait can.
- **One row for the whole baseline.** It reaches all three hosts, so *Canary hosts stay apart* requires three PRs. `AllowGroups ssh-users` makes the group's move a possible lockout.
- **`sysusers.d` for `ssh-users`.** The tree runs `systemd-sysusers` only from the users arm, on its own file, and only for a missing user. Bootstrap step 4 creates the group before step 5 installs `AllowGroups ssh-users`.
- **Adding the rsyslog filter and the holder scan to `host-tuning` and `claude-code`.** Both hosts list those components, so a file there would skip the canary. Each gets its own component, listed per host. `/usr/bin/uv` alone reaches both hosts in one PR, because shared templates read it, and it only adds a path.
- **A canary for H7.63.** It deletes read-only checks and tasks nothing on a host depends on.
- **A new test for the index.** The issue says to change the plan only, and H7.53's strict census is the enforcement that already exists. The check below was a scratch run.

## Services touched

None. Docs only.

## Deploy

- [ ] Deployed after merge (`land.sh` printed `VERDICT: settled`)
- [ ] Deliberately deferred — reason:
- [x] Nothing to deploy (docs-, test-, or `tasks/`-only)

## Render-diff

Render-diff: none

## Verification

- [ ] `uv run python scripts/diagnostics/probe.py health <svc>` passed. Not run: nothing deploys.
- [x] Exercised the changed behaviour itself: a scratch script walked `git ls-files 'ansible/roles/setup/*/tasks/*'` against the index and read the three rows' edges.

```text
task files: 67; named in the row index: 67; missing: []
index paths that are not task files: []
H7.34 H2 edges: ['H2.8a']; names H2.8c: False
H7.35 H2 edges: ['H2.2c', 'H2.3a', 'H2.3c', 'H2.3d', 'H2.3f', 'H2.8b']; names H2.8c: False
H7.48 H2 edges: ['H2.2c', 'H2.3d', 'H2.3f', 'H2.4c', 'H2.5b to H2.5d', 'H2.8b']; names H2.8c: False
H7.49 rows: ['H7.49a', 'H7.49b']
```

`uv run python scripts/dev/repo_guards.py`, run after the last commit:

```text
2400 passed, 72 skipped in 75.52s (0:01:15)
exit: 0
```

Live reads the plan quotes, from 2026-11-07. On daniel-server:

```text
ls: cannot access '/etc/systemd/system/cpu-governor-performance.service': No such file or directory
powersave
snapd  2.78     28332  latest/stable  canonical**  snapd
ssh-users:x:1001:root,ubuntu,claude
```

On daniel-pi and daniel-box, `dpkg -S` names `base-files` for `/etc/issue` and `/etc/issue.net`, `dpkg-query` lists both as conffiles, and `getent group ssh-users` prints `ssh-users:x:1001:ubuntu`.

Not measured: `sshd -T | grep -i banner` needs root and printed nothing, so H7.58 reads it before it decides `/etc/issue.net`. No tree or live read confirms that `chezmoi init --apply`'s replacement keeps daniel-box's dotfiles current, so H7.62's body owes that statement. The destinations in items 34 and 35 are plan, not built code: H7.58 to H7.62 confirm each against the tree when they land.

## Tests fail without the change

No tests added or changed. The PR is plan text only, so there is nothing to run against the merge base.

## Blast radius

- [ ] This is a **broad** change. It edits no path under `ansible/`.
- [ ] New check, guard, or probe. It adds none.

Filed for later: #7525

body:
## Goal
FR-3.5 follow-up, PR 3.4b (decided by the orchestrator in PR 4.4's open questions). The interviewer's hand edits are refused by the hook, so it needs typed commands for the writes SKILL.md "Hand edits" still listed: creating access.yaml, a golden's role, user, reference and tolerance, and a source's description.

## Plan
- [x] `sl set access mode open|closed` creates a draft access.yaml (`mode`, `status: draft`) when none exists. It validates first, never writes through a link, and prints what it wrote and the next step. An existing file behaves as before.
- [x] `sl set golden:<g> role|user|reference|tolerance (<value>|--unset)` keeps comments and validates. `role`/`user` are refused until access.yaml exists. `user` is a JSON object without control characters, `tolerance` a decimal in [0, 1), `reference` is folded to one line.
- [x] On a confirmed golden: `tolerance` is refused, naming `sl readback --targets golden:<g> --tolerance <t>` and `sl goldens confirm`. A `role`/`user` change is written and listed in `reapprove` unless a recorded owner yes matches. `reference` is outside the hash.
- [x] `sl set source:<s> description <text>` (folded to one line, control characters stripped).
- [x] Unknown keys are refused with the list of keys each target takes. Malformed golden/source names are refused, naming `sl status`.
- [x] Spec rows, `--help`, SKILL.md "Hand edits", and the access/verify/intake phase cards are updated. The hook allows the new commands for `sl-interviewer`.

## Changes
- `scripts/lib/set-targets.ts` (new): `createAccess`, `setGolden`, `setSource`.
- `scripts/commands/set.ts`: routes `golden:`, `source:` and the missing-access.yaml case, and extends usage/summary. `--json` is `{ changed, file, reapprove, ref, key, value }`, plus `created: true` on creation.
- `scripts/lib/validate.ts`: an access.yaml given only as an override counts as present, so creation is validated before it is written.
- `scripts/lib/edit.ts`: the missing-access.yaml message names `sl set access mode`.
- Docs: `references/spec.md` (set row and Typed-edits bullets), `SKILL.md`, `references/access.md`, `references/intake.md`, `references/phases/access.md`, `references/phases/verify.md`.

## Invariants touched
- Write only inside the semantic root, keeping comments: access.yaml is created with `wx` after an lstat check, so it never writes through a link. Guarded by 'never writes through a link at the path, even one to nothing outside the root' and the byte-exact comment-preservation tests.
- No approval without the owner's yes: a confirmed golden's tolerance is refused, and role/user changes are routed to re-confirmation. Guarded by the confirmed-golden tests and 'a change back to what a recorded owner yes matches asks for no re-confirmation'.
- Data text is evidence: source description and golden reference are folded to one line, and control characters in user attributes are refused. Guarded by the source-description and user-value tests.
- Deterministic outputs: guarded by 'is deterministic: the same call on two copies writes the same bytes'.

## Tests
- `tests/typed-edits-3.test.ts` (20 tests):
  - access.yaml creation: open and closed modes, `--json`, determinism, refusals, refusal when validation would fail (including the closed-mode hint), link safety, and the existing-file path.
  - golden keys: comment-preserving writes and unset round trip, idempotence, and value validation (hex/binary tolerance, control characters).
  - no access.yaml: role and user refused, with access creation still possible afterwards.
  - refusals: malformed names, unknown keys and confirmation fields.
  - confirmed goldens: tolerance refusal and the default-tolerance no-op, role/user re-confirmation routing, and a change back to a recorded yes.
  - source description: write, unset and refusals; `--help`.
- `tests/agent-roles.test.ts`: the hook allows the new commands for `sl-interviewer`.
- `tests/skill-docs.test.ts`: pins the spec row against `--help` and the new SKILL.md/phase-card lines.
- `bash scripts/verify.sh` after merging the latest `release/v1`: 2939 pass, 0 fail, `verify: ok`. With 4.5 and 6.1a merged in too: 2978 pass, 0 fail.

## Eval delta
None.

## Open questions
None. [B] Decision: tolerance is limited to [0, 1) as a decimal literal, matching `sl goldens confirm --tolerance`. This is stricter than the handoff's "number >= 0". To revert, widen the check in `goldenValue`. About 265 changed lines outside tests, within the size target.
