body:
### Summary
Restricts direct host access to LiteLLM in production while preserving access through Nginx.

### Changes
- Production now binds LiteLLM host port `8030` to localhost only:
  ```yaml
  LITELLM_HOST_PORT: "127.0.0.1:8030:8080"
  ```
- The LiteLLM container remains accessible internally on port `8080`.
- Public clients continue accessing LiteLLM through:
  ```text
  https://litellm.ideaxiom.org
  ```
- Updated the deployment completion message to indicate that `8030` is loopback-only.
- Updated the LiteLLM HTTPS documentation accordingly.

### Expected behavior
- Remote access to production port `8030` is blocked.
- Localhost access from the production VM remains available.
- Nginx can continue proxying public HTTPS traffic to LiteLLM.
- Staging and `next-dev` keep their existing port bindings and are unaffected.

No LiteLLM API, authentication, Nginx routing, or certificate configuration was changed.

author: lusetto
body:
Branch: `feature/238-pause-on-buffering` (from master 7aa6293), tip edef0a5

## What changed
- **New host switch** in the party menu, under "Wait for everyone": **Pause when someone is buffering** ("Hold playback while someone's video stalls"). Off by default. Stored in the room's rules as `stall`; rules from an app without it read as off.
- **The hold:** with it on, a member whose video stalls mid-video (shown as Buffering after 1 s, as before) holds the room once the host has seen the stall for another 0.5 s, using the same `held` flag as loading. The picture says "Waiting for <name>…". The hold starts where the stalled member stopped (if that's at most 10 s behind the room), so the others go back the second or two the stall took to notice and nobody misses anything; play resumes for everyone from there when the member plays again.
- **Limits:** the room gives up on a stall after 20 s, and holds for one member at most 3 times in 2 minutes. After that the member shows as Buffering and catches up by itself (the existing follower), as it does with the setting off.
- **Stalls go with the position report, not only presence.** Presence updates are rationed (5 per 30 s, #227), so a stall told by presence alone was seen late or not at all after a join or a few stalls, and a release could wait for the budget with everyone paused. A member now sends its position report at once when it stalls and when it plays again, with `stalled: true/false` (and every 5 s as before). The host goes by that, and by presence's Buffering for an app that doesn't send it. A stalled player's report also says it isn't moving, so "N s behind" doesn't count on.
- Short stalls (under about 1.5 s) never hold. With the setting off nothing changes.

## Tests
- Harness cases (#203, `tests/partyChaosCases.test.ts`, with `stall()` in `tests/partySim.ts` doing what `usePartySync` does): a stall holds everyone where it stopped and play resumes together (positions within 0.5 s); the room gives up after 20 s and doesn't hold again for that stall; three holds in two minutes, not a fourth, and again once the window has passed; stalls of 0.8, 1.3 and 1.5 s never hold; with the setting off a stall is shown and nobody pauses.
- `tests/partyMessages.test.ts`: `stall` in the rules (absent = off, not a boolean = rejected) and `stalled` on "at".
- `tests/dom/partyMenu.test.tsx`: the new switch changes the rules; the hold overlay names the stalled member only when the room pauses for stalls, from presence or from the earlier position report.

## Checked
`bun run typecheck` (with e2e), every unit test file, DOM tests (102), `vite build`, cycle check (only master's known cycle), e2e chromium desktop/phone/TV 52 passed; desktop-webkit party test fails only where playback starts (local WebKit plays no media). No Rust changes.

## Not covered
- Real networks with real stalls: needs two or more devices in a party with one on a throttled connection.
- A member on an older app doesn't send `stalled`: the host goes by its presence's Buffering, which comes a second or two later and is subject to presence's rationing; its hold starts where the room is, not where it stopped.


Closes #238

body:
## User impact

With snap paging, a Carousel row narrowed under a finger rests short of its end, cutting off its last item: 0.6 px after 1 px; 99.9 px after 100 px, three per view.

## Problem and solution fit

- Why? A held row keeps its takeover travel, so the last stops clamp to it after a resize. A release also moves at most one page from the drag's start index, which a narrower view renumbers.
- Why does it harm the task? The lift rests at the old end, or a page short.
- Why does it matter? The row stops short of its last item.

Now the held travel follows a resize, and a drag keeps its start page.

## Expected behavior and authority

`component:Carousel` FR7: the last stops are "clamped where the row ends so no empty space shows"; representative state: "The last page rests where the row ends." No record changes.

## Smallest restoration

- `remeasure()`, first in `measurePages`, moves the takeover's travel by the change in span and width since, rounded once. The span shares `snapStops`' scale read.
- `usePager`'s `measure()` maps a drag's start page by offset when the pages change.
- The travel rounds to whole pixels, as WebKit truncates scroll offsets.
- When the travel drops below the held scroll offset, the browser clamps it; `remeasure()` moves the held offset with it.
- Review notes: two comments trimmed, one case title corrected.

## Evidence

iOS 26.2 simulator, Mobile Safari.

| | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Partial last page, 1 px | ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vjeux/astryx/46bac23f33ec003852d39a9997c4345264a6935c/ios-held-resize-before.gif) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vjeux/astryx/46bac23f33ec003852d39a9997c4345264a6935c/ios-held-resize-after.gif) |
| Three per view, 100 px | ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vjeux/astryx/46bac23f33ec003852d39a9997c4345264a6935c/ios-three-up-resize-before.gif) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vjeux/astryx/46bac23f33ec003852d39a9997c4345264a6935c/ios-three-up-resize-after.gif) |

Before: 411 of 412, 616 of 716; after: the end. Frame gaps ≤ 25 ms.

- Reproduction before the change: NOT-FOR-LANDING arm ac95af7d3476153c22a0f8e5ccc659e3f219d35c (these tests on main) fails every unit and narrowing run, in both engines.
- Result after the change: 10 of 10 per case in each engine.
- Unchanged: the SnapPaging, Carousel and press-trace specs.
- Mutation-sensitive proof, each a NOT-FOR-LANDING commit removing one hunk: without the moved travel (70e36cc6707ff830898b1eec2cc9fdd2a0f131b0), both narrowing stories fail; without the page mapping (2c577ba61621c355d32dc07d20e2013ec6a1395d), the unit and three-per-view paging cases; without the clamp re-base (35a4704131c1c228b22e6608eb9880ae49ae4a15), the widening and multi-frame cases; rounding at each resize (ef4ac455284047b34749ce441e56eed8db621f68), the multi-frame case.

## Scope

- [x] One defect is restored.
- [x] Separable contradictory or unsettled tagalongs were removed or split.
- [x] No new public API, visual representation, default, or interaction model is hidden under the bug-fix label.
- [x] Public text and artifacts contain no internal Meta context.

## Testing

- `pnpm exec vitest run --project ui packages/core/src/{Carousel,SnapPaging,hooks,gestures}`: 96 files, 1,930 tests pass.
- `tsc` for core, Prettier, ESLint, `pnpm check:changesets` and `pnpm check:knowledge`: clean.
- The SnapPaging, Carousel (with its two snap-paging specs) and usePager interaction specs, 3 runs each: Chromium 192 passed, 0 failed; WebKit 200 passed, 1 failed at a host load of 23 to 50. That one is the one-item-per-view flick case: its flick never moved the row ("Received: 0"), as the three-up flick case also fails on main under load.
- The resize tests, 5 runs per mode in each engine: the narrowing cases red on main (411 of 412; 616 of 716) and green here; the widening and multi-frame cases (items 40 % of the row, narrowed 1 px a frame for 20 frames) green on main and here, and red on their mutants.
- The press trace ("a press reads the row before its first write"): 5 of 5.

author: rafaelguerrae
body:
## Problema

O broker Mosquitto de produção (`data-track.duckdns.org`) exige TLS na porta 8883 e usuário/senha, mas o firmware usava `WiFiClient` (sem TLS) na porta 1883, então o ESP32 não conseguia publicar em produção. Resolve o M-12.

## Alterações

- Troca `WiFiClient` por `WiFiClientSecure` e valida o servidor com a raiz ISRG Root X1 (Let's Encrypt) via `setCACert()`, sem `setInsecure()`. A raiz, que é pública, fica versionada em `src/ca_cert.h`.
- Sincroniza o relógio via NTP antes de conectar ao MQTT, porque o TLS valida a data de validade do certificado. A sincronização usa `millis()` (sem `delay()`) e tenta de novo se o NTP não responder em `NTP_TIMEOUT_MS`.
- `config.example.h` passa a apontar para o broker de produção (host, porta 8883, usuário `device`) e ganha `NTP_SERVER` e `NTP_TIMEOUT_MS`. A senha continua só no `src/config.h` local, que é ignorado pelo git.
- Adiciona o template de PR em `.github/pull_request_template.md`.
- Os tópicos (`temperature`, `status` retido com LWT, `fault`) não mudaram.

author: bjstabi
body:
PR 6 of plan 1 (`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-06-format-4-writer.md`), the format-4 writer. Targets the long-lived branch `feat/format-4`. The default stays `writer.format: chunks`.

## What changed

- **Compaction** (`src/writer/compaction.ts`): when a session closes with two or more flush partitions, `close()` merges them into one partition per table.
  - The merge is streamed through parquet-wasm, reading the inputs' row groups and writing the output incrementally. It merges at most eight files per round, through temporary files in the new folder.
  - The output is byte-identical to encoding the sorted union of the rows, and a test compares the two.
  - Spans, logs and points keep every row. Traces are re-aggregated by trace id and patterns by cluster id, so each compacted partition still has one row per trace and one per cluster.
  - Only the report's own `flush:` partitions are compacted. A pattern cluster id is only meaningful within that lineage.
- **Commit order in `close()`**: state v2 first, then the manifest listing the compacted entry, then the flush folders are deleted. Before compacting, the session's dedupe set, normalizer and Drain are serialized and released. The final state is byte-identical to what it would have been without the release.
- **Prune on open**: opening an existing report removes the partition folders the manifest does not list. It also removes unlisted files inside listed folders and leftover merge files, but keeps each listed file's `.js` wrapper. A crash at any step of `close()` therefore reopens to a consistent report, and tests cover each step.
- **File system port**: a directory removal and a lazy file blob for streaming reads, in both the real and the memory file system.

## Decided on the way

- **A failed compaction is not fatal.** It is logged, and the report closes with its flush partitions listed. Such a report is still valid.
- **No session use after release.** Once `close()` has released the session state, adds and flushes are rejected. A retried `close()` still works.
- **A corrupt input file makes compaction fail instead of hang.** parquet-wasm panics inside the stream, and the panic only surfaces as an uncaught `WebAssembly.RuntimeError`. While a compaction runs, one shared `uncaughtException` listener turns such a panic into an `invalid-report` rejection. Any other error goes to the host's own listeners, or crashes the process as before when there are none. A panic fails every compaction running at that moment.
- **Partition entries stay in ascending order** in the manifest.
- **An open fails if prune cannot remove a file**, rather than leaving a stale file a later cut could list.

## Measurements

These are peak RSS when converting the e2e scale data (100k spans, 1M logs, the scale metrics) to one compacted partition, on an Intel Core Ultra 7 265K:

| runtime | format | wall | peak RSS |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Bun 1.4.4 (the single binaries) | chunks | 10.0 s | 466–489 MB |
| Bun 1.4.4 | site, before this PR | 11.4 s | 567 MB |
| Bun 1.4.4 | site, with compaction | 16.9–17.0 s | 640–664 MB |
| Node | site, with compaction | 18.5 s | 695–757 MB |

This is over the plan's rule that a site convert stays within 25% of chunks. The maintainer accepted the numbers for the format-4 work. #210 tracks revisiting them before format 4 is released. Most of the rise is Bun not yet having collected the ingest garbage when the spans merge starts. The compacted output is about 1 MB.

## Review

Every task passed a task review on Opus 5.5 (implementers on Sonnet 5.5). Fix rounds followed, and Opus 5.5 re-reviewed each one. The Task 6.1 review found that a source error partway through a merge produced a valid but truncated file, which `close()` would then have listed, deleting the originals. That is fixed and tested. The branch review ran on **Opus 5.5**:

> PR 6 is ready to merge after two small fixes, I1 and I2. There are no Critical findings.

The review built the linux-x64 single binary and ran a site convert in it. The convert compacted 262 partitions into one, and appending after the compacted close kept numbering, series ids, deltas and cluster ids. Two findings were fixed in the last commits:
- a `close()` after `abort()` could write without holding the lock;
- CI's binary smoke step never compacted. It now runs a second convert that does, on all three binaries.

The same commits prune leftover folders at close, fold trace and pattern rows as they are read, move the checkpoint code into its own module, and document compaction in the README. An Opus 5.5 scoped re-review checked them. The review's notes for the `local` wrappers (PR 7) and `merge --compact` (PR 8) are in those PRs' briefs.

`mise run check` and the Chromium e2e suite passed on the branch.

body:
An AI player may keep a **private notebook on each rival** -- off by default (`ai-game --notebook-cap N`).

- One note per RIVAL (never itself, never a seat that does not exist), rewritten when it wants; an empty note forgets.
- Each note is capped: the cap forces the choice, and what it cuts is **counted** as forced forgetting (`notes_cut`).
- Every version of the notebook is journaled (`notes` in each decision) -- the game forgets for the player, the journal does not.
- The notes live in the player, **never in the view**: another player never reads them (a test checks it).
- **A defect found on the way:** the answer parser cut the reply at the FIRST closing brace (a non-greedy regex) -- a nested `"notes": {...}` object would have been split in two and the answer read as invalid. It now reads the first complete JSON object (`parse_reply`); the old parser, put back as a mutation, fails 7 tests.

**Checks:** 10 tests; 10 mutations, all killed (one survived at first -- an empty note kept; the test now checks the notebook itself). Full suite: 364 passed. Public guard: 0 identity pattern.

Its measurement (lean Claude vs 3 Normals, 6 games, prediction written before) follows in the private journal; the TRUTH of the notes is judged later, with rules written before anyone reads them.

author: scadoshi
body:
Item 65.

## What it is

From 960px (60rem, where the kit draws sheet forms as modals, as the oracle tag dictionary's modal does), the printing picker is `SheetFrame { wide: SheetWide::Modal }` with the card filter's sheet markup: a dimmed backdrop, the title bar's ×, Esc and a backdrop click to close (with the same Printing unchanged toast as before), sized like the dictionary's modal (`min(76rem, 100vw - 4rem)` by 92vh) and layered over a details sheet as `.sheet-over` layers the narrow picker.

Inside, a cover flow in **3D perspective**: the stage has `perspective: 1600px`, and each card is `translateX / rotateY / scale` from its offset, with side cards turned 38 degrees toward the middle. I chose 3D over a flat fan because it reads as a cover flow and still animates only `transform` (plus the veil's `opacity`), which stay on the compositor. Each step out is shifted further, smaller (0.82, then 0.05 less a step, floor 0.36), lower in the stack and darker.

Darkness is a black `::after` veil per card driven by `--flow-dim` (0.3 at the first neighbor, 0.05 more a step, up to 0.75), not opacity: opacity would show the cards behind through each other. `filter: brightness()` worked too, but the veil is simpler to layer.

- Moving: the wheel or a trackpad's sideways scroll (60px a step, the larger axis), Left/Right, a drag (70px a step), or a click on a side card. Every card is keyed by printing id, so one 0.3s ease transition glides the whole stack.
- Selecting: Enter, a click on the centered card, or Select. It is the existing save (toast, close); like the old checkmark, it does nothing and Select stays grayed while the centered printing is the one the sheet opened on. A read-only sheet has no Select.
- Under the stage: set name, collector number, the price chips (zwipe-ui's `info::prices`), "n of N", then Select.
- Many printings: only the selected printing and up to 10 each side render (`flow_window`), images are the Large size with `loading=lazy`, and the wheel and drag step by thresholds, so a 146-printing card stays light.
- Reduced motion: no transition on the cards or the veil.
- Below 960px: today's picker, unchanged. The 900 to 960px range keeps today's centered modal, because the kit draws the modal form only from 60rem; this matches the dictionary.

`cover_flow.rs` holds the pure math, `flow_slot(offset)` (shift, scale, turn, layer, shade) and `flow_window(selected, count)`, with 7 unit tests: center slot, mirror symmetry, turning toward the middle, monotonic steps, floors, and window bounds.

Local zerver, signed in, headless Chromium at 1280x900:

Replace the two dynamic spelling tables with one canonical UTF-16 slot index. Use fixed-width packed hashing and reuse cached hashes during growth. Preserve symbol IDs, exact spelling equality, lone surrogates and both stored encodings. The macro generates ordered spelling arrays and rejects duplicate decoded spellings. The common index is immutable and built at compile time.

Verification covers the all-feature interner and macro tests, collision wraparound, cross-encoding hashes, duplicate macro rejection, the parser and engine suites, strict lint, WebAssembly, public API audits and independent source review. Unicode UTF-8 hits moved from 19–22 ns to 33–39 ns and Unicode UTF-16 hits from 11–13 ns to 17 ns. Short ASCII and common hits were noisy. In the paired engine fixture with 32 parameters and 32 lexical declarations, ordinary ASCII medians were 92–93 µs before and 89–90 µs after. The Unicode identifier variant was 89–93 µs before and 88–90 µs after. These are exploratory measurements. Fallible work admission remains the next part of #1979.

author: manny536
body: ## Goal PEAICE FREE SHOOTER should use the full box it is given, keep a square-pixel canvas, and stay readable on a narrow or short frame. Arrow keys, WASD, Space, and touch or wheel gestures during a round must not scroll this document or the pages wrapped around it. Scrolling has to work again on the title, after pause or game over, and after the frame blurs. The catalog and the IONOS services module size the iframes. This change does not edit those repos. It only reports the wrapper contract they need. ## Why Two separate bugs were showing up as one small, jumpy embed. The title, pause, and game-over screens, plus the combo, boss bar, and power HUD, were still inside `#hud` because that element was never closed. `#hud` is only as tall as its header. Those screens are absolutely positioned, so they filled that short strip. Centering the intro in an ~84px box pushed **PEAICE FREE SHOOTER** above the iframe, where `overflow: hidden` clipped it. The canvas itself already filled the frame. The game document is not a scroll container. The key handler cancelled Space only. Arrow, Page, Home, and End keys, and the wheel, therefore bubbled to the nearest scrolling ancestor. On the live page the catalog iframe is grown to its content height, so that ancestor is the services page. WASD do not scroll on their own; they are cancelled during play so they cannot start to. Before the fix, one ArrowDown moved the catalog about 36px and a 240px wheel moved it 240px, while the game document stayed at scroll 0. ## What changed - Close `#hud` so overlays and screens position against the full frame. The stage fills the iframe. The canvas buffer uses the same aspect as its CSS box, so it is not stretched or cropped. - Cancel gameplay keys, wheel, and touchmove only while a round is playing. Title, pause, game over, blur, and hide release the lock. Blur and hide also pause, drop held keys, and zero velocity so a key released outside the frame cannot stick. - Tab still leaves the playfield. Ctrl/Cmd/Alt shortcuts, including Ctrl+R, are not captured. Focus moves to the playfield on start and to Resume or Re-engage afterward, without a scroll-into-view jump on same-origin parents. - Full screen uses the stage. If an ancestor iframe does not allow it, the button explains that and offers **Open full page**. - Touch controls stay hidden until play, including on a coarse pointer, so they do not cover the intro. Names, weapons, and the enemy line are unchanged, including **Benevolence Drift** in full. peaice.org links are unchanged. ## Checks `node tests/scroll-lock.mjs` (Playwright, Chrome). 89 checks passed. - Game alone at 1280×800 and 390×844: stage and canvas fill the frame, buffer aspect matches, title and **Benevolence Drift** stay inside the frame, arrows and WASD move the player, Space shoots, the document stays at scroll 0, Tab reaches Pause, Ctrl+R is not cancelled. - Short 960×448 iframe, the size the catalog uses today: intro is inside the frame instead of clipped above it. - Nested cross-origin services page → same-origin catalog → game. On the title, arrows and the wheel scroll an ancestor. After start they do not, including PageDown, while the player still moves and shoots. Pause lets the wheel scroll again. Resume locks it. Blur clears a held direction. After blur, arrows scroll the services page. - Content-sized catalog, matching the IONOS `embedHeight` pattern where the catalog itself does not scroll: play does not move the services page; after pause a wheel moves it by the gesture amount. - Touch drag does not scroll during play and does scroll after pause. - Full screen: the stage goes fullscreen on its own. With `allow="fullscreen"` on both ancestor iframes, the nested game fullscreen the stage. Without it, `document.fullscreenEnabled` is false and the note names the missing permission. ## Wrapper contract for the catalog agent This file fills the iframe. It does not choose the iframe’s size. Today `.demo-frame` is `height: min(28rem, 70vh)` inside a narrow column, which is why the game looks small. Recommended game iframe: ```html ``` ```css .demo-frame-shooter { width: 100%; display: block; border: 0; background: #0a0a12; height: min(100dvh, max(36rem, 56.25vw)); } @media (max-width: 640px) { .demo-frame-shooter { height: 100dvh; min-height: 32rem; } } ``` `56.25vw` is 16:9 of the viewport, with a 36rem floor so a narrow column does not collapse to a short strip. Below 640px, use the viewport height. Fullscreen needs `allow="fullscreen"` and `allowfullscreen` on **every** ancestor iframe, set before the frame navigates: 1. The catalog `demo-frame` around `https://manny536.github.io/peaice-games/`. 2. The IONOS services HTML-module iframe around `https://manny536.github.io/peaice-grok-index/references/`. Fullscreen permission is `self` by default and does not pass through a frame that omits `allow`. No parent script is required for the scroll lock. Do not put `pointer-events: none` on the iframe. ## Limitations - Keys are delivered only after the iframe is focused. The game cannot cancel keys while the parent page is focused. - Same-origin parents are pinned for a few frames after focus so Chrome’s scroll-into-view does not nudge the catalog. A cross-origin parent cannot be scrolled back from inside the game. - iOS Safari does not fullscreen a plain element. **Open full page** is the fallback. - The live wrapper stays `min(28rem, 70vh)` until the catalog agent applies the contract above. Inside that box the intro now fits; it scrolls inside the frame only if the box is shorter than the copy.

author: asyraf2003
body:
Implements #21 on top of #20.

Android authorizes GitHub with device flow, stores and refreshes tokens inside its encrypted portable vault, selects an owned private repository and explicit branch, publishes ciphertext with read-back/conflict checks, and downloads encrypted recovery ZIPs. Native amendment preserves vault identity and recovery configuration; rotating tokens replicated to another device require fresh authorization there.

Enrollment provides password Show/Hide and inline errors. Account/login/sudo accepts valid 4+ characters; root stays locked and disk passwords remain 12+. Independent recovery is optional: schema 1 retains a passphrase capsule, schema 2 requires a surviving device key. Neither backup exports an opening identity. Repository and branch labels remain visible, and existing-repository uploads require an explicitly named branch.

Validation: 56 foundation, 14 native portable and 27 JVM tests; Go vet and Android build/lint pass. Full disposable 4 GiB VM run 42326651995 passes installation, numeric-four-character account login/sudo, retained no-recovery vault, real TTY/Openbox startup, and LTS recovery boot. Physical isolated POCO F6 tests cover Keystore, enrollment, token amendment and refresh-journal failure cases. The owner completed actual enrollment, GitHub authorization, private upload and ZIP download. The downloaded ciphertext matched its GitHub object/digest, and the commit only added allowlisted backup files. The actual ZIP recovered on Linux with a key received through owner-approved pinned USB; recovered account and GitHub credentials match without exposing values, while missing-key recovery is rejected. Evidence remains private outside the public repository.

Limits: cloud backup 8 MiB; native amendment 16 MiB. Draft experimental APK; no PR merge, stable release or physical formatting. Automated checks are not an independent human review.

## Summary

These are fixes from a full audit of the live site. The audit covered:
- a crawl of all 40 sitemap pages, desktop and phone;
- every internal link;
- a Lighthouse run on 5 pages.

The crawl came back clean. Lighthouse found three things, fixed here:

- **Contrast:** a grey (`#737373`) on the CTA cards, the split cards and the footer copyright fell just under WCAG AA. It is now `#6b7280` on the light cards (4.6:1) and `#8b8b8b` on the dark footer (6.0:1).
- **Blog tables:** eight comparison tables had an empty top-left header cell, so the first column had no header for screen readers. The cell now reads "Compare".
- **Security headers:** every response now sends `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN`, `Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin` and a `Permissions-Policy`. `X-Powered-By` is turned off. Vercel already sends HSTS.

Lighthouse accessibility goes from 96 to 100 on the homepage, `/legal/mva` and a blog post. Best Practices stays at 100.

author: qkrtkddn218
body:
회전 후 몸 방향이 정확해도 복셀 누적과 추적 확인 때문에 첫 STOP이 늦게 나오는 문제를 다룹니다. 가슴 보정 PR #98 위에 쌓은 변경이며, 기존 map.minHits·Tracker 확인 횟수는 유지하고 현재 깊이의 공간 지지와 서로 다른 연속 장 확인으로 근거리 STOP 후보를 추가합니다. policy.nearStop=null 기본 OFF입니다.

NearStopDetector는 기존 신뢰도/앞단/바닥 처리를 거친 현재 장 점을 공간 셀별로 줄이고, 셀 수·높이/좌우 폭·바닥 여유를 확인합니다. 동일 시각 깊이는 재확인으로 세지 않고 비관측/긴 공백/바닥 불명/RESET에서 후보를 끊습니다. 정식 근거리 track과 중복 제거, 현재 머리 ROI·관측 나이 재검사, STOP 전용 처리, 기존 확인 STOP 우선 순위를 적용합니다. 실험 문턱은 near-stop.experimental.override.json에만 두며 HITS/paired chestMount/prioritizeStop을 요구합니다.

합성 비교(기본 회전 각 방식당 16조건, 같은 정답 사건 표본):
- 회전 중 STOP 12/72(16.7%) → 53/72(73.6%).
- 회전 직후 1초 448/480(93.3%) → 479/480(99.8%), 이후 2초는 양쪽 976/976.
- 첫 평가 사건 → STOP 표본 지연 약 167~200ms → 0~67ms. 물리적인 센서/오디오 지연 0ms라는 뜻은 아닙니다.
- 빈 방 회전·평행 측면 벽 대조는 각 방식 22조건/2,542표본에서 STOP 0회. 지속 깊이 유령·실제 촬영 오탐률을 검증하지 않았습니다.

검증: core main/test Kotlin 2.4.20 CLI 컴파일 후 JUnit 6.1.3 core 404/404 통과(새 9개 포함). 186조건/558구간 독립 JVM 두 번의 cases/trace CSV 바이트 일치. OFF 기존 112조건의 모든 공통 열 값 동일. PC 단계 시간은 별도 stage_timing.csv에 기록(기본 회전의 추적+근거리 p95 약 0.853ms, 다른 테스트 동시 실행 중 측정). git diff --check 통과.

남은 한계: 빠른 −180도/0.5초는 여전히 회전 중 STOP 0%인 조건이 있고, 임시→정식 인계로 대상 STOP ID 수가 1→2로 늘어납니다. 독립 음향 청취·ID 연속성·움직이는 물체 TTC/기존 필터와의 조합·실제 반사/블러/추적 오차·하네스 치수는 별도 검증 대상입니다. 프로필 maxGap/maxAge 150ms 때문에 낮은 처리율에서 같은 개선을 보장하지 않습니다. Gradle 다운로드 Network is unreachable로 Gradle 작업/Android 빌드는 확인하지 못했고, 실기 설치·청취·촬영은 하지 않았습니다. 기본 채택하지 않습니다.

docs/ROTATION_NEAR_STOP.md에 정의·실패 조건·재현 명령, docs/rotation_near_stop_cases.csv에 전 조건 결과를 기록했습니다. Windows에서 CSV 잠금을 피하도록 새 -Pout 폴더를 쓰는 실행 방법을 안내합니다.

## Windows 재현 및 실제 회전 검증 범위

Windows에서 합성 186조건을 재생해 기본 회전 중 대상 STOP 비율 12/72 → 53/72를 재현했다. 기존 실제 촬영 61개에서 추적 정상 프레임의 수평 카메라 방향 범위를 확인했다. 실내 13개 중 최대 10.3°(중앙 캐리어), 야외 48개 중 최대 5.2°였다. 실제 90° 회전에서의 STOP 개선과 오탐률은 아직 검증 전이다. 동일 촬영본 A/B 재생 설정과 절차는 `docs/ROTATION_REAL_AB.md`에 있다.

body:
A standalone Video Keypad currently has a camera entity but no way to see its cached battery reading or tell whether a live session is starting, streaming, or failing. This adds diagnostics and a **Refresh battery and power** button to the same device created by the current `develop` camera implementation.

- Battery, reported power mode and sample time are read from a private cache. The button requests metadata for that camera, with a 15-second timeout and a one-minute cache for repeated presses. Loading entities, reading sensors and restarting HA do not request a battery sample or wake video.
- Session phase, active consumers, first-frame time, session errors, credential renewals, streaming/problem indicators and video transport are driven by the existing shared session. Transport reflects the observed media sender and remains unknown until observed. Diagnostic callback failures do not interrupt video.
- Uses upstream's per-camera inventory and exact target resolver. The 12 new entity labels are localized in all supported locales, and user-assigned names take precedence.

This is directly based on `develop` (`f271fb2`); it does not depend on #11 or #12–#16. Recording controls and preview timestamps belong with their respective features in #15 and #14.

Validation: 293 tests, Ruff lint/format, strict mypy and pinned Hassfest passed at `2cdf03e`. Metadata GETs retain the device headers, reject redirects and cap the response at 1,024,000 bytes. Tests include camera-only discovery, two distinct camera targets, cache/refresh behavior, media sender classification, translated registry entities and preservation of a custom name. The exact upstream port has not been retested on hardware.

Integration check: a local merge rehearsal of #14, #15 and #17 passed 325 tests, including HA setup with two standalone keypads and 17 pre-existing registry entity IDs per keypad. All 34 IDs survived setup, record/cancel targeted their respective cameras, and setup made no image, alias or power requests. The branches overlap in platform registration and translations, so preserve both sets of entities when reconciling later merges.

author: damianvtran
body:
## The problem

Release: patch — a failed Reconnect in the app no longer marks a never-tripped or already-reconnected MCP server as "keeps dropping"; breaker and monitor wording no longer promise a Reconnect restores the server.

Follow-up to #3523. Its review and design rounds deferred five findings to one PR ([review remediation](https://github.com/damianvtran/local-operator/pull/3523#issuecomment-6698717775), [design remediation](https://github.com/damianvtran/local-operator/pull/3523#issuecomment-6698718418)):

- **R2-1.** `reconnect_server()`'s failure arm re-paused every server and armed a probe, including servers the breaker had never tripped. The monitor then said such a server "keeps dropping" when it had never dropped.
- **R2-2.** If a `reload()` connected the server while a manual Reconnect's dial was in flight, the dial's failure still marked it paused, leaving a live server suspended with a probe armed against it. When that probe woke it tore the live connection down and redialled it.
- **D1/D2.** The breaker row's tail said Reconnect "restores it at once", which a failed Reconnect falsifies. It had also dropped the model's do-not-hammer instruction.
- **D3.** The monitor detail "paused and retried" paired two opposite verbs.

## The change

- **`reconnect_server` (manager.py).** Reads `was_paused` before its reset. The failure arm re-pauses and arms a probe only when `was_paused` is true **and** the server is not connected. That is the same connected check `_rearm_paused_probe` makes. A server that never tripped fails exactly as it did before #3523.
- **Probe connected check (manager.py).** `_schedule_probe` snapshots the connection registered when the probe is armed (`armed_on`). On waking, a probe that finds a *different* connection in the slot closes the breaker (suspension, burst history, cool-down) and exits without teardown or redial. It compares by identity rather than by `name in _connections` because a call-site trip (`_reconnect_for_call`) deliberately leaves its *failing* connection registered, and the probe must still replace that one. The naive check fails `test_a_call_site_trip_arms_the_probe_too` (mutation-checked).
- **Copy.**
  - `MCP_BREAKER_TAIL` is now `It is retried automatically, so the agent need not call its tools until it is back; Reconnect on its row in the app's Integrations settings retries it now.`
  - The monitor detail is now `MCP server "<name>" keeps dropping; reconnects are paused for a cool-down, then retried automatically`.
  - Both pins are updated. The constant's comment explains both clauses.

**Unchanged:** the burst limit, the cool-down ladder, the auth arm, the guides, `# i18n: ignore` pragma count (`incidents.py` stays 16).

## Testing evidence

New tests in `TestHalfOpenBreaker` (tests/unit/mcp/test_manager.py), run against `5e0a68da186`'s manager.py with this branch's tests:

| Test | base 5e0a68da186 | this head |
|---|---|---|
| `test_a_failed_reconnect_repauses_only_a_server_that_was_paused[never_tripped]` (R2-1) | FAILED `assert True is False` (suspended) | PASSED |
| `…[was_paused]` (R2-1 control: the preserved behaviour) | PASSED (by design) | PASSED |
| `test_a_failed_reconnect_never_repauses_a_server_connected_meanwhile` (R2-2) | FAILED `assert True is False` | PASSED |
| `test_a_probe_that_finds_the_server_connected_stands_down` | FAILED `assert 7 == 6` (redialled) | PASSED |
| `test_a_call_site_trip_arms_the_probe_too` (existing; guards `armed_on`) | PASSED | PASSED; FAILS if the identity check is weakened to `name in _connections` |

**Notice clip.** The new detail is 95 chars plus the server name. With the longest legal name (`SERVER_NAME_RE`, 100 chars) it is 195 chars, inside the stall notice's 200-char `NOTICE_ERROR_CHARS`. The monitor pin test now asserts this.

**Suites.** All run with an isolated HOME, `scripts/run_bounded.py`, `-n 0`:

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| tests/unit/test_incidents.py | 103 passed |
| tests/unit/guides | 75 passed |
| tests/unit/monitors | 607 passed |
| tests/unit/i18n/test_harness_enforcement.py | 2 passed |
| tests/unit/mcp | every test passed (no F/E), then the conftest real-store tripwire exited 1 (see below) |

The tripwire reported that two real session directories had vanished from `~/.local-operator/sessions`. The run's HOME was a scratch dir, and other sessions on this host were active at the time. CI's run of the same suite is authoritative.

**Lints.** black 26.1.0, isort 5.13.2 and flake8 are clean on the changed files, and pyright 1.1.414 reports 0 errors.

author: elian-perez
body:
## Mostrar el mensaje de error de la API al crear un reporte
Cuando la API rechazaba un reclamo (por ejemplo, `FUERA_DE_LA_CIUDAD`), la app mostraba "No se pudo enviar ahora", guardaba el reporte para reintentarlo y volvía atrás. Estaba mal por tres motivos:
- El vecino no se enteraba del problema real.
- El reintento iba a fallar siempre, porque el punto sigue estando fuera de la ciudad.
- Al volver atrás, no podía corregirlo en el mapa.

### Qué cambia

**`app/reclamos/nuevo-reporte.tsx`**: el `catch` de `alEnviar` ahora distingue dos casos.

- **La API respondió con un error:** muestra `error.mensaje` tal como lo manda la API (por ejemplo, "Ese punto queda fuera de Gualeguaychú. Corregilo en el mapa.") y se queda en la pantalla para que el vecino lo corrija. No lo guarda para reintentar.
- **La API no respondió** (sin señal o servidor caído): hace lo mismo que antes. Lo guarda en la cola offline y lo reintenta solo.

Para distinguirlos se usa `axios.isAxiosError(e)` y se mira si viene `e.response.data.error.mensaje`.

### Cómo probarlo
1. Como vecino, crear un reclamo con el punto fuera de Gualeguaychú y enviar: sale el mensaje de la API y la pantalla no se cierra.
2. Mover el punto dentro de la ciudad y enviar: sale "Reporte enviado" con el código.
3. Con modo avión, enviar: sale "Reporte guardado", como antes.

author: danielrall
body:
Currently, `StandardFont` requires `FontResolverFn` to return `Some((font_blob, index))` for unembedded PDF Standard 14 fonts (`Helvetica`, `Times-Roman`, `Courier`, `Symbol`, `ZapfDingbats`, etc.), even though `hayro-font` already compiles in the static AFM advance widths, standard/symbol/dingbats encodings, and Adobe Glyph List Unicode mappings unconditionally.

As a result, downstream consumers building with `default-features = false` (disabling `embed-fonts` to keep binary size small or avoid bundling font files) cannot use `hayro-interpret` for non-rasterizing workflows—such as text extraction, bounding-box/layout measurement, or PDF structural conversion—on documents referencing unembedded Standard 14 fonts unless they supply external `.pfb`/`.ttf` blobs.

This PR makes the resolved font blob optional inside `StandardFont`:
- When `FontResolverFn` returns `Some(...)` (including the default `embed-fonts` feature), behavior and glyph rendering are completely unchanged.
- When `FontResolverFn` returns `None`, `StandardFont` still loads successfully and provides exact compiled-in AFM glyph advance widths, encodings, and Unicode mappings, while returning an empty `BezPath` from `outline_glyph`.

Includes unit tests in `hayro-font` and `hayro-interpret` verifying Standard 14 glyph widths, CMap/encoding character resolution, and `Device::draw_glyph` callbacks with a `None` font resolver.

### Why this is useful
Many `hayro-interpret` consumers implement custom `Device` backends that do not rasterize glyph outlines—for example, text/search indexers, layout and bounding-box analyzers, accessibility/structure extractors, or document converters—and disable `embed-fonts` to avoid shipping hundreds of kilobytes of bundled font binaries or in `no_std`/Wasm/embedded builds without host system fonts. Allowing `StandardFont` to operate from its already-compiled AFM tables lets those lightweight builds process unembedded Standard 14 text with exact glyph positioning and Unicode decoding out of the box.

author: thientran01
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"thientran01"} -->
_Requested by **Thien** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_0193Ny6wzPSqFqzscstUKBL7?thread=cmsg_0193Ny6wzPSqFqzscstUKBL7HwoDj7EamqrxruCoNRQuta)_

I audited every animation in the app against Emil Kowalski's `review-animations`, `improve-animations`, `remove-animations`, `choreograph` and `animation-performance` skills ([emilkowalski/skills](https://github.com/emilkowalski/skills)). Most of the motion already meets that bar. This PR fixes the three things that didn't. It also fixes the lyrics ⇄ queue swap, which Thien flagged afterwards. Search was reviewed the same way in #204, so it isn't touched here.

## Findings

| Before | After | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Track-change slides (expanded lyrics and album block, focus seats) animate Motion's `x` | Same variants with a `transform: translateX()` string, and `transitionEnd: { transform: "none" }` | In motion 12.42 only opacity, transform, filter and clip-path go to WAAPI (`motion-dom` `acceleratedValues`). `x` ticks on the main thread, which during a skip is busy with the new track's render, the lyrics fetch and the art decode. |
| Skip flick, seek spin and bracket pulse use `useAnimate` with `x` / `rotate` / `scale` | `element.animate()` on the CSS `translate` / `rotate` / `scale` properties | Same reason. These presses land right as the widget re-renders. The computed `translate`/`rotate` still read back mid-flight, so mashing continues from where the glyph is: the seek spin extends to 720° from its current angle, and the flick rewinds a width. |
| Mode buttons press with `whileTap` (Motion, main thread) | CSS `active:scale-95` with `scale 90ms`, like every other IconButton | The release plays during the mode change's remount. The native `scale` property composes with the transform that `layoutId` owns. |
| Queue rows hover with `background-color 600ms` | `140ms`. The newly-queued wash is its own `.row-flash` layer (`-z-10`, under the content) | The hover shared the flash's 600ms fade-out, so it trailed the cursor. History rows already used 140ms. |
| Queue popover, right-click menu and first-run bubble fade in with opacity only | Fade plus `scale 0.97 → 1` from the shell-facing corner, the cursor, or the tether tip | Panels with an obvious source shouldn't appear from nowhere. The popover uses transitions so a re-toggle reverses mid-flight. `scale` leaves `offsetHeight` alone, so the hit rect is unaffected. |
| Expanded's peer layers (lyrics · album · queue) crossfade 200ms in / 140ms out, overlapping | `.view-off`: 120ms fade into a 2px blur. `.view-on`: 180ms fade and sharpen, starting 40ms in | Two dense text views overlapping showed queue rows printed over lyric lines at half strength (Thien: "it just looks weird"). Now the old view is about 20% gone, and blurred, by the time the new one starts. |
| Focus: the lyric column unmounts the instant the queue opens, and the queue fades in | The column fades out (`view-off`), then unmounts after 120ms. On close it remounts with `.view-in`. The queue box uses `view-on`/`view-off` | Same handoff in both sizes. Before, the lyrics blinked out. |
| Focus: after closing the queue, the lyrics slide from the top down to the current line | `LyricsPanel` arms its scroll transition two frames after mount, not in a plain effect | A mount inside a click flushed the effect before first paint, which armed the 220ms transition before the anchor offset landed. This is the bug that code's own comment warns about. |

## Kept on purpose

- **Shell width/height glide:** content is fixed-size and absolutely placed inside it, so each frame lays out only the shell.
- **Lyric cascade and break-dot rows:** the cascade and dots are unchanged. The only `LyricsPanel` change is the anchoring fix above.
- **Hover gating:** Tailwind v4 already wraps `hover:` in `@media (hover: hover)`.
- **Hand-typed ms values:** consolidating them changes nothing visible.

## Verification

- `npm run build` and `npm test` (119 passed). No Rust changes.
- Browser mock, checked with `document.getAnimations()`:
  - A skip in expanded now shows native `Animation` objects on `transform=translateX(14px)→translateX(0px)` (enter) and `0→-14px` (exit). Focus seats behave the same at ±20px.
  - At rest, the inline transform is `none`.
  - The flick is a `translate` animation. A double seek press animates `rotate 27°→720°`. The bracket pulse is `scale 1→1.2→1`.
  - Popover origin is bottom-right when docked bottom-right. The menu origin is at the cursor. The bubble origin is at the tether tip.
- Lyrics ⇄ queue was recorded at 0.06× playback, before and after, in expanded and in focus (1280×720). Expanded no longer shows a double exposure. Focus fades both ways, and the lyrics land on the current line with no slide.
- Merges cleanly with main (`ddac766`, merged in).
- **Feel check on the PC:**
  - Spam Next in expanded and in focus.
  - Toggle the queue in both sizes.
  - Open the queue popover and right-click the widget.

author: k2b-cloud-agents[bot]
body:
## What is wrong

On a 390 px phone the dashboard key figure tiles cut their figures: "48…", "1…", "€2…" (integrated preview, Newsletter and Liquidität dashboards). The value must never be truncated.

## Cause

`.k2b-stat-cell__value` ended overflowing text in an ellipsis, and only `size="lg"` moved the change badge under the figure and shrank it in narrow tiles. The dashboards use the default `md` size, so figure and badge stayed side by side at a fixed 20 px in a ~150 px tile.

## Fix

- The value never ends in an ellipsis. In a grid tile its font size follows the tile's width (`cqi` of the tile container) within fixed bounds: `lg` 18–28 px, `md` 16–20 px, `sm` 14–16 px. A text value that still does not fit wraps at its spaces and the tile grows (`lg` heights are minimums now: 136 px, 164 px at ≤600 px).
- At a grid of 600 px or less the change badge moves under the figure in every size (was `lg` only); a tile below 200 px does the same. Only `lg` drops its trend there, as in the mockup.
- Desktop is unchanged (28 px `lg` figure, 136 px tile).

## Every consumer at phone width

The guard renders all three sizes with the longest figure shapes the consumers use (grouped counts, currency before and after the number, "Mio." values, text values such as "Action needed") in 300 px and 366 px frames at 390 px, 296 px at 320 px, and the desktop width. The inventory from #2748 maps every StatGrid consumer to one of these sizes and column counts. Pulse number panels set their own fixed figure size and now wrap instead of ending in an ellipsis.

## How do we prevent this next time?

Guard: `packages/ui/src/surfaces/stat-tiles.browser.test.ts` — "a figure always fits its tile, in every size, down to a 320 px phone" fails when a value overflows its tile or computes `text-overflow: ellipsis`. Verified red against the previous stylesheet and green with the fix. Lesson: `docs-site/docs/en/contributing/lessons/2026-11-07-stat-tile-value-never-cut.md`.

## Screenshots (light, invented data)

Before/after at 390 px and 1440 px: https://artifacts.qdt-dev-1.k2b.dev/cloud/stat-value-fit/compare/1-2/

## Checks

- Browser (one file per run): `stat-tiles.browser.test.ts` (5 tests, incl. the new guard), `single-frame.browser.test.ts`, `cloud/src/ai/chat/view-block.browser.test.ts`: pass.
- `surfaces.render.test.tsx`, lessons test, `check:docs`, rules `css css-variables motion hover-motion`, biome: pass.

author: vjeux
body:
**Symptom.** In a file with several audio tracks (one per language, say), `canBePairedWith()` says the audio tracks pair with each other. The docs' track pairability section says they don't: "the video track can be paired with each one of them, but the audio tracks cannot be paired with each other; they're not intended to be played at the same time." It happens in MP4, MOV, Matroska/WebM, MPEG-TS and the other single-file formats, and with HLS audio renditions of the same group. So `getPairableAudioTracks()` on an audio track returns the other languages, and `getPrimaryPairableAudioTrack()` returns another audio track. Conversion takes input pairability over to its output, so converting such a file to HLS logs "Illegal pairing of two audio tracks detected, which is not possible in HLS; treating them as unpaired." Realism: real-world (any multi-language file). Found by lane L55.

**Repro.** `test/node/input.test.ts` › "Tracks of the same type are not pairable with each other" (an MP4 and an MKV with one video and two audio tracks, plus an HLS master playlist with two audio renditions in one group) and "Converting a file with two audio tracks to HLS keeps the audio tracks apart" (expects no warning). Both fail on main.

**Cause.** Single-file demuxers give every track the same pairing mask, and HLS gives every rendition of an audio group the bits of the variants that use the group. Pairability is tested as masks intersecting, so tracks of the same type pair whenever they're presented with the same track of the other type.

**Fix.** `InputTrack.canBePairedWith()` returns false for two tracks of the same type, as the output side already does within a track group (`OutputTrack.canBePairedWith()`) and as the HLS muxer requires. Pairability across types is unchanged. This is simpler than per-type masks in every demuxer, and no input format Mediabunny reads can express same-type pairing.

_Written by an AI agent (Claude) auditing Mediabunny on behalf of @vjeux._

author: hiking90
body:
## Summary

`rsbinder-topic` gets a version of its own, starting at **0.1.0**, instead of inheriting the workspace version (0.13.0). It has not been published yet, and crates.io always picks the highest version, so this is the last point at which the number can change.

- **Why a separate number:** the crate is Experimental. Sharing the workspace version would publish it as 0.13.0, and an rsbinder 1.0 would make it 1.0 too, promising a stability it does not have.
- **`=` requirement on `rsbinder`:** `rsbinder-topic` calls `rsbinder`'s `#[doc(hidden)]` `__` items (`__sync`, `__spawn_transact`, `__encode_end_record`, `__panic_message`), which no semver covers. With the caret requirement it had, an rsbinder 0.13.x patch that changed one of them would break a published rsbinder-topic. It now requires `rsbinder = "=0.13.0"`, the same way the workspace requires `rsbinder-aidl`.
- **Requirements on rsbinder-topic:** `rsbinder-tools` (optional, `topic` feature) and `tests` now require `0.1.0`. `Cargo.lock` and the lockfiles of `bench/ipc-compare` and `fuzz` follow.
- **Release scripts (`envsetup.sh`):**
  - `version_update` used to match `rsbinder[a-z-]*`, which would have rewritten the requirement on rsbinder-topic to the workspace number. It now rewrites only `rsbinder`, `rsbinder-aidl`, `rsbinder-macros` and `rsbinder-fmq`, still moves rsbinder-topic's `=` on rsbinder, and returns the failure if a step fails.
  - The new `topic_version_update X.Y.Z` sets rsbinder-topic's version and the requirements on it.
- **Release rule (CONTRIBUTING.md "Releasing"):** because of the `=`, every rsbinder release is also an rsbinder-topic release:
  - a patch of rsbinder takes a patch of rsbinder-topic;
  - a minor of rsbinder takes a minor of rsbinder-topic, since its API carries rsbinder's types;
  - a break in rsbinder-topic's own API also takes a minor.
  The publish order is unchanged.
- **Docs:** the book (`topics.md`, `stability-tiers.md`), the crate README and the CHANGELOG `[0.13.0]` entry say the version is the crate's own and name the `=` requirement.

## Test plan

- [x] Previewed both scripts' sed without writing:
  - `version_update 0.14.0` changes the four workspace requirements and rsbinder-topic's `=` on rsbinder, and leaves the requirements on rsbinder-topic alone.
  - `topic_version_update 0.2.0` changes only rsbinder-topic's version and the requirements in `rsbinder-tools` and `tests`.
- [x] `bash -n envsetup.sh`
- [x] `cargo check --workspace --all-targets`
- [x] `cargo check -p rsbinder-tools --features topic,rpc`
- [x] `cargo check -p tests --features topic-uds --all-targets`
- [x] `scripts/excluded_lockfiles.sh --check`
- [x] `cargo package --no-verify` for the six published crates. The packaged rsbinder-topic manifest is version 0.1.0 and requires `rsbinder = "=0.13.0"` and `rsbinder-aidl = "=0.13.0"`; rsbinder-tools requires `rsbinder-topic = "0.1.0"`.
- [ ] `scripts/local_gate.sh` not run: the change is manifests, the release script and docs.

author: chs-haple
body:
## Symptom and evidence

The B1778 Xiaomi 15 Pro screen recording (2026-11-07) shows the second-level **Battery Colors → custom scheme → mode color editor** sheet visibly jumping/flickering as it exits onto the parent scheme sheet. This is a **UI nested-modal transition**, not the battery runtime callback issue in PR #1229. The video confirms a transitional visual defect but does not on its own isolate renderer vs scrim/backdrop.

Reviewed the accepted pinned MIUIX source `compose-miuix-ui/miuix@f4cfe9b0adaa5151b68ec169ed18d470b957a6f6`:
- `GlassBottomSheet` delegates to native `OverlayBottomSheet` / `BottomSheetContentLayout`.
- `show=false` animates `animationProgress` to zero with the native Folme spring while `internalVisible` remains true; `onDismissFinished` only fires after this completes.
- Guiyuan's nested color editor retains `detailRequest` until that finish callback, but the parent formerly set `allowDismiss = !detailVisible`, releasing its dismissal/gesture lock **immediately on close request**, before the child has actually left the overlay stack. The native parent switches `pointerInput(allowDismiss)` and predictive-back handling on that change.

## Minimal single-variable change
Keep the existing parent lock until the existing owned child request is cleared at `onDismissFinished`:
`allowDismiss = detailRequest == null`.

This removes an objectively mismatched ownership window without adding state, timeouts, duplicate sheets, animations, transparent overlays, or changing MIUIX/source revisions. No dependency, resource, app UI style, battery hooks or hot-reload modifications. Both OS3 and OS4 presentation styles share this native sheet lifetime; OS4 Glass source remains pinned and native animation-owned.

## Gates

- Source/CI: validate exact SHA and inspect final diff.
- Required Xiaomi 15 Pro **focused device acceptance**: close editor through header Back, system Back and drag; ensure no one-frame blink, no double dismissal, no blocked parent after exit, no touch-through while exiting. Also verify ordinary parent dismiss afterward and quick reopen.
- This is a **rooted, evidence-led candidate**, not yet a proven complete fix for the visible flash. If unchanged, inspect MIUIX surface/backdrop capture sequencing rather than adding a timing mask.
- Keep unmerged pending focused device acceptance. The B1779 Build has now been explicitly issued, source-validated and trusted-signed as documented below; no extra Build or stable release is authorized.

## B1779 source-matched signed acceptance candidate (2026-11-07)
- Frozen source: `128706b74a2b274be5dbc35cbadd54465358ae02`, from `fix/battery-color-nested-sheet-dismiss` based on `dev=ba91190b451287f7e1977f07be4f8aeb21a07d9f`; one Kotlin lifetime-lock correction plus the deliberate B1779 version identity. Battery source is inherited unchanged from dev; no second battery fix was introduced.
- Exact-HEAD [Android Runtime CI #42338592765](https://github.com/CHS-Haple/Guiyuan/actions/runs/42338592765) passed Android tests, compiled unsigned Canary and metadata/non-debuggable gates. [Trusted Work Branch APK #42339235610](https://github.com/CHS-Haple/Guiyuan/actions/runs/42339235610) completed and signed [artifact #13561270517](https://github.com/CHS-Haple/Guiyuan/actions/runs/42339235610/artifacts/13561270517), `Guiyuan-1.0.0-HyperOS-20261107-1779-canary.apk`. Signing job logs verified source `128706b74a2b274be5dbc35cbadd54465358ae02`, `versionCode=261107779`, `buildId=20261107-1779`, trusted cert SHA-256 and v3 signature. This is **not** an accepted stable Release.
- Independent source recheck: accepted pinned MIUIX `f4cfe9b0` keeps a nested sheet visible through the hide animation; `onDismissFinished` owns final cleanup. Both OS3 and OS4 UI styles use the same parent request lifetime. No extra timer, observer, polling or backdrop writer was added. No deterministic code issue warrants another B1779 patch at this point.
- **Device gate remains open:** the original B1778 flash was intermittent, so even a single non-reproduction cannot prove complete optical repair. Test one B1779 installation on Xiaomi 15 Pro: second-level header Back, system Back and drag-down exit; immediately reopen, then dismiss parent. Verify no one-frame jump/double dismiss and no parent lock/touch-through while the child is leaving. Existing B1778 battery-state success is scenario-limited and does not prove other OEM battery callbacks.
- Keep this PR unmerged until focused device evidence; do not distribute additional equivalent candidates or promote to main. A fresh fix is justified only if B1779 reproducibly fails or new diagnostics isolate the next mechanism.

## Maintainer merge authorization (2026-11-07)
The maintainer explicitly approved promoting the distributed, trusted-signed B1779 Canary candidate represented by this exact PR head into `dev`. This is authorization to merge, not a claim that the formerly intermittent one-frame sheet flash has been exhaustively disproven across all conditions. Focus remains on B1779 battery behavior and nested Sheet dismissal; no additional code change, new APK, merge to `main`, or release promotion is implied. If the intermittent symptom recurs, pursue a separate evidence-led report.

body:
Workflow graphs and children views collapse logical slots and continued runs, so clients cannot inspect every recorded agent attempt. This adds `GET /api/runs/:id/attempts`, gated by `workflow.attempt_history.v1`, with stable filtered pages over a bounded immutable snapshot of the owner’s active or archived ledger.

Rows retain original agent-run IDs, continuation links, execution-host provenance, and transcript locators. Missing or partial ledger evidence remains explicit; the API does not invent completion status or treat missing rows as proof that nothing ran. Authenticated cursors bind owner, run, and filters; size, concurrency, retention, and expiry limits are documented. This read-only route adds no dispatch, resume, or messaging authority.

Stacked on #946 (`codex/builtin-session-harness`). The implementation branch passed 12 focused attempt-history tests, 13 graph tests, and 3 workflow-history tests. Scoped formatting and whitespace checks passed. Strict combined CI Clippy passed under pinned Rust 1.95. The dedicated preview returned real recorded attempts and a continuation cursor for an existing workflow, with clean ledger parsing and execution completeness correctly left unknown. Native UI acceptance remains separate.

MCP clients use `runs.attempts` through the same owner-local API, including filters, immutable cursor paging, and missing-ledger evidence. It remains read-only and local.

Combined integration verification: 154 MCP integration tests passed at `8f0623b3`, covering catalog/route lockstep, query forwarding, cursor pagination, and owner guards. [Full build gate](https://github.com/Section9Labs/rupu/actions/runs/42338292027) passed all nine jobs on the same combined commit, including macOS ARM and Linux x64/ARM release builds, strict lint, and the full test suite; the final local binary built successfully and the dedicated preview instance is running it. Real project checks passed for the four-skill preset and opt-out, unchanged legacy session state, actual checkout context, and clean recorded attempts with a continuation cursor. A real current-branch GitHub review query also succeeded. Provider execution and native UI acceptance are separate checks.

AI-assisted implementation and review by OpenAI Codex. Contract and validation: `docs/plans/2026-11-06-workflow-attempt-history-design.md`.

author: superkat13
body:
## Independent second-pass finding on PR #80 at `281296237fbd4e9979c16ace95c4539d9bca7a79`

**Root cause:** `sage_brain.cpp::nativeContinueGeneration` called `invalidate_continuation_locked()`, clearing `g_continuation_token` to zero, then read `g_continuation_token` for its first `llama_decode` batch. The next segment thus decoded token ID 0 instead of the final sampled token from the preceding segment. Unit tests with mocked bridges and the existing real native ASAN harness did not exercise `nativeContinueGeneration`, explaining why exact-source 833 tests and the old native test remained green.

**Changes on this separate branch (original PR #80 branch not modified):**
- Capture the saved sampled token into a local `resume_token` *before* revoking the old continuation lease, then decode that exact token.
- Add a real-model ASAN harness regression that captures the last sampled token and intercepts the first actual `llama_decode` call in the native continuation, asserting token equality and observable generation progress. Update the success label to prove continuation was exercised.
- Allow verification workflows targeting the audit branch, so the new test can run on the actual PR SHA.

**Required proof:** Exact-head CI native job ASAN and Kotlin Android 833+ tests/lint/build. Inspect job logs for the new `exact saved-token KV continuation` signature. Do not claim pass until CI completes. Then add a second pass for context exhaustion, cancellation, repeated segments and cross-turn cache isolation. Test with real owner's model on physical tablet before release.

No merge, no tablet installation, no owner-data reset, and no overwrite of OpenCode's working tree.

author: denisvmedia
body:
On CockroachDB and YugabyteDB a migration file that failed reported `failed` with `applied: 0` while a schema statement stayed. `ptah migrations status` then said that no statement reached the database and pointed at `up --allow-dirty`, which ran the `CREATE TABLE` again and failed for as long as anyone retried. A `DROP TABLE` in such a file was gone with nothing saying so.

The revision row and the run document now say what stays. A run that does not fail reports what it reported.

## What each engine does

Both engines take a schema statement inside a transaction, and a `ROLLBACK` does not take it back. They differ in what happens to the rest, measured through the driver on every statement kind below.

- CockroachDB, with `autocommit_before_ddl` on, its default from v25: a schema statement commits the transaction first, and the session then has none. Data ahead of it and after it both stay. The server's `ReadyForQuery` status byte says so: `I` after the schema statement, `T` or `E` before it.
- YugabyteDB, with `yb_ddl_transaction_block_enabled` off, its default: a schema statement commits on its own and the transaction stays open, status `T`. Data ahead of it and after it both roll back.

`CREATE` of a table, index, view, sequence, type, schema or function, `ALTER TABLE`, `DROP TABLE`, `TRUNCATE`, `COMMENT`, `GRANT` and `CREATE TABLE AS` all stayed on CockroachDB v26.3.5 and YugabyteDB 2024.2.11, 2025.2.5 and 2026.1.2, and none did on PostgreSQL 18.6. A `DO` block that creates a table stayed on YugabyteDB. `SET LOCAL`, `SELECT` and `INSERT` did not change anything on any of them.

The setting decides it. CockroachDB v24.3 has `autocommit_before_ddl` off, and nothing stayed. YugabyteDB refuses the setting per session (SQLSTATE 55P02), and a 2026.1.2 server started with `ysql_yb_ddl_transaction_block_enabled` rolled every one of those statements back.

## How it answers

The migrator reads a new engine service, `migratorext.RollbackSurvivors`, for the two engines. Every other engine has none and sends nothing new.

- CockroachDB asks the session. `OutsideTransaction` is read before the rollback is sent, and costs no round trip. Outside a transaction, every statement that ran stays. A body with its own `COMMIT` or `ROLLBACK` reads `unknown`, because the session state says nothing about the statements ahead of it.
- YugabyteDB reads the first word of each statement, and asks the server for the setting only when a statement that could stay ran. Schema statements stay and data goes. A word nobody measured, such as `DO` or `CALL`, reads as "cannot tell". A `SELECT` counts with the data, so a resume runs it again rather than skipping a write a function may have made. A temporary table counts with the data too, because the run discards its session.

## What each engine reports

`migrations up --json`, default `--tx-mode file`. Each cell is the outcome and the count the row records.

| Body | CockroachDB holds | master | this change | YugabyteDB holds | master | this change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `CREATE TABLE`, then a failure | the table | `failed` 0/2 | `partial` 1/2 | the table | `failed` 0/2 | `partial` 1/2 |
| `CREATE TABLE`, `INSERT` into it, then a failure | the table and its row | `failed` 0/3 | `partial` 2/3 | the table, no row | `failed` 0/3 | `partial` 1/3 |
| `INSERT`, `CREATE TABLE`, then a failure | the row and the table | `failed` 0/3 | `partial` 2/3 | the table, no row | `failed` 0/3 | `unknown` 0/3 |
| `INSERT`, then a `CREATE TABLE` the server refuses | the row | `failed` 0/2 | `partial` 1/2 | nothing | `failed` 0/2 | `failed` 0/2 |
| `DROP TABLE`, then a failure | the table is gone | `failed` 0/2 | `partial` 1/2 | the table is gone | `failed` 0/2 | `partial` 1/2 |
| `INSERT`, then a failure | nothing | `failed` 0/2 | `failed` 0/2 | nothing | `failed` 0/2 | `failed` 0/2 |

- PostgreSQL 18.6: `failed` 0/n in every row, nothing stays, before and after.
- MySQL 26.10 and MariaDB 12.3: DDL commits implicitly, and the witness already reports `partial` with the right count, so nothing changes in the first three rows. Where a schema statement is refused after an earlier statement, the witness writes the "outcome unknown" marker, and that row reads `unknown` 1/2 where master read `partial` 1/2. See the policy choices.
- `up --allow-dirty` after a `partial`: on master CockroachDB and YugabyteDB fail with `relation "k" already exists`. With this change they resume at the next statement and report `applied`.
- `migrations down`, `DROP TABLE` then a failure: CockroachDB and YugabyteDB record `applied=0/2` on master and `1/2` now, and the table is gone on both. PostgreSQL records 0/2 and keeps the table, and MySQL records 1/2, before and after.
- `--tx-mode all`: CockroachDB v25 and later refuses it, before and after. YugabyteDB accepts it. A failed run reads `failed` 0/2 on master and `unknown` 0/2 now, and every schema statement of the run stays.
- `--tx-mode none`: `partial` with the same count on all five, before and after.
- `schema apply`: `unknown` once a statement was dispatched, on all five, before and after. The document says a transaction may have rolled them back or a run may have left some, and to read the database. That is honest, so it did not change. PostgreSQL held nothing afterward and the other four held the new table.

## Policy choices

- **Report, do not refuse and do not reroute.** A preflight refusal or a warning would hit every clean multi-statement file on these engines, and those runs work. Running each statement with its own checkpoint changes what a clean run does: `SET LOCAL` becomes a no-op, an index builds online, and data loses its transaction on YugabyteDB. So only the failure path changes.
- **`partial` where a count is true, `unknown` where none is.** `partial` is documented as "committed some and not the rest", with a resume as the recovery, and it holds wherever what stayed is a leading run of statements. On YugabyteDB, data ahead of a schema statement breaks that: a resume at either point is wrong. That row records a new marker and reads `unknown`. `up --allow-dirty` and `repair --resume-from` refuse it, and a plain `repair` ends it.
- **A row marked unknown reads `unknown`.** The document defines `unknown` as a dirty row that does not say how far it got, and the run document read those rows as `failed` or `partial`. `repair --resume-from` refuses the row that `partial` says to resume. This also moves an interrupted `--tx-mode none` statement to `unknown`, and the MySQL row above. Pre-GA, so no compatibility is owed.
- **`TransactionalDDL` stays true on YugabyteDB.** At its default the key's sentence is false there. Turning it off refuses `--tx-mode all`, including runs that succeed on master, so I left it and report the failure honestly. A refusal is a one-line change if that is preferred. `schemaclean` and the provider host read the same key.

GENERAL CAPABILITY: this lives in `migration/migrator` and `internal/migratorext`, and the native surface is what it reports through. `ptah-compat migrate apply` takes the same path and says `Executed Files: 1 (last one partially)` in `migrate status`.

## How it was verified

- `integration/migrateup/schema_statement_rollback_e2e_test.go` drives the built binary and reads every server back: the failure shapes above on all five engines, clean runs, a resume, a resume that fails again, a failed commit on a deferred constraint, the row no count describes, `migrations down`, `--tx-mode all`, `--tx-mode none`, and `--revision-format atlas`.
- Unit tests: `internal/migratorext/postgres/rollback_survivors_test.go`, including the setting on and a lost connection, `migration/migrator/rollback_survivors_internal_test.go`, `run_result_test.go`, and the status hints.
- I disabled each piece in turn and watched a test fail: the service call, the CockroachDB count, the YugabyteDB count, the leading-run rule, the outcome of a marked row, the down-path correcti

### glibc: glibc DNS stub resolver: Denial of Service via long search domain in configuration
[CVE-2026-8674](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-8674)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
A flaw was found in the GNU C Library (glibc) DNS stub resolver. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker on the local network to cause a denial of service by providing a specially crafted, excessively long search domain. When the resolver attempts to initialize with this long domain from /etc/resolv.conf or the LOCALDOMAIN environment variable, it triggers an assertion failure, which aborts the process. This can be exploited without privileges on the target system, potentially through network configuration mechanisms like DHCP or a VPN server.

#### Severity
Moderate

### glibc: glibc: Privilege escalation and arbitrary code execution via TOCTOU race condition in dynamic loader
[CVE-2026-86805](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-86805)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
A flaw was found in glibc, specifically within its dynamic loader (ld.so). A local attacker can exploit a time-of-check to time-of-use (TOCTOU) race condition to escalate privileges and execute arbitrary code. This occurs when the dynamic loader expands $ORIGIN in DT_RPATH for setuid/setgid programs, validating a normalized path but then opening an un-normalized path. By hard-linking such a program and winning a race to swap a path component with a symbolic link, an attacker can direct the loader to an attacker-controlled shared object, gaining elevated privileges. This vulnerability is mitigated on systems with fs.protected_hardlinks enabled.

#### Severity
Moderate

body:
## Intent Improve the subscription/pricing UX end to end. Five related gaps: 1. No navigation to upgrade. A free-tier user can only reach the plans by clicking the logo → landing page. Add clear in-app navigation to a pricing/upgrade page (e.g. a nav link or an upgrade button in the header/layout). 2. No success/failure feedback after subscribing. After checkout completes, the user is redirected straight to the new-session page with no message. Add clear success/failure feedback (e.g. a success banner on return, and an error banner on cancel/failure). 3. No current-plan indication. There is no indication anywhere of which plan the user is currently on. Surface the user's current tier. 4. Main page still lets a paid user pick any plan. A Pro/Unlimited user visiting the landing page can still click any plan. Detect the current plan and treat the user's current tier as "Current plan" (disable re-selecting the same plan), while still allowing an upgrade to a higher tier. 5. No subscription management panel. There is no place to see/manage the subscription (current plan, what it includes, cancel/manage). Add a simple account/subscription page. Context: - src/lib/tiers.ts owns tiers (user/pro/unlimited/admin) and getTier(); user_roles.role + stripe_subscription_id/stripe_customer_id are the persisted state. - The landing pricing grid is src/components/Welcome.astro (+ src/components/CheckoutButton.tsx island); the upgrade modal is src/components/interview/JDInput.tsx. - Checkout is POST /api/stripe/checkout (returns { url }); the webhook (src/pages/api/stripe/webhook.ts) updates user_roles on checkout/subscription events. What to build: 1. A pricing/upgrade page (src/pages/pricing.astro or similar) with the three plans, linked from the header/nav and from an "Upgrade" button shown to signed-in users. 2. A current-plan display: read user_roles.role server-side and render "Free / Pro / Unlimited" with a label. On the pricing page + landing grid, mark the user's current tier as "Current plan" and disable that button; still allow upgrading to a higher tier. 3. Success/failure feedback after checkout: a return route (the success_url/cancel_url currently point somewhere — verify) that shows a clear success banner or a friendly failure message, and a way to return to the app. 4. A simple subscription/account page (src/pages/account.astro or similar) that shows: current plan, plan features, and a "Manage subscription" link (Stripe Customer Portal or a link to Stripe's customer page — if the Customer Portal isn't set up, add a link to the Stripe billing portal or note it). 5. A "Cancel subscription" affordance on the account page that triggers the existing cancellation path (or clearly notes how to cancel via Stripe). Acceptance criteria: - Signed-in users can reach a pricing page from the app (not just the landing page). - Current plan is shown, and re-selecting the current plan is blocked while upgrades remain possible. - Post-checkout success/failure is surfaced with a clear message. - An account page shows current plan + features + a manage/cancel path. - npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm test && npm run build pass. Note: This is a multi-part UX change; keep each part small and cohesive. Do not change the Stripe price points, tier limits, or the webhook logic. ## What Changed - Added a dedicated `/pricing` page backed by a shared `PricingGrid`/`PlanCard` component set (also reused on the landing page) that marks the signed-in user's current tier as "Current plan", disables re-selecting it, and keeps higher tiers upgradeable. - Added an `/account` subscription page showing the current plan, its features, and a "Manage subscription" button wired to a new `/api/stripe/portal` endpoint that opens the Stripe Customer Portal. - Surfaced the current tier in the Topbar (plan badge plus an Upgrade link for free/pro users), added post-checkout success/cancel banners via the `?checkout=success|cancelled` return params, and resolved the user's tier once per request in middleware (`Astro.locals.role`). ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The change is well-bounded and cohesive: it adds a shared plans module, pricing/account pages, a Stripe Customer Portal route, and checkout success/cancelled feedback, with tests for each new logic unit and no changes to price points, tier limits, or webhook logic. ## Testing I installed dependencies, ran the targeted Vitest suite covering the new/changed modules (plans, checkout-notice, tiers, ManageSubscriptionButton, CheckoutButton, stripe portal and checkout endpoints — 53 tests, all green), and ran a full production build successfully. To demonstrate the actual end-user surface I served the app and captured live screenshots of /pricing and the landing page, then used Astro's Container API to render the pricing grid in each signed-in tier, the signed-in Topbar, and the account page (Pro, checkout=success), verifying the Current plan badge/disabled button, blocked downgrades, remaining upgrade buttons, the Upgrade nav link, the plan badge, the success banner, and the current-plan feature list — all captured as reviewer-visible PNG + HTML artifacts. The only limitation is that the manage/cancel portal button on the account page renders conditionally on a stored Stripe customer id (unavailable without live Supabase credentials), so that path is evidenced by its dedicated component and endpoint tests rather than a live screenshot. - Evidence: Landing page with pricing grid (local file: /var/folders/38/j6vj2kpn3yj2yzgfpzwf9c_40000gn/T/no-mistakes-evidence/01M6T1B132RVKXVD7RYTDJK0K1/landing.png) - Evidence: Pricing page (signed-out, live server) (local file: /var/folders/38/j6vj2kpn3yj2yzgfpzwf9c_40000gn/T/no-mistakes-evidence/01M6T1B132RVKXVD7RYTDJK0K1/pricing-signedout.png) - Evidence: Pricing grid as Free user (Free=Current, Pro/Unlimited upgradeable) (local file: /var/folders/38/j6vj2kpn3yj2yzgfpzwf9c_40000gn/T/no-mistakes-evidence/01M6T1B132RVKXVD7RYTDJK0K1/pricing-grid-user.png) - Evidence: Pricing grid as Pro user (Pro=Current, Free downgrade-blocked, Unlimited upgradeable) (local file: /var/folders/38/j6vj2kpn3yj2yzgfpzwf9c_40000gn/T/no-mistakes-evidence/01M6T1B132RVKXVD7RYTDJK0K1/pricing-grid-pro.png) - Evidence: Pricing grid as Unlimited user (all downgrades blocked) (local file: /var/folders/38/j6vj2kpn3yj2yzgfpzwf9c_40000gn/T/no-mistakes-evidence/01M6T1B132RVKXVD7RYTDJK0K1/pricing-grid-unlimited.png) - Evidence: Signed-in Topbar showing Pro badge + Upgrade link (local file: /var/folders/38/j6vj2kpn3yj2yzgfpzwf9c_40000gn/T/no-mistakes-evidence/01M6T1B132RVKXVD7RYTDJK0K1/topbar-pro.png) - Evidence: Account page (Pro) with success banner, current plan, features (local file: /var/folders/38/j6vj2kpn3yj2yzgfpzwf9c_40000gn/T/no-mistakes-evidence/01M6T1B132RVKXVD7RYTDJK0K1/account-pro.png)

author: lil-bobcn
body:
## Summary

把[客户澄清的问题树：题与题的依赖怎么存、怎么重算](https://github.com/Lil-BobCN/grilling-remote/issues/30)的决定记下来：每个需求一份 `问题树.md`，客户侧 `grilling` 登记，运营者侧 `question-tree` 按依赖边重算。本 PR 只改文档，不碰客户包。

```diff
 docs/
 ├── adr/
+│   └── 0007-问题树单独存一份.md       # 六列格式、六种状态、三堆视图、重算步骤
 └── research/
     └── 客户澄清的问题树（旁支记录）.md
+        （开头加更新注，草稿方向标已废）
 GLOSSARY.md
+  问题树：一次澄清里的题和题的依赖
```

关键规则：

```text
提问时   问题树.md 记一行：编号、题、当前结论、出处、依赖、状态
改一条   从直接下游开始
         仍成立 → 停
         作废   → 标作废，继续往下
         要补问 → 标待补问，暂停等客户
视图     未定 + 待补问 / 客户不懂 / 待核实 / 作废
```

## Evidence

- **Before:** 草稿方向写「问题树由运营者这侧的技能读回传文件生成。客户机不加技能」；`GLOSSARY.md` 没有「问题树」。
  **After:** 同一段加了「2026-11-07 按 #30 作废」的注；ADR-0007 定为客户侧 `grilling` 登记、运营者侧 `question-tree` 重算；`GLOSSARY.md` 加词条。

```text
$ wc -l docs/adr/0007-问题树单独存一份.md
135 docs/adr/0007-问题树单独存一份.md
$ gh issue view 30 --json state,title
{"state":"CLOSED","title":"客户澄清的问题树：题与题的依赖怎么存、怎么重算"}
```

## Merge Danger

**Door:** one-way

Docs are easy to revert, but the decision is hard to reverse once the customer package ships. Treat the merge as locking the design.

**Blast Radius:** process

No code or runtime in this PR. The customer-side rule, the operator-side `question-tree` skill, and the package rebuild are tracked in [客户包收尾](https://github.com/Lil-BobCN/grilling-remote/issues/44)、[官网技能包发布](https://github.com/Lil-BobCN/grilling-remote/issues/35)、[客户机安装实测](https://github.com/Lil-BobCN/grilling-remote/issues/36)。
