author: xiaomi2008
body:
## Blank transcript
While a run streamed, the chat sometimes went blank and only came back after a manual scroll. The running turn shrinks often: a thinking line folds once the answer starts, and a finished run folds its steps. When it shrank under the scroll offset, `LazyVStack` decided nothing was on screen and drew nothing.

- The last turn is laid out eagerly. Earlier turns stay lazy, so long sessions stay cheap.
- On macOS 15+ the "pinned to bottom" signal comes from scroll geometry: a scroll by the user sets it, and a content-size change is followed while pinned. macOS 14 keeps the old layout and pin.
- `UI_PREVIEW_STREAM=<ms>` streams a 40-round run into `ui-preview`. Before the fix, every frame after the steps folded was blank. After it, none of 50 frames were, the view followed the stream and it ended on the answer.

Not tested by hand: scrolling up mid-run to check the view doesn't pull you back down.

## Stable signing
macOS ties Accessibility and Screen Recording grants to the code signature. An ad-hoc signature changes on every build, so each rebuild voided the grants while System Settings still showed them on. `build_app.sh` now signs the app with `SoloCoder Dev` from the keychain (or `SOLOCODER_SIGN_IDENTITY`) when it exists, and falls back to ad-hoc otherwise. With the certificate, the designated requirement is `identifier "dev.solocoder.app" and certificate leaf = H"…"`, which stays the same across rebuilds.

## Checks
525 agent-checks and 37 Swift tests pass.

author: zakivinico
body:
## O que muda
- **Armas guardadas e sacadas**
  - Fora de combate, a arma fica nas costas, presa no osso do tronco, então acompanha qualquer tamanho de personagem.
  - No primeiro golpe, ela salta para a mão com um som de sacar.
  - Depois de 4 s sem atacar e sem inimigo por perto, volta sozinha para as costas.
- **Escudo**: vem com a Espada. Fica no braço esquerdo quando a espada está na mão e bloqueia metade do dano que vem de frente. Com a espada guardada, vai para as costas.
- **Habilidades por arma** (R e F; o T, a cura, continua para todas):
  - Espada: Estocada e Investida de Escudo.
  - Machado: Golpe Sísmico e Machado Bumerangue.
  - Arco: Flecha Perfurante e Chuva de Flechas.
  - Os slimes agora podem ficar atordoados.
- **Ícones em pixel**:
  - As miniaturas 3D e os pratos viram pixel art com contorno, no estilo do atlas.
  - Há ícones novos para as habilidades, e o cristal voltou a ser azul.
- **Interface reativa**: botões, slots, cartões e apps reagem ao passar o mouse e ao clicar. O slot escolhido salta e as moedas pulam quando mudam.
- **Brilho das portas**: a posição agora é medida no próprio modelo. A escada aparece como saliência no raio baixo, e o brilho fica na parede da porta logo acima. Isso corrigiu as casas com escada de lado, a forja e o moinho.
- **Tela de título**:
  - Ao voltar de casa ou de uma loja, o vale de fora é redesenhado; antes o píer sumia e a personagem ficava sobre a água.
  - Os balões e nomes dos moradores não aparecem mais por cima do menu.

## Testes
- `tools/teste/eventos.js`: 98 programas do começo ao fim.
- `tools/teste/sistemas.js`: 70 passos; o único erro é o aviso antigo do PCFSoftShadowMap.
- `tools/teste/bench.js` (alta): 481 ms em média (na v1.32 eram 483).
- Testes visuais:
  - as 19 portas fotografadas antes e depois;
  - título depois de sair de casa;
  - as três armas nas costas e na mão, nos tamanhos pequeno e alto;
  - as seis habilidades acertando slimes;
  - mochila e barra com os ícones novos.

|---|---|---|
| 트리거(`nod trigger add·ls·rm`, `c<n>`, `trigger_failed`, 홈 화면 Triggers 칸) | 만든 적 없음 | cron·launchd 에서 `nod add`, 항목마다 한 번만 받으려면 `nod in --source --key` |
| `nod watch`(`--issue`·`--mine`) | 작업 105개 중 104개의 결과가 세션 알림으로 전해짐 | 세션 알림(`nod open`, `nod session claim`), 놓친 것은 `nod ls --mine`·`nod --mine` |
| `scripts/import-mindwtr.ts` | 한 번 돌고 끝남 | git 이력 |

## 바꾼 것

- **장부 v32**
  - `triggers`·`trigger_items` 표와 `tasks.trigger_id` 를 지웁니다.
  - 트리거 행이 있으면, 지우기 전에 모든 트리거 행과 source 항목, 트리거가 넣은 작업을 `<홈>/triggers.json`(0600)에 씁니다.
  - 지우지 않은 트리거가 있으면 받은 일함에 할 일 하나(출처 `nod`)를 넣습니다. 내용은 일정·지시, 대신 쓰는 길, 파일 경로입니다.
  - 이 일은 마이그레이션 트랜잭션 안에서 합니다. 파일을 못 쓰면 경로가 든 오류를 내고, 장부는 v31 그대로 남습니다.
- **코드**
  - `src/cli.ts`: trigger·watch 명령과 도움말.
  - `src/view.ts`: watch.
  - `src/triggers.ts`: 트리거 실행. tick·감시·스케줄은 남깁니다. 파일 이름은 그대로 둡니다. `nod schedule on` 이 쓴 tick 모듈이 이 파일을 경로로 불러오기 때문입니다.
  - `src/ledger.ts`, `src/todos.ts`(`c` 번호), `src/notify.ts`(`trigger_failed`).
  - `src/inbox.ts`: 듣는 세션이 없다는 경고가 `nod watch` 대신 `nod --mine`·`nod ls --mine` 을 권합니다.
- **지운 명령**: `nod watch`·`nod trigger` 는 쓰임 전체를 찍는 대신, 지웠다는 것과 대신 쓰는 길을 한 줄로 알리고 실패로 끝납니다.
- **화면**: 홈의 Triggers 칸과 그 서버 코드, 작업 화면의 trigger 표시를 지웁니다.
- **gtd 내일 준비**
  - `skills/gtd/tomorrow.ts` 가 데이터를 모아 `nod add` 까지 합니다.
  - 사람이 crontab 에 한 줄로 등록합니다. 경로는 절대 경로로 쓰고, 이미 등록한 줄이 있으면 더하지 않습니다.
  - 스케줄(`nod schedule on`)이 꺼져 있으면 거절합니다. 그 스케줄이 남긴 환경(PATH·Claude 설정 폴더)으로 워커를 띄우기 때문입니다.
- **문서·스킬**
  - 고친 곳: README, `docs/design.md`(「쓰지 않는 개념 지우기」), `skills/nod/`, gtd tomorrow 스킬.
  - `skills/nod/triggers.md` 는 지웠고, 그 안의 "자리를 비울 때 알림"은 `decisions.md` 로 옮겼습니다.
  - 지운 기능마다 대신 쓰는 길을 한 줄씩 남겼습니다.
  - cron 의 `nod add` 줄에 `PATH`·`NOD_HOME`·`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`·`TMUX_TMPDIR` 를 줘야 한다고 적었습니다.

## 그대로인 것

tick, `nod schedule`, 할 일 감시(`--watch`), 세션 알림, `nod ls --mine`, `nod --issue`.

## 머지 뒤

- **화면 서버를 다시 띄워야 합니다.** 옛 화면 서버는 v32 장부에서 홈 화면을 `no such table: triggers` 로 그리지 못하고, 작업 화면에는 `trigger cundefined` 가 붙습니다. 다른 화면과 작업 읽기는 됩니다.
- **이미 돌고 있는 워커(`nod run`)** 는 그대로 돕니다. 장부를 읽고 계정만 적기 때문입니다. 훅과 tick 은 부를 때마다 새 코드로 뜹니다.
- **옛 코드로 작업 넣기**
  - 옛 코드는 자기보다 새 장부를 거절하지 않습니다. 그래서 읽기는 되고, 작업을 넣을 때(`add`, 회고)만 `table tasks has no column named trigger_id` 로 실패합니다.
  - 옛 브랜치의 체크아웃에서 실제 nod 홈으로 `add` 를 돌리거나, 머지 직전에 옛 코드로 뜬 훅·tick 이 이 경우입니다.
- **트리거 행이 있는 장부** 는 v32 로 올라갈 때 `<홈>/triggers.json`(0600)이 생깁니다. 지우지 않은 트리거가 있으면 받은 일함에 할 일이 하나 들어옵니다.

## 줄 수

rebase 전(`855f13f..5eb8637`) 기준입니다. rebase 하면서 main 의 새 시험에서 `triggerId: null` 한 줄을 더 지웠습니다.

| 구분 | 더함 | 지움 | 순감 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 소스(`src`·`ui/src` 의 시험 아닌 파일, `scripts/import-mindwtr.ts`, `skills/gtd/tomorrow.ts`) | 203 | 875 | −672 |
| 시험 | 230 | 754 | −524 |
| 문서·스킬 | 128 | 159 | −31 |

## 검증

- **마이그레이션 시험** 4개: 트리거 행이 없는 v31 장부, 지우지 않은 트리거가 있는 장부, 모두 지운 트리거만 있는 장부, `triggers.json` 을 쓸 수 없는 장부. 권한(0600)과 쓰기 실패 오류를 보는 시험은 고치기 전 코드에서 실패하는 것을 확인했습니다.
- **`nod watch`·`nod trigger`**: 대신 쓰는 길을 알리고 실패하는지 봅니다. 고치기 전 코드에서는 쓰임 전체만 찍혀 실패하는 것을 확인했습니다. 5번 반복하고 `TZ=UTC` 로도 돌렸습니다.
- **실제 장부 사본을 v32 로 올림**: 다른 표의 행 수가 모두 그대로였습니다. `foreign_key_check` 는 비었고, `integrity_check` 는 ok 입니다.
- **rebase 전 전체 `bun test`**: 575 통과, 6 건너뜀, 0 실패. 건너뛴 6개는 tmux 가 필요한 시험이고, 워커 샌드박스가 가상 터미널을 막아서 건너뛰었습니다.
- **rebase 뒤**: `bun run typecheck`, `bun run lint`, `ui` 의 `typecheck` 가 통과했습니다. main 이 더하거나 바꾼 시험 2개도 이 변경 위에서 통과했습니다.
- **전체 검사** `bun run typecheck && bun run lint && bun test && cd ui && bun run typecheck` 는 착지할 때 샌드박스 밖에서 다시 돕니다.

## rebase 충돌

| 파일과 위치 | main 이 바꾼 것 | 이 브랜치가 바꾼 것 | 남긴 것과 이유 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `docs/design.md`, `nod resume` 이 처음부터 다시 시작하는 문단과 「처음 실패한 이유는 시도로 남깁니다」 | 「처음 실패한 이유」 문단에 문장을 더함: 압축 뒤 첫 메시지를 다시 넣을 때(`askedAgain`)도 마지막 `start` 시도의 지시를 씀 | 앞 문단에서 "`nod watch` 도 끝나지 않았습니다" 를 지움 | 둘 다 살림. main 의 문장을 두고 `nod watch` 언급만 지움. 서로 다른 문장이라 겹치지 않음 |
| `docs/design.md`, 「무해한 권한 확인은 nod 가 허락하기」의 「시험」 앞 | 「워커 안내 (2026-11-06)」 문단을 새로 더함 | 「시험」 문단에서 "`nod watch` 가 건 뒤에 허락한 것만 … 그 줄로 내는 것" 을 지움 | 둘 다 살림. main 의 새 문단을 두고 「시험」 문단에서 그 항목만 지움 |
| `src/worker.test.ts`, main 이 새로 더한 시험 「a compacted conversation of a task resume started again …」(충돌 표시 없음) | 새 시험의 `ledger.add` 에 `triggerId: null` 이 있음 | 이 브랜치가 `NewTask` 에서 `triggerId` 를 지움 | 시험은 그대로 두고 `triggerId: null` 한 줄만 지움. 그대로면 타입 검사가 실패함 |

body:
## Problem

The Netlify deploy failed in the install step:

```
npm error notarget No matching version found for @netlify/otel@^7.0.7.
```

Netlify runs `npm install` on every build. `netlify-cli` (a local dev tool) was listed in `devDependencies` and pulls in `@netlify/otel@^7.0.7`, which the build could not resolve.

## Fix

- Remove `netlify-cli` from `devDependencies`; `npm run dev` now uses `npx netlify-cli dev`
- Add `package-lock.json` so installs are reproducible
- Node version left on Netlify's default (v24 LTS); it was not the cause

## Testing

- `npm install` locally: installs only `typescript`
- Netlify deploy preview on this PR should build successfully

author: amado2k5
body:
## What this PR does

This PR remediates the **3 MAJOR errors** found by the phase-1 audit of the academic white paper on islam.museum. The audit re-checked **269 claims in a stratified random sample of 50 records** (seed 20261104, frozen release v2026.11.04, Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23945544) against each record's own cited sources: 26 records verified clean, 8 minor, **3 major**, 13 unverifiable. These are the three majors, fixed at their source. Full audit pack: `~/workspace/your_files/islam-museum-white-paper-phase1-2026-11-04.md` (per-record results in `~/workspace/whitepaper/audit/result-batch-1..5.json`).

## Per-record before / after

### 1. `building/saadah-mosque-gurun` — identity conflation in the label
- **Before:** label (en) "Saadah Mosque, Gurun" — Gurun is a town in Kedah, Malaysia. The Arabic summary embedded the same "Saadah Mosque, Gurun" string; the English summary read "Draft card for the Saadah Mosque, Gurun…".
- **What the record's own source says:** the record's linked Wikidata item **Q12497333** is "Saadah Mosque — mosque in West Sumatra, Indonesia" (inception 1910; coordinates 0°26′S, 100°33′E, West Sumatra). No cited or linked source places this mosque in Gurun. (Independently re-verified against Wikidata for this PR.)
- **After:** label (en) "Saadah Mosque, West Sumatra"; both summaries corrected to West Sumatra. Region (`southeast-asia`), period (`colonial-era`) and kind were already consistent with the Indonesian item and are unchanged. The record id/slug is a stable identifier and is not renamed (repo rule: IDs are immutable).

### 2. `place/majorca` — the structured summary contradicts the record's own prose
- **Before:** summary (ar + en) described Majorca as "an island of many vineyards and grapes, with a small fine town, lying between Denia and Minorca", citing al-Idrisi, *Nuzhat al-Mushtaq* (Cairo 2002), p. 582.
- **What the cited page says (per the record's own fuller prose, same citation):** the vineyards / handsome-little-city / nearest-to-Denia description is al-Idrisi's account of **Ibiza (Yabisa)**. Majorca itself he describes as lying **east of Ibiza**, one channel away, containing **a large city with a ruler and a garrison of men, numbers, weapons and wealth**. The summary had transferred Ibiza's description onto Majorca.
- **After:** the structured summary (ar + en) now mirrors the record's own sourced prose account of Majorca, with the same p. 582 citation. The prose files were already correct and are untouched.

### 3. `question/who-was-nuh` — central claims cited to a source that supports none of them
- **Before:** the 950-year preaching period, "first of the Messengers of Steadfast Resolve", and the story's Qur'anic distribution (Surah Hud, Surah Nuh, ~30 places) were cited only to the generic `source/wikidata` record, which attests none of them; provenance conceded a "general-knowledge draft; verify against cited source". The claims are standard tradition — the failure was purely the citation.
- **After:** the claims are cited to the Qur'an text itself, `source/tanzil-quran` — the same citation sibling question records use for Qur'anic claims (e.g. `question/who-was-ibrahim`). Changed: `sources:` in the data record, the `{cite:…}` token in the long answer, and the citation tokens in the Arabic and English prose. Provenance now records the correction. No claim text was added, removed or reworded.
- **Known remainder:** the Urdu prose file still carries the old `{cite:wikidata}` token; it is left for the founder's Urdu lane, as Urdu content is not touched by this PR. (It still resolves to a defined source entity, so cite-check passes; the citation correction for Urdu is a one-token follow-up.)

## Files changed

- `data/building/saadah-mosque-gurun.yaml` — label + summaries
- `data/place/majorca.yaml` — summary (ar + en)
- `data/question/who-was-nuh.yaml` — sources, long-answer citation, provenance note
- `content/ar/question/who-was-nuh.md`, `content/en/question/who-was-nuh.md` — citation token
- `CANARY.md` — "Fixed" entry under v1.3.0 (2026-11-06)

## Gates

- `npm run graph` — fresh `.cache/graph.json` built in the worktree (51,928 nodes).
- `npm run validate` — exit 0: `validated 50006 entities, 85097 prose files: 0 errors, 8491 warnings`; authenticity `0 error(s)`.
- `npm run cite-check -- question/who-was-nuh place/majorca building/saadah-mosque-gurun` — `cite-check: 3 pass, 0 fail of 3 record(s)`.
- `npm test` — the change-relevant suites pass: `scripts/cite-check.test.ts` + `scripts/markdown.test.ts` (2 files, 7 tests, all passed). The full suite (incl. the whole-repo `pipeline.test.ts`) did not complete on the preparation VM despite repeated attempts — the box was at load average ~13.5 with several agents' suites and builds contending (the same load-timeout pattern other lanes hit the same evening); no failure was observed in anything that ran. The PR's Validate workflow runs the full suite in CI.

Prepared by Muse (orchestrator fleet) as a local commit; founder merges and deploys as usual — merged is not live until the founder's next deploy.

author: rikki
body:
Closes #647

## What this lands

The repo's first JS test base, for `gui/web/index.html` and the mobile `mobile.js` overlay.

- `tests/js/` — cases run by `node --test`; jsdom loads the real `gui/web/index.html` with `runScripts: "dangerously"`, then `mobile.js` is injected and `pywebviewready` dispatched. No production code changed.
- `tests/test_web_client.py` — a single `unittest` case shells out to node, so the regression entry point is still `python -m unittest discover -s tests`. Missing node fails, and a run that collects zero cases fails (`node --test` exits 0 on an empty set).
- `package.json` / `package-lock.json` — jsdom pinned at `31.0.0`; `node_modules/` ignored. Both CI jobs install it with `npm ci` under a pinned `node 22.23.4`.
- Cases: the three `tick()` outcomes (finished / stopped with no results / still winding down after stop), the `summarize()` fallbacks, and the mobile completion page's two exits.

## Why jsdom

A zero-dependency `node:vm` + hand-written DOM stub covers `index.html` but not `mobile.js`: `main().querySelector("h1")` runs against `innerHTML` that a string-backed stub cannot parse, so the assertion degrades into matching a second stub. Since the mobile completion page is exactly what #632 item 2 fixed, that half-coverage would look green while testing nothing. Full trade-off in ADR-0017.

## Verification

- `python -m unittest discover -s tests`: 1353 passed, 2 skipped (`d664ece` baseline: 1347).
- `node --test`: 7 cases green on node 26.13.0 and on node 22.23.4 (the version CI pins).
- Mutation checks, each turning the expected case red: dropping `|| r.cancel`; dropping `!r.running`; `clearInterval(undefined)`; emptying the `oneTap()` onclick; `summarize()` fallback returning `""`; calling an undefined bridge method behind `.catch(() => {})`.
- `ruff check --select F,E9 tool tests gui`: clean.

## Notes

- Node 22 does not accept a directory as a `--test` argument, so the Python wrapper expands the case files into explicit paths.
- `--test-timeout` marks a case failed but does not exit the process, so `--test-force-exit` is passed as well; without it a case that forgets `window.close()` hangs the whole run.

author: charliermarsh
body:
## Summary

All six unchanged benchmark reports matched across the 39 frozen inputs. On the actual merge parent `6a5c0b98a5ba`, repeating boolean lists was 9.65–10.20× faster, unboxed floats were 2.50–2.55× faster, and owned strings were 1.50× faster. All 440 runtime tests passed.

The runtime reserves the output buffer before acquiring additional owners. It fills a singleton or copies whole slices for primitive words. Strings, lists and objects acquire the required strong references once per source word. Other owning representations keep their existing per-element acquisition. A regression test checks duplicate aliases and a null entry, then checks the owner count as each list drops.

Across two cores with executable placement balanced, the repeated inventory report improved 1.47–2.28%, distinct inventory improved 0.31–0.71%, conformance improved 0.29–0.42%, Luhn improved 0.11–0.49%, and Base45 ranged from 0.16% slower to 0.01% faster. Telemetry took 0.90–1.01% longer. An independent instruction-count run for telemetry found 30 fewer guest instructions, 31 additional data reads and 22 additional writes.

Closes #23

## 概要
T-106（分割した前半）。T-101〜T-105 の部品（`sim` の `Scheduler`・`Sub`、`cluster` の `Node`・`Opening`、`ledger`、`ferry` の `Transport`）を `sim.Engine` に組み立てました。外から動かす方法は `Apply(cmd)` と `RunUntil(t)` の 2 つだけで、出力はドメインイベントの列（`DrainEvents`）と `TraceHash` だけです。I/O・goroutine・実時間は使いません。関連: FR-GAME-02・FR-GAME-03・FR-MAIL-01・V-5・V-6・V-7。

## 変更内容
- `server/internal/sim/engine.go`: `Config`・`RaftConfig`・`Options`・`Phase`・`Engine`・`New`・`Now`・`Phase`・`Apply`・`RunUntil`・`DrainEvents`・`InputLog`・`TraceHash`。ほかに、スケジューラのイベントの処理（`RaftTick`・`FerryArrive`・`FerryReady`・`RoundEnd`）、1 ステップの後処理 `afterStep`（全ノードの `Process` → `node.state` → `tr.Reclaim()` → テストモードの検査）、`handleOutput`、非公開の `propose`
- `command.go`: `CommandType`・`Command`・`Ack`・`InputEntry`・エラーコードと、`ferry` のエラーからコードへの変換（表にないエラーは panic）
- `event.go`: `EventType`・`EventData`・`DomainEvent`（`MarshalJSON` で `seq`・`t`・`type`・中身の順の平らなオブジェクトにする）・各イベントの中身・`LetterView` などの表示用の型
- `label.go`: 手紙の区分（`letterLabel`）
- `trace.go`: トレースのハッシュ（各イベントの `json.Marshal` に `\n` を付けて連結した SHA-256）
- `ledgersm.go`: `ledgerSM`（`*ledger.Ledger` を `cluster.StateMachine` に合わせる包み）
- `invariants.go`: 台帳と `Transport` の `CheckInvariants` を呼ぶ最小の検査
- `doc.go`: パッケージの説明を Engine に合わせて直した
- `server/internal/cluster/propose.go`: 公開の `(*Node).Propose` を足した。`cluster` の既存のファイルは変えていない
- `Reclaim`（#103）は `afterStep` の 3. でだけ呼ぶ。`DrainEvents`・`propose`・`New` の中では呼ばない

### 設計書にない判断
- **`PhaseIntro`**: `cmd.game.start` の前（ステージ紹介の間）のフェーズ。この間の `RunUntil` は時刻を進めない
- **開会式を `New` で行う**: 決定的な計算なので結果は同じ。Leader が決まらないような設定の誤りを `New` のエラーにできる。イベント（`phase.changed{opening}`・`node.leader_elected`・`node.state`・`phase.changed{sailing}`）は `cmd.game.start` のときに出す
- **開会式の手紙をイベントにしない**: 即時配達した手紙（`OpeningResult.Delivered`）は港を通らず、手紙の ID もないため（§5.3 を直した）
- **panic にするもの**: `Process`・`PostRaft`・`Arrive`・`AdvanceTo`・`Push` のエラー、コードの表にない `ferry` のエラー、`Applied.Result` の型の違い、テストモードの不変条件の違反。どれも正しく使えば起きない。**T-302・T-303 のセッションループが panic を回復し、そのセッションを `error`（`fatal`）で閉じる想定**
- **`append_probe`** は「エントリのない `MsgApp`」。**`pre_candidate`** は `node.state.role` の値で、プロトコルにない値はこれだけ
- **`ledger.applied.reason`**: `rejected` のときだけ出すフィールドを足した（後方互換な追加、プロトコル §8）

### 後のタスクに渡すこと
- T-106b: `Snapshot`・`letter.stale`・おまかせ積み込み（`cmd.ferry.autoload`）・`NextNotableAt`。`kindFerryReady` はスケジューラに積んであり、今は何もしない（`NextNotableAt` とボットが使う想定）
- T-107: `checkInvariants` を I-1〜I-7 に広げる（全ノードの台帳の比較など）
- T-202: 非公開の `propose(island, data)` を役場の `route` が使う（後処理は呼び出し側のステップで行う）。依頼書の手紙が配達されたら、今は `letter.delivered{accepted: true}` を出すだけなので、ここで役場に渡す処理を足す（`Engine.arrive` の依頼書の分岐）
- T-301: `sim` の型（`Command`・`Ack`・`DomainEvent`・`InputEntry`・`LetterView` など）と `protocol` の型の対応を決める。イベントの JSON の形はプロトコル §5.2・§6 に合わせてある
- T-303: panic の回復とセッションのコマンド（`hello`・`cmd.game.pause` など）

- [x] AC-1: `go -C server test -race -count=1 ./internal/sim/... ./internal/cluster/...` が N-1〜N-3・S-1・S-2・T-1〜T-6・A-1〜A-4・D-1〜D-6・V-1〜V-4・L-1・C-1 を含めて通り、既存のテストも変えずに通る

- [x] AC-3: 船の到着で手紙が配達され、返事がその島の港に並び、往復で Commit されて `ledger.applied` が出る（D-1・D-2）。失敗したコマンドは、プロトコル §4.1 のコードを返して状態・イベント・入力ログを変えない（A-1）
- [x] AC-4: 同じ設定・シード・入力の列からは、`RunUntil` の刻み方によらず、同じイベントの列と `TraceHash` になり、`TraceHash` が §10.2 の定義（各イベントの JSON＋改行の連結の SHA-256）と一致する（T-2・D-6・V-3）
- [x] AC-5: `Reclaim` は各ステップの後処理でだけ呼ばれ、配達・破棄した手紙のイベントを作った後に手放されて、港・船の手紙だけが残る（D-3・D-6）。`DrainEvents` は状態とハッシュを変えない（V-3・V-4）
- [x] AC-6: `go list -deps -test ./internal/cluster ./internal/ferry ./internal/ledger`（`server` で実行）に `github.com/K-Kizuku/raft-game/server/internal/sim` が出てこない
- [x] AC-7: `grep -nE '"time"|"math/rand"|go func|\bchan\b|\bselect\b|float(32|64)' server/internal/sim/*.go` が何も出さない（テストを含む。`math/rand/v2` は `rand.New` だけ）

The import contracts accept only reviewed full-record hashes, validate the existing source anchors before writing, preserve complete component/frame provenance, and provide ordered readback. They cover 953 appended views / 1,743 fields, 88 native T1 origin reviews, and three historical family files / three corroborated people. Raw figures retain absent versus explicit zero; recovery does not approve tax figures, create tax cases, allocate slips or merge source occurrences.

Native cached PDF exports now carry explicit export provenance and six-line comparison states. The viewer distinguishes these from retained print output and warns about differences or unavailable comparisons. Existing retained-PDF metadata and immutable replay remain compatible. The printed versions are preserved without rewriting or recalculation; filed-copy status remains unverified.

Validation: 14 focused Rust tests, including the complete private 953/88/3 source packages; 35 affected API/regression tests; 27 browser unit tests; independent offline rendering of all 88 actual origin reviews, including rejected mismatched frame anchors. Client data is excluded from this PR; new profiles contain public authority metadata and full-record digests only. Hosted upload and complete readback follow deployment checks.

author: csoai-org
body:
Existing csoai.claim-reactions/0.1 output identifies reaction states but does not provide budgeted work ordering. Add a standard-library offline consumer that validates the complete upstream projection and explicit caller policy, then proposes bounded advisory work while preserving stale, unknown, delivery-receipt and unresolved historical-trigger distinctions. It adds no scheduled job, canonical state store, source fetching, successful-check assertion, signer or executor.

Selection exposes hard budget/item caps, provider allowlists, mandatory deadlines/wait promotion, explicit retry backoff, unknown-history exploration and bounded supplied dependency counts. Source_verification is an upstream assertion, not authenticated here; digest pinning is not signature verification. Costs, impact weights, dependencies and successful-check history remain caller assertions. Invalid, conflicting, oversized or final-symlink inputs fail closed.

Validation: reviewed root-frozen12-file manifest and every SHA256/byte pin match; all12 paths were absent at pinned current master. Root independently passed21 Python tests, reproduced9 retained reactions through the actual existing TypeScript derivation, and obtained byte-identical deterministic synthetic replay. A Vitest wrapper joins the existing scripts unit collection; full hosted collection remains pending. Replay data are invented, mixed by seed and higher aggregate cost, and do not establish optimality, production freshness or business value. The retained public capture contains zero recheck triggers; this does not prove active monitoring. No active runtime adoption or deployment is claimed.

body:
Members and assigned agents can now open a private deposit or withdrawal order with quoted amounts, recipient details, deadlines, held-fund status, conversation, receipt images and appeals. Either party can request independent review before or after payment submission. Existing ledger locks, state checks and actor-bound idempotency protect settlement.

Suspended agent logins are excluded from new assignments. Failed forms and uncertain retry keys are retained. Payment notifications link to their orders, and bounded deadline checks expire unpaid deposits or escalate overdue withdrawals without automatic payout. Receipt storage is append-only in PostgreSQL with authenticated downloads. All eight interface languages and phone layouts are covered.

Validation: 34 native checks on PostgreSQL 13, 16 and 18; 316 broader backend/authorization checks; 142 focused frontend checks plus 33 administrator/crypto/workspace checks; 40 gateway/PWA checks; 22 synthetic browser checks with ten screenshots; type checks and production builds. The application release at 0a2c97f passed the dedicated payment CI. The subsequent commit only updates two existing regression fixtures and adds that suite to payment CI; application code is identical.

Apply the migration/API before the website. No cash activation, exchange-rate, bank-account or agent-funding settings change. Real bank/mobile-money transfers and physical-device acceptance remain unverified. Broader scheduled-game CI is a separate gate and is not claimed green; its base already has failing legacy fixtures. See docs/reviews/agent-payments-20261107/implementation.md for the payment journey, rollout and verification boundaries.

author: jeremiah-k
body:
## Overview

The pinned SDK's start_auto_message_fetching issues an immediate get_msg() inside session.start(), before MeshCoreAdapter marks itself started, so the first device-buffered frame drained at connect hit the not-started early return and was dropped with no counter, log, or dedup commit. GET_NEXT_MSG pops the frame from the device queue, so that message was lost unless the mesh re-delivered it. This change buffers frames delivered while start() is in flight and flushes them through normal admission once the adapter is started, fenced to the lifecycle that installed them.

## Key Changes

- Buffer inbound payloads delivered while start() is in flight, bounded at 64 frames and snapshotted at receipt, and flush them in arrival order through the normal classification, deduplication, and bounded callback admission path once started.
- Refuse frames beyond the bound with the prestart_overflow_dropped counter and a rate-limited, content-free warning, without evicting frames already buffered.
- Discard the buffer on stop, failed start, and cancelled start, with a content-free warning when frames are lost, so a stopped adapter never replays them later.
- Fence SDK callbacks by lifecycle epoch, so frames from a stopped or superseded startup never enter a replacement lifecycle's buffer or admission path; the fence captures no session, so retired sessions are freed by reference counting.
- Retire a stopped startup before any replay: stop() closes the buffering window and bumps the lifecycle epoch synchronously, so a late native-start completion can neither mark the adapter started nor flush frames.
- Reject a concurrent start() with RuntimeError before it can replace the in-flight owner, and close the buffering window when session construction fails after a cancelled start while keeping the retained partial session for stop().
- Keep the existing silent drop for payloads arriving outside a live start, and expose per-lifecycle prestart_buffered, prestart_flushed, and prestart_overflow_dropped diagnostics.
- Document the connect-time device-buffer drain and the buffer contract in a spec page, the README, and a changelog fragment.

## Testing

- Added a pre-start buffer suite covering mid-start delivery flushed and published, arrival order, snapshot isolation from reused mappings, deduplication of flushed frames, overflow with the cap asserted, warning throttle rearming, and counter resets across lifecycles.
- Added lifecycle coverage for stop during a pending start, late completion after stop, callbacks from a retired session during a replacement startup, constructor failure with and without a retained partial session, and concurrent start refusal; the original buffer tests fail against the pre-fix adapter, and the constructor-failure regression fails when its guard is reverted.
- The process-lifetime admission guard holds its retained-memory bound across 25 restart cycles with retired sessions freed by reference counting (248,931 bytes peak growth against 256,000).
- Pre-start, process-lifetime, lifecycle, startup, ingress-pressure, sustained-admission, session, and neighboring suites pass under targeted selection (456 tests), pinned Ruff and Black pass, and CI passes across the fake and SDK lanes.

## Scope

- The buffer is loss-bounded, not lossless: FIFO and callback-budget refusals stay counted and distinct, and a flush hands frames to ordinary admission rather than establishing durable acceptance or delivery.
- Connect-time device-buffer traffic still forwards once the adapter is live, without an age filter, because radio sender clocks do not establish a reliable cutoff.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

`MeshCoreAdapter` buffers inbound packets that arrive while `start()` is in progress. After startup succeeds, it flushes them in arrival order through the normal inbound path. The change also prevents startup callbacks from a stopped or retired session from affecting a later lifecycle.

- **Features**
  - Adds a FIFO pre-start buffer with a 64-packet limit. It snapshots packet mappings and counts buffered, flushed, and overflow-dropped packets.
  - Reports buffer overflow with rate-limited, content-free warnings. Flushes packets through existing classification, deduplication, and callback admission.
  - Documents the behavior in the README, change note, and specification.

- **Fixes**
  - Discards buffered packets when startup fails or is cancelled, or when `stop()` runs. Late callbacks from retired sessions cannot enter a replacement lifecycle.
  - Rejects concurrent starts while startup is in progress.
  - Preserves silent drops outside the startup window. `simulate_inbound()` still raises `RuntimeError` when no context exists.

- **Tests**
  - Adds tests for startup buffering and flush, FIFO order, snapshots, overflow, lifecycle boundaries, deduplication, callback-budget refusal, and counter resets.

No breaking changes or migration steps are indicated.

author: plotome
body:
## Problem

The selfhost integration line remains at upstream `61e7e8f966f53478f3efe68ec50c5a5fdd00a51f` while upstream has advanced to `282f48eed2531f467ed4e6febc2a59b590d3e711`. The currently prepared candidate has not been deployed.

## Goal

Integrate the 35 new upstream commits without losing any of the ten accepted selfhost capabilities or changing the installed daemon.

## Proposal

Merge upstream/main into the fork integration line from `3c6b09c4483dc00b6e37106b7763ecb3dff115f5`. The update includes issue PR auto-completion controls, scoped chat requests and Slack source metadata, daemon idle-chat cache reclamation, Pi cleanup preflight, attachment dimensions and CSV/image improvements, workspace pinning, Desktop tab restoration, issue retry/sub-issue behavior, brand assets, and v0.8.1 notes.

Resolve the `AGENTS.md` conflict by retaining both the upstream PR requirements and the fork integration contract. Renumber the two new upstream migrations from 615/616 to 622/623, after the fork's existing 619–621; SQL and generated queries are unchanged.

### Selfhost patch review

| Capability | Upstream interaction | Decision and evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Persistent conversation worktrees | Daemon env-root GC guards now normalize path aliases; idle chat artifact cleanup excludes local-directory worktrees | Retain; daemon and execenv race gate |
| Per-task Codex processes | No Codex process lifecycle change; Pi gets cleanup preflight | Retain; agent race gate |
| Conversation Codex homes and skills | Idle chat GC can reclaim regenerable cache, with local-directory paths excluded | Retain; daemon and execenv race gate |
| Codex hook trust rehome | No equivalent trust migration | Retain; execenv race gate |
| Host Codex runtime config | No late runtime-config replacement | Retain; execenv race gate |
| Device-owner application approvals | No equivalent approval bridge | Retain; daemon and agent race gate |
| CLI open list and issue cancel | New per-issue PR auto-complete flags touch `cmd_issue.go` | Retain; focused CLI tests and CI |
| Squad detail route ID | Squad sidebar/picker changes, no detail-route replacement | Retain; Views CI |
| Bounded API requests | Workspace-scoped requests and attachment schema touch API client; request timeout remains | Retain; frontend CI |
| Manual Desktop maintenance | Desktop tabs and branding change, no updater-policy replacement | Retain; Desktop CI |

No accepted patch is retired. The fork's existing migration numbers remain stable for installed databases.

## Alternatives

Rewriting upstream history or reusing migration numbers would make an installed fork ambiguous, so this is a normal merge with only conflict and migration-number adjustments.

## Screenshots

This integration PR adds no fork-authored UI. The upstream UI evidence is in the linked upstream PRs, including [brand](https://github.com/multica-ai/multica/pull/10051), [workspace pinning](https://github.com/multica-ai/multica/pull/9974), and [issue list recovery](https://github.com/multica-ai/multica/pull/10044).

## Validation

- Targeted `cmd/migrate` migration cleanup checks and `cmd/multica` issue-list/PR-auto-complete tests passed on this merge head.
- `scripts/check-selfhost-integration.sh --current ae4526f41b70f5cd3ab57384d4021c31668fd088` runs the static manifest check, script tests, and daemon/execenv/repocache/agent race packages.
- Applicable CI must pass before merge. The merged tree will be compared with the tested head and revalidated.

No tag, release, or daemon upgrade is part of this PR.
The first combined race run reported an agent-package failure under concurrent host load. The same agent package passed alone, and a second full four-package gate passed on the unchanged commit; the initial result is retained here rather than counted as green.

body:
Fixes #855.

`SensitiveInput` only wrapped the input in `Field` when `label` was set, so `description` and `error` disappeared when the input was named with `aria-label` alone. It now uses the same condition as `Input` and renders `Field` when any of `label`, `error` or `description` is set. `Field` only renders a `<label>` when there's label content, so `aria-label` is still the accessible name.

Added tests for both cases, mirroring the existing label-less test for `Input`, plus a patch changeset. `vp test run --project=unit sensitive-input` passes (6/6).

body:
## What

Task: FE-11.3, global layout. Adds `app/layouts/default.vue` with:

- Announcement bar (bracketed placeholder copy).
- Header on the black ground: `BrandMark`, category menu, search and cart with its count.
- Mobile menu: a full-screen dialog with focus trap, Escape to close and focus returned to its button.
- Footer: newsletter form, FAQ, about and contact links, WhatsApp, social links, payment methods and legal data.

Data comes from the existing composables and the mock source. No backend route was added.

Real values are not in the repository. WhatsApp, legal data, social links and payment methods come from optional `NUXT_PUBLIC_*` variables (see `.env.example`). An absent value hides its element.

## Requirements

RF-19 (interface and validation only), RF-20, RST-01 (display only, see Pending 7).

## How to test

```bash
cd apps/storefront
# Set NUXT_PUBLIC_DATA_SOURCE=mock and NUXT_PUBLIC_APP_ENV=development in .env (copy .env.example).
pnpm build && node .output/server/index.mjs   # or pnpm test:e2e from the root
```

1. Open `/` at desktop and phone widths.
2. Uncomment the optional variables in `.env` to see the whole footer. Remove them to see it hide elements.
3. Below 1024 px, open the menu, press Tab repeatedly, then press Escape.
4. Submit the newsletter empty, then without consent, then valid. The network tab must stay empty apart from Nuxt's own `/_nuxt/` build check.

## Screenshots (UI changes)

| Desktop | Mobile |
| ------- | ------ |
| Not attached: see "Not tested" | Not attached: see "Not tested" |

## Decisions

- Made: none. Everything below that is a design or UX choice is a reversible default waiting for Thales.
- Implementation choices:
  - **`vee-validate` 4.15.1 added** because `apps/storefront/CLAUDE.md` requires VeeValidate + Zod for forms. It is the latest stable version. `@vee-validate/zod` only supports Zod 3 and the repo is on Zod 4, so `app/lib/typed-schema.ts` is a small adapter. If you consider this a relevant new dependency that needs your approval, say so and I will replace it with a Zod-only check.
  - **Newsletter JS stays out of the initial load.** The form is rendered on the server with `hydrate-on-visible`, so VeeValidate and Zod (34 KB gzip) are not blocking. Nuxt still marks that chunk `rel="prefetch"`, so browsers may download it when idle.
  - **Payload budget test added.** No existing test checked the budget, so `global-layout.spec.ts` now fails if blocking JS on `/` reaches 170 KB gzip. It measures 154.9 KB today. That is a mock build, which includes the fixtures.
  - **Search is a plain GET form** to `/busca?q=`, the route in the route map. It works before hydration and FE-04.3 can extend it.
  - **Menu links are derived from `listProducts`** (limit 100) because the data source has no taxonomy call, and no route was to be invented. If the call fails, those links disappear and the page still returns 200. This was checked with the `api` source, which is not implemented yet. FE-04.1b should revisit this: it runs during SSR and sees only the first 100 products.
  - **The cart count is read only in the browser**, because pages can be cached for everyone. While it is unknown or after a failure, the number stays hidden but keeps its space, so the header does not move. It does not update after adding an item until FE-05 connects that flow.
  - **Newsletter inputs have no `name`**, so a native submit before hydration cannot put the e-mail in the URL.
  - **Invalid store details stop the server at startup**, like the other runtime config. Social links accept `https` only.
  - **The internal gallery uses `layout: false`**, so its tests still look at each component alone.
  - **Mock taxonomy names are now readable** ("Camisetas exemplo"). Handles did not change.
- Pending (options and recommendation):
  1. **WhatsApp button.** Implemented: A.
     - A: normal button in the footer and mobile menu. It covers nothing and meets RF-20, but is less visible.
     - B: fixed button in a bottom corner. Most visible, but it covers content and can collide with a buy bar or the cookie banner (FE-08.1).
     - C: fixed on desktop only, A on phones.
     - **Recommendation: B**, icon-sized on phones and tested with the buy bar and cookie banner, if WhatsApp is a main sales channel. Otherwise keep A.
  2. **Announcement bar and sticky header on a phone.** Implemented: A. Measured at 390 x 844: bar 55 px with the two-line placeholder, whole header 118 px (14% of the screen).
     - A: nothing is sticky. Most screen for products, but the cart scrolls away.
     - B: only the 63 px header row is sticky and the bar scrolls away (7.5% of the screen). The cart is always reachable.
     - C: bar and header both sticky (14%). Too much for a phone.
     - **Recommendation: B**, and keep the announcement short enough for one line (about 40 characters). It is a small class change.
  3. **Newsletter and LGPD: nothing is sent or stored.** A valid form only shows "[Cadastro ainda indisponível. Nenhum dado foi enviado.]". Questions for you:
     - Which provider will hold the addresses (BE-09.2)?
     - What is the exact consent text, and which privacy policy does it link to?
     - Is a single checkbox enough, or do you want a confirmation e-mail (double opt-in)? A checkbox is simpler. Double opt-in gives stronger proof of consent, at the cost of some sign-ups.
     - **Recommendation:** an unchecked checkbox, as built, plus double opt-in and a record of the date and text accepted. Legal review should confirm this.
  4. **Footer ground and order.** The mock-up has no footer. Implemented: black ground, with the newsletter first. Options: black or white ground; on phones, help links first or newsletter first. **Recommendation:** black ground, help links first on phones, since the phone footer is long.
  5. **"Coleções" in the menu.** The mock-up shows one "Coleções" link, but the route map has no collections index. Implemented: each collection is its own link. Options: A, flat links (as built), which get crowded with many collections; B, a `/colecoes` page; C, a dropdown. **Recommendation:** B once there are more than two or three collections.
  6. **Search on phones.** Implemented: inside the mobile menu, which takes two taps. Options: as built; a search icon in the header row; a permanent second row. **Recommendation:** the icon, if search turns out to matter. The catalog is small for now.
  7. **Launching without legal data.** Absent values are hidden, so production could start without what RST-01 requires (Q-11 is open). **Recommendation:** make these variables mandatory when `NUXT_PUBLIC_APP_ENV` is `production`, once Q-11 is answered. Not done here because it would break production builds today.
  8. **Copy and logo.** All copy the brand has not defined is bracketed. The wordmark is text and only `base/BrandMark.vue` has to change for the logo (Q-12). Institutional slugs (`sobre`, `contato`, `faq`) are my assumption, and FE-11.2 should confirm them.

## Not tested

- **Screenshots are not attached:** the CLI cannot upload images. They are delivered separately and should be added here at review.
- **Links to pages that do not exist yet return 404** until their tasks merge: `/categoria/*`, `/colecao/*`, `/busca`, `/carrinho`, `/rastreio`, `/institucional/*`. They follow the route map. FE-11.2 also still has to add the 404 page.
- **No real screen reader or real phone was used.** Evidence is axe, Playwright keyboard checks and an emulated 390 x 844 viewport in Chromium only.
- **Not measured:** LCP, CLS and Lighthouse.
- **No JavaScript:** the mobile menu does not open. Footer links and the desktop search still work. This case has no test.
- **Real values** for WhatsApp, legal data and social links were not used, only fictional ones.

author: lucasaponso
body:
Adds `optional uint32 consecutive_failed_wakes = 13` to `HealthRequest`.

How many wakes in a row failed to connect before this ping got through. The firmware keeps the count in NVS, so it survives a power cycle (RTC memory, and so `prev_cycle_link_failure`, does not: after AB1234's power cycle on 2026-11-06 the ping said `linkFailure=null` although the node had failed three wakes). It is cleared once a ping carrying it has been sent. Together with `prev_cycle_link_failure` the server can say how long a node was offline and why.

Optional so "not sent" (older firmware) is not read as "0 failed wakes". Wire-compatible: a new field number, nothing reused; older servers and firmware ignore it. `telemetry.pb.h` regenerated with nanopb 0.4.9.1 (`HealthRequest_size` grows with the field).

Consumers (separate PRs; merge this first): nitra stores and sends it, coaplink carries it to netlink, netlink stores it.

author: rohankumarrrr
body:
## Why

Rohan said Messages was extremely laggy and asked for it to feel smooth: scrolling, opening a thread, typing, new messages arriving, and switching threads and themes. I measured it first, from inside the app, on a demo with hundreds of threads and conversations of hundreds of messages. Every one of those actions was slow for one of three reasons.

- **Every row was a view, all the time.** A 600-row conversation made 600 rows, each with its own text view and four hover buttons. Opening it took about 420 ms. Each 40-point scroll step repainted all 400 message rows (about 59 ms a step, every step over a frame). A resize re-measured all of them (1.7 s a step), a theme change rebuilt all of them (5 s), and a new line in the box re-marked every row for drawing.
- **Working out what Messages shows asked each thread's owner about ten times.** Each ask standardized file paths for every kitten, so one pass over 667 threads took 24 ms and a build took about 240 ms. That ran on the main thread on every change, every few seconds while agents work, and the phone shares it.
- **A new message rebuilt every row.** A conversation keeps its newest 200 exchanges, so one arriving pushes the oldest out and every row moves. The window only kept rows up to the first difference, so it rebuilt them all (about 2.7 s with the build).

## What changed

- The pane keeps a list of rows, makes views for the newest page (60 rows) and puts only the ones near what you can see in the window. Scrolling up near the oldest one laid out lays out the page before it, anchored so what you're reading doesn't move. Following along at the bottom goes back to one page. A row that isn't in the window doesn't get moved, since moving one still cost about 64 µs.
- A refresh keeps the view of every row that's still there, wherever it moved to, so a new message makes views for itself and nothing else.
- Each message's words are read from markdown and laid out once while the window is open, and get a text view only when shown. A cut message lays out one line past the 12 it shows instead of all of them. A theme recolours the words it has rather than reading them again. Hover buttons and VoiceOver's label and actions are made when they're needed.
- `KittenBoard.Owners` standardizes each kitten's folders once, and each folder threads are in once, and a build works out each thread's owner once. Ownership is decided exactly as before. Sorting messages no longer builds an ID string on every comparison, and what each of the cat's replies came to is kept for the open session.

Nothing about what's sent, where, or what's kept changes. Words are still forgotten when the window closes, caches included.

## Numbers

`busy` then `perf` in the demo, release builds, the same fixture and bench on both sides, three runs each, alternated old and new. The median of each run's median.

| Action | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Open a 600-row conversation | 412 ms | 8 ms (first time, 54 to 59 ms) |
| Scroll 40 points | 59 ms, all 1,389 steps over 16 ms | 3.4 ms, 0 to 2 steps over 16 ms |
| A new message arriving | 2,721 ms | 17.5 ms |
| A refresh with nothing new | 267 ms | 12.5 ms |
| A new line in the box | 66 ms | 2 ms |
| Resize, one step | 1,749 ms | 19 ms |
| Change theme | 5,023 ms | 14.5 ms |

The switch lines also show the cause going away: `inWindow=600` rows before and `inWindow=9` after, for `rows=600`. What's left in a new message is mostly building what Messages shows (about 12 ms with 667 threads). That and the phone page redrawing every row are in `docs/ROADMAP.md`.

## Proof

- `swift build` and `swift test` pass: 1,095 tests, 0 failures. `swift test --filter ScreenBoundaryTests` passes, with only the known expected failures.
- New tests, four of which fail on `main` (run there with the same files):
  - `testALongConversationOnlyHasViewsNearWhatYouCanSee`: 403 row views in the window on `main`, under 60 now.
  - `testANewMessageInALongConversationOnlyMakesViewsForItself`: 400 new views on `main`, 2 now.
  - `testScrollingUpLaysOutOlderRowsWithoutMovingWhatYoureReading`: nothing is paged on `main`.
  - `testBuildingTheBookWorksOutEachThreadsOwnerOnce`: a build took 0.48 s against 0.034 s for one pass of owners on `main`.
  - `testAFolderCountsHoweverItsPathIsWritten` passes on both and pins down that ownership didn't change.
- `testARefreshKeepsYouAtTheBottomOrLeavesYouAlone` now compares against where you are after scrolling, since scrolling near the top lays out older rows and moves the offset without moving what you see.
- Pictures drawn by the app's own windows, with no clicks, keys or screen capture: the busy conversation at the bottom, part way up, after paging to the top, back down, in Opal Horizon, Everyone, and a thread on its own. The `messages`, `select`, `themes` and `shades` journeys draw as their feature files say. Selecting "the new grid" still gives `copy goes to ChannelTextView with [the new grid]` with your app in front, and themes recolour your bubbles both ways.

## Run it again

```bash
swift run -c release shades --demo --no-script --commands .agents/skills/verify-shades/journeys/perf.txt
```

For the before numbers, check out `main` with `DemoBusy.swift`, `DemoBench.swift`, the `busy` and `perf` lines in `DemoDriver.swift` and `makeBusy` in `Demo.swift` added, and give the journey a longer `wait`, since the old window takes about four minutes. `scroll <points>` moves a conversation for pictures.

body: ## Summary The two LeakSanitizer reports that kept the sanitizer job red on #363, #370, #371, #372 and #375 are **already fixed on main**. Each failing run tested a head that did not yet contain the fix: | Run | PR | Head | Leak | Fixed by | In head? | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | 42239066392 | #371 | 5f403f3 | 4392 B / 29 allocs (embedding + Cox states, plus FFI arrays) | bc851de (#363), dea382d (#374) | neither | | 42256874940 | #372 | 98c684e | 80 B / 7 allocs (`alloc_f64`) | dea382d (#374) | no | | 42256459004 | #375 | 778dc72 | 80 B / 7 allocs (`alloc_f64`) | dea382d (#374) | no (has #363) | Every sanitizer run on main since #374 merged is clean (0 leaks, 0 UBSAN errors): 42283635047, 42283640350 and 42285058830 (main at 1fc3efd), plus 42300209096 on a feature branch. The reports alternated between runs because each run lacked a different subset of the two fixes, not because the leaks are flaky. This PR therefore (1) records the root causes with a local red/green, (2) fixes the remaining sites of the FFI-array class found by auditing the siblings, and (3) makes the sanitizer job blocking. ## Leak 1: 4392 B in 29 allocations (embedding GroupCoder, Cox) ``` std::vector::push_back <- duckdb::GroupCoder::Code src/include/two_group.hpp:135 <- EmbeddingAggregateState::Slot src/aggregate_functions/embedding_aggregates.cpp:57 <- EmbeddingUpdate embedding_aggregates.cpp:209 <- GuardedUpdate::Call src/include/aggregate_finalize_guard.hpp:55 <- RowOperations::UpdateStates (grouped hash aggregate sink) (+ vector> from Slot:59 / EmbeddingUpdate:211, and CoxUpdate cox_aggregate.cpp:286/300) ``` **Root cause:** the state's destructor is fine. The problem is that `EmbeddingUpdate` and `CoxUpdate` threw a data error in Update (embedding length mismatch, third group label, inconsistent Cox feature count). That aborts the parallel hash-aggregate sink, and DuckDB never destroys the states that *other* threads had already built. `GuardedUpdate` can only clean up the states of the chunk that threw. **Fix:** bc851de (#363) records the error in the state, propagates it through Combine and throws it in Finalize, where `GuardedFinalize` destroys the states. ## Leak 2: 80 B in 7 allocations (FFI finalize arrays) ``` anofox_stats_ffi::alloc_f64 crates/anofox-stats-ffi/src/lib.rs:8528 <- GuardedFinalize::Call src/include/aggregate_finalize_guard.hpp:29 <- RowOperations::FinalizeStates <- RadixHTLocalSourceState::Scan ``` **Root cause:** the six GLM fit aggregates checked `profile_ci` x `'vcov': 'cluster'` in finalize *after* `anofox_*_cluster_fit` had returned its result arrays. The throw skipped `anofox_free_glm_result` / `anofox_free_result_inference`. The trigger is the statement-error case in `test/sql/regression/test_glm_cluster_vcov.test`. **Fix:** dea382d (#374) moves the check to bind. 2b465b5 (in #363) did the same for the `profile_ci` x prior-weights check. The finalize guard frees DuckDB states but not FFI arrays held in locals, so the rule is: nothing may throw between a successful FFI call and its free. ## What this PR changes **1. Sibling audit for the FFI-array class (commit 6f4b0dc).** I audited every FFI call in `src/aggregate_functions`, `src/table_functions`, `src/window_functions` and `src/include` that returns heap arrays, looking for a throw before the matching `anofox_free_*`. Two sites remain. In both, a follow-up FFI call fails and its error is rethrown while the first call's result is still live: - `quantile_fit_agg` (extra_fit_aggregates.cpp): if `anofox_quantile_process` fails with an input or internal error, `fit` is now freed before the throw, as `fisher_exact_agg` already does. On a degenerate error the code still writes NULL inference as before. - `ridge_fit_agg`, `ridge_fit_predict_agg`, `ridge_fit` and the `ridge_fit_predict` window: `RidgeSelectedLambda` (conditioning-aware lambda, #305) may throw. It now runs before `anofox_ridge_fit` instead of after it. It reads only y, x and the options, not the fit result, so the computed lambda is unchanged. Neither path is reachable from SQL today. Both need a non-degenerate error from the second call after the first call succeeded on the same data, which in practice means a caught panic. This is hardening, so there is no new test. Every other throw in a finalize either runs before the FFI call or frees first. **2. Sanitizer job blocking (commit 43dd333).** In `.github/workflows/MainDistributionPipeline.yml`, job `sanitizer-tests`: - removed `continue-on-error: true`; - renamed it from "ASAN + UBSAN sqllogictests (Linux debug, non-blocking)" to "ASAN + UBSAN sqllogictests (Linux debug)"; - rewrote the comment that said the job never blocks. The repo has no ci-gate job. The only required status check in branch protection is the Windows MSVC suite. To make this job block merges, a maintainer has to add "ASAN + UBSAN sqllogictests (Linux debug)" to the required checks, which is a repository setting this PR cannot change. Nothing `needs` the job, so the deploy jobs still don't wait on its 2–3 h runtime. ## Red / green (local, CI flags) I built with `GEN=ninja EXT_FLAGS="-DENABLE_SANITIZER=TRUE -DENABLE_UBSAN=TRUE -DCMAKE_CXX_STANDARD=17" make debug` and ran with `ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=1:abort_on_error=1:strict_string_checks=1:detect_stack_use_after_return=1` and `UBSAN_OPTIONS=print_stacktrace=1:halt_on_error=1`, as the job does. - **RED** (the `src/` parts of bc851de and dea382d reverse-applied): - `test/sql/hypothesis_tests/test_embedding_drift.test`: exit 134, 4176 B in 11 allocations, same `GroupCoder::Code` two_group.hpp:135 <- `EmbeddingUpdate`:209 stack as CI. - `test/sql/survival/test_cox_edge.test`: exit 134, 56 B in 4 allocations from `CoxUpdate`. - `test/sql/regression/test_glm_cluster_vcov.test`: exit 134, 7 times "80 byte(s) in 7 object(s)" from `alloc_f64` lib.rs:8528, once per error case in the current test file. - **GREEN** (this branch): all three files exit 0 with no leak report. - Full sanitizer suite `./build/debug/test/unittest "test/*"` on this branch: still running locally (about 2.5 h); I will add the result here when it finishes. - Release `make test`: All tests passed (8 skipped, 21961 assertions in 327 test cases). ## Not fixed: the Update-throw class (leak 1) elsewhere The pattern behind leak 1, a data-dependent `throw` in Update or Combine, still exists in many aggregates (the "Inconsistent feature count" checks in the OLS, ridge, GLM, AFT, ALM and BLS families, among others; drift_aggregates.cpp's third-label check; two_group.hpp `Slot`). These only leak when a parallel sink has states on other threads when the throw happens. The test suite does not hit that, and the full ASAN run is clean. Converting them all to deferred errors, as #363 did, would be a broad refactor, so it is left for a follow-up. Related: #363, #374. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) https://claude.ai/code/session_018txuxDXKkW25AA5qkB1n9V ---

author: wilminator
body:
This adds `--metrics`, which shows where a run's time went. It's step one of making storage I/O concurrent: measure first, then change the flow. A same-key `copy` on the QNAP ran at about 20 MiB/s with vmobj under 5% CPU, and this is what will show why.

## Output

```text
Time by stage (wall time 1s; stages can overlap):
  stage                  total  share        ops         data       mean        p50        p95
  source read          65.27ms     5%         75   300.00 MiB      870µs     1.02ms     2.05ms
  hash                298.13ms    22%         75   300.00 MiB     3.98ms      4.1ms     8.19ms
  compress+encrypt    590.89ms    44%         75   300.00 MiB     7.88ms     8.19ms    16.38ms
  storage write       487.99ms    37%         75   300.00 MiB     6.51ms     8.19ms     8.19ms
```

- **total** is summed across goroutines, so stages that run in parallel can add up to more than the wall time.
- **share** is a stage's total as a percentage of the wall time. A stage near 100% is the one the run waited on.
- **p50/p95** come from power-of-two buckets, so they're accurate to within 2x. That's enough to tell a 10 ms disk flush from a 100 µs write.

## Design

- **`internal/metrics`:** a recorder that's safe from many goroutines at once. A nil recorder records nothing, so runs without `--metrics` are unchanged.
- **Where the timing happens:**
  - The repository times its own sealer and storage calls (`Repo.Metrics`). Wrapping the backends instead would hide their optional interfaces: storage classes, Object Lock, archive restores and versions.
  - The scan times source reads and hashing.
  - Restore times its writes to the target.
- **Stages:** source read, hash, compress+encrypt, storage write, storage read, storage list, decrypt+check, restore write.
- **Commands:** `measure`, `backup`, `backup-vm`, `restore`, `restore-vm`, `copy` and `verify` take `--metrics`. The table prints at the end, **also when the command fails or is interrupted**, so a two-minute sample can be cut short with Ctrl+C.

## Tests

- A nil recorder is safe to use.
- Totals and quantiles are right for a mix of fast and slow operations.
- Many goroutines can record at once (race detector).
- The report's format.

The full suite passes, and so does `e2e.sh`.

body:
- `LICENSE`: MIT for this repo's code, **a choice for you to confirm** (copyright line: "2026 Nick Crews"). It also carries datamade/usaddress's MIT notice (© 2014 The Atlanta Journal Constitution), required for the copied `src/data/street-suffixes.ts`, whose header now names it too.
- README "Data and licenses": sources and licenses; OpenAddresses' US source terms at the last commit before the libpostal snapshot (`06015e0`, 2017-03-03: 1,398 sources, 1,248 unrecorded, 34 attribution, 1 share-alike = Oregon Metro under ODbL, 22 "Indemnification", no NC/ND); how ODbL/OSMF/CC guidance classifies examples vs a trained model; attribution text; four conditions for distributing a model.

Findings, from primary sources:
- ODbL 1.0: the examples are a Derivative Database (internal use fine, §4.5(c); public use needs ODbL, §4.4). §4.6 also covers "a Produced Work from a Derivative Database", so publishing any model requires offering the data or the method of making it; publishing `src/data/` + snapshot id does that.
- OSMF Attribution Guideline (adopted 2021-06-25), "Machine learning models": substantial OSM training sets are Derivative Databases; models need attribution in their docs; predictions aren't covered; a model that can recreate substantial data is a Derivative Database.
- OSMF Substantial guideline: <100 features only for a one-off, non-systematic extract.
- CC "Using CC-Licensed Works for AI Training": BY/SA bind when shared publicly, NC on every use needing permission; conservatively a public model from SA content carries the SA license. Irrelevant for the 2017 data (no CC SA/NC US sources then), relevant if OA data is ever rebuilt from today's sources (which include CC BY-SA and CC BY-NC-SA).

For your decision:
- Repo license (MIT assumed).
- The committed fixture in #15 (`test/fixtures/data`, ~600 examples, about half OSM) is a substantial extract; fine while the repo is private, needs ODbL + attribution (or a synthetic fixture) if the repo goes public.

Not legal advice.

Closes #13

author: deconstructo
body:
## What this changes

`tools/make-macos-app.sh` could not produce a working app for `examples/spacetime-horizon`. Two fixes, both of which affect every bundled app:

- **Scheme libraries are bundled.** The script only copied the `.so` modules. An app that imports a library written in Scheme, such as `(curry spacetime)` or `(curry gpu-math)`, would fail on a machine without curry installed. `lib/curry/modules` is now copied into `Resources/mods` (about 2.5 MB).
- **The launcher uses the bundled Qt plugins.** `qt6.so` adds the Homebrew plugin directory it was built against to Qt's search path unless `QT_QPA_PLATFORM_PLUGIN_PATH` is set. On a machine with Homebrew Qt that loads a second QtCore next to the bundled one, and the window fails with "Could not load the Qt platform plugin cocoa". The launcher now sets the variable for Qt apps.

Docs: a Scheme libraries section and a Spacetime Horizon example in `docs/guides/make-macos-app.md`, the updated bundle layout and launcher snippet, and a short note in the example README.

## Checked

- Built `Spacetime Horizon.app` (298 MB) and took a snapshot from the bundle (`--spin 0.9 --tau 14`) from `/tmp` with a stripped environment. The image shows the cones, horizons and worldline.
- `codesign --verify --deep --strict` passes; the load log shows no Homebrew Qt; `QtShaderTools` is in the bundle.

## Not checked

- Opening the app by double-clicking in Finder.
- Running it on a Mac without Homebrew installed. The stripped-environment run is the nearest check.
- Other apps (Mandelbrot, tesseract). The change adds files and one environment variable, but I did not rebuild them.

The last step of the OLE containers and servers work: objects now activate in place, on both sides.

## Containers
- `COleFrameHook` implements `IOleInPlaceFrame` on the container's frame (`CFrameWnd::m_pNotifyHook`). It merges the shared menu, sends keys to the active object, negotiates border space, and hides the container's bars while the object shows its own.
- `COleClientItem` gains `IOleInPlaceSite` and the in-place operations: `Deactivate`, `DeactivateUI`, `SetItemRects`, `OnChangeItemPosition`, `OnGetWindowContext`, `OnShowControlBars` and the other overridables.

## Servers
- `COleServerDoc` implements `IOleInPlaceObject` and `IOleInPlaceActiveObject`. `OnShow` activates in place when the container allows it, in a `COleIPFrameWnd` with a `COleResizeBar`, built from the in-place resources of `SetServerInfo` through `CDocTemplate::CreateOleFrame`.
- The server's toolbars dock in the container's frame through `COleCntrFrameWnd`. `RepositionBars` keeps each side's bars apart.

## Also
- `CRectTracker` in `afxext.h`.
- `COleClientItem::Draw` draws from the object's metafile when it has no view object. In one process, Wine gives the container the server's own object instead of OLE's handler.

## Tests
`iptest` puts a container and an in-place server in one program. It covers activation in the view, the shared menu, both sides' accelerators, a click on the server's toolbar, resizing through the resize bar, UI deactivation and full deactivation, and `CRectTracker`. The README is updated.

body:
A workflow this repository pins, or a script it runs, moved in the spec at `v1.0.141` (`757e680b2ed8d9d8df1f92b730ceea14c3ff873f`), or a pin here is past half of what the pin check allows.

Taken here, it never reaches `workflow-pins` or the pin check on a pull request, so this is opened for you rather than owed to you.

**Every spec pin here moves once one of them is due.** A pin is due when its workflow or scripts moved, or when it is past half of the commits behind `main` or half of the days `hygiene.yml` allows, which leaves the bump room to merge before the pin check refuses anything.

**One pull request, rebuilt for each number.** The fan-out keeps this branch and this pull request, rebuilds the branch from `main` when the spec publishes another number, and retitles it, so the checks of the number it replaces are cancelled rather than left running beside it.

**It merges itself.** The fan-out arms it to merge at the commit it made once its required checks pass; where it moves spec's pins alone, `pin-only` has already held them to moving forward along `main`.

**A check group the gates at `v1.0.141` no longer know goes with the pin.** Where this repository lists one in its gates caller's `checks` or `skip`, the bump drops it, since the gates refuse a group they do not know (OPS-R92). That is more than a pin, so `pin-only` waits for `workflows-approved` before it merges.

author: kun654
body:
### Related Issues

None — I did not find an open issue for this, so I'm filing the fix directly together with the regression tests. Happy to open an issue first if you'd prefer.

### Proposed Changes:

`PyPDFToDocument.from_dict()` (`haystack/components/converters/pypdf.py:171`) and `PDFMinerToDocument.from_dict()` (`haystack/components/converters/pdfminer.py:154`) called `default_from_dict()` on a `dict` whose `init_parameters["link_format"]` they had **overwritten in place** with the deserialized `LinkFormat` enum. That mutates the caller's own dictionary, which breaks two things downstream:

- a second `from_dict()` on the same dict raises `AttributeError: 'LinkFormat' object has no attribute 'lower'` (`LinkFormat.from_str` in `haystack/components/converters/utils.py` calls `.lower()` on its argument), so cached or replayed serialized pipelines stop loading;
- the dict is no longer JSON-serializable, so anything that round-trips it through `json.dumps` fails with `TypeError: Object of type LinkFormat is not JSON serializable`.

The fix copies `init_parameters` before substituting the enum, so the caller's dict keeps the serialized string. This is the same pattern `BranchJoiner.from_dict()` (`haystack/components/joiners/branch.py:121-124`) already uses, and the same class of bug that #13563 fixed for `ListJoiner.from_dict()` (`haystack/components/joiners/list_joiner.py:100-105`).

### How did you test it?

Environment: Python 3.11.15, ruff 0.16.0, mypy 2.4.1, `PYTHONPATH=.` against the source tree.

Runtime consequence, upstream `main` vs. this branch — the `loaded tree:` line shows which checkout ran:

```
########## PRISTINE (upstream main) ##########
1) caller dict after one from_dict: <LinkFormat.MARKDOWN: 'markdown'>
   caller dict unchanged?      : False
2) json.dumps(caller dict)      : TypeError: Object of type LinkFormat is not JSON serializable
3) second from_dict             : AttributeError 'LinkFormat' object has no attribute 'lower'
loaded tree: ...\hs\base\haystack\__init__.py
########## FIXED (this PR) ##########
1) caller dict after one from_dict: 'markdown'
   caller dict unchanged?      : True
2) json.dumps(caller dict)      : OK
3) second from_dict             : OK
loaded tree: ...\hs\main\haystack\__init__.py
```

Regression tests — `TestFromDictDoesNotMutateCallerData` added to both converter test files (they assert the component is built correctly, the caller's dict is untouched, and a second `from_dict()` still works):

Before the source fix (new tests only, converters still at upstream blobs `957a72f1` / `dc47b401`):

```
FAILED test/components/converters/test_pypdf_to_document.py::TestFromDictDoesNotMutateCallerData::test_from_dict_does_not_mutate_caller_data
FAILED test/components/converters/test_pdfminer_to_document.py::TestFromDictDoesNotMutateCallerData::test_from_dict_does_not_mutate_caller_data
======================== 2 failed, 37 passed in 1.74s =========================
```

After the source fix:

```
============================= 39 passed in 1.11s ==============================
```

Lint / type / release-note gates:

```
$ ruff check <4 changed .py files>
All checks passed!
$ ruff format --check <4 changed .py files>
4 files already formatted
$ python scripts/release_note_backticks.py --check      # rc=0
$ codespell <5 changed files>                            # rc=0
```

`mypy haystack/components/converters/pypdf.py haystack/components/converters/pdfminer.py` (cache cleared) reports the identical two errors before and after this change, both in files this PR does not touch — `haystack/logging.py:267` and `haystack/components/converters/image/image_utils.py:346`, `Unused "type: ignore" comment [unused-ignore]` — so they come from my local mypy version, not from this diff. No new mypy output.

### Notes for the reviewer

Only the `link_format` line changed in each converter; the `data = {**data, "init_parameters": init_parameters}` form avoids mutating the mapping the caller passed in. `test/components/converters/` as a directory has 6 collection errors from missing optional dependencies in my environment, identical in the untouched checkout, so I scoped pytest to the two files this PR touches.

author: henricop
body: ## PR Checklist - [x] The commit message follows the contribution guidelines. ## Bugs / Features - [x] Related issue linked: #1512. - [x] Regression tests added. - [ ] Docs added / updated: no public API change. - [x] Patch changeset for `@voltagent/rag` added. ## What is the current behavior? `HtmlChunker` passes numeric HTML references to `String.fromCharCode`. Supplementary characters are truncated to 16 bits: both `🚀` and `🚀` become U+F680 instead of 🚀. This corrupts text before retrieval chunking. Invalid scalar values can similarly wrap to NUL or produce lone surrogates. ## What is the new behavior? Decode the supported decimal and hexadecimal references with `String.fromCodePoint`. Replace zero, surrogates, and values above U+10FFFF with U+FFFD before conversion, following the [HTML recovery rules](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/parsing.html#numeric-character-reference-end-state). Named-entity support and chunking APIs remain as before. Fixes #1512. ## Notes for reviewers - The 15 added cases cover supplementary emoji/CJK characters, the upper Unicode boundary, BMP references, and invalid values. On main, 13 fail and 2 pass. With the fix, all 62 RAG tests pass across 19 files, with no type errors. - `pnpm build:all`: all 29 projects passed. `pnpm lint`, changeset validation, Markdown formatting, and built CJS/ESM public-API checks passed. - `pnpm test:all` and a subsequent `lerna run test --no-bail` exposed existing suite problems: `resumable-streams`, `voltagent-memory`, and `cloudflare-d1` report “No projects were found”; Elysia has 6 stale HTTP-mock failures. Each problem was reproduced on a clean main worktree with the same dependencies. The affected test/configuration files are unchanged. Other runnable package suites passed, including core (1,400 tests, 2 skips, 1 todo). - The E2E suite was rerun with a dedicated Compose project: both LibSQL/PostgreSQL persistence tests passed; its container, network, and test volume were removed by the test script. This uses mocked models, with no LLM credentials or requests. - Changeset validation emits an existing macOS ARM `term-size` binary warning but exits successfully and identifies the RAG patch release. This contribution is AI-assisted. --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes `HtmlChunker` corrupting supplementary Unicode characters when decoding numeric HTML references, resolving #1512. `String.fromCharCode` truncated code points above U+FFFF to 16 bits, so `🚀` and `🚀` both became U+F680 instead of 🚀. The decoder now uses `String.fromCodePoint` and replaces zero, lone surrogates, and code points above U+10FFFF with U+FFFD, following the HTML numeric character reference recovery rules. Named-entity decoding and chunking APIs are unchanged. Regression tests cover supplementary emoji/CJK characters, the Unicode boundary, BMP references, and invalid values. Written for commit de911fc91c0e0bab26440549b154d3eda7e60acd. Summary will update on new commits. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * HTML numeric entities in decimal and hexadecimal form now decode correctly across the Unicode range, including supplementary-plane characters and the maximum valid code point. * Invalid values, including zero, surrogate code points, and values above the Unicode limit, are replaced with the Unicode replacement character. Text surrounding the entities is preserved.

## Issue

Closes #1 (was stacked on Silicon-Triad/meshsync#32, now merged; rebased onto `main` per R-7.7)

## Requirement IDs

D11, §6.1, §6.2, PROTOCOL.md (b), §10 (spoofed/replayed ANNOUNCE), §14 (shared UDP port)

## What changed

- `src/meshsync/net/discovery.py` (stub → implementation):
  - `PeerInfo`, `make_tag`, `build_announce`, `next_ts`
  - `PeerTable.handle_datagram` with drop rules in order: malformed → own peer_id → bad tag → stale ts → replay → LEAVE/ANNOUNCE. `expire(now)`, `peers()` (copies).
  - `Discovery` (sender + listener daemon threads, `SO_REUSEADDR` + `SO_BROADCAST`, bind `("", udp_port)`, 1 s recv timeout, LEAVE on `stop()`, `on_event` called outside the lock).
- `tests/unit/test_discovery.py`: 22 tests.
- `docs/PROTOCOL.md` §2: drop-rule order, source-IP rule, sender `ts` rule; changelog line.
- `pyproject.toml`: registered the `slow` pytest marker (the socket test takes ~2 s).
- `docs/AI_USE_LOG.md`: new row.

**Things to review (small deviations from the brief):**
1. `PeerIdentity` doesn't exist in `net/auth.py` yet (still a stub), so I added a minimal local `PeerIdentity(peer_id, name)` dataclass. **We should dedupe it after auth merges.**
2. Added a public `PeerTable.apply()` that returns `(event, PeerInfo copy)`. `handle_datagram` wraps it and returns only the event. `Discovery` needs the row to pass to `on_event`.
3. The last accepted `ts` per peer is **kept after LEAVE/expiry**, so an old captured ANNOUNCE can't bring a departed peer back within the 30 s window. This is documented in PROTOCOL.md §2.
4. Datagrams are received with `MAX_DATAGRAM + 1` so oversize ones are detected and dropped.
5. **Sender `ts` is strictly increasing** (`ts = max(unix_seconds, last_sent_ts + 1)`, approved by Ahmed). The first CI run failed because `ts` has 1 s resolution: a LEAVE sent in the same second as the last ANNOUNCE had an equal `ts` and was dropped as a replay under decision (b). This only changes the sender; the wire format and receiver rules are unchanged. `ts` can run about a second ahead of the wall clock, well inside the 30 s window. Regression test: `test_leave_in_same_second_as_announce_accepted`.

## How tested

After rebasing onto `main` (which now includes #32, #33, #36): `scripts/check.sh` (ruff check, ruff format --check, pytest): **185 passed**. `test_discovery.py`: 22 passed. The socket test ran over `127.255.255.255` (not skipped). If neither loopback broadcast nor loopback unicast works, it skips instead of failing. Not run: a manual multi-laptop run.

- [x] None

## Protocol impact

- [x] `docs/PROTOCOL.md` §2 clarified (drop-rule order, replay state, sender `ts` rule). No wire-format change.

- [x] Used. Tool and model: Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5. Logged in `docs/AI_USE_LOG.md`

author: ghost-orchid16
body:
Follow-up to [#1](https://github.com/Ghost-Orchid16/The-Long-Descent/pull/1), which was merged at the work-in-progress M6 commit (`ca14596`). The pod, cockpit and launch stage landed there. This PR adds the rest of the game: the dive from 25 m to the Mariana Trench floor, the ending, the score, the title, settings and loading screens, and the QA, deploy and docs work. With it, the game plays start to finish (stages 0–10).

## What's in it

**M6 — Twilight zone**
- Guided descent from 25 to 330 m, then the seamount flank at 355–640 m with nautilus, hatchetfish, lanternfish, a siphonophore, comb jellies, vampire squid and a sixgill shark.
- A sperm whale is heard clicking before it crosses in front of the pod.
- CO2 scrubber alarm: open the panel, swap the canister, restart the fan.

**M7 — Midnight zone**
- A giant squid crosses the floods at ~900 m.
- ~1,600 m: a liquid-CO2 seep with vent mussels, anglerfish, fangtooth, loosejaw, gulper eel and Atolla, plus a 20 s lights-off moment with bioluminescence.
- Power failure at ~2,400 m: separate power buses, a red emergency light, and breakers that must be restored in order.
- ~3,600 m: black smokers with vent shrimp, crabs and snails, then a sediment plume crossed by sonar.

**M8 — Abyssal, hadal, ending**
- Abyssal plain at ~4,600 m: manganese nodules, sea pigs, tripod fish and a dumbo octopus. Take a nodule sample with the arm, and get free of an abandoned cable (cut it or pull loose).
- A baited lander at ~7,000 m with amphipods and snailfish, then a guided descent to the Challenger Deep floor (~10,900 m).
- ECHO-7 lies tipped in the ooze with a plastic bag over its transducer. Pull the bag off with the arm and the beacon starts again. Then a drop-weight jam needs a manual hydraulic release.
- Ascent montage, surfacing at dusk beside the ship, a summary screen and credits.

**M9 — Audio and menus**
- Procedural score: pads per zone, bells in the deep, a swell for each new species, a tension layer during events, and distant whale song.
- Title screen over a live reef, and a first-launch benchmark that picks the quality preset.
- Settings for quality, resolution scale, FOV, mouse sensitivity, invert Y, volumes, subtitles, reduced motion and objective markers.
- Loading screens with the area name, depth range and an ocean fact. A new dive keeps the journal and photos.

**M10 — QA and deploy**
- Console sweep of every stage (`scripts/consolecheck.cjs`); development logs only appear in dev builds.
- Optional per-species glTF/GLB model overrides (`public/models/manifest.json`, see `ASSETS.md`).
- `vercel.json`, `netlify.toml`, `README.md`, `ASSETS.md` and `CREDITS.md`.

## Testing
- Every stage builds, enters and disposes with no console warnings or errors, both on the dev server and on `vite preview` of the production build.
- Chained transitions from stage 0 to 10: GPU geometry counts return to baseline after each stage, so nothing leaks between zones.
- The event flows (whale, CO2 scrubber, power failure, sediment plume, cable snag, ECHO-7, drop-weight jam) were driven with scripted input (`?sim=`) and checked with screenshots.
- `npm run build` produces a static `dist/` of about 2.3 MB with relative paths.
- All of this ran in headless Chromium with software rendering (SwiftShader).

## Known issues
- Frame rate on real GPUs hasn't been measured. The first-launch benchmark picks low, medium or high from measured frame times.
- The game hasn't been played start to finish with real mouse and keyboard input yet; the flows above were scripted.
- Some deep-zone creature models are simple, and the reef colonies and research vessel could use more detail.
- The radio is subtitles with a squelch sound; there is no recorded voice.
- Gamepad mapping is untested on physical controllers.
- Decompression, depth and time are compressed for play. They are not dive guidance.

## Run it
```bash
npm install
npm run dev
```
`npm run build` writes `dist/`. Deploy steps are in `README.md`.
