body:
## Summary

Root cause: the classic settings read in _required_contexts_for_default_branch_uncached only fell back to the readable branch-metadata endpoint (GH#34965) when the captured error text matched 404 markers. On the supervisor runner the read returns exit 1 without those markers, so every merge cycle failed closed on a ruleset-only private repo and CI-drift kept re-running CI. Reproduction through the real stack (shared-constants + shared-gh-wrappers + _gh_with_timeout, with the repo gh PATH shim and native gh 2.103.3) on this runner preserves 'gh: Branch not protected (HTTP 404)' on both consecutive calls; 404 is never recorded as a cooldown (cooldown only records 403/429/remaining=0/secondary text), so the exact production layer that drops the marker could not be identified from this runner. The fix therefore removes the dependency on error text instead of guessing a layer: (1) exit 75 (local admission/cooldown) and exit 124 (timeout) are logged as deferrals ('branch protection read deferred locally' / 'timed out') and spend no further read; (2) every other settings failure falls back to branch metadata, which is independent, authoritative evidence (protected=false -> no classic contexts; protected with a valid required_status_checks shape -> those contexts; anything else fails closed); (3) unclassified recoveries log 'branch metadata resolved classic requirements (GH#37026)' with a bounded exit/HTTP-status hint and no body, and unresolved ones still log 'branch protection API failed ... caller will fail closed'. shared-gh-wrappers.sh needed no change (the transport preserved the 404 in every reproduction). Step 4 (CI-drift rebase at most once per head) is out of this scope and is split to a follow-up issue.



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-required-checks.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-phantom-pending-checks.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-required-checks-filter.sh

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Medium
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-required-checks-filter.sh: 114/114 pass, including new cases that source the real shared-constants.sh + shared-gh-wrappers.sh so _pmrc_gh_read runs through _gh_with_timeout (cooldown preflight, capture, replay, cooldown recording) and call _required_contexts_for_default_branch twice: native 404 shape (body on stdout, '(HTTP 404)' on stderr) and an unclassified exit-1 failure both resolve via branch metadata (pass/unprotected) or fail closed (unknown) on both calls; a local deferral (exit 75) fails closed as a deferral with no extra read. Against the origin/main version of pulse-merge-required-checks.sh the new unclassified/deferral cases fail (5 failures), proving the regression coverage. Scoped suites also pass: ruleset-fallback, gh-check-status-cache, preflight-snapshot, admin-safety-check, full-loop-merge-cases, update-branch, phantom-pending-checks (generic-error case now also fails the branch-metadata read to keep testing fail-closed), ci-repair-routing, primary-first-diagnostics, descriptor-safe-log. shellcheck -x: zero findings on the three changed files. Runtime: with the real PATH shim and native gh on this runner, _required_contexts_for_default_branch_uncached against a ruleset-only private managed repo returned rc=0 with the four ruleset contexts on two consecutive calls and logged 'active rulesets add required contexts'.

Resolves #37026

author: mrwick1
body:
`customElements` did not exist, so `class X extends HTMLElement` could not run. Now `window.customElements` works (`define`, `get`, `getName`, `whenDefined`, `upgrade`). The HTML element interfaces that bare has are constructors that read `new.target`. `new X()` and `createElement('x-foo')` follow the construction stack of the standard. Elements that exist before `define` are upgraded in tree order. `connectedCallback`, `disconnectedCallback` and `attributeChangedCallback` run after each DOM call, the fragment parser and `cloneNode`. `:defined` is a selector. `toggleAttribute` was missing and is added.

Design: the native tree watcher only queues reactions. `Host::call` runs them when a call ends, as `[CEReactions]` does. The element state is in the native document. Nothing runs before the first `define`: the globals are lazy and a host call pays one `Cell` read.

Checks:
- 42 cases and 4 page cases match headless Chrome 155 (`tools/fixtures/ui/chrome-custom*.txt`).
- `cargo test -p bare` (1,001), `-p bare-html`, `-p bare-css` and `-p bare-js` pass. Two older tests changed: `new HTMLButtonElement()` and `new HTMLIFrameElement()` now give `Illegal constructor`, as Chrome does.
- Cost (`tools/js/instr.sh`, main 3018876): 178 `bare` rows at scale 1 and 10 and 28 `bare_js` rows. One row is over +0.5%: `resources_load largechunk 10` (+0.542%). It runs no custom element code, and repeat runs overlap, so it is noise. The next worst is `style_load shown 10` (+0.446%). With jemalloc the worst is +0.384%.

Deviations from Chrome: the page is parsed before scripts run, so the parser never calls a constructor; no `HTMLUnknownElement`; `adoptedCallback` is never called; no scoped registries. All are listed in `docs/progress.md#custom-elements`.

Not tested: a real Web Components library or live page, `formAssociated`, iframe documents, the two limits (65,536 definitions, 1,048,576 reactions), `tools/js/*_check.sh`.

Die Lern-Seiten sehen jetzt einheitlich aus, mit dem Lern-Tool als Vorbild:

author: michaelcrosato
body:
This implements the language infrastructure from the AI Hub's `lib/hub/languages.md` (**AI Hub Languages v1**) in the engine, its kits and its modules, so a game made on my-3D2dge can be played in the player's own language once a translation step adds one, without changing its code. No translations ship; this is the infrastructure only. `docs/LANGUAGES.md` says how a game uses it.

## The engine (both editions, section 6b; the same text, which contract-test holds)
- **`E.t(id, values)` and `E.lang`:**
  - reads the page's `game-lines` and `game-translations` blocks;
  - fills `{blanks}`, formatting numbers in the player's language;
  - picks plural forms by `{count}`;
  - fills `{key:jump}` control tags with the player's key or button;
  - wraps values in Unicode isolates in right-to-left languages;
  - shows the original line when a translation is missing, empty or broken (the spec's Critical rule);
  - chooses the language from `?lang=`, then the saved choice, then the browser's languages, then the game's own, matching as the spec orders (zh-TW gets zh-Hant, es-MX gets es-419);
  - makes the three test languages: `en-XA`, `zh-XC`, `ar-XB`.
- **Fonts** (D84): a letter the pixel glyphs lack is drawn with the device's font, a run at a time so letters join.
  - Right-to-left lines are drawn whole, and in a box they start at its right edge.
  - Chinese, Japanese and Korean are at least 12 px, and lines grow taller when the language needs it.
  - Scripts without spaces wrap between words.
  - English is pixel-identical (see Verification). A line is scanned for missing glyphs once and then cached.
- **`E.Dialog`**: types whole letters (whole words in Arabic script), gives a translated line the original's time, chirps by syllable, and starts right-to-left lines at the box's right edge.
- **The engine's own words are lines** (`engine.*`: 236 in the full engine, 344 with its modules'): menus, settings, controls and rebinding messages, the controls screen's screen-reader labels, save slots, notices, the boot screen's sayings, the touch START, key, gamepad, action and view names, the Shell's objective distance, and the 3D engine's settings. Sentences that were built from pieces are whole lines with blanks.
- **The Language menu**: Settings → Display, and a Shell title screen. It shows when the page has two or more languages and the address has no `?lang=`; a choice restarts the page in that language.
- **Sessions** record the browser's languages, so a replay chooses the same language.

## The kits and modules
- **Every kit's words are lines:** the 2D shell and its 22 slices, the 3D shell and its 7 slices, and the handoff template game.
  - Each part's lines sit beside it (`src/starter*/<part>.lines.json`), with notes, names and a brief for the translator.
  - Sentences built from pieces became whole lines with blanks, counts got plural forms, and key names became control tags. On a gamepad, a hint now shows the pad's own button.
- **The modules' words are lines** (`engine.<module>.*`): click, fight, arcade, drive, rpg, rooms and strategy. Click's verb buttons grow to fit longer translations.
- **The build** writes each page's `game-lines` block: the parts' lines, the engine's, its modules', and the 3D engine's on 3D pages.

## Tools and tests
- **`tools/lines.mjs`** adds the engine's lines to a page and checks its blocks as the hub will. **`tools/lines-scan.mjs`** plays a page in en-XA and lists words that aren't lines. Both are in the handoff package too.
- **kits-test** checks each kit's block, and that each kit starts in the three test languages with no error and, in en-XA, draws no word that isn't a line.
- **contract-test** covers the language core on both editions, plus a Chromium check that the font fallback draws.

## Docs and decisions
- `docs/LANGUAGES.md`, both editions' headers, the 3D manual, the API card, `AI_GUIDE.md` (hard rule 8), the README and the handoff README.
- **D83** raises the budgets, on the owner's word: the agent edition's header to 10,600, the API card to 22,000, the 2D kit cap to 216,000, and each kit with its own budget to its measured size plus room.
- **D84** lets the fonts draw what they lack with the device's font.

## Verification
- **English is pixel-identical.** `kits-test --compare` filmed the title and play of every 2D kit against the build before the kits were converted: all 44 films are identical. Before that, my engine changes were checked the same way against `main`'s kits: also 44 of 44 identical.
- **Every proof hash and bot result is unchanged.**
- **The Language menu** was tested end to end in a browser.
- **Every suite:** `npm run test:changed` ran all 30 suites on `b7f603a` (50 min). 27 passed and 3 failed:
  - **standard:** the controls screen's bind buttons had changed what they say to a screen reader ("Jump, Keyboard: …" and "—" in place of "Jump, keyboard: …" and "none"). They now say exactly what they said before, as whole lines with blanks (`c0ce3de`).
  - **contract** and **modules** (the same check): it required every engine line to be a string, but the fight module's `engine.fight.hits` is a count's plural forms, which the spec allows. The check now accepts them (`cf5fd6f`).
- **After the fixes, on `c0ce3de`:** standard (125 checks), contract (665), modules (17) and kits (29 kits) all pass. A rebuild changes nothing, and the version check passes (0.90.0 in 29 places).

## Not in this PR
- Emberdeep and the demo pages keep their English text.
- Some controls-screen names keep the engine's generated English ("Walk l", "Cmd 1"), because renaming them would change English. They're lines with notes, so they're easy to rename later.
- A pre-existing RPG spoils-window glitch that shows a raw item id during the fade-out is left as it was.

Move stage classification policy into the Python runtime while keeping semantic stage signals and conversational guidance in Markdown.

## 做了什么 每轮成功结束后，用辅助模型（没有配置时用会话的主模型）增量更新会话要点。只记录用户明确说过的目标、约束和偏好。与上一版相同则不发 `session.brief.updated`。 顶栏「更多」里的「会话要点」打开右侧抽屉，用 Markdown 显示，可以编辑。用户改过的文字由代码保住，之后的自动更新只在后面追加。 压缩时这段要点放在摘要前面，不会被写进被替换的那一段。每次调用模型前也会按最新要点放一次，所以改完后下一轮就能看到，这次不发 `context.compacted`。 设置「通用」里可以关闭自动更新（默认开）。关掉后仍可手动编辑。 ## 验证 - `pnpm typecheck`、`pnpm lint`、`node scripts/check-i18n.js` - `pnpm test:coverage`：语句 97.51%，分支 94.32%，函数 97.29%，行 98.38% - `pnpm build` 后 `xvfb-run -a pnpm e2e`：21 通过，1 跳过（key-leak）

author: djosh34
body:
Part of #500.

`race-sim` on main failed at #533's merge (`c7383b9f`, [run 42335185730](https://github.com/djosh34/tigerstore/actions/runs/42335185730)): `go test -race` hit its 1h50m timeout in `TestSnapshotFromCorruptLeader`, 43 minutes into it, at seed 182. Before, the job passed in 75–91 minutes.

**Why:** the test runs seeds until one fences a node, up to 200.
- Under gosim, seed 2 does that, so the test takes 1.6 s.
- Under the race detector, the runs are not the seeds' and a fence is rare. Locally, at main and at `87064ea6` (before #533), the first fence came at the 48th and the 40th run, each run 6–14 s. So a run costs the same as before #533, and how many it takes varies a lot.
- CI's run went 182 runs without a fence, at about 14 s each.

**Change:** under the race detector the test stops after 60 runs, fenced or not. When none fenced, it logs that race coverage of the path was skipped that run. That bounds it at about 14 minutes on CI. A fence still runs under the race detector whenever one comes, as it did before. Under gosim nothing changes: the seeds must fence, and seed 2 does.

**Why a cap, not a forced fence** (the manager asked for the forced one first): the fence needs a damaged node to serve a snapshot from its damage, so it must lead, or be the node a follower fetches from, while that follower is behind its compaction. Elections decide both, and under the race detector the timing is the machine's. A forced version would mean a scenario that pins the leader and holds a follower down past compaction, with its own tuning, and it could still miss. The node's part of the path, a serve that reads a damaged record, stops the node, and a restart that refuses the log, runs under `-race` in every `ci` run, in `internal/node`'s `TestServeCorruptRecordStops`. The simulator's part, `servedDamage` and fencing at the start, is counted under gosim.

**TestSlowFetch** (from the Astra review) searches the same way, up to 200 runs for three events, and fails under the race detector if one never came. It takes the same cap and log line. Both tests use `searchSeeds` and `raceRuns`.

Test only, so no run changes and no bench. Checked: the test under gosim, and under the race detector with the cap at 1 (each log line, a pass).

author: bikiran
body:
## Problem

Seven marketing routes answered **any** address with a page and a 200:

- `/industries/anything` showed the SaaS page.
- `/phones/anything` showed a fallback phone page.
- `/product`, `/channels`, `/solutions`, `/ai-assistant` and `/integrations` did the same.

Search engines treat these as endless duplicate pages (soft 404s). `/compare` and `/for` were already correct.

## Fix

- **Product, channels, solutions, industries:** these pages now build only their real slugs (`generateStaticParams` + `dynamicParams = false`) and call `notFound()` for anything else, the same pattern `/compare` already uses. Side effect: they're pre-rendered at build time now (360 static pages, up from 280) instead of rendered on every request.
- **Phones, AI assistant, integrations:** these pages are client components, so a small server `layout.tsx` in each `[slug]` folder does the same check.
- **Slug lists:** `lib/marketing-routes.ts` gains `PHONE_SLUGS`, `AI_SLUGS` and `INTEGRATION_SLUGS`. This also adds those **35 real pages to the sitemap**, where they were missing.
- **`scripts/marketing-routes.test.mjs`** (`node scripts/marketing-routes.test.mjs`):
  - Checks every list against the page data it mirrors, allowing for the `/industries` → `/for` redirects.
  - Checks that each route is guarded.
  - So a newly added page can't be left out and 404 by mistake. Verified it fails when a slug is removed.

## 404 page suggestions

Made-up and mistyped addresses now land on the branded 404. Its "Did you mean" only knew the hubs and a few channels. For example, `/phones/call-fowarding` suggested *Live chat widget* and could auto-redirect there.

- It now matches against every page in `lib/marketing-routes`.
- The last-part shortcut only applies within the same section, or when there's no section. So a typo under `/phones` can't jump to `/channels`, while `/sms` still finds `/channels/sms`.
- Auto-redirect confidence is measured on the last part of the address. Measured on the whole path, the long section name let `/industries/aquarium` pass for *Agencies*.
- Guesses that are too far off (e.g. a missing blog post) show no suggestion at all, just search and quick links.

## Testing

All of this runs against a local server.

- **201/201 address checks:**
  - All 94 real slug pages and every hub return 200.
  - 5 made-up addresses per route (45 in total) return 404 with `noindex`, including uppercase and near-miss slugs.
  - The `/industries/ecommerce` and `/industries/real-estate` redirects still work.
  - The sitemap has 155 URLs, including the phone, AI and integration pages, and no made-up ones.
- **14/14 typo cases in the browser:**
  - Typos auto-redirect to the right page (`call-fowarding`, `shopfy`, `voice-typng`, `/chanels/sms`, `/pricng`, `/sms`, `/ivr`…).
  - Near misses get a suggestion without auto-redirect (`/ai-assistant/ai-reply`, `/phones/sms`).
  - Made-up addresses get neither (`/phones/not-a-real-one`, `/industries/aquarium`, `/blog/some-old-post`).
- **Slug-list sync test:** passes.
- **Marketing sweep:** 216/216 on phone and desktop. One earlier run hit a single timing blip right after the server started; it didn't reproduce in two further runs.
- `tsc`, lint (no new errors) and `next build` pass.

author: hyukjinkwon
body:
### What changes were proposed in this pull request?

[SPARK-61085](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/SPARK-61085): `spark.profile` now collects and shows the results of the UDF profilers, as PySpark Connect does.

As PySpark Connect's:
- `spark.profile` is a `pyspark.sql.profiler.Profile` of the session's `ConnectProfilerCollector`, also exposed as `spark._profiler_collector`.
- The client updates the collector from the `__python_accumulator__` observed metrics of each execution. Each value is a pickled `(id, update)` of `specialAccumulatorSer`. The updates of the UDF profiler (`SQL_UDF_PROFIER_V2`, enabled by `spark.sql.pyspark.udf.profiler`) update the collector. A value that does not unpickle is logged as a warning and skipped.
- So `spark.profile.show`, `dump`, `render` and `clear` show, write and clear the perf and memory profiles of the UDFs.

`pyspark.sql.connect.profiler` is vendored from Apache Spark v4.3.0, and the drift check covers it.

The core hands each pickled update of the Python accumulators to the handler of the new `SparkSession::set_python_accumulator_handler`. It no longer keeps the observed metrics of each execution as text in a `ProfilerCollector`; that type and `SparkSession::profiler()` are removed.

### Why are the changes needed?

`spark.profile` returned a `ProfilerCollector` of the client's own, which never held a UDF profile:
- it stored the observed metrics of each plan as text instead
- its `show()` returned a str rather than printing the profiles
- `dump(path)` and `show(type="perf")` raised `TypeError`s

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. `spark.profile` collects and shows the UDF profiles of PySpark 4.3.0.

### How was this patch tested?

- A new live test enables the perf UDF profiler, runs a UDF, shows its profile with `spark.profile`, and clears it. It passes with official PySpark 4.3.0 and fails without this change.
- A new offline test sends the pickled updates of the UDF profiler, of another accumulator, and a value that does not unpickle, from a mock Connect server. It checks the profiles of the collector, the warning, `show` and `clear`.
- A new lib test checks that the handler takes the updates of the Python accumulators, and not the metrics of observations.
- On a local server, the profile of a UDF is shown, dumped and cleared as with official PySpark 4.3.0.
- The lib tests of both crates (584 passed), the build of all tests, also with `wasm-udf`, the offline Python suites (2040 passed, 12 skipped), and the live drop-in and Arrow suites (145 passed) and live cases (10 passed) against a local Spark 4.3.0 server. Clippy reports no diagnostics in the changed lines.

author: pooza
body:
## 何が起きていたか
GitHub の `ubuntu-latest` が新しい環境（ImageMagick 7.1.2.18・Ghostscript 10.06.0~dfsg-3ubuntu1.2）に替わり、`.pdf /convert` だけが Ghostscript の `Permission denied` で落ちていた。picon のコードとは関係ない（11/3 に緑だった master を流し直しても落ちた）。

診断の枝で測ったこと:
- `/tmp` の上の PDF を `convert` するのは通る（拡張子があってもなくても）
- ImageMagick の一時ファイルの置き場を作業ツリーの下（`MAGICK_TMPDIR=$PWD/tmp`）にすると、同じエラーで落ちる。picon はアップロードを作業ツリーの `tmp/` に受けるので、これに当たっていた
- AppArmor のプロファイルは当たっていない

## 何をしたか
ランナーを `ubuntu-24.04` に固定した。3 つの Node の版で全部通る。

⚠ 根本の原因（新しい Ghostscript が作業ツリーの下のファイルを読めない理由）は突き止めていない。picon の実機は FreeBSD なので、今すぐには効かない。#187 は開けたままにして、実機の ImageMagick や Ghostscript を上げるときに確かめる。

Refs #187

author: pcbeingused333
body:
By creating this pull request, I grant the project maintainers an unlimited,
perpetual license to use, modify, and redistribute these contributions under any terms they
choose, including both the AGPLv3 and the Fossorial Commercial license terms. I
represent that I have the right to grant this license for all contributed content.

Fixes #463

**Root cause.** `OnConnect` only calls `clientsOnConnect()` (which sends `newt/wg/get-config`) when `!n.connected`. The request is sent with `SendMessageInterval`, which gives up after 16 attempts (~32 s). If the first connection after startup is a half-open websocket, the request is abandoned while `pendingConfigChainId` stays set, and no later reconnect re-sends it, so the clients WireGuard device is never created.

**Fix.** Add `WireGuardService.ResendPendingConfig()`, which re-sends the outstanding `newt/wg/get-config` with the same chain ID if one is still pending. It is called from the reconnect branch of `OnConnect`. It deliberately does not call `LoadRemoteConfig`, which would start another endless `periodicBandwidthCheck` goroutine on every reconnect. `SendMessageInterval` and the first-connect path are untouched.

**Test.** `clients/resend_config_test.go` runs against a fake token endpoint and websocket server: a pending request whose sender has stopped is re-sent with the same chain ID; nothing is sent when nothing is pending; nothing is re-sent after the response was handled. With the method made a no-op the first test fails; with the fix all three pass (`go test ./clients/ ./newt/ -race` green).

AI assistance (Claude) was used to prepare this change and its tests.

author: bench-cloud[bot]
body:
Ticket: [TOPPINGCTL-11](https://plane.burntbytes.com/home/browse/TOPPINGCTL-11/). Plan: `docs/plans/2026-10-26-web-ui-architecture-plan.md`, "Build order" step 2 (code only).

## What changed

- **`toppingd.py`**, the per-host agent, read-only. It runs on stdlib `http.server.ThreadingHTTPServer` and has two routes:
  - `GET /v1/room`: host, room, the DAC found by USB enumeration (which sends no frames), its `DEVICES` key and `status`, read path, capabilities (`writes: []` for every model), `mode`, version.
  - `GET /v1/state[?fresh=1]`: state from the model's read path. Each field is `{value, source: device|written|unknown, at}`, plus a reason when the value is unknown. Without `fresh=1` you get the cached read and its `age_s`.
- **Read paths per model**, following the plan's table:
  - DX5 II: GetSettings through `devstate.read_settings(h=…)`. Volume is decoded with the device's own `volumeStep`, and is `unknown` if `volumeStep` is missing.
  - DX1 II: `devstate.dx1_state(skip_peq_dump=True, h=…)`, so the vendor read-safe list only and no `11 06`. Gain and input show as `unknown` (write-only on this model). Volume is reported per output (`volumes_db`).
  - D90 III and anything else: identity only. The device is never opened.
  - Preset and preamp come from `state.json` as `source: "written"`, labelled "last written". `state.json` is opened with `O_NOFOLLOW`.
- **Send-path guard.** `ReadOnlyHandle` wraps the opened handle. Before anything reaches the device it refuses three kinds of frame: anything that isn't a readNack, any readNack not in `CONFIRMED_READS[model]`, and the `NEVER` set (SaveC1/SaveC2/FactoryReset/FirmwareUpdate, resolved by name through `vendor_commands`). There are no write routes: any other method returns `405` and any other path `404`. `mode: live` (and any unknown config key) is refused at startup.
- **HMAC, as the plan describes:**
  - What is signed: HMAC-SHA256 over method, path including the query, timestamp, nonce and a body hash.
  - What is refused: a bad signature, a timestamp more than 30 s off, a replayed nonce, and anything before `timedatectl` reports NTP sync. The floor is taken at first sync, and timestamps earlier than it are refused, so a restart doesn't reopen the replay window.
  - Responses are signed over the request's nonce, status, a timestamp and a body hash. Each message type has its own prefix, so a response signature can't pass as a request signature. `verify_response()` is the client-side check for toppingweb.
  - Requests that fail the check get an unsigned reply.
- **Device lock:** taken once per read, waiting 2 s, with a `423 busy` that names the holder. A process-local lock keeps device operations to one at a time. Open failures are retried, as `read_settings` does, then reported as `423` "another app may hold it".
- `devstate.dx1_state` takes a passed-in `h=`, as `read_settings` already does, so a DX1 II read is one open.
- `toppingd.yaml.example` (YAML), plus short notes in README and AGENTS.md (the agent takes the lock per operation, not in `main()`).

## Choices to check

- **D90 III gets identity only.** That is the plan's proposal (a) for Q17. I didn't find an answer to Q17 in the plan. `CONFIRMED_READS["d90iii"]` is empty, so nothing else is possible without changing that table.
- **The wire format is my proposal.** The plan doesn't specify one. Header names are `X-Toppingd-Timestamp`, `X-Toppingd-Nonce` and `X-Toppingd-Signature`. The canonical messages are in `request_message` / `response_message`. The key is the stripped contents of `key_file`: at least 32 bytes, and the file must be mode 0600.
- **CI:** I have no Workflows permission, so `test_offline.py` gets a `load_tests` hook that adds `test_toppingd`. CI's existing `python -m unittest test_offline` step therefore runs the agent tests on 3.11 and 3.14. If you'd rather have a separate CI step, that's a workflow edit you'd make. `pyyaml==6.0.3` is added to `requirements-dev.txt` so CI can import it, and Renovate will bump it like ruff.

## Not in this PR (per the ticket)

The homelab install PR, and the step-2 hardware measurements: 8740 reachability, GetSettings timing and record count, asleep and unplug behaviour, the CLI and the vendor app at the same time. Step 2b waits on those measurements. Nothing here was run against hardware.

## After three /critique passes (each fix commit has a test that fails without it)

- The NTP floor is taken by a watcher thread at sync, not by the first request: a client a second behind was being refused. The floor is the next whole second.
- The signature header's format is checked before `compare_digest`: a non-ASCII header raised `TypeError` and dropped the connection. There is now a socket timeout too.
- A read that fails, or finds no readable DAC, drops the cache. A device lock held by another process drops it as well. Only the agent being busy with its own read keeps it.
- One 2 s budget covers both waits: the agent's own mutex and the device lock.
- Two DACs of one model show as `several`. To support that, `find_devices` now also reports `serial`.
- `ReadOnlyHandle` also requires a zero data field.
- `"defaults (no cache yet)"` isn't shown as a written preset.

## Open points for you

- **The DX1 II read takes about 8.5 s** with devstate's current listen windows (0x810a block 1.5 s, plus 10 queries at 0.7 s). That is over the plan's 2 s read and close to toppingweb's 10 s timeout. I didn't shorten the windows without hardware; that belongs with the step-2 timing measurements or step 2b.
- **Replay across a restart is bounded, not closed.** Timestamps up to 30 s *ahead* of the host's clock are accepted, per the plan's "more than 30 s off". So a request signed ahead of the agent's clock, and captured before a restart, could still be replayed after it. It is harmless while there are only GETs. Before writes land, either set the floor at sync + 30 s, which refuses everything for 30 s after each start, or narrow the future-skew allowance. Your call.
- **Requests right after sync are refused.** For up to about 1 s after NTP sync, requests get 503, and requests signed in the sync second itself get 401 (floor). toppingweb should treat both as retryable.
- **Two identical DACs that report no serial, or the same serial, look like one.** That is the same rule `_check_model` uses.

## How I verified it

- `ruff check .` and `ruff format --check .`: clean.
- `python -m unittest test_offline`: **183 tests OK** locally on Python 3.11.2, including the 59 in `test_toppingd`. CI runs them all on 3.11 and 3.14 (checked in the run log: 183 on each).
- The tests start the real server on 127.0.0.1 and send signed requests to it, with a fake `hid.Device` / `hid.enumerate`. They cover:
  - signing: good and bad signatures, path/query/method binding, skew, replay, a clock that starts a day in the past and then syncs, the floor across a restart, and a response replayed against another nonce;
  - routes: no write route, and no write frame from any route;
  - DX5 II: decoding under `one_db` and `half_db`, missing `volumeStep`, an empty read, open retries, the cache and its age, `state.json` written values, a symlinked `state.json`;
  - DX1 II: only `CONFIRMED_READS` readNacks are sent, never `11 06`;
  - D90 III, no DAC, an unrecognised DAC (D50s), several DACs, a different DAC than configured: none of them is opened and nothing is sent;
  - the lock held by another open file: `423` within the wait, naming the holder;
  - frames built by hand against `ReadOnlyHandle`, including the NEVER set, every confirmed write, and a DX1 II 0x810a volume write;
  - config: `live` mode, unknown keys, key-file permissions, and that the example file loads.
- Mutation check: disabling the opcode check, or the `CONFIRMED_READS` check, in `ReadOnlyHandle` makes the tests fail.
- I ran `toppingd.py --config …` by hand. An unsigned request got `401`. A signed one got `503 clock_unsynced`, because this container has no `timedatectl`. `mode: l

author: athrvk
body:
## Why

- A client certificate whose file moved after registration is dropped by the resolver, yet Settings still lists it as healthy; the resolver's log also says "sent without it" when another entry answers.
- A plain `http://` send shows the mTLS chip, because the lookup matches host and port and ignores the scheme.

Closes #3260

Refs #3254

## What changed and why this way

- **Scheme gate inside `apply_client_certificate`.** One place covers design send, stream, connection test and load, and the null writes of the cert options stay, so a reused handle never keeps an old identity. Gating at each caller would have missed one.
- **One check, `check_client_cert_row`, decides "presentable".** The resolver and `GET /client-certificates` both call it, so the card cannot disagree with the engine about which rows are dropped. An earlier draft kept a second copy in the route; review caught the drift risk.
- **`usable` and `problem` on the list route only, not in the shared `serialize()`.** POST and PUT already answer 400 for an unusable row, so their responses never carry the fields (a test locks that). The app types match: `ClientCertificateListEntry` adds them, `ClientCertificate` does not, so a create result cannot be read as "unusable".
- **Resolver log now says "this entry is not used".** The resolver has no transfer URL, so it cannot know which entry answers. Deviation from the issue's "names the entry that answered": the card badge carries the reason instead.
- **Wording "was offered", not "presented".** libcurl gives no signal that the server asked for the certificate, so "offered" is the claim the engine can back.

## Review guide

**Look closely at:**
- `engine/src/http/event_loop/curl_utils.cpp` scheme gate: a miss shows a certificate on a send that never made a handshake, or hides one on an https send.
- `check_client_cert_row` and `list_client_certificates_response`: the list reads files per row on each call. Fine for a handful of rows; it runs outside the DB lock.
- Two existing tests encoded the bug (`ADesignSendRecordsTheEntryItMatched`, `AnSseStreamRecordsTheEntryItMatched`). They now assert an empty entry over cleartext.

**Safe to skim:**
- Docs kept in step with the code (api-reference, api-integration, mcp, engine/CLAUDE.md, app COMPONENTS and state-management).
- `tool-list-budget.test.ts` caps rose by 100 B for the new MCP description wording.

## How it was verified

- Engine: full `ctest --preset linux-dev` 6922 of 6922 before the review fixes; after them the touched suites (`ClientCertificate*`, `ClientCertMatching*`, `MutualTls*`, `Diagnostics*`) pass 97 of 97. Mutation checks (drop the https condition, case-sensitive compare, `usable` always true, drop the format check, always emit `problem`) each turn the new tests red.
- App: `pnpm test` 1312 files / 18841 tests before the review fixes; after them the touched files pass, plus `pnpm type-check`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`. The type split is mutation-checked: assigning a create result to the list type fails tsc.
- Pre-push clang-tidy passes on the branch.

## Docs and follow-ups

- Updated: `docs/engine/api-reference.md`, `docs/app/api-integration.md`, `docs/engine/mcp.md`, `engine/CLAUDE.md`, `docs/app/COMPONENTS.md`, `docs/app/state-management.md`.
- No deferred work. All four slices of #3255 are merged; #3255 itself still awaits the owner's close.

## Visual changes

Settings > Network & connectivity > Client certificates. The second row has `usable: false` with a long problem string. The chip and the line sit in the row, the text wraps, and the delete button keeps its place. Usable rows are unchanged.

![Client certificates card, light theme, one row marked Not presented with a wrapped Skipped on every send line](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/athrvk/vayu/95e80c2cb71b54916f8dd85138a0dd6c1a0c1b61/.pr-assets/3260/client-certificates-light.png)

![Client certificates card, dark theme, same rows](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/athrvk/vayu/95e80c2cb71b54916f8dd85138a0dd6c1a0c1b61/.pr-assets/3260/client-certificates-dark.png)

Connection test result. The last line reads "Client certificate registered for mtls.example.com was offered".

![Connection test result with the offered line](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/athrvk/vayu/95e80c2cb71b54916f8dd85138a0dd6c1a0c1b61/.pr-assets/3260/connection-test-offered.png)

- Captured from the real renderer under vite in Chromium on Linux, not the Electron shell. A pre-branch engine binary answered every call except `GET /client-certificates` and the connection test, which were stubbed with the new fields.

body:
## What and where

New figure `refraction-of-light`: physics-9-10 › 9.1 › p243 (আলোর প্রতিসরণ, with ৯.১.১ প্রতিসরণের সূত্র and ৯.১.২ আপেক্ষিক প্রতিসরণাঙ্ক), next to চিত্র ৯.০১–৯.০২ and টেবিল ৯.০১; it carries the laws of refraction (pp. 244–247, not the coin নিজে করো, which is `coin-in-cup`) and the relative refractive index (pp. 247–248).

- A thick glass block on a plain table against the chapter's calm blue backdrop; a torch rides a graduated arc round the point of incidence, so the student turns it (drag or arrow keys, 0°–80°) and the arc reads θ₁. Rays are traced with n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂ at every boundary; a faint reflected ray grows with the angle (Fresnel), as p.245 says.
- Five steps, one tap each: ① the light goes in, bends and slows (marching wavefronts; why it bends in one line; v = c/n for টেবিল ৯.০১ as bars; n = c/v); ② the normal at the point of incidence and the angles named as the book does (আপতন কোণ θ₁, প্রতিসরণ কোণ θ₂), a θ₂–θ₁ graph, and a toggle for the same path the other way (dense → light, away from the normal); ③ the first law in true 3D: the upright plane at 90° to the surface, and the camera swings round to look along it, where the incident ray, the normal and the refracted ray fall on one line; ④ the second law: মাপো at three angles fills a table (θ₁, θ₂, sin θ₁ ÷ sin θ₂) and a square sin θ₁–sin θ₂ graph whose line has slope n₂ (water, glass, diamond); ⑤ water poured over a glass slab: 1.14 for glass with respect to water, 0.88 the other way.
- Test: five tap questions from the book (speed in water, the first law, উদাহরণ 45° into n = 1.6 → 26°, 60°/45° → 1.22, water → glass 1.14); every wrong choice has its own note; the picture shows the answer once it is given.
- Stylised on purpose: the beam is drawn (not seen from the side in clean air); light is shown much slowed (a corner note says so); a diamond block the size of the glass block is not realistic.
- For the book team: "লম্ব" as in every chapter-9 page (chapter 8 says "অভিলম্ব"); the glass speed is shown as 1.97 × 10⁸ m/s (the book rounds to 2 × 10⁸); the diamond relative indices (1.82, 0.55, 1.59, 0.63) are not on screen for lack of room on phones.
- Weight: 24–30 draw calls and 9–12k triangles per frame, 0 draws idle, GLB 317 KB, zip 470 KB.

## Definition of done

- [x] `npm run verify -- refraction-of-light` passes (check, browser tests, offline zip, GLB, pictures)
- [x] I looked at the pictures in `test-results/refraction-of-light/` (phone portrait and landscape included), plus every step, the reverse toggle, the edge-on swing and every test reveal at 390×700, 844×390, 390×520 and 1280×800
- [ ] The Bangla wording matches the book (NCTB terms), digits are Bangla: needs a person to check
- [x] It is simple for a student: the object, the one idea, a short tap-to-answer test
- [x] Version in `asset.json` (0.1.0, new figure)
- [x] Open reviews handled (none yet)
- [ ] For a kit change: not a kit change

Touch-tested in a phone browser (390×700 and 844×390, pixel ratio 3). Reviewed by an independent reviewer; all must-fix and should-fix findings addressed. Local gate (GitHub CI is off): `npm run check`, `npm run verify` (14 browser tests), `npm run test:unit` (1662 pass), Biome clean, `npm run test:visual -- --changed` (no other figure changed), and the panel never scrolls in any state or test answer at any of the six sizes.

author: owner-webrainfriends
body:
## What & why

PS-18 (#848): Elite para-sport academies (Nadal, Barcelona FC, Real Madrid standard) need specialist equipment management beyond generic inventory — sports wheelchairs, handcycles, throwing frames, boccia ramps, guide-runner tethers and similar specialist kit must be tracked as inspectable, loanable, serviceable, event-allocatable objects tied to an athlete's para class. This is a verified gap: `supply.js` has generic inventory, `academy-kit.js` has uniform issuance, `coach-adaptive.js` has an `adaptive_kit` consent signal — none track adaptive assets through the full lifecycle required for elite para programmes.

## Changes

**API — 32 `cap()` endpoints** (`apps/api/src/capabilities/adaptive-equipment.js`):
- Asset registry: register, list, get, update, retire, add serial-numbered units (barcode/QR)
- Loan/hire workflow: request → confirm + deposit → handover → return → reconcile; guardian check for ward loans; deposit waiver; sponsor-funded allocation
- Incident management: report damage/loss (encrypted description), severity, decide (waive / charge / replace)
- Event allocations: reserve an asset for an event window, list by event, cancel
- Fitting appointments: book with optional `para_case_id` (FK only, not stored on asset record), record recommended size/adjustments (operational specs only — no diagnosis)
- Service calendar: log routine / safety / repair / recall / pre-event service, next-due tracking; per-asset and venue-wide readiness checks
- Athlete profile: own active + past loans, register athlete-owned equipment for venue records
- Sponsor-funded allocation: `funding_agreement_id` on asset/loan, hidden from athlete view (financial privacy)

**DB migrations** (additive, backwards-compatible, no existing tables modified):
- `182_adaptive_equipment.sql`: 9 new tables. All personal fields encrypted (`_enc` suffix). Soft deletes only; no `ON DELETE CASCADE` on user data.
- `183_adaptive_equipment_audit_cols.sql`: additive audit/workflow columns (`ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS`, all nullable).

**App — 8 screen components** (`apps/app/src/screens/adaptive-equipment.js`):
- `AdaptiveEquipmentExplore`: searchable catalogue (sport/type/size/venue filter) → loan request flow
- `AdaptiveEquipmentHub`: fleet dashboard with metric strip, service calendar, allocation board
- `AdaptiveLoanFlow`: 4-step loan request (asset → dates/purpose → deposit → confirm)
- `FittingAppointmentFlow`: 3-step fitting (clinician search → slot picker → outcome)

author: ajaykr089
body:
Stacked on #103 (base `feat/ui-phase1-foundation`); merge #103 first, then retarget this to `main`.

## App-wide density
`<ThemeProvider density="compact" | "default" | "comfortable">` (or `tokens.density` with `applyTheme`) rescales the shared control tokens every control sizes itself from: default-size controls 28 / 32 / 36px, padding, font size and the default gap. A component's own `density` still overrides.

## One router-agnostic link API
`<NavigationProvider navigate={(href) => router.push(href)}>` routes the links of Sidebar, Breadcrumb, route Tabs (`Tabs.Tab href`) and Pagination (`hrefTemplate="?page={page}"`, real `<a>` links) through any router. Each component takes `onNavigate` (runs first). New-tab clicks stay native. Web components: the same cancelable `navigate` event, or `navigation="client"`.

Fix on the way: React's `Breadcrumb.Item href` never rendered a link (wrapper passed `data-href`, element read `href`).

## Brand colours on dark surfaces
A custom-brand dark-theme audit over every story found the contrast variants still painted in the default light blue: 54 hard-coded `#93c5fd` across 35 components now use the new `--ui-color-accent-on-dark` token (light tint of the primary), unchanged without a theme.

## Testing
ui-core 1195 / ui-react 577 unit tests, lint 0 errors, registry and size checks pass; e2e-ui 81 specs pass in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit (new: navigation, density); axe sweep found one regression (contrast Wizard step at 4.09:1 with a warm brand), fixed by darkening the fill.

author: sayfu11a
body:
## Что это

Замена неоновых эффектов на блоках намаза настоящим **liquid glass**: полупрозрачное стекло с кромкой-бликом, преломлением фона и пружинным растяжением к курсору.

Два новых файла (`glass.css`, `glass.js`) подготовлены отдельным агентом; здесь они подключены к проекту, а старый слой эффектов вычищен.

## Что сделано

- `glass.css`, `glass.js` в корне, подключены в `index.html` (стили — после `styles.css`, скрипт — после `app.js`)
- `sw.js`: файлы в `SHELL`, версия → `vp-tracker-v32`
- `vercel.json`: `glass.css glass.js` в `buildCommand`
- `BUILD_LABEL` → «сборка v32»

## Исправленные баги (без них эффект бы не работал)

1. **Дубль `id="namazDrop"`** — он висел и на слое капли, и на `<filter>`. `getElementById` возвращал слой, фильтр не находился никогда. Это и была причина, почему преломление не запускалось в прошлых версиях. Оба узла удалены.
2. **`is-lit` ставили два обработчика** — `app.js` и `glass.js` на `mouseleave` гасили класс друг друга, стекло не включалось. Теперь класс ведёт только `glass.js`, в `app.js` осталась лишь позиция блика (`--mx`/`--my`).
3. **Конфликт `transform`** — старый `scale(1.06)` из `styles.css` дрался с `--sx`/`--sy`. Удалён вместе с блоком неона.
4. **Мёртвая разметка** — из `index.html` убраны `namaz-drop`, `namaz-glow-layer`, `lens-defs`.

## Удалено

- неон, волны по краю, лучи и свет по странице, капля-лупа
- `app.js`: `-242` строки неиспользуемого кода (генераторы SVG-волн, слой свечения, модуль капли)
- `styles.css`: `-208` строк
- `lens-map.png` (91 КБ) — `glass.js` строит карту смещений в рантайме

## Тесты

jsdom-прогон, 17/17: обе вкладки, 4 намаз-блока, каркас дня 09:00–23:00 без дыр и наложений, `glass.js` без ошибок, стекло включается/выключается, `--sy` = 1.3, переменные очищаются, клик ставит отметку, ошибок JS нет. Синтаксис всех JS и `vercel.json` проверен.

## Ограничения

- Преломление (`backdrop-filter` + SVG-фильтр) работает **только в Chromium** (Chrome, Edge). В Safari и Firefox остаются размытие, блики и растяжение — там `backdrop-filter` с SVG-фильтром не поддерживается.
- Крутилки эффекта — в начале `glass.js`: `BASE_SY` (растяжение по высоте), `K`/`DAMP` (жёсткость и «желе»), `BEZEL` (ширина линзы).

## Как проверить

1. Vercel Preview этой ветки → вкладка «День» → «Каркас дня».
2. Навести мышь на золотой блок намаза: он должен плавно набухнуть, стекло — дать преломление текста соседних строк (в Chrome).
3. Проверить на телефоне касанием и удержанием; при системном «уменьшить движение» — только статичное стекло.
4. Клик по блоку по-прежнему ставит отметку намаза.

---

**Подробный отчёт по аудиту безопасности и производительности** (RLS, XSS, дубли пушей, точность расписания намаза) — в предыдущем сообщении; правки по нему в этот PR не входят.

author: teamleaderleo
body:
Leo, 2026-11-07, on his own 515-character message showing as "Pasted text · 515 characters", folded, as a card inside the bubble:

> Also, like, okay, this is not good. Like, it says pasted text, but this is just the normal text that I had. And it's also got, like, you know, these two... what? Two card? Like, this is not good. You don't want to show it as pasted text when it wasn't pasted text in the first place. This is a misattribution. And it's also, like, fundamentally, this is not that long to, like, necessitate the sort of folding.

Then:

> Like, sometimes this isn't interesting to attribute, but a lot of the time, I feel like you only necessarily care if it's too big, or, like, yeah, a slightly oversized bit. [...] you can either just paste it and it just becomes this, like, .txt, kind of like an attachment, um, or you can just make it raw.

Leo, 2026-11-07, again on a 707-character message that showed as "Pasted text · 707 characters":

> And also, like, we do not want to have this card thing going on, this double card thing. [...] we don't want to show it as pasted text. We want to show the actual characters. We don't want to limit this that hard.

This PR covers that case end to end: the bubble draws an ordinary-size pasted range as plain text whatever its record says, so a message already recorded as pasted shows plain too. No renderer path decides "pasted" by itself: the only sources are the composer's `_meta.cmux.pasted` blocks and the placed `pasted` parts it records.

## Root cause

A regression from #37191:

- `webviews/src/agent-session/acpmux/composer/pasteMarks.ts:23-26` (base ae00bf6e). `marksPaste` marked any paste of 200 or more characters (`MARKED_PASTE_CHARS`, line 17), or of more than one line, as pasted.
- A clipboard paste event reaches that through this path:
  - the MarkdownField paste handlers;
  - `ComposerBox.tsx:348` `pastedChips.take`;
  - `composer/pastedChips.ts:107` `remember`.
- At send, `Composer.tsx:1589` `markPastes` turns the remembered paste into its own `_meta.cmux.pasted` block.
- `conversation/PromptText.tsx:64` (`promptParts`, then `<PasteChip>` at :204) draws every pasted range as a folded "Pasted text · N characters" card nested inside the bubble. `conversation/InlinePromptContent.tsx:101-108` does the same for the placed `pasted` parts.

cmux's own dictation never takes this path: it splices text in with `writeText` (`dictation.ts:175`, `MarkdownField.tsx:1390`), not a paste. So Leo's text most likely came in as a clipboard paste, for example from a dictation app that pastes its result. I have not confirmed which app it was. The fix gives the right result whatever the source.

## What changes

- **Only agent output or an oversized paste is marked.** `marksPaste` now marks a paste only if it reads as another agent's output (`agentText.ts`: a "From" header, a Trace-ID line, a generated-with footer, a review receipt) or is past the chip's size (`pastedText.ts` `isLargePaste`: more than 750 words or 10,000 characters, the limit settled in #31226). An ordinary paste is the person's text again, whatever its length or line count. Dictation, typing, IME commits and programmatic inserts were never paste events and are still never marked.
- **The sent bubble is #37675's.** #37675 (ask-792a64a12f) landed first and already draws every sent paste as the bubble's own text, under the prompt's one twenty-line fold, with no card inside the bubble (the `sent-paste-look` experiment, default `text`). It answers the same words from Leo. This PR keeps that whole. I dropped my parallel bubble change at the base merge: a thirty-line fold, a fold for oversized pastes only, and the `pasted-block-look` experiment with its gallery entry.
- **The composer offers both choices for an oversized paste.** The chip already expanded to text when clicked ("Edit in Prompt"). It now also has a visible **Keep as .txt** button, plus the same item in its right-click menu, which sends the paste as a `Pasted text.txt` file attachment instead. This works in both the inline view and the strip view. The new string `composer.pastedText.keepFile` is translated in all 21 locales.

- **Keep as .txt follow-ups.** The inline chip's right-click menu has Keep as .txt too. The kept file takes the chip's place, not the caret's, and any selected text stays. Undo brings the chip back with its whole paste. `marksPaste` measures the paste's size before trimming, as the chip does.

## How an agent still sees a pasted handoff as not the person's

When the person pastes another agent's output, `readsAsAgent` recognizes it and the composer still sends it as its own `_meta.cmux.pasted` block. acpmux records it as a pasted range, and #37190's `prompt_attribution` wraps it for the agent as "[Pasted by the person, not their own words …]". acpmux also flags typed text that reads as agent output (`agentText`). The bubble draws a marked paste as the prompt's own text (#37675); the agent sees the same attribution as before.

## Design inputs

This lane VM has no `design/<surface>.md` spec for the transcript bubble and no checkout of the design references. The variants follow the bubble's existing surface rules in `conversation.css`.

## Tests

The commands, run from `webviews/`:

```
bun test src/agent-session/acpmux/composer/pasteMarks.test.tsx test/composer-paste-text.test.tsx test/composer-paste-again.test.tsx test/user-bubble-inline-parts.test.tsx test/user-prompt-collapse.test.tsx
```

New tests:

- **A dictated insert is not a paste.** `writeText` of agent-looking text sends no pasted block (`composer-paste-text`).
- **A short real paste stays inline.** Leo's 515-character text, pasted, sends as plain text with no chip (`composer-paste-text`).
- **An oversized paste offers both choices, and each works**, in the inline and strip views (`composer-paste-text`):
  - clicking the card expands it into the prompt's text (the existing test);
  - Keep as .txt makes it a `Pasted text.txt` file attachment and leaves the prompt empty.
- `marksPaste("one\ntwo")` and a 515-character paste are now false; a paste over 750 words is true.
- **Leo's 707-character message.** A 707-character dictated message with no paste event renders as plain text, with no label and no card (`pasteMarks.test`), and goes as typed text from the composer (`composer-paste-text`).
- **Keep as .txt with text selected** keeps that text, and undo brings the chip back whole, in both views (`composer-paste-text`). It fails without the fix in `inlineAttachments.tsx` and passes with it.
- **Keep as .txt places the file where its chip was**, not at the caret (`composer-paste-text`).

The bubble's tests and galleries are #37675's, unchanged.

### Observed / Not run

- Observed (at the base merge d519a38b):
  - 1607 of 1608 tests in the paste, bubble, composer and row-estimate files pass. The one red, `rowEstimates` "a 2,300-line paste drawn as text is estimated at the prompt's fold", fails only when run with other files, and fails the same way on base;
  - `bun run check` passes;
  - `prepush-gate.py` reports no new violations.
- Not run: a nightly capture of Leo's message. I will read that back after this lands.

author: derek-x-wang
body:
Part of #251 (Plan B slice 5, part a). Slice 4 was #410 and #411. ## Spirit Today every run uses fixed clock bounds: 2 ms between the frontend and control, and 3 ms between the frontend and a worker. Plan B replaces them with bounds measured before the calls start. This PR adds the selector that computes those bounds from chrony's tracking log, and a receipt that records the inputs and the result. Nothing uses the receipt yet. Gates, judge input and verdicts are unchanged. Later parts wire it into the rehearsal (5c) and then make the gates and judge enforce it (5b). ## Technical details ```mermaid flowchart LR A[chrony tracking rows
per server host] --> S[clock-select] F[falsification probe records] --> S P[policy: f, s, A, K, ceilings] --> S S -->|admitted| R[receipt + evidence digest] S -->|any doubt| X[refuse, never clip] ``` - **Formula:** `H(M) = ceil_ns(max(f, s·M) + A)`, `B_control = H(M_frontend) + H(M_control)`, `B_worker = H(M_frontend) + H(max(M_w1, M_w2)) + K`. `M` is the largest column-14 error over the admission window. Exact rational arithmetic is used, and each host term rounds up before the sum. - **Printed rounding:** chrony prints column 14 to four significant digits, so each value is padded by half a printed unit. - **Admission:** the trailing window must be at least 120 s long, with at least 10 distinct chrony updates per server slot. It must have no gap over 60 s and normal leap status on every row. It must have no step, restart or source change, and no falsification. Frontend and control slots come from the inventory. Any break, leap or reference change after the window start also refuses, as do an expired lease and tracking more than 60 s old. - **Receipt:** run ID, admission window, slot mapping, per-slot counts and `M`, leap mode, policy, selected bounds, drift (100 ppm) and the SHA-256 of the evidence. The same inputs always give the same bytes. - **Lease data (host reader, opt-in):** the error at report time, `|offset| + RootDelay/2 + RootDispersion` with a 2 ns print pad, plus the dispersion growth rate from two reads. The recorded age is host-only; 5b adds transport time before leases refuse anything. ## Evidence | Status | Check | Result | | --- | --- | --- | | `VERIFIED` | `go run ./scripts/ci/gate-mutation` | 349 mutants KILLED, 0 INVALID. New mutants include inward rounding, clipping to the ceiling, latest-sample-only `M`, duplicate updates, ignored worker 2, wrong slot, missing frontend, K omitted or doubled, mixed leap mode, missing print pad, a post-window break, and control hard-coded to `shared` | | `VERIFIED` | Judge neutrality | The report and judge input stay byte-identical with lease data present; both pinned-release comparisons (a0d9744, 85e1043) pass | | `VERIFIED` | Race tests for touched packages, Python host tests, vet, gofmt, rules, lint | 362 tests and 1,582 subtests pass; 53 Python tests pass; lint reports 0 issues | | `VERIFIED` | `make check` on the host (final tree) | exit 0; lint 0 issues; judge-src passed in 551 s | | `VERIFIED` | Independent cross-model review (R2) | Design review: APPROVE WITH CHANGES, all findings taken. Code review: APPROVE WITH CHANGES; targeted re-review: APPROVE | | `NOT-RUN` | Live rehearsal with selected bounds | Needs the probe helpers in 5c; this PR's rehearsal only confirms nothing else changed | https://claude.ai/code/session_016k5kTaqcQwQ8ESojRPbFxX

author: sherzoddadoboev
body:
## Что изменилось
- **Значки у покупателя.** Знак надёжности и тариф видны в кабинете покупателя (боковое меню и заголовок главной, хук `useBuyerMarks`). У поставщика значки показываются рядом с покупателем: в заявке, в сделке, в списке заказчиков и в профиле заказчика. Общий помощник `profileMarks` работает для профиля любой роли.
- **Знак из API — окончательный.** `pickReputationTier` больше не пересчитывает `"none"` от сервера по локальной статистике: сервер учитывает обе роли и решение админа. Локальный подсчёт остаётся только для демо-данных без API.
- **Чёткие маленькие значки.** До 24 px знаки и тарифы рисуются упрощённой версией на сетке 20×20 (`components/bm/small-marks.tsx`): плотные заливки, линии не тоньше 0.9, без размытия и свечения. У маленького алмаза остаются буква B и световой блик. В `CompanyName` теперь целые размеры: sm 18/16, md 20/18.
- **SVG-файлы.** Все значки лежат в `public/icons/marks/` (17 файлов): знаки, тарифы и значок «проверено», каждый в большой и маленькой версии. Файлы генерируются из тех же компонентов командой `npm run icons:export`.
- **Админка** показывает, на каких профилях виден знак.
- **Подсказка тарифа** подходит к обоим профилям: «платная подписка и продвижение на площадке, не знак надёжности».

## Проверка
- `npm test`: 58 тестов. Новые: маленькие значки без фильтров и тонких линий в размерах 16–24; значение знака из API, включая `"none"`, не пересчитывается.
- `tsc --noEmit`, `next build`: без ошибок.
- В браузере, локально, на тестовом аккаунте с двумя компаниями: золото и «Бизнес» видны в кабинетах покупателя и поставщика. Маленькие значки я рассмотрел попиксельно на 16, 18, 20 и 24 px: всё читается.

body:
A caller's LoRA view used to re-read the base model from disk on its first call, though the same bytes were already on the GPU. This PR makes a weight fill copy them from where they already are instead.

**Stacked on #2568** (the 0.21.2 batch, `claude/xs138-0212`). This PR's code is 506874c07, 98c555090 and 83adb27ca; once #2568 merges, the diff is just these three. The tree also equals 83adb27ca: a follow-up, a9b8fd768 and bbeb01ba2, was reverted in 0e21aa08f (see below).

- **Content-addressed fill.** Every Source indexes its stored object ranges by object, offset and length on the GPU's tier. A fill takes each range from another Source holding the stored bytes: its ready Region on this GPU first (one D2D copy, `io::COMPLETE`, so it never waits on compute), then its kept host page (pinned H2D, one window at a time), then the store. Each origin is its own fill row: `resident`, `host`, `store`. A fill that finds no other Source reads exactly as before.
- **Why the LoRA case needed it.** A caller's LoRA view is the base's own chunks renamed, so its first fill used to read the whole DiT from the store before the bake, though the base was on the card (Klein base: 9.98 GB at 4.4 GB/s).
- **`varena::Region::try_pin_unused`.** Pinning a donor no longer counts as a use of it. A donated base block keeps its reclaim order, so the view's next block evicts blocks already copied rather than its next donor.
- **DoRA.** The bake and DoRA paths are untouched; they run on the copied bytes.

## Proof
Every run was on an RTX 4090 rental (`rtx-4090`), int8 lane, default home, TensorD d7174d600. Old is the 0.21.2 batch (TensorFS d7174d600, Runtime 936422609); new is this branch (TensorFS 98c555090, Runtime bfecf445a). Peak VRAM is the driver's peak.

Pod pingu (local NVMe), Klein base `generate`, 28 steps, 1 MP:

| run (old → new) | case | total ms | step 1 ms | steady ms | peak | fills |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 42059 → 42064 | no LoRA | 9196 → 8576 | 300 → 302 | 285 → 285 | 23.4 GiB | — |
| 42060 → 42065 | first LoRA (`akhaliq/angles`) | 12983 → 10771 | **2274 → 1278** | 285 → 285 | 23.42 → 23.42 GiB | store 9.98 GB at 4.4 GB/s → resident 9.90 GB at 104 GB/s + store 0.08 GB |
| 42061 → 42066 | first LoRA (`ausboss/consistency-klein`) | 13799 → 11196 | **2625 → 1485** | 285 → 285 | same | store 10.06 GB → resident 9.90 GB + store 0.16 GB |

Pod percival (slow small reads). Each step-1 cell reads no LoRA / LoRA old → new:

| model | runs | step 1 ms | steady ms | fills, new |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Klein base | 41969–41973 → 42006–42009 | 324 / 3838 → 3261 | 289 | resident 9.90 GB in 93 ms + store 0.08 GB in 2.0 s |
| Fibo Edit-Turbo, 2 steps | 41983–41986 → 42013–42015 | 1249 / 7340 → 6233 | 1162–1189 | resident 14.2 GB + host 1.0 GB + store 0.83 GB |
| qwen-image-2 Turbo | 41993–41998 → 42019–42022 | 352 / 4652 → 5314 | 243 → 163 | host 6.0 GB + resident 2.5 GB + store 7.9 GB |

- **qwen comparison:** confounded. The old phase streamed its weights (allocated 3 GB) and the new one held them (11 GB).
- **Kernels:** unchanged: `cozy-int8` GEMM, `kitchen-int8`/`sdpa` attention, LoRA `bake/fused`.
- **Byte identity:** 17 of 18 old/new same-request pairs are byte-identical, every baked-LoRA pair among them. The odd one, qwen's first no-LoRA run, used no donor. So the fill copies exactly the stored bytes.
- **Records:** `~/cozy_v2/outputs/lora-merge-at-bind/{runs,diag/runs}`. Both pods are ended and gone.

**Tried and reverted (0e21aa08f).** Two changes aimed at the remaining per-block factor reads, which take ~9–25 ms a block depending on the pod:
- page-cache read-ahead of a derive set's cold bytes (a varena worker `warm`, then a set-wide `POSIX_FADV_WILLNEED`);
- demand reads taking local chunks first.

Neither beat noise on pod dera (runs 42138–42160: old / new / old, page cache evicted before each cold run):

| step 1 ms | old | new | old again |
|---|---|---|---|
| Klein first LoRA, angles | 2618 | 2117 | 2220 |
| Klein first LoRA, consistency | 3781 | 3809 | 3259 |
| Fibo first LoRA | 4608 | 5027 | 5212 |

No-LoRA step 1 was unchanged throughout (Klein 330/330/333, Fibo 1301/1245/1278). The cost of each factor read is not the page cache; it stays open for later.

author: chloe4ai
body:
A code review confirmed that every README number reproduced from the code. It also found that three of the lab's claims came from how the simulation was built, not from what it measured. This PR fixes the measurement so its numbers can be trusted, and the README now says what each number does and does not show.

## What was wrong, and what changed

1. **The detector changed the ground truth it was scored against.** `run.py` drew a random number only when the detector found a link, so swapping in another detector shifted the random stream for every later answer. With a detector that finds nothing, the number of truly included answers went from 859 to 899 on the same seed. Agents and clicks now have separate seeded streams, and the click draw happens on every answer. A new test runs a null detector and checks that ground truth and clicks don't change; it fails on the old code.
2. **The "strict rules are a business decision" trade-off wasn't in the model.** Every spoofer had an unverified IP, so the IP rule caught all of them and the page-count rule caught none. The ~6% of genuine sessions rejected came only from the simulator putting 4% of them at exactly 7 pages. The model now has **relayed sessions**: scripted traffic run through a real assistant, so the IP checks out and only behaviour can catch it. Genuine sessions get a smooth long tail up to 20 pages. A threshold sweep from 3 to 20 pages is added to `results.json`, the dashboard and the README, so the trade-off is measured rather than asserted.
3. **The 100% precision was guaranteed by construction, and the README now says so next to the headline.** A held-out set (`fixtures/heldout.json`, 21 disclosure answers and 10 claim paraphrases) scores the detector on wording it was not written for. The detector was **not** tuned to fit it. Results: disclosure precision 50%, recall 28.6%; claim paraphrases precision 100%, recall 50%.
4. **Single-seed point values.** A seeds 1–20 readout (min / median / max) is added for the overcount, recall, billable vs truth, and per-agent rates. It shows that click rates are too noisy to rank agents on, and the README now says that.
5. **Crashes.** `--n 0` raised ZeroDivisionError and is now an argparse error. A run with nothing delivered and labeled raised TypeError; it now reports the overcount as undefined, and the dashboard shows "n/a".
6. **The README names the overcount's denominator:** fetches ÷ answers detected as included and labeled.

## Headline numbers, old → new

| Figure | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Funnel | 2,400 → 855 → 637 → 32 | 2,400 → 891 → 685 → 24 |
| Overcount if billed on fetch | 3.8× | **3.5×** (seeds 1–20: 3.4× to 3.9×, median 3.6×) |
| Inclusion detector | precision 100%, recall 99.5% | precision 100% (by construction), recall 99.1% |
| Billable share of user-token fetches | 23.4% | 19.5% |
| Default 5-page rule | "catches every spoofer", ~6% genuine rejected, −15% vs truth | 4.8% genuine rejected, 39 invalid page fetches billed, −12.6% vs truth |

One claim was softened: the summarizing agent kept its label in 50.4% of answers in this run, so "drops the label more than half the time" is now "about half the time (37–54% across seeds)".

## CI
Before deploying, the Pages workflow regenerates `results.json` and `index.html` and fails if they differ from the committed files. A new test checks the README's headline numbers against `results.json`. Output is identical on Python 3.11, 3.12 and 3.13.

## Testing
- `pytest`: **22 passed** (was 14).
- `python -m lab.run` reproduces the committed `docs/results.json` byte for byte; re-checked independently after the agent's run.

## Not in this PR
- Precision and recall still show 0% when there are no detections (the dashboard's formatting needs a number there).
- The README test checks the headline numbers but not every row of the sweep table; the CI regeneration check keeps `results.json` itself current.
