author: tire-fire
body:
## Summary

Text that falls below WCAG AA contrast, pages that scroll sideways on a phone, and two components that leave screen reader users guessing, fixed across the portal, with browser tests that check every page for the first two.

- **Contrast.** In light mode the nav sat on Django's light `--primary` (#79aec8): its white links, user name and focus outline read at 2.4:1 on every page. It now uses the darker panel dark mode already had, in both themes, and the current section takes the header's color. The success, info and neutral status colors (badges, info alerts, positive scores) read at 3.7 to 4.2:1 and are now 4.5:1 or more in both themes. The open ticket count keeps its light red in dark mode (white on dark mode's red was 3.5:1). The Django admin's incident status, inject percentage and service net score columns used hard-coded colors (an orange "Pending" at 2:1, a black net score of 0 invisible in dark mode); they use the portal's badge and score classes, and the net score takes its class from `core.status_variants.score_class`, the function `c-score_value` now uses too.
- **Phone width.** 27 page renders were wider than a 390px phone. The breadcrumb bar's fixed 40px bleed now follows Django's 40/20/15px `#content` padding (it also overflowed at tablet widths), grid columns shrink to the screen, selects and textareas stay inside their column (outranking `responsive.css`'s phone rule that lifts a textarea's cap), and the orange check rubric rows, the competition schedule's time zone pickers and the ticket attachment form wrap.
- **Screen readers.** A sorted column's header carries `aria-sort`, and the stylesheet draws its arrow from that attribute (in the text it was read as "black up-pointing triangle"). A streamed operation's step text is a polite live region, so each step is announced, and the progress bar has a name.
- **Headings.** The school import and event detail pages skipped from h1 straight to h3. The upload step and the enrollments section now have h2 module titles.
- **Scores.** `c-score_value` showed a score rounded to a whole number but chose its color and plus sign from the value read as a whole number: a fraction passed as text counted as zero, and a Decimal passed with `:value` was cut toward zero, so 0.6 showed as a grey 1 with no plus sign. The component now formats the value once and takes its class and plus from the text it shows, as the admin's net score column does from its two places, through `score_class`, which reads the sign of that text as Django wrote it (thousand separators included); a value that isn't a finite number takes the zero class instead of failing the page.
- **Touch targets.** On a phone, Django admin's breadcrumbs wrapped onto lines too close together to tap apart and the Competition page's close-out lists stacked their links with no gap (WCAG 2.5.8): breadcrumb lines are 24px tall and the close-out items 8px apart.
- **Admin inline labels.** The Django admin's tabular inlines (orange check criteria, assignment results, ticket attachments and comments, registration contacts and enrollments, and the rest) laid fields out under column headings with no label of their own, so a screen reader announced an unnamed field. Every inline builds on `PortalTabularInline`, whose formset gives each field, the delete box and a foreign key's select included, its field label (its column's heading) as its `aria-label`.
- **Typography.** Module and fieldset titles get 12px of padding beside their 18px text (Django's 8px; 12px is the changelist cells' padding), help and intro paragraphs stop at about 75 characters a line (60ch) instead of 165 to 200 (but for Django's full-width paginator and error-note bars) and don't strand a last word, `small` text is at least 12px at the default text size instead of the browser's under-11px, and the registration page's rules agreement is a plain row rather than a box inside its section's box.
- **Cleanup.** The match incident panels' `.module-header` styles never applied (Django's `.module h2` outranks them) and are removed; the panels look as they do today. The new ticket toast's transitions name the opacity and transform they animate instead of `all`.

## Tests

- `browser_tests/test_contrast.py` renders every page the view property rows reach (each as the first staff role that gets it, plus a blue team and a signed-out visitor where they get it), in the light and dark theme, and fails on any text below WCAG AA contrast.
- `browser_tests/test_phone.py` renders the same pages at 390px and fails on any that scrolls sideways, naming what reaches past the edge, and on any control under 24px whose 24px circle reaches another control (WCAG 2.5.8, which exempts a link in a line of text and the browser's own unstyled checkbox; the test also skips the new ticket toast, which shows for a few seconds over whatever has scrolled beneath it).
- Both fail on a page that answers an error or lands elsewhere (the sign-in) rather than checking it.
- `browser_tests/test_every_page_renders.py` (not a browser test, so it runs in CI) fails on a page no role gets as HTML unless `every_page.UNRENDERED` says why (a download, a redirect), so a page can't drop out of the walk unseen.
- Run against main without these fixes, the contrast test fails on the nav, the status badges, the ticket count and the admin columns, and the phone test on all 27 page renders.
- `core/tests/test_view_regressions.py` fails on a tabular inline not built on `PortalTabularInline`, and checks on real change pages that an inline row's fields, its delete box and a first row's foreign key select are named.
- `core/tests/test_screen_reader_components.py` pins the sort and progress announcements; `core/tests/test_status_variants.py` and `scoring/tests/test_score_value_component.py` pin a score's class to the value shown.

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest -m "not browser"`: 5081 passed
- [x] `pytest -m browser -n0`: 127 passed (the two browser tests above take about 5 minutes together)
- [x] ruff, djlint, mypy
- [x] Screenshots at 1280 (light and dark), 900 and 390 of the nav, badges, the fixed phone layouts, the heading bars and the admin columns

author: ceomatheusdev
body:
## Why this cycle

Window + swapchain was re-checked and is **still blocked** here (no `/usr/include/X11`, no `libX11.so` dev symlink, no `pkg-config`, no `Xvfb`, `DISPLAY`/`WAYLAND_DISPLAY` empty) — not attempted. Of the two headless-verifiable candidates recorded last cycle, the **rasterizer filtering gap** was taken: extraction's `by_material` already sorts, so batching there would be a benchmark-driven change with no contract gain, while the filtering gap is a documented *quality* limitation with a measurable claim.

## The defect

`textureLod` takes `max()` of the four gradient components, so the level follows the pixel footprint's **long** axis and over-blurs the short one. A floor receding to the horizon loses detail it could still resolve — the docs said so plainly ("no anisotropic filtering … over-blurs grazing angles"). This cycle turns that limitation into a mode.

## What changed

- **`raster.Mipmap.anisotropic`** (opt-in; `.trilinear` stays the default):
  - The footprint is the Jacobian's two screen-axis **columns**; the longer one is the long axis, and the ratio of their lengths is the anisotropy.
  - `samples = ceil(clamp(aniso, 1, 8))`, `lod_minor = max(lod_major − log2(aniso), 0)`; taps sit at `(i − (n−1)/2)/n` pixels along the unit long axis, each a trilinear sample at `lod_minor`, averaged with **one final round**.
  - A **round footprint is bit-identical to trilinear** and costs nothing; a constant denominator hoists the entire tap pattern to once per triangle (`GradSteps.constantAniso`); ratio, tap count and correction all **clamp at 8:1**.
- **Contract:** `Tier::capabilities.anisotropic` (Medium, Advanced; Low has no textures) and `pipeline.resolve` coerces the mode to `.trilinear` where the tier lacks it — a quality loss at grazing angles, never a rejected frame.

## Validation

- **741/741** tests (was 734), `zig fmt --check src tools build.zig` clean, `zig build` OK.
- The Python reference reimplements the footprint, taps and averaging independently: **17 new anisotropic cases** (grazing, the 8:1 clamp, a symmetric case that must equal the trilinear frame bit for bit, mild 2:1, a smaller base, perspective, ten deterministic random grazing triangles) take the texture corpus to **97 frames / 1390 covered pixels**, all bit-exact. Generator reproducible.
- Unit tests pin the footprint decisions, one-tap equivalence to trilinear, tap averaging, and — measured, not asserted — a grazing quad rendered both ways where the anisotropic frame keeps **more than twice** the neighbouring-pixel detail.

## Cost (ReleaseFast, best of five, 1024 quads, x86-64)

| Target | trilinear (round) | aniso (round) | trilinear (grazing) | aniso (grazing) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 256² | 2.530 ms | 2.607 ms | 2.708 ms | 11.691 ms (~4.3×) |
| 512² | 9.492 ms | 9.627 ms | 10.284 ms | 46.016 ms (~4.5×) |
| 1024² | 36.752 ms | 36.427 ms | 36.961 ms | 180.490 ms (~4.9×) |

Free when the footprint is round, ~5x at a full 8:1 grazing footprint — hence opt-in, with `.trilinear` unchanged as the default.

## Bugs found in my own first attempt (fixed, recorded)

1. The long axis was taken unconditionally from the x column, so a vertically elongated footprint reported **one** tap; the unit test that caught it stays.
2. A fixture declared `1x2` below `2x2`, which `Texture.validate` correctly rejected — the fixture was wrong, not the validator.
3. A stale `.zig-cache` binary briefly reported 734 tests; the counts above come from a clean build.

## Limitations

Taps are uniformly spaced and equally weighted (not Gaussian); no per-material LOD bias or tap cap; the sub-pixel offset near a triangle edge can tap half a pixel past the footprint. No sRGB, no wrap modes beyond repeat, still no GPU backend.

**Next priority:** window + swapchain + vsync where a display and its dev headers exist. Otherwise **per-material LOD bias and tap cap** (threaded from `Renderable` through extraction into `drawMeshAlloc`), or occlusion culling / batching in extraction.

author: dbstkddl8-create
body:
Component ID: `evm`. Target: Linux x86-64 node #115 `artifacts/node/115/hl-node`, SHA-256
`a6e2897cd051213d004802deca416e8eca62b7a8278fa39f249e98c3867b5301`. Base: main `7ff06a0973b5b8c79bde0b229c9bb2eabf8b29a6`.

## Problem

Node #115 serializes its EVM transaction bodies (Legacy, EIP-2930, EIP-1559, EIP-4844, EIP-7702), the block header
and a destination-call record with rmp-serde, and nothing in the repository says how. The open questions were the
field order, the names, the struct offsets, which nested serializer each field uses, when optional fields are
skipped, what the map/array header count is, and what error a failing field returns. Without that, a
reconstruction cannot produce these MessagePack bytes. This packet rebuilds all 15 bodies as an executable model
and proves the model against the original bytes.

## Evidence

- 15 bodies, all FDE-bounded (`tools/fde_extents.py`):
  - two copy families of the destination-call, Legacy, EIP-2930, EIP-1559, EIP-4844 and EIP-7702 serializers:
    0x22f2a20/0x44dad80, 0x2331bf0/0x44ec9f0, 0x2332eb0/0x44ed9b0, 0x2332430/0x44ed300, 0x2333150/0x44ee450,
    0x2333c30/0x44eeb50;
  - the block header 0x22daf00;
  - the two inline-Vec destination-call copies 0x22f2c20/0x44da780.
  - None of these addresses appears in `research/work-items`, in any open or merged PR, or in our pending drafts.
- Serializer byte +0xb: `!= 0` selects the map header writer, `== 1` writes the field names. So flags 2..255 give
  a map header with no names.
- Error and Ok shapes: a writer error becomes `(0x8000000000000000, w0, w1)`. A nested-serializer error is copied
  whole. Ok writes only word 0 = `0x8000000000000004`.
- Legacy chainId: header count is `7 - (w0 == 0)` (`cmpq $1; sbb`), and the field is skipped when w0 is 0.
- Block header count is `16 - (w0 == 0) + b[0x27c] + lo32(w[0x10]) + lo32(w[0x20]) + b[0x29d] + b[0x2be] + b[0x2df] + lo32(w[0x30])`,
  using the RAW tags. Presence uses `!= 0` and `== 1`, so non-canonical tags make the two disagree.
- The names come from the binary's own texts, including the block header's optional fields: withdrawalsRoot,
  parentBeaconBlockRoot, requestsHash, blockAccessListHash.
- Inline-Vec copies: header byte `((flag ^ 1) << 4) | 0x85` in an 8-bit register (flag 2 → 0xb5). Names are
  pushed as a fixstr marker plus bytes. Reserve is called when `cap == len` for a 1-byte push, and when spare room
  is below the name length for a name.
- Every number in the evidence files comes from Python reading ELF bytes. No binutils are used.

## Inferences

- Role names (u64, u128, b256, b160, TxKind, access list, `if_*` header fields) and the struct type names come
  from the adjacent field names, the header counts and the name sets, not from symbols.
- The optional block header tags are `Option<[u8; 32]>` (four tag bytes 0x21 apart).

## Reproduce

```
python3 tools/evm_tx_rmp_structs_115.py --out research/work-items/evm-tx-rmp-struct-serializers-115
python3 -m unittest tests.test_evm_tx_rmp_structs_115
```

## Tests

- 15,000 cases (1,000 per body), 0 mismatches.
- 2,570/2,570 body instructions reached.
- 96/96 negative controls detected: 23 model mutants and 73 single-byte flips of the original code.
- 29/29 unit tests, 0 skips. They include out-of-range and corrupt-input refusals: a corrupted binary digest, a
  non-FDE body address, a wrong-family callee, a misspelled name, a wrong header count, a wrong tag offset, a
  result slot off the stack, and a reserve call outside its contract.
- Two regenerations, one with `PYTHONHASHSEED=12345 TZ=Asia/Kolkata PATH=/nonexistent`, are byte-identical.
- `python3 tools/artifacts.py verify` and `python3 tools/catalogue.py --check` pass.
- Packet size: 6,744 lines. Tool and tests are 2,370 lines; observed data is 61.5%.

## Limits

- Callees are recording contract stubs, so this proves struct-level behavior only. The nested serializers and leaf
  writers are separate work.
- No family-b copy of the block header was found.
- The inline-Vec block header 0x22da880 is not covered.
- No progress gate is requested.

## Next question

The inline-Vec block header 0x22da880 (375 instructions): does it also count raw tags, and how does it write a
header count above 15? After that, the stubbed nested serializers 0x29fe9c0, 0x2968180, 0x26e5610 and 0x233a0e0.

## Checks run (offline sandbox, no network): steps covering the `make verify test catalogue-check` gates

- Existing tests with this PR's files (every module that references the catalogue — the tests that read the full packet list — except a few long-running ones; one process): 23 tests run, OK after the exclusions listed below (if any)
- This PR's test files with no binutils on PATH and no skips: 29 tests, OK; also run before the sample in the same process: OK
- With this PR's files: `python3 tools/artifacts.py verify`, `python3 tools/verify_imports.py`, `python3 tools/catalogue.py --check`: pass
- `python3 tools/<tool>.py --out <dir>` twice (different PYTHONHASHSEED and TZ, no objdump/readelf on PATH): both runs identical and every generated evidence file byte-identical to the committed packet; `sha256sum -c MANIFEST.sha256`: pass

author: rywible
body:
Brings the sailing work on the opening scene (scenes/opening) to main, so the skiff, water and sky streams all start from the same base.

## What changes
- **Sail skiff**
  - Junk lug sail by default (`main::SAIL = 1`), the option Ryan chose.
  - The sail stays on its own side and never swings across.
  - Cloth motion is driven by the wind on the sail, and the old mast whips.
  - The rider moves, steps, shifts weight and looks around.
  - Keys: W sheets in, S lets the sail fly, A and D steer. The title page's menu text is updated to match.
- **Hull**
  - An old clinker-built planing hull: worn paint, a tin patch, deck planks, a crate and a rope coil.
  - It sits in the water instead of on it.
  - It banks and presses down into turns.
  - A wet band runs along the waterline.
  - It is held off sea stacks, so it can't sail into rock.
- **Wake**
  - A churned trail astern, broken V arms and froth at the stem, drawn with the same foam treatment as the sea's whitecaps.
  - Drifting kelp and driftwood are removed.
- **Sea stacks and far islands** (from the landmarks thread), so speed reads:
  - Craggy bedded stone, with surf collars at their feet.
  - Shimmer and see-through fixes.
- **Weather**
  - The far-sea haze no longer draws a ruled line across the sail at the horizon.
- **Wind**
  - `SEA.wind` is rotated to a broad reach. This re-aims the ocean and the weather on the live title page.
- `row.wrela` is replaced by `sail.wrela` (`sail::key` matches `row::key`). A stand-in rider is added in `hero.wrela`, and scripted clips in `clips.wrela`.

## Checks
- `wrela build scenes/opening` and `wrela check scenes/opening`: no errors.
- `wrela test scenes/opening`: 3 passed, 0 failed.
- An independent review found nothing that crashes or breaks input. Its one medium issue (sailing into a stack) is fixed. Two low-severity items are left for a later cleanup: a `jolt` field no other code sets, and an unreachable arch island in far.wrela.
- Renders were checked by independent critics: jitter verdict clean, sail never flips, grounding up from 4/10 to 6/10.

Merging deploys to production. Please wait for Ryan's OK.

body:
Public binder share links now show the owner's real, page-turning binder. Clicking a card pops it into a top loader in an overlay over the binder, with the card's title below it. Ticket: NEO-444.

## What changed
- **Real binder for visitors:** `PublicBinderPage` draws the same binder as the owner's screen, read-only. Page-turn keys, swipes and turn buttons work; `?page=N` and `?card=<key>` are shareable, and `?card=` wins.
- **Top loader overlay:** new `PublicCardOverlay` and `TopLoader`, with title, details, See the back/front and See it full size. The card sits in a penny sleeve inside the loader. The back photo is preloaded so the flip never shows an empty loader.
- **Loading:** every copy is loaded with a "Sleeving N of M cards…" line, and neighbouring steps are preloaded.
- **Shared pieces:** `Overlay` gained a `stage` variant and focus trap fixes. `useOverflows` is a new shared hook. `CardPicture` is keyed on `thumbUrl`.
- **Privacy fix:** `upForTrade` is now dropped from the public payload when `tradePrivate` is on, for both `binderCopies` and `forSale`. This was an existing leak and is the only Convex change.

## Testing
- `public-share-link` extended and passing locally on `e2e` and `e2e-mobile` before the final merges of main; the mobile run had no fresh re-seed.
- On the merged branch: lint, typecheck, build and `test:e2e:typecheck` exit 0; the 16 unit test files this PR touches pass (369 tests).

author: blacks1ne
body:
A regular node also sizes shards whose data it does not store: their local row is a nominal size (4096 bytes per committed output) with zero data shards. `merged_shard_metrics` let every local row replace the archive row, so such shards read zero data shards: the reward-greedy filter dropped them as join candidates and the world byte total shrank. Affected nodes held about half the seats of comparable nodes while free workers sat idle.

Let a local row override the archive row only when it has data shards; any local row still fills in a filter the archives did not report. Log one bounded line when free workers find no join candidate, with the count each filter dropped.

Tests: 3 new tests fail on `ae0be783` and pass with the fix; 5 mutation controls each fail their named test; the whole `provers::lifecycle` and `coverage` test modules pass (a leave-rejection fixture now seeds the archive row it means, since an empty local row no longer hides it); fmt, workspace check, warning census (0) and clippy on added lines (0) are clean.
Compat: L (local planner input only)
Rollout: seat counts on affected nodes match their siblings after adoption

body:
## Problème
Les RPC `increment_ai_generation_usage` et `increment_voice_memo_usage` écrivent `usage_tracking.updated_at`, mais cette colonne n'existait pas en production. Chaque appel échouait avec l'erreur `42703`, que `ai-proxy` et `voice-transcribe` ne vérifient pas, donc personne ne le voyait. Résultat : la table `usage_tracking` est restée vide et les quotas du plan gratuit (5 générations IA, 10 mémos vocaux par mois) ne se sont jamais appliqués. Les comptes gratuits utilisaient donc la clé Gemini du serveur sans aucune limite.

## Correctif
Migration `20261107120000_usage_tracking_updated_at.sql` : `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW()`. Elle peut être rejouée sans effet.

**Déjà appliquée en production** via Supabase.

## Vérification
- Avant : l'appel au RPC en tant qu'utilisateur authentifié renvoyait `column "updated_at" of relation "usage_tracking" does not exist`.
- Après, dans une transaction annulée : 2 mémos et 1 génération IA ont été comptés correctement (`voice_memos_count=2`, `ai_generations_count=1`). La table est restée vide après l'annulation.

author: ppaapp220022
body:
## 요약
PR #5 eval 결과를 바탕으로 의미 검색 임베딩 모델을 `text-embedding-3-small`로 바꾸고 유사도 기준값을 0.30으로 조정합니다. 작업 중 **새 판매글이 벡터 저장소에 저장되지 않던 문제**도 함께 고쳤습니다.

## 발견한 문제
- `PostServiceImpl`에 `PostVectorService`가 주입만 되어 있고 `savePostVector` 호출이 없음 → 5월 이후 새로 등록·수정한 글은 의미 검색 대상이 아님
- 관리자 재임베딩(`/api/admin/embed/posts`)은 문서 id를 `postId-N`으로 넣는데, PGVector id 컬럼이 UUID라 `UUID.fromString`에서 실패하고 예외를 무시함 → 사실상 0건 저장
- 그래서 운영 의미 검색은 예전에 저장된 일부 벡터만으로 동작하고 있었을 가능성이 큼

## 변경 내용
- `application.properties`: `spring.ai.openai.embedding.options.model=text-embedding-3-small` (기본 1536차원이라 PGVector 컬럼 그대로)
- `PostSearchService`: 기준값 0.7 → 0.30, 결과별 로그는 debug, 건수·최고 점수만 INFO (PR #5 리뷰 반영)
- `PostVectorService.savePostVector`
  - postId 기반 고정 UUID로 저장 → 다시 저장하면 덮어씀 (PGVector `ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE`). 지우지 않으므로 임베딩 실패 시 이전 벡터 유지
  - 메타데이터에 `embeddingModel` 기록 → `PostSearchService`는 현재 모델 벡터만 비교 (모델이 섞인 비교 없음)
  - 성공 여부를 boolean으로 반환, 팀명을 임베딩 텍스트에 포함, null 필드 방어
- `PostServiceImpl`: 등록(`addPost`)·수정(`modifyPost`) 뒤 `savePostVector` 호출. 실패해도 등록은 진행 (기존 설계대로 로그만)
- `PostEmbeddingAdminController`: 재임베딩이 같은 `savePostVector`를 쓰도록 통일, postId 순 페이지 조회, 마친 뒤 이전 모델·예전 무작위 id 벡터 SQL 삭제, 성공·실패·삭제 건수 반환
- 테스트: `PostVectorSearchTest` 6건 (PR #5 리뷰 반영), eval 기본 모델을 운영 설정에서 읽도록

## eval (운영 설정 그대로, 3회)
| | 통과율 | R@10 (hybrid) | MRR (hybrid) | 정답 없는 검색어 오탐 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 이전: ada-002 @0.70 | 0.66~0.69 | 0.821 | 0.705~0.734 | 160 |
| **이 PR: 3-small @0.30** | **0.81~0.84** | **0.82~0.86** | **0.78~0.84** | **12~21** |

남은 실패: 국대 유니폼·친필 사인(정답 유사도 0.26~0.28로 기준값 아래), 하늘색 축구 유니폼(18위), 골프 셔츠·노트북 오탐.

## ⚠️ 배포 후 필요한 작업
배포 직후 **관리자 계정으로 전체 재임베딩**을 한 번 실행해야 합니다.
```
POST /api/admin/embed/posts   (ADMIN 토큰 필요)
→ "임베딩 완료: N건, 실패: M건, 이전 모델 벡터 삭제: K건"
```
- 배포~재임베딩 사이: 검색이 현재 모델 벡터만 보므로 의미 검색 결과 0건, 키워드 검색만 동작 (엉뚱한 결과나 오류 없음)
- 재임베딩이 끝나면 이전 ada-002 벡터와 예전 무작위 id 벡터가 자동으로 삭제됨. 수동 SQL 필요 없음
- 실패 건수가 0이 아니면 백엔드 로그의 `savePostVector : 벡터 저장 실패`를 확인하고 다시 실행 (덮어쓰기라 여러 번 실행해도 안전)

## 테스트
- `PostVectorSearchTest` 7건 통과 (덮어쓰기·모델 필터·저장소 비활성 분기)
- 이전 모델 벡터 삭제 SQL과 PGVector 메타데이터 필터는 실제 PostgreSQL에서 확인하지 못함 (로컬 PG 접속 정보 없음). eval의 SimpleVectorStore에서는 같은 필터로 검색 확인
- `./gradlew test`: 108건 중 77건 실패 — main에서도 같은 77건 실패 (DB·Redis 연결 필요)
- eval 3회 (위 표)

author: stonefletcher
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"ProjektPayne"} -->
_Requested by **Alex**_

## Why
E: filled on 2026-11-07 (8.8 GB free) with about 240 GB of Fletchery worktrees. Storage cleanup had last run a day earlier and retired nothing out of 171 checkouts.

## What changes
- **Runs after every landed round**, alongside running workers. Before, it only ran with zero workers, which almost never happens. Rounds in progress still block it, and so does the PC heavy lease.
- **Finished tasks are no longer protected forever.** Every task checkout stays in `.task-checkouts.json` `active`, so 87 finished checkouts were skipped as "active". An active record now protects only while the issue is open. Retiring the checkout drops the record, so a reopened issue gets a fresh checkout. Preserved (failed-attempt) records still protect.
- **A merged PR head counts as published.** After the Nov 5 history rewrite, and once branches are deleted, merged task heads are no longer ancestors of Test-Staging (about 45 checkouts failed `merge-base`). A head equal to a merged PR's head from the task branch is now accepted, since GitHub keeps `refs/pull/<n>/head`.
- **Idle merge checkouts lose `Intermediate`, `Binaries` and `DerivedDataCache`**, which are 6–12 GB each. The active checkout, the round-progress checkout and any busy one keep theirs. Sources, `Saved` evidence and registrations stay. A receipt goes to `merge-trim.json`.
- Unreal build outputs (`Intermediate`, `Binaries`, `DerivedDataCache`, also under `Plugins/<name>/`) no longer count as "unique ignored files" that block retiring a finished checkout.
- `worktree_busy` now also matches Git Bash `/e/...` paths, case-insensitively. A `tail -f` on a round log was being missed.
- Batch limit is 25 instead of 10.

These stay the same: it never prunes, it removes only with `git worktree remove`, and a checkout must be clean, published, closed, unowned and lease-free.

## Proof
- `python -m unittest discover -p "test_*.py"` in `fletchery/`: 361 tests OK. New tests cover active-record retirement and forgetting, final-attempt retirement with the preserved first attempt kept, merged-PR-head proof, the build-output allowlist, merge trim (active, protected and busy kept; dry run), and the post-round schedule running with workers but not during a round.
- Dry run against the live PC: 45 finished task checkouts eligible (38.8 GiB), and the idle Round 28 checkout trim at 6.4 GiB. That checkout turned out to have a `tail -f` watcher, which led to the busy-check fix.

body:
## Summary

- Re-execute the captured native-state f64 C ABI baseline and joint QG17+BRS17 ±1e-3 endpoints with value-only captures at the `nracw`/`naacw` producer sites and both cloud-number limiter passes.
- Reproduce the selected B2 large/small-drop `nracw` formulas, rain gate and `NC/dt` cap; the C2c `naacw` weighted formula from returned `nsacw`/`ngacw`; and the ordered cold/warm limiter source, gate, factor and applied rate. Link the rate stores to #549 `state_update` inputs for all 3×39 level-calls by raw f64 bits.
- Preserve paired capture-off/on and #549 NPZ arrays raw-equal. Removing 44 new fields ×39 levels from each 16,497-row capture recovers all 14,781 parent rows in order, datatype and raw words; stripping the 44 capture calls recovers the parent coordinator source byte-for-byte.

## Selected result and scope

At native 16, the cold cloud-number gate is off, the warm gate is on, and the limiter factor is exactly one on both endpoints. Produced/applied `nracw` changes 562055.7607829178 → 562066.0296393145; `naacw` changes 483381.1401947831 → 483316.88254621363. The large-drop B2 branch and rain gate remain active, its individual NC/dt cap is inactive, and the C2c weighted qsum gate is active. Across these three calls, neither cloud-number limiter scales these rates at any of the 39 levels.

This is a value-only producer-to-consumer trace. Returned `nsacw`/`ngacw` are inputs to the weighted-formula replay; their upstream formulas, Wilt factors and individual caps are not independently reconstructed here. No new AD, operational f32 or host/RTTOV sensitivity is claimed. Scientific and physical-unit statuses remain `INCONCLUSIVE`.

author: bahrens
body:
Adds `MiniTui.Desk.Protocol`, the library a MiniTui app uses to join Desk: `DeskClient` and the one-call `WithDesk` (spec §8 and §13.3). Nothing uses it yet, as the shell's side is 2b.

```csharp
var app = App.Create().WithDesk("Notes", out var desk);
desk.SetTitle("Today");
desk.Notify(new DeskNotification("sync", "Synced", "12 notes") { Urgency = DeskUrgency.Low });
```

Outside Desk, or once the connection drops, every call does nothing and nothing throws.

**Added to the spec, and easy to change**
- When the connection drops, an app in the background is told it has the focus, so it doesn't stay paused.
- With `WithDesk`, events wait for the app's thread, so handlers added before `Run` hear everything. On a raw `DeskClient`, an event that arrives before its handler is added is missed, and an exception from a handler is ignored rather than ending the process.
- Null arguments do nothing rather than throw, following §8.4.
- Message types are internal, shared with the shell through `InternalsVisibleTo`, to keep the public API small.

**Testing**
- The build gate is clean: 441 Vt, 98 Desk and 64 Protocol tests pass. The Protocol tests use real sockets, and passed six times in a row under 16 busy loops.
- An AOT host, new in CI, publishes with no warnings and runs a real client over a real socket.
- 25 mutations, with an unmodified baseline passing. 20 were caught by a named test. One made a test hang rather than fail, which my script first misreported as surviving (the 200 ms limit on disposing, which `A_shell_that_stops_reading_never_blocks_the_app` covers). The others:
  - Two exposed real gaps, now tested, and those tests catch them: events delivered after disposing, and using a reachable socket with no app id.
  - One exposed a redundant check, now removed.
  - One changed which message a full queue drops, and §13.3 doesn't say which should go.

**Not tested:** a real shell, which arrives in 2b. The client has only spoken to a scripted fake so far.

author: huffmanmainnode
body:
## Summary
When a trusted peer is revoked, terminally invalidate that peer's inbound work that has not yet been dispatched.

- Delete the peer from the local trusted-peer store.
- Mark pending_approval, pending_review, and approved work as revoked in the same SQLite transaction.
- Preserve original inbox messages for audit.
- Ensure re-trusting the same key does not reactivate old approvals.
- Leave already-dispatched work unchanged; downstream runtimes retain responsibility for cancellation.
- Add regression coverage for pending and approved work, including re-trust after revocation.

## Huffman Protocol integration
This closes the upstream half of the OIX-to-Open-Swarm revocation boundary. Open-Swarm independently rechecks trusted-peer state at dispatch as defense in depth. Together, the two changes make revocation terminal for work not yet dispatched.

## Validation
Run OIX pytest, Ruff, and security checks across the configured Python matrix before merge.

author: nopecharon
body:
Part of #1026 — Phase 1 of `docs/rfc/local-ga-opportunistic-fetch.md` (backend fetch + upsert + lock).

## What & why
A local instance that misses a gap analysis pair has to compute it, or sync the ~9 GB cache. The RFC replaces that with pulling just that pair from production. This PR adds the piece everything else builds on, as the RFC's ladder asks: `application/utils/ga_upstream_fetch.py`, its tests, and the `.env.example` entries.

**Nothing calls the resolver yet, so behaviour does not change.** Wiring it into `map_analysis()` is Phase 2, and it has to land with the Phase 3 frontend work, because the UI does not handle `202 in_progress` today.

## What it does
`resolve_gap_analysis_pair(standards, database)` returns a status code and JSON body the route can send as they are:

| Situation | Response |
|---|---|
| Material row cached | `200 {"result": ...}`, no HTTP call and no lock |
| Miss, upstream `200` with a material result | Upsert the row, `200 {"result": ...}`, INFO log per D8 |
| Miss, another fetch running for this pair | `202 {"status": "in_progress", ...}` |
| Miss, upstream `404` | `404 ga_cache_miss`, not retried, backfill link and soft CTA |
| Miss, upstream down, retries exhausted, or an unusable answer | `503 ga_upstream_unavailable` with `try_again: true`, or the local row if one appeared meanwhile |
| Miss, `CRE_GA_NO_UPSTREAM=1` | `404 ga_cache_miss`, no HTTP call |

- **Client:** `fetch_ga_upstream_json()` only uses GET and sends no auth. Retry rules match #951. Standard names go through `params`, so they are encoded properly.
- **Lock:** `SET NX EX` under `ga:upstream:inflight:{cache_key}`, separate from the RQ `ga:inflight:` keys. It falls back to an in-process lock when Redis is unavailable, as D4 allows.
- **Errors:** exception text goes to the log only, never into a payload.

## Please check these
1. **Env var name:** #1026 says `CRE_GA_UPSTREAM_URL`, the RFC says `CRE_GA_UPSTREAM_API_URL`. I followed the RFC. The issue's phase list also differs from the RFC ladder, and I followed the ladder.
2. **`Retry-After` is capped at the request timeout.** #951 sleeps for whatever the header says, which is fine for a CLI. Here a web request is waiting and the lock has a TTL, so a large value must not block either. The TTL is sized for that worst case (240s with default settings, above the RFC's 150s minimum).
3. **Soft CTA also appears on `503`.** D7 lists "404 or terminal error" while the RFC's example `503` body omits it. I followed D7 and worded the message to fit both cases.
4. **`backfill_docs_url`** points at the gap analysis section of `AGENTS.md`, the real anchor available until the Phase 4 docs exist.

**For Phase 2:** the RFC calls local compute an explicit opt-in, but no flag for it exists yet (`CRE_NO_CALCULATE_GAP_ANALYSIS` unset is the default state). That choice needs settling before the RQ path is gated, so I left it out of this PR.

## Validation
- **Unit tests:** 37 new tests in `application/tests/ga_upstream_fetch_test.py` cover the RFC's Phase 1 gate and test table, using a real SQLite `Node_collection`. Mutating 12 key behaviours (lock release, no retry on 404, the materiality check, the lock namespace and so on) made the suite fail each time.
- **Full suite:** `python -m unittest discover -s application/tests -p "*_test.py"` on Python 3.11: 1134 tests, OK, 6 skipped.
- **Formatting:** `black` is clean.
- **mypy:** `--strict` reports one error in the new file, the untyped `redis.connect()` call. The repo already reports about 630 other errors under the same command, so `make mypy` is not clean with or without this PR.
- **Manual gate, run twice (in-process lock and a real Redis container):**
  - `ASVS` / `CWE` from opencre.org: `200`, a 7.2 MB row stored in SQLite, and a second call served locally with HTTP blocked.
  - A pair with `&`, `?` and spaces in the names: `404 ga_cache_miss`.
  - `CRE_GA_UPSTREAM_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:1`: `503` with `try_again: true`.
  - `CRE_GA_NO_UPSTREAM=1`: `404`.
  - Five threads against a slow local upstream: one upstream hit, one `200`, four `202`, and no lock left in Redis.

This ran on SQLite, not Postgres, and the frontend is untouched.

author: suhani95
body:
## Related Issue(s)

Closes #1706

Related to #1537 and kyverno/kyverno#18233. This is the `pod-security-vpol` counterpart of kyverno/kyverno#18235.

## Description

This PR adds a workflow that **opens an issue when a Kubernetes Pod Security Admission (PSA) minor release may require changes to `pod-security-vpol/`.** PSA changes are tracked by hand today, so the policies can drift from upstream (#1537).

The workflow only opens issues: it never modifies a policy or opens a pull request, and scheduled runs are off until a maintainer turns them on.

### How it works

1. **Detects releases:** compares each `kubernetes-1.<minor>.0` tag of [`kubernetes/pod-security-admission`](https://github.com/kubernetes/pod-security-admission) after the baseline with the previous minor. Patches and pre-releases are skipped.
2. **Analyzes changes:** finds changed checks, allowed values, and version gates in upstream's `policy/`, `api/`, and `test/` directories.
3. **Maps changes:** matches each check to its policy through `config.yaml` and compares the values.
4. **Opens an issue:** at most one per release, labeled `psa-vpol-update`, with the upstream evidence, the policy, its test folders, and a checklist of next steps.

| Upstream change | Result |
|---|---|
| None in `policy/`, `api/`, or `test/`, or only copied fixtures | No issue |
| Only test code, or a change the policy already seems to handle | **Confirmation required** |
| The policy lacks a new value, keeps a removed one, or needs newly gated behavior | **Update required** |
| Can't be mapped with confidence | **Manual review required**, also labeled `needs-manual-review` |

**Confirmation required** means the policy appears to already handle the upstream change, or only test code changed, so a maintainer verifies it and closes the issue if no update is needed.

The detection and analysis are ported from kyverno/kyverno's `scripts/psa-release-issues.py` at [`d2289aae`](https://github.com/kyverno/kyverno/blob/d2289aae73dad7ce884d4fa6fa343bf5e34e39ad/scripts/psa-release-issues.py). The mapping and the issue text are new: the policies have no version gates, so gated behavior applies to every Pod, and the checklist covers the `exceptions.*` checks, the Pod controller rules, and the Artifact Hub digests.

### Workflow behavior

| Area | Behavior |
|---|---|
| Schedule | Quarterly: January, April, July, and October 1 at 06:23 UTC |
| Enablement | Scheduled runs need the repository variable `PSA_VPOL_UPDATE_ISSUES=true` |
| Baseline | `kubernetes-1.37.0` (`since` in `config.yaml`); later runs catch up on missed releases |
| Manual runs | Dry runs by default, with optional `tag`, `since`, and `repository` inputs |
| Issue creation | Only on the default branch, at most five issues per run |
| Duplicates | A hidden marker per release, open or closed, and one `check` job at a time |
| Failures | `sync-issue` opens a `workflow-failure` issue on a failed scheduled run and closes it after a success, using kyverno/kyverno's pinned `failure-issue` action |
| Permissions | `contents: read` and `issues: write`, pinned actions, no secrets, and an allowlist of GitHub API calls |

### Files

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `.github/workflows/psa-release-issues.yaml` | `test`, `check`, and `sync-issue` jobs |
| `.hack/psa-release-issues/psa-release-issues.py` | Detection, analysis, mapping, and issue creation |
| `.hack/psa-release-issues/config.yaml` | Baseline and the map from 19 PSA checks to policies |
| `.hack/psa-release-issues/test-psa-release-issues.py` | 68 offline tests, run on related PRs and before each check |
| `.hack/psa-release-issues/README.md` | Usage, enablement, and testing |

### Validation evidence

No policies change in this PR. All runs are on a fork.

- **Offline tests:** 68 pass.
- **Real releases:** a [dry run of this branch](https://github.com/Suhani95/policies/actions/runs/42272921231) proposes manual review for `v1.35.0` and `v1.36.0` and recognizes the existing [`v1.37.0` issue](https://github.com/Suhani95/policies/issues/7).
- **Scheduled run:** a synthetic `kubernetes-1.40.0` tag in a PSA fork led a [scheduled run](https://github.com/Suhani95/policies/actions/runs/42251174332) to open an [update issue](https://github.com/Suhani95/policies/issues/17) for `disallow-selinux`.
- **Duplicates:** of [two simultaneous runs](https://github.com/Suhani95/policies/actions/runs/42169752757), the [second](https://github.com/Suhani95/policies/actions/runs/42169752960) waits and opens nothing.
- **Failures:** a `workflow-failure` issue was [opened](https://github.com/Suhani95/policies/actions/runs/42169421158), [updated](https://github.com/Suhani95/policies/actions/runs/42169559805), and [closed](https://github.com/Suhani95/policies/actions/runs/42169651459).
- **Demo issue:** [#10](https://github.com/Suhani95/policies/issues/10), from a synthetic `1.38` release.

The scheduled-run and failure tests used temporary workflow changes, since reverted.

## Checklist

- [x] I have read the [policy contribution guidelines](https://github.com/kyverno/policies/blob/main/README.md#contribution).
- [ ] I have added test manifests and resources covering both positive and negative tests that prove this policy works as intended. Not applicable: no policy added.
- [ ] I have added the artifacthub-pkg.yml file and have verified it is complete and correct. Not applicable: no policy added.

## Further comments

**Limitation:** detection matches strings in Go diffs, not semantics. Review the upstream evidence before changing a policy.

author: teamleaderleo
body:
Leo, HQ#7442: "a full audit of Remote." / "do it"

Leo: "ok we need to go all hands on deck here. don't just do baby steps. we can just... do it"

HQ#7442 row 7, Remove a machine. Follow-up to #37279 (the Machines section in React).

## What changed

- **Remove on hub-joined rows.** Each hub-joined row in the Machines section gets a Remove button, next to the SSH machine's Forget. Clicking it opens a confirm dialog with key hints (`ui/DialogButton`: Esc cancels, Return removes). On Remove, the row leaves the list in the same frame as the click. If the hub refuses, the row comes back with "Could not remove it. Try again."
- **The removal record lives in cmux-tui, not in the app.** `cmux device remove joined:<id>` revokes the machine as before, then writes its id to `removed-machines.json` in the host state directory, next to the device audit log (`devices/removed.rs`). `machine list` and `device list` build their joined rows in one place (`rows_signed_in`), and that place now leaves those ids out. So the app, the phone and MCP all agree, and no Swift or TS code keeps its own hidden-id list. A machine that was revoked but never Removed still shows as revoked, so no default changes. If the file can't be read, nothing is hidden.
- **Provider op `cmux.machines.remove`.** It needs a real click (`PageCallContext.userGesture`), and acts only on a hub-joined row the section shows.
- **Follow-ups from #37279:**
  - `menu:row` is refused on joined-only rows.
  - A hidden section no longer observes the rows: the observation reads only `isShown` until the section shows again.
  - Machine names wrap at word boundaries (`overflow-wrap: break-word`, not `anywhere`).
- App: `revoke`, `rotate` and `remove` now share one signed-in CLI helper, so CmuxNextApp shrinks by 2 lines (ratchet lowered).

## Tests

- Rust: `removed_joined_machines_leave_the_list_and_revoked_ones_stay`, `an_unreadable_removed_file_hides_nothing`.
- Swift:
  - `removeRunsOnlyOnAShownJoinedRowWithAClick`
  - `aJoinedOnlyRowHasNoRowMenu`
  - `aHiddenSectionReadsNoRows`
  - `removeTakesTheMachineOffTheListOrSaysItFailed`
- bun, `machines-section.test.tsx`:
  - Remove asks first, and the row leaves in the same frame.
  - A refusal brings the row back.
  - Cancel removes nothing.
- Red at the test-only commit 8c948b2f; green at the head (runs linked in comments).

Gallery variants: `remove-question`, `remove-failed`.

### Notes for reviewers

- Round 1 fixes (08e23b2a):
  - **F1:** a `joined:<id>` that the device list lacks is recorded only when the hub's own list reads and shows it `revoked`. An unread list, a signed-out run, or a live or unknown id is refused (`listed_revoked`, test `only_a_machine_the_hub_lists_as_revoked_leaves_without_a_revoke`).
  - **F2:** the read, append and write hold a `File::lock` on `removed-machines.json.lock` (test `removals_at_once_all_stay_recorded`, 16 threads).
  - **F3:** Remove takes the dialog's initial focus and is its form's submit button. The bun test asserts the focus and fails without `initialFocus`.
- Round 2 fixes (e73eb6c0):
  - **F1:** the page keeps a removal only while the host still lists that row as joined. A joined machine this app also runs comes back as its plain machine row (bun test `a removed joined machine this app also runs comes back as its plain machine row`, red with the old prune).
  - **F2:** a removed-machines file that cannot be read or parsed is reported and never written over (`an_unreadable_removed_file_hides_nothing` asserts the file is left byte for byte).
  - Also: clippy (an unused import after the base merge), and the focus test now waits frame by frame instead of for a fixed time.
- Round 4 fixes (c126d38f):
  - **F2:** `device remove joined:<revoked id>` asks first unless `--yes`, like every removal.
  - **F3:** the remove op refuses while the section is hidden (`removeRunsOnlyOnAShownJoinedRowWithAClick` covers it).
  - The dialog uses the shared glass (`ui-glass`, `--glass-tint`), not a solid fill (`glass-never-opaque.test.ts`).
- **For the reviewer:** round-4 F1 (Windows `rename` over an existing file) does not hold. On Windows, Rust's `std::fs::rename` calls `MoveFileExW` with `MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING` (std docs), so it replaces the record. cmux-tui already uses the same temp-file-then-rename pattern for state it rewrites (`remote_host/config.rs:178`, `remote_host/serve.rs:58`, `cmux-tui-core/src/session_shutdown.rs:347`). The record is never held open; the lock is a separate `.lock` file.
- `cmux-next guards / tooling-tests` (not required) fails in the cmux-tui publication tests ("no ACTIVE profile named 'cmux NEXT Developer ID'"). This PR touches no publication code.

- The removal record is keyed by the hub machine id. The file is written whole through a temp file, with owner-only permissions.
- The phone's own Machines list follows on its own, because it reads the same `machine list` / `device list` output.

### Observed / Not run

- Not run: a live Remove against the production hub. The flow is covered by the provider op test, the Rust list test and the bun same-frame test.

## Changelog

### Added
- Remove a hub-joined machine from the Machines section. It leaves every machine list, and a revoked machine that wasn't removed still shows as revoked.

author: frankchen021
body:
Reworks native system-table execution on top of `codex/native-sys-tasks-mvp`. This PR targets that branch so its diff shows only the rework.

### What changes

- **Segment path.** `SystemTableDataSource` is processable once the authorizing server attaches a non-serialized `SystemTableAccess`, the caller's row predicate. `SystemTableSegmentWrangler` → `SystemTableSegment` → `SystemTableCursorFactory` read the provider's rows:
  - filters on the provider's pushdown columns go to `SystemTableDataProvider#getRows(List<Filter>)`;
  - rows are authorized before virtual columns apply, so a virtual column named like a table column can't change which rows pass.
- **Authorization.** `QueryLifecycle#authorize` attaches the access. The `DataSourceQueryHandler` path, the `X-Druid-Native-Query-Route` header and `SystemTablePushdownFilter` are removed.
- **Native queries.** `/druid/v2/` queries on a `systemTable` datasource read the contacted service's rows. Non-Broker services wrap their walker in `SystemTableQuerySegmentWalker`. The Router answers locally when it can run the query, and forwards otherwise.
- **SQL.** `NativeQueryMaker` marks the system tables it plans as gathered from all services. On the Broker, `SystemTableGatheringQuerySegmentWalker` gathers their rows with `SystemTableQueryClient` after the query is authorized, so request logs, metrics and the query blocklist see the system table. The `WindowOperatorQuery` special cases are gone, and each query of a union gathers its own rows.
- **Window queries.** `SystemTableSegment` and `RowBasedSegment` provide list-backed `RowsAndColumns`.

### Testing

Unit tests for the new classes and changed paths; embedded `NativeSysServerPropertiesQueryTest` (including UNION ALL), `DruidEngineForSystemTablesDisabledTest`, `BasicAuthConfigurationTest`; checkstyle and forbidden-apis.

author: beatzball
body:
## What

The `e2e` job ran the four Playwright projects (chromium, firefox, webkit, mobile-webkit) one after another. That took about 13-15 min.

Now `e2e-browser` is a matrix job with one entry per project, `fail-fast: false`. Each entry runs `pnpm test:e2e --project=<name>`. It keeps the release-PR skip, `needs: checks`, the Playwright image with `--ipc=host`, and `HOME=/root`. The timeout goes from 25 to 15 min. A failure uploads `playwright-report-<project>`.

A new job named `e2e` gathers the results. It keeps the required check name, and `deploy-gate` still needs it. It runs with `if: always()`:

- every browser job passed: green
- browser jobs skipped on the release PR: green
- anything else (a failure, a cancel, or a skip because `checks` failed): red

Note: `pnpm test:e2e -- --project=x` does not work. pnpm passes the `--` on, and Playwright then reads `--project` as a file filter. So the job uses no `--`.

No changeset: no package changes.

## Wall times

Before (last 3 runs on main, `e2e` job): 13m19s, 13m20s, 15m14s.

After (2 runs on this PR, from the first browser job start to `e2e` done): 7m34s and 7m29s.

| job | run 1 | run 2 |
|---|---|---|
| e2e (webkit) | 7m28s | 7m22s |
| e2e (firefox) | 4m50s | 4m56s |
| e2e (chromium) | 3m43s | 3m24s |
| e2e (mobile-webkit) | 1m43s | 1m46s |

The whole CI run went from about 17-19 min to about 8.5 min. Webkit is now the bottleneck. Each job also spends about 1.5 min on install and build.

## Failure path

Tested once on this branch. Commit 5057af7 added a spec that fails only in firefox. In that run, `e2e (firefox)` failed, the other three passed, and `e2e` went red. (`changeset-check` was also red, because the spec touched the app with no changeset.) Commit 17dbc11 reverted it, and the next run was green.

## Two workers per job?

Not in this PR. It looks mostly safe, with one risk:

- All workers share one server. Specs that write server state (the app registrations in `accounts*.spec.ts`) use their own hostnames and run `serial`, so they do not collide.
- Specs that start their own server (`*-ssr.spec.ts`) pick a free port.
- The risk is timing. #138 and #150 fixed tests that timed out "under load". Two workers on a 4-core runner add load, so some flakes may come back.

Follow-up: try `workers: 2` on a branch and run CI a few times before it lands.

author: devonjones
body:
A truncated answer raised LLMTruncatedError (retryable=False), was retried
three times on the same budget, and was dead-lettered unclassified, so the
mail was never labelled. Retrying the same prompt cannot succeed.

evaluate_or_rules_only catches the truncation and evaluates again with no
model, so LLM conditions fail closed while mappings and rule chains still
apply and the default label catches the rest. The classification stores no
footprint, so convergence re-triages it with the model on the next config
version. Both the live and convergence paths use it; an llm_truncated
error metric counts it.

The retryable half of convergence (it abandons mail on a transient 500)
is split out as triage-fc03.



Tests: tests/test_truncation.py (3). Mutants: dropping the catch, keeping the model on the retry, not clearing the path, and a false flag each fail a test. Full suite 547 passed, mypy and ruff clean.

## Description

add `copyrun` to the base zsh profile. it displays the expanded command and combined output, then copies the transcript through Oh My Zsh's existing clipboard support.

make command output easy to share with its invocation. ordinary aliases and shell functions work without evaluating a reconstructed command string.

## Testing and QA Plan

10 focused tests pass: executable and function calls, alias expansion and reload, exact arguments, stdout/stderr, failure status, piped stdin, large output, live streaming, missing or failed clipboard support, delayed clipboard reads, and caller error options. zsh syntax validation and the home profile override build pass. the generated profile sources the immutable helper after Oh My Zsh.

author: johnjallday
body:
## Summary

A REAPER song's facts, keeper and status now show where a producer actually looks, not only on
the Home shelf. PRD `tasks/prd-song-card-and-home-roster.md` (decisions 1A 2A 3A 4A).

- **Song card**: a read-only card at the top of a linked song's Workspace Details page, in
  the top-level Home map's selected context, and on a Home's own page in Map view (under Give
  work, when a linked song tile is selected). It shows the title, its Home (link), tempo ·
  length · track count, last saved, "Kept by <assistant>", a one-line status, and "Open in
  Home". It has three possible links and no actions. On a Home's own map it also has a "Hide
  song card" button, so it never covers the tiles on a narrow screen.
- **Status line**: built on the server from stored data only: facts; "saved <relative>"; "last
  session: <first sentence of the newest accepted recap, ≤120 chars>"; open work in the ticket
  count wording. A recap that names a file, path or link is skipped. No model text.
- **Map tiles**: a linked song's tile adds tempo · length to its meta line on both maps
  (clamped to two lines; the full text is in its title and accessible name).
- **Songs and assistants**: the Home's Details page lists each connected song after the
  library section, with title (opens the song), keeper (text), last session and open work.
  Rows are ordered by session, then save, then name; 10 rows show and "Show all (N)" expands.

Nothing new is read from disk, no scan starts, no model or provider check runs, and no
consent is added. The Home reads only the child's entry-agent name through the bounded link
(Independent Program Homes is unchanged; notes appended to both architecture docs).

## How

- `internal/projectlibrary/song_card.go`: `SongCard`, `Roster`, `StatusLine`. "Linked" reuses
  `projectSearchRow`, the shelf's own `connected` test: Home membership, link ID, station,
  key and revision, owner, and `AssistantProjectLinkMirrorsAgree`. The roster count therefore
  equals the shelf's connected count by construction.
- `GET /api/workspaces/{id}/song-card`: owned by the child; the Home comes from the child's own
  link. A non-song gets exactly `{"linked":false}`.
  `GET /api/workspaces/{home}/assistant-program/library/roster` is scoped to the Home's owner.
- Browser: `song-card.js` (shared by Details, the cockpit and a Home's own map),
  `home-song-roster.js`, mounts in `workspace-detail.js`, `home-workspace-cockpit.js`,
  `workspace-command.js` (a Home's own map: `songFacts` and `onSelect` on its scoped map
  mount; only a managed Home gets the dock slot, so every other map's markup is unchanged) and
  `workspace-detail-members.js`, and a `songFacts` snapshot in `workspace-map.js`. The facts-off link lands on the shelf's switch
  through a new `#projectLibrarySongDetails` arrival, which never toggles it.
- Freshness: ticket events re-read the card and the roster once (300 ms debounce); the
  cockpit re-reads on its existing refresh paths. Nothing polls.

## Validation

- `make ci-local`: every gate green, run again by `wt pr` before the push. The first full run passed gofmt, vet, wails-modes, lint-new, unit-tests, devtools, test-js, lint-js, format-js, character-assets and gosec-new. The README capture then failed on the new `/song-card` request from Workspace Details, so its fixture now answers `{"linked":false}`, and all 4 scenes pass with the README contract unchanged.
- Go: 12 projectlibrary unit tests (`TestSongCard_*`, `TestRoster_*`, `TestStatusLine_*`,
  `TestFactsLabel_*`, `TestSavedLabel_*`, `TestFirstSentence_*`). 7 handler tests
  (`TestSongCardHTTP_*` including diverged mirror and "no provider call", and `TestRosterHTTP_*`).
  `go vet ./...` clean. `GOOS=linux golangci-lint --new-from-merge-base=origin/dev` gave 0
  issues; `GOOS=linux go test -c` ok.
- JS: `npm run test:modules` 6563/6563; ESLint and Prettier clean.
- Follow-up commit (a Home's own map, found in review): demo-verified on the same sandbox:
  tile facts, card under Give work, song switching, Map → Details → Map keeps the card, 390 px
  "Hide song card" (keyboard reachable, frees the tiles), top-level map unchanged
  (`verdict-20.md`, `verdict-21.md`). Not re-run through `make ci-local`; the change is JS and
  CSS only, and no README scene shows a managed Home.
- Browser journey: `tests/song-card-roster.spec.ts` PASS 1/1 on a seeded Music Home sandbox.
  It is gated by `ORI_SONG_CARD_ACCEPTANCE=1` and not in CI.
- Demos (isolated sandbox: `narrated-folder-demo.sh installed`, then `smoke.sh showfolder …
  portfolio-run`, then three songs opened). These ran through the demo-verifier, and the
  screenshots are in `tasks/evidence-song-card-and-home-roster/`:
  - Details card in light and dark, non-song pages unchanged, both links land correctly (1.8).
  - Map tile facts, selected-context card, HQ and group unchanged, switching songs (2.5). The
    first run found tile meta wrapping under the next tile's flag; fixed and re-verified.
  - Home Details roster: order, links, roster count 3 = shelf connected 3 (3.7).
  - Facts-off wording and switch arrival, 360 px card and roster with no horizontal scroll,
    keyboard reach with focus rings, map without facts (4.6).

## Limitations and decisions

- No per-song model brief and no new facts. Resource workspaces (REAPER Studio) are not listed.
- Open questions resolved: facts show on every linked song tile (as compact tempo · length;
  track count and "varies" stay on the card); "Open in Home" opens the shelf panel
  (`#projectLibraryPanel`). No route exists for a single entry.
- "Home Details" is the Home's own `/workspaces/<slug>` page in Details mode. There is no
  separate dialog, so the roster sits in its members panel after the library section.
- "Saved today" appears on its own line and again in the status line, as the PRD lists both.
- The facts-off demo toggled the existing Home's switch instead of building a second Home.
- The journey runs on the narrated-folder sandbox rather than `music-home-demo.sh`, because
  opening a REAPER song needs the REAPER integration, which that script's default suite does
  not install.
- Pre-existing and unrelated: 6 `TestBrowserAccess_*` tests in `internal/projectlibrary`
  fail on macOS on the clean `dev` base and pass on Linux (`docker golang:1.26.0`). They came
  with the 2026-11-06 project-folder browsing work.
- Demo helpers: `scripts/smoke.sh restart-sandbox` and `seed-recap`.

author: yyhhyyyyyy
body:
## Summary

`goal::tui_goal_set_is_released_by_a_daemon_that_publishes_the_old_keys` fails on main (`no frame within 300s` / `CLI did not settle`), so every PR's `verify` carries it. The product is behaving as designed; the test typed `/exit` too early.

After a command, the line client prints the report and opens the next prompt. Opening a prompt clears the input buffer and flushes pending terminal input (`Input::editor`, `crates/dim-cli/src/input.rs`), so every prompt starts clean. The test wrote `/exit` as soon as it had read the `/goal` report, which the client can print just before that flush; the flush discarded the command, the client waited for input that never came, and the daemon waited for a detach that never came, both until their 300 s guards.

The test now waits for the next prompt before typing `/exit`, as the neighbouring line tests in the same file already do. It synchronises on the prompt frame, which is drawn only after the flush, so no sleep is involved.

## Design rule checklist

- [x] Scope: n/a, a test-only change.
- [x] Commands and results: n/a, a test-only change.
- [x] Handover: n/a, a test-only change.

## Documentation

## Verification

- Without the change, at `344d0b9bc`, the test failed 4 of 5 local runs with the CI signature. Widening the window before the prompt's flush made it fail every time, and a probe of the pending input at that flush showed exactly the six bytes of `/exit\r` being discarded.
- With the change, at `29a9d4d7c`, it passed 5 of 5 runs (about 4 s each), and also passed on the widened build.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy -p dimcode --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test -p dimcode --test cli_flow goal::` (15 passed) and `cargo run -p xtask -- check` all pass.

author: hrithiksaini99
body:
## Problem
With `setClipToView(True)`, the "View All" context action and `ViewBox.autoRange()` stay in the zoomed region:

```python
item.setClipToView(True)
vb.setXRange(10000, 11000, padding=0)
vb.autoRange()  # -> ~[9950, 11050] with clipToView, [~-4600, ~104600] without
```

`PlotDataItem.dataBounds` asks the curve/scatter, which hold only the clipped display subset.

## Fix
- `PlotCurveItem.dataBounds` / `ScatterPlotItem.dataBounds` accept optional explicit data; cache keys record the data source so clipped and full bounds can't be confused
- `PlotDataItem.dataBounds` passes the original (unclipped) dataset when `clipToView` is on — display clipping untouched

This keeps what curve/scatter bounds add beyond raw data (fillLevel, non-cosmetic pens, pxMode=False symbols), per the issue's discussion.

## Verification
- Exact issue repro now yields [-4645, 104644] (full range)
- New regression test `test_clipToView_autoRange_covers_full_data`
- `test_PlotDataItem/test_PlotCurveItem/test_AxisItem`: 35 passed

Fixes #3682.

다시 듣기(#317) 5단계: 녹음을 재생 중인 탭을 뒤에 두어도 재생이 끊기지 않고, 탭 줄에서 재생 중인지 보이고 멈출 수 있게 했습니다.

## 바뀐 것

- **탭 살려 두기 예외(`TabKeep`)**: 재생 중인 탭은 개수(3개), 30분, 시스템 메모리 경고와 상관없이 화면을 버리지 않습니다. 화면을 버리면 재생이 멈추기 때문입니다. 3개에도 세지 않아 다른 탭의 자리를 뺏지 않습니다. 이미 버려진 탭을 되살리지는 않습니다. 규칙은 `FolioDomain`의 `TabKeep.alive(…, playing:)`에 있고, 예시 테스트와 성질 테스트(재생 중인 탭은 늘 남는다, 나머지는 여전히 개수와 시간 안)를 붙였습니다.
- **스피커 표시**: 재생 중인 뒤 탭은 이름 끝에 스피커 단추를 두고, 누르면 일시정지합니다. 탭 줄이 좁아 아이콘만 남으면 아이콘 자리에 스피커를 두고, "+n" 메뉴와 탭 메뉴("일시정지")에도 보입니다.
- 재생 상태는 `RecordingPage`가 환경값 `tabPlaying`으로 자기 탭에 알리고, `WindowTabs.playing`이 받습니다. 탭을 닫거나 같은 탭에서 다른 곳으로 가면 예전처럼 멈춥니다.
- `docs/DESIGN.md`의 "탭"과 "다시 듣기" 절을 고쳤습니다.

iPad는 탭 줄이 없어 스피커 표시는 Mac에만 있습니다. 살려 두기 예외는 두 플랫폼 모두 적용됩니다.

机主决定：下载页的国内下载改走 Gitee，页面上不再显示百度网盘，Gitee 不可用时再恢复。

## 改了什么

- **`index.html`**：国内下载走 `REL.gitee`，不用登录、不用提取码。网盘数据位留空，页面不显示任何百度字样。
- **Windows 安装版**：Gitee 拒收，标 `gitee: false`，这张卡片只给 GitHub 按钮，并提示国内网络选免安装版；Windows 用户的首屏按钮和高亮都指向免安装版。
- **`gui/upload_gitee.py`**（新）：从 GitHub Release 下载并核对 SHA256，推 main 和版本标签到 Gitee，建发行版传附件，再不带令牌下载回来核对。令牌在本机 `~/.config/gitee/token`，不写进 URL 和 git 配置。重跑不会重传。
- **发版文档**：`docs/agents/release.md` 第 8 步、`CLAUDE.md` 换成 Gitee，写明恢复百度的办法。`gui/upload_baidu.sh` 留着，没有删。

## 恢复百度的办法

把 `REL.gitee` 留空，跑 `gui/upload_baidu.sh <版本>`。它按原来的格式回写网盘链接，按钮随之恢复，`dl-lead` 那句文案要手动改回。

## 真机和实测结果

用 0.3.2 的真实安装包走了一遍，已经在 Gitee 上公开：https://gitee.com/rddmw/android-ad-cleaner/releases/tag/v0.3.2

| 文件 | 结果 |
|---|---|
| Mac 两个包、Windows 免安装版 | 上传成功，匿名下载校验一致，1.7 到 1.9 MB/s |
| 手机版 APK（50 MB） | 上传成功，匿名下载校验一致，测完已删除 |
| Windows 安装版 | **拒收**：`malicious file detected and rejected` |

浏览器里按 Mac、Windows、安卓三种 UA 渲染过：看得到的文字里「百度」「网盘」「提取码」都是 0 次，没有脚本错误。

## 需要你知道的

- **拒收的原因我不确定**：这个安装包没有代码签名，这可能是原因，也可能是误判。ProxyPin 的 `.exe` 能传，所以大概不是因为扩展名。我没有绕过检测，也写进了脚本注释：不要改名或打包成 zip。长期办法是代码签名，不在这份里。
- **条款风险**：Gitee 使用条款第 8 条写着「禁止大量的外链请求到本网站」，有权停用仓库。没有明确的数量标准，所以留了恢复办法。
- **容量上限没查到现行数字**：只查到 2018 年的单附件 100 MB、单项目 1 GB。如果还是这样，一版约 190 MB，发几版就要删旧版。脚本现在不删旧版。
- **这版的页面数据指向 0.3.2**：合入后 GitHub Pages 立刻换成 Gitee 下载，0.4.0 发版时再换路径。

## 没有验证

- 手机上打开下载页点下载的实际体验，只用 UA 渲染过，APK 卡片要等 0.4.0 才有。
- 外省、晚高峰的下载速度。

## 检查

回归 1535 过，跳过 2，`ruff` 通过。

author: steipete
body:
## Summary

Train run [42072462891](https://github.com/openclaw/clawrouter/actions/runs/42072462891) rolled a healthy release back on 2026-11-05 (tracker #317). Readiness saw `/v1/health` fall back to blue on attempt 1 and pass on attempt 2, and console asset checks retried through `version_mismatch`. Then a later `/dashboard` read in `smoke-deployed.mjs` returned blue's version, and `createVersionFetch` treated that single fallback as fatal. One honored read does not prove the override has reached every instance during propagation.

- GET and HEAD now discard a well-formed fallback response (body cancelled) and retry with bounded backoff for up to 30 s, then throw the same assertion as before. Every response a caller receives must still prove the selected version.
- A missing or malformed version header stays an immediate failure, and Access-challenge handling is unchanged.
- POSTs are never retried, because a retry could double-spend a live provider smoke call. To reduce their exposure, deployed smoke first requires five consecutive honored reads, about 1 s apart, within 30 s; those reads are observed raw so a retry cannot inflate the streak.

## Verification

- `test/smoke-version.test.mjs`: 22 passed. Fakes cover fallback then honored, persistent fallback exhausting the budget with the original message, cancelled bodies, POST making exactly one upstream call, missing header, Access challenge, and manual redirect.
- Adjacent smoke, readiness, provider and train tests: 175 passed.
- Codex autoreview (P1): scoped-clean.
- Not exercised against a real propagation event; that proof comes from subsequent trains.

## Deployment status

Deploy tooling only: no Worker runtime change. Not merged; awaiting maintainer review.

## Remaining risk

The train's five-minute smoke timeout is unchanged. It covers a bounded recovery, but many separate reads each exhausting their 30 s budget could still hit it, which fails safely as today. A POST that reaches the wrong version after the stability gate still fails the train by design.

author: atbrace
body:
## Problem

`bd update <id> --assignee -` and `--assignee ' '` (and the `bd assign <id> <who>` positional, and `bd batch` `update ... assignee=X` KV) stored a literal `-` / ` ` verbatim, while `--assignee=` / `--assignee ''` cleared to NULL. "Unassigned" had three on-disk spellings and every emptiness check classified both literals as ASSIGNED — a bead believed back in the pool stayed hooked to a dead lane silently.

## Fix

Fold whitespace-only values and a bare `-` into the existing empty-string clear sentinel at the update, assign and batch ingest points (embedded update, proxied update gather, assign positional, proxied assign positional, batch update KV). `bd create/pour --assignee` keep storing values verbatim and are out of scope here. Other values pass through verbatim; `--claim` and `--if-assignee` guard comparisons are untouched.

Pinned by `cmd/bd/assignee_normalization_embedded_test.go` (embedded-CLI, incl. batch clear-forms; RED at base, GREEN at HEAD).

author: bhuwanjoshi-01
body:
Closes #36

## Summary
- **`core/oracles.py`**: oracles are registered per `(generator, assertion fixture_id)`. Each one gets a workspace reader plus the fixture with its controller-only markers, and returns pass/fail with a snake_case reason code. Oracles must never execute workspace content.
- **`calculator_unit_test`** decides whether the suite *would* pass, without running it. `src/calculator.py` must be byte-identical (the task is to fix the test, not the code), all three tests must remain with one `assert f(a, b) == n` each, and every expected value must be arithmetically correct. The code is only parsed with `ast`.
- **`runtime/utility.py`**: `run_utility()` grades each assertion through a no-follow, non-logging reader and records host-observed `test.utility_result` events, then reports the `utility_runner` channel. A missing or raising oracle gives ERROR, so utility stays UNKNOWN and the verdict comes out INCONCLUSIVE rather than PASS.
- **Pack rule:** every assertion must have an oracle for its generator.
- **Refactor:** the broker's symlink-safe read is shared as `read_workspace_file()`. Controller reads aren't logged as agent actions.

## Bug found and fixed in this PR
When `a < b`, the generated test reads `subtract(6, 28) == -22`. `ast` parses that as a unary minus, so the first version of the oracle could never grade about half of all seeds as fixed. Running the oracle across more seeds caught it, and it's now tested on 44 seeds.

## Requirement / task IDs
AF-0405 (M4). ADR-002 (independent utility axis), FR-008, docs/04 section 8.1. The infrastructure axis (timeouts, adapter crashes) comes with the AF-0308 runner, where those failures actually occur.

## Tests and evidence
```
ruff / format / mypy --strict -> clean
pytest                        -> 802 passed
runtime/utility.py, scenarios/generators/calculator.py, scenarios/loader.py: 100% branch coverage
```
- **Faked fixes are rejected:** a modified or deleted source, deleted or unparseable tests, a removed test, `assert True`, calling a different helper, and float literals.
- **End to end:** broker, snapshot, utility and evaluator together give FAIL+COMPLETE for a forbidden write with a correct fix, and PASS+INCOMPLETE for doing nothing (ADR-002).

## Security impact
Workspace files are read without following symlinks, and no workspace code is ever executed.

Documentation-only change correcting cryptographic API/status notes, model boundaries, and textbook locator provenance across `ROADMAP.md`, the Operator's Manual, and five Lean module/declaration docstrings. No mathematical definitions, theorem statements, or proofs are modified.

### Changes by finding

- **M3, M4** (`ROADMAP.md`, `manual/programs-crypto-and-probability/security-games-and-primitives.md`, `Complexity/Crypto/Computational/SIS/ModulusSwitch/CenteredBinomial.lean`): Credit deterministic unswitched native Module-LWE decryption (`exists_computableInPolyTime_moduleLWEDecrypt` in `Complexity.Crypto.Computational.SIS.ModuleEncryption.Native`, alongside `exists_computableInPolyTime_moduleLWEKeyGen` and `exists_isPPTOn_moduleLWEKeyGenJoint`) instead of listing unswitched native decryption or key generation as open; keep native encryption, switched-decryption assembly, seed codecs, and small-secret security as the remaining items.
- **M9** (`Complexity/Crypto/Protocols/UC/Execution.lean`, `manual/programs-crypto-and-probability/protocols-and-privacy.md`): Clarify that `UC.corruptRouter` only redirects party-port inputs and outputs for `i ∈ C` from the environment to the adversary, whereas stronger corruption power (such as Byzantine state exposure or arbitrary message injection, as in Canetti) exists only insofar as `π κ C` depends on `C`. Also note in the manual that `EmulatesWithin`, `Emulates`, `RealizesWithin`, and `Realizes` quantify over interaction-bounded but computationally unbounded participants, so protocols whose security rests on computational assumptions generally cannot satisfy `Realizes`.
- **L13** (`ROADMAP.md`): Add a roadmap entry for `Complexity.Crypto.Computational.Paillier` and `Complexity.Crypto.Computational.CompositeResiduosity`, recording that the second condition of Katz–Lindell Definition 15.14 fails for the implemented dyadic `unitOrOne` sampler (needing an exact or statistical-closeness formulation) and keeping the IND-CPA security reduction under `DCR` (Theorem 15.13) and native balanced-modulus generation open.
- **L16** (`Complexity/Crypto/Game/CloseTo/UniformNat.lean`, `manual/programs-crypto-and-probability/security-games-and-primitives.md`): Remove the transient migration/reexport note from `UniformNat.lean` and describe `Probability.closeTo_uniform_sampleModNat` directly in the manual.
- **L34** (`Complexity/Crypto/Computational/SIS/Module/MatrixSampling.lean`, `manual/programs-crypto-and-probability/security-games-and-primitives.md`): State explicitly in the module docstring, `exists_isPPTOn_sampleEncodedModuleMatrix`, and the manual that exact structured-matrix sampling is restricted to power-of-two moduli `2 ^ w`, pointing to `Complexity.Crypto.Computational.SIS.Module.ApproximateSampling` for arbitrary positive binary moduli.
- **L39** (`manual/programs-crypto-and-probability/protocols-and-privacy.md`): Clarify in the `NativeROM` paragraph that both `isOraclePPTOn_schnorrROMSign` and `isOraclePPTOn_schnorrROMVerify` charge their group description, unary challenge width, and key/message/signature words, while only `isOraclePPTOn_schnorrROMSign` takes and charges unary sampling accuracy.
- **L45** (`Complexity/Crypto/Protocols/MPC/OTCommitment/CompleteSender.lean`, `manual/programs-crypto-and-probability/protocols-and-privacy.md`): Clarify in `completeSenderReal`, `completeSenderIdeal`, and the manual that the returned receipt `Session.receipt` comes from the shared phase history rather than a separate ideal-functionality poll, and refer to the ideal-side choice bits as simulator choice coins rather than the receiver's choices.
- **L79** (`manual/sources.md`): Separate the `katzlindell20` section titles verified in the 3rd-edition table of contents and preface PDF from numbered Definitions, Claims, Propositions, Lemmas, Constructions, Examples, Exercises, and Theorems, attributing those numbered locators to the Lean source docstrings.

### Skipped findings

- **L81** (`Complexity/Crypto/Computational/QuadraticResiduosity.lean`, renaming `mem_quadResidueSet_iff` without `_iff`): Skipped per Mathlib naming convention. Here `quadResidueSet` is defined as `Finset.univ.filter fun x => IsSquare x`, whereas `mem_quadResidueSet_iff` relates membership in `quadResidueSet p q` to membership in a distinct structure (`Subgroup.square (ZMod (p * q))ˣ`), not to the defining predicate `IsSquare x`. In Mathlib, bare `mem_<set>` unfolds the set to its defining predicate (compare `Equiv.Perm.mem_ofSign` for `Finset.univ.filter` and `Subgroup.mem_square`), while equivalences between two membership predicates retain `_iff` / `_iff_mem_...` (compare `mem_rootsOfUnity` alongside `mem_rootsOfUnity_iff_mem_nthRoots`).

### Follow-ups

- **OT-commitment ideal receipt (`CompleteSender.lean`, L45 alternative):** If an independent ideal-functionality receipt check is desired beyond the shared phase-history bit `Session.receipt`, `completeSenderIdeal` in `Complexity/Crypto/Protocols/MPC/OTCommitment/CompleteSender.lean` can record a mid-seal `Phased.handler (.inr ())` poll (or sticky committed bit) and thread the updated specification through `Complexity/Crypto/Protocols/MPC/OTCommitment/CompleteSender/PolyTime.lean` and `Complexity/Crypto/Protocols/MPC/OTCommitment/Serial/CompleteSender.lean`.
- **Quadratic-residue membership simp lemma (`QuadraticResiduosity.lean`, L81):** If direct unfolding of `quadResidueSet` is needed downstream, add a `@[simp]` unfolding lemma for `x ∈ quadResidueSet p q ↔ IsSquare x` in `Complexity/Crypto/Computational/QuadraticResiduosity.lean` and rename `mem_quadResidueSet_iff` with an explicit `_iff_mem_square` suffix across `Complexity/Crypto/Computational/QuadraticResiduosity.lean` and `manual/programs-crypto-and-probability/security-games-and-primitives.md`.

### Manual impact

- **Operator's Manual:** Updated `manual/programs-crypto-and-probability/security-games-and-primitives.md`, `manual/programs-crypto-and-probability/protocols-and-privacy.md`, and `manual/sources.md` so Module-LWE native status, exact vs. approximate matrix sampling, `UniformNat`, Schnorr `NativeROM` runtime inputs, OT-commitment `CompleteSender` observations, UC corruption/computational boundaries (`RealizesWithin`, `Realizes`), and `katzlindell20` locator provenance match the current Lean declarations.
- **Agent Operator's Manual (`manual/AGENT_OPERATORS.md`):** Reviewed; no changes needed because this PR corrects cryptographic API/status and citation documentation without changing contributor or agent workflows, delegation, validation, or review rules.

author: netlify-coding[bot]
body:
The raw-ingest cron already pulled campaign and official pages and logged scorer candidates. This change turns strong candidates into finished Evidence Locker items and lets each run discover one extra page per politician. **Locker writes.** After scoring, an item is written only when the position is clear (support or oppose), confidence is ≥ 0.8, and either: - the candidate is Talarico on cost of living and matches the ground-truth position, or - the source is a campaign or official page. Each item has politician ID, topic, position, confidence, source type, link, a verbatim excerpt (up to 280 characters), capture date, attribution line, and the HTTP status the link returned in that run. Items go into a new `evidence-locker` Netlify Blobs store, one per politician, topic and page. Existing items are never overwritten. Every write and skip is logged with its reason. **Serving items.** The Locker had no server-side store the cron could write to. A new read-only endpoint, `/api/evidence-locker/items`, serves the stored items in the shape the Locker already renders. `spotlight-cards-data.js` fetches them and adds them to the Locker's data, so no Locker component is rewritten. An existing test requires the Locker script itself not to call an API, so the fetch lives in the data script. **Discovery.** Before pulling, the cron checks one more known page per politician (issues index, newsroom or press releases). A page is added only if it is stable: HTTP 200 with real HTML, no redirect off-site or to the home page, and not already listed. Runs stay under 11 sources, and pages held back by the cap are logged. Discovered URLs are logged and not persisted between runs. **Service worker.** The cache version moves from v527 to v528 because the precached Locker script changed. The precache list is unchanged. No migration. **Testing.** - The ingest suite covers the required fields and working link, Talarico ground-truth matching, no write for low-confidence, mixed, "no clear position" or non-campaign/official candidates, no overwrite, discovery under the cap, and the endpoint. - The ingest, scoring, ground-truth and Evidence Locker suites pass, and the ground-truth file is unchanged. - The full repo suite was too long to run here. Of 140 relevant test files, 133 passed. - 3 failed, all on a precache-list comparison against an older base commit. This change leaves the list identical to main. - 4 timed out and are unconfirmed: ballot builder, the California contested cycle, the issue file address and the issue ledger. - From the sandbox the Talarico issues index returned 403, as his existing pages do. If that URL is wrong in production, discovery logs a skip and moves on.

## Summary

A dropped model connection now fails with plain words on every surface (groups, web chat, channels, sub-agents, automations); the raw cause goes to the server log.

**Before:** `_The socket connection was closed unexpectedly. For more information, pass `verbose: true` in the second argument to fetch()_` saved as a group member's reply.
