author: palbirmin
body:
## What changed

**One demo, every device.** The practice session behind `/judge/demo`, `/commentary/demo` and the scoring APIs with `?sample=1` was one in-memory copy per signed-in person, so a judge on a phone and a commentator on a laptop never saw the same thing. It is now one shared session stored in a new `scoring_training_sessions` table (service role only, versioned saves, one retry on a lost race), so every device reads and writes the same demo; Reset restarts it for everyone. Until the migration is applied the site falls back to memory and the banner says so. A laptop with `SCORING_SAMPLE_MODE=1` keeps its own in-memory session.

**Demo feed for the graphics team.** `?sample=demo` on the four vMix feeds, `/api/live/state`, `/live` and every overlay follows the shared demo live (every row `sample = Yes`), beside the existing scripted `?sample=solo` loop. The Graphics Rehearsal Feed card on `/admin/scoring` lists both sets of addresses.

**Close the demo for the event.** A switch on the same card (audited admin route). Closed: the demo pages say so and link to the live panels, demo requests are refused, and the `?sample=demo` addresses answer frozen sample rows marked SAMPLE, never anything live. Rule throughout: a sample address never returns real results; a real address never returns demo data.

**Judges start each rider.** Score → nobody on course while the rider leaves → the judge taps one large **Start <name>** button → score. Skip, Take out and a pool call-up also leave nobody on course. Built in the training engine and the judges' panel, and the public scoreboard, overlays and commentary now name the same up-next rider as the Start button (new `next-to-ride.ts`), never a rider passed over earlier.

## Migrations (applied by hand in the SQL editor)

| File | When | What |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `20261107120000_scoring_training_sessions.sql` | Any time; safe | Two service-role-only tables for the demo. Nothing real. |
| `20261107130000_scoring_judge_starts_each_rider.sql` | **Only when the organisers say so, after rehearsing on the demo, before 11 Nov** | Changes real scoring: patches `scoring_record_result`, `scoring_set_run_status`, `scoring_take_out`, `scoring_call_pool`; adds `scoring_leave_course`. `supabase/migrations/revert/` holds the undo. Until applied, the real panel keeps the old auto-advance while the demo has the Start flow. |

## Not done, by decision

Rebuilding the demo from the real registered riders was asked for and approved for the staff panels, but the automated data-protection check blocked copying registrants' names onto the public `?sample=demo` addresses. The demo keeps the 30 invented riders; a staff-only version is the proposed follow-up.

## Checked

- `tsc`, `lint`, 283/283 tests, production build; the three guide PDFs rebuilt.
- Rehearsed on the dev server at 375 px: Start → Carried → Confirm → "Last: … Carried 4" and Start for the next rider; the commentary demo and `/live?sample=demo` followed.
- Not checked: the two migrations against a real database (the version race, the missing-table fallback in production, the switch), the admin card button in a browser, a real phone.

body:
## Problem

The coding skill uses "Layered" for the wrong rule. Section 1 defines the Layered axis as "workflow separate from rules and from wiring", and files the real dependency rule (the Arrow test) under Hexagonal. The sdlc skill's law 6 and the architecture skill repeat this. The adherence engine in tds-utils copied the definition verbatim, so its "Layered" quality never looks at an import edge, and the rule the owner means by Layered (each unit depends only on its own layer or a layer below it, Clean/Hexagonal/Onion) has no name of its own in the skills.

The per-function rule the old text was reaching for also has no name. The owner's rule is Todd's LAW: every function is logic, action, or workflow, never two of them. The old text described it as a property of layers ("the layer decides which kinds a file may contain"), which is wrong: every layer holds all three kinds.

## Evidence

At Skills `origin/main` b2d804b, `skills/coding/SKILL.md` Section 1: the axes table row `Layers inside the core | Layered / Clean | is workflow separate from rules and from wiring? | Trace, Purity, Wiring`, and the Arrow test listed under `Core vs edge (Hexagonal)`. The tds-utils design record `docs/design/DESIGN.ARCH-ADHERENCE.md` Qualities table at f28ea3c carries the same definition, and the engine's dependency ordering lives in `adherence/src/adherence/domain/checks/hexagonal.py` (`INWARD`, `is_inward`), not in `layered.py`.

## Solution

Section 1 of the coding skill is now "Four Rules", each with its own tests:

- Layered: a unit imports only its own layer or a layer below it; application and adapters are peers that never import each other. Tests: Arrow, Wiring.
- Core vs edge (Hexagonal): the core names no mechanism. Tests: Grep, Swap, Change.
- Todd's LAW: every function is exactly one of logic, action, workflow. Tests: Kind (new), Purity.
- Language and boundaries (DDD): Trace, Decision, Language, Boundary. Trace moves here from the old Layered row.

Section 1.7 is retitled "Todd's LAW: the function taxonomy" and restates the five function shapes by kind. The smells list gains "Import that goes up or sideways" and "Function of two kinds". The sdlc skill's law 6 and the architecture skill's module-map note are reworded to match. Second commit is a plain-language pass over the same text.

Deletion audit: every removed sentence is restated under its new rule except "the layer decides which kinds a file may contain", which was the misstatement.

The adherence design record and engine in tds-utils follow in their own PR once this lands: the Layered quality becomes Arrow plus Wiring, a new LAW quality takes Kind, Purity, Anatomy and Two jobs, Trace moves to Domain-driven.

## Checks

At 89a89d6: `node scripts/skill-lint.mjs` passes, `npm test` 68 pass 0 fail, no byte over 0x7F in the three changed files. The husky hooks did not run in this cloud sandbox.

## Not proven

No consumer repo's `AGENT.md` or tds-utils `clai.d/AGENT.global.md` names "three axes" or "layers inside the core" (grepped), so no copies need sweeping. The architecture skill still cites "Trace, Purity and Wiring" nowhere else; other skills were not re-read end to end for the old vocabulary.

Opened under the owner's identity, not `9atatimer-bot`, so CODEOWNERS approval cannot be given from this PR; it is human-merge.

author: pierrez
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"PierreZ"} -->
_Requested by **Pierre** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01DS2jy7NSy5EfL5kQq5bWCJ?thread=cmsg_01DS2jy7NSy5EfL5kQq5bWCJ8ht9XiWg2WCKY35nGJbSWw)_

Fix-main PR for the main red that CI shard 4 of #886 found: replay-main 6120504210761534645 on c4ed4ab, oracles "fleet: no tenant is left mid-operation after chaos" (a tenant stays `Removing`) and "fleet: an operation an operator stopped in ends in the recovery tail".

## Mechanism

A set move froze the cell tenant's matchmaker set, which also serves the election journal, and the move was abandoned early. After that, every campaign on the election journal was refused with `Stopped { successor: None }`, so no coordinator term served. After chaos ended, a refused campaign finished the handover (generation 1 chosen). But its election journal then waited for its next backed-off election timeout (14 s) before it campaigned. The coordinator term served at 127 s, after the operator's removal deadline at 119.7 s, so the tenant stayed `Removing`.

## Fix

The `MatchStep::Superseded` path already asks the successor at once. Now the journals whose campaign the frozen generation refused do the same. The handover driver keeps them (`HandoverDriver::note_met` / `take_met` / `forget_met`). Once the successor is learned, each one campaigns above its ballot (`campaign_above`) with no backoff. With the fix, the election journal elects at 109.4 s and the removal ends at 113.9 s.

## Testing

- `cargo test -p paros-roles --lib handover` (3 new tests)
- Witness: RED before, GREEN after. A 100-seed hunt shows 0 reds.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy -p paros-roles --all-targets -- -D warnings`

body:
When workflows on `main` operate on another branch (such as
`release/X.Y`), calling reusable workflows via `uses:` mixes `main`
workflow definitions with target-branch scripts. In addition, merging a
draft PR via `gh pr merge` fails unless the PR is marked ready first.

Document cross-branch `gh workflow run --ref` dispatch, fast-fail ref
parsing, and contextual `::error::` reporting in the workflow rules and
review prompt, and instruct the merge skill to run `gh pr ready` before
merging draft PRs.

author: ppenna
body:
Pins `openvmm` to microVM v5.1: the microVM chain of `feature/microvm/dev` rebased onto the latest upstream OpenVMM `main` as a minor promotion. Upstream landed none of the chain's commits, so the rebase drops none and every commit keeps its position. One commit conflicted with upstream and was resolved in place, and no fixup was needed. The second commit maps the rebased chain in the OpenVMM upstream roadmap.

OpenVMM CI passed on the pin, NVX CI passes on this head, and `feature/microvm/dev` points to the pin, so this merges through the merge queue; see [Landing order](#landing-order).

## OpenVMM source

- **Pinned revision:** `bced18bec5c29c2ef43376ad443b52e3d0cddafb`, the head of [`feature/microvm/release/v5.1`](https://github.com/microsoft/openvmm/tree/feature/microvm/release/v5.1) (new).
- **Previous pin:** `db42fde04`, the head of `feature/microvm/dev`: the 212 commits of `feature/microvm/release/v5.0` (`f1e1d8545`) and the seven that microsoft/openvmm#4953, microsoft/openvmm#4954, microsoft/openvmm#4955, microsoft/openvmm#4970, microsoft/openvmm#4968, and microsoft/openvmm#4969 landed after it.
- **New base:** microsoft/openvmm `main` at `ba105dd7f` (2026-11-06), nine commits past the v5.0 base `61994293a`. None of the roadmap's upstream pull requests merged, and `git cherry` finds no chain commit upstream, so the chain drops none.
- **Upstream `main` since:** none; `ba105dd7f` is still its head.
- **OpenVMM pull request:** none. As with v2.2-v5.0, the release branch was pushed directly, and its push runs OpenVMM CI.
- **Signatures:** all 219 commits carry good SSH signatures, and there are no merges. Each keeps its author, date, subject, and trailers.
- **Open into `feature/microvm/dev`:** microsoft/openvmm#4981, one commit on `db42fde04` that #1336 pins, is not part of this release. Now that `feature/microvm/dev` points to the pin, it and #1336 need a rebase onto it; its commit applies to `bced18bec` without conflicts.

## What changed in OpenVMM

**One conflict, resolved in place.** microsoft/openvmm#4944 splits `guestmem`'s page locks into kernel and user modes: `supports_locking` becomes `supports_kernel_lock` and `supports_user_lock`, and `lock_gpns` becomes `lock_kernel_gpns` and `lock_user_gpns`. Position 183, `guestmem, virtio: admit only a set of ranges to a device's memory`, adds views of guest memory that admit only a set of ranges, so its resolution:

- keeps upstream's two lock capabilities next to the commit's restriction in `GuestMemoryInner`, and a restricted view copies both from the memory that it restricts;
- has the view's backing, `RestrictedAccess`, forward `lock_kernel_gpns` and `lock_user_gpns` instead of `lock_gpns`;
- has `test_restrict` lock through `lock_user_gpns`, as its `lock_gpns` calls without kernel access did, and keeps the two restriction tests in `mod tests`, where the merge would have appended them to upstream's new `lock_mode_tests`.

No other commit of the chain uses the APIs that microsoft/openvmm#4944 renames.

**Nothing else.** The other 218 commits replay with identical patches. The other eight upstream commits, among them the RTC fixes of microsoft/openvmm#4959 and microsoft/openvmm#4963, which change `cmos_rtc.rs` beside the chain's RTC persistence without superseding it, merge with the chain without conflicts. Checking every commit that changes one of their files found nothing to fix, so the rebase adds no fixup.

## What changed in NVX

The gitlink commit moves `openvmm` from `db42fde04` to `bced18bec` and changes nothing else: what `nvx-rs` copies from OpenVMM, its vectors, excerpts, contract versions, and CPU profiles, matches the pin.

The roadmap commit maps the rebased chain in `doc/openvmm-upstream-roadmap.md`: the scope, upstream status, open upstream pull requests (states as of 2026-11-07; none merged, and microsoft/openvmm#4607 is a draft again), the v5.1 conflict, the graph, branch DAG, commits after the mapped tip, PR summary, and commit mapping. Every position stays: the mapped tip is position 131, and the pin is position 219, 88 commits past it. Replaying positions 207-219 on the new base conflicts in the same files as on the old one, so the remarks on them hold.

## Equivalence

- **Patches:** `git range-diff 61994293a..db42fde04 ba105dd7f..bced18bec` pairs all 219 commits in order: 218 have identical patches, and position 183 differs only by the resolution above. No commit is dropped, added, or reordered.
- **Tree:** outside `vm/vmcore/guestmem/src/lib.rs`, the pin's tree, `864a036ae`, is the tree of a three-way merge of upstream's nine commits into `db42fde04`, which conflicts only in that file. The pin differs from `db42fde04` in exactly the 43 files that those nine commits change.

## Validation

OpenVMM, with Rust 1.97.1, the release of OpenVMM's pipelines:

- **Per-commit:** on x86_64 Linux (Azure Linux 3) and x86_64 Windows, at the 86 commits that change the pipelines, conflicted, or change a file that upstream's nine commits change, the pin among them: `cargo check --locked --workspace --all-targets` passes, on Windows without `vtpm_util`, which upstream's Windows jobs exclude too, as do `cargo xtask fmt --pass lints`, `rustfmt --check --edition 2024` on each changed `.rs` file, and `cargo xtask fmt --pass verify-flowey` at the five commits that change the pipelines, positions 002, 003, 127, 128, and 187. No commit warns; on Windows, only `vmfirmwareigvm_dll`'s build script notes that `UH_IGVM_PATH` is unset.
- **At the conflict:** the unit tests of `guestmem` and `virtio` pass at position 183 (171 of 171 on Windows, with Rust 1.98.0).
- **At the pin:** `cargo xtask fmt` passes all four of its passes, and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` passes on Linux and on Windows, there without `vtpm_util`, `guest_test_uefi`, and `opentmk_executor`, as upstream's Windows job. The documentation of `guestmem` and `virtio` builds, and their unit tests pass, 185 of 185, on each.
- **microVM VMM tests:** `cargo xflowey vmm-tests-run --filter "test(microvm)"` passes 2 of 2, the TTRPC microVM lifecycle and snapshot test and the microVM phase 1 lifecycle test, on each of KVM and MSHV (Azure Linux 3) and WHP.
- **OpenVMM CI:** [run 42353627227](https://github.com/microsoft/openvmm/actions/runs/42353627227), started by the release branch's push, passed the six jobs that NVX's `openvmm-ci` job requires: unit tests on x64 Linux and Windows, and the VMM tests on KVM, MSHV, Windows Intel, and Windows AMD. `python scripts\nvx.py check-openvmm-ci --revision bced18bec5c29c2ef43376ad443b52e3d0cddafb --wait-minutes 300` reports all six passed. The run passed all 37 of its jobs, the others among them AArch64 Linux and Windows, the macOS clippy, the TDX and SEV-SNP VMM tests, and the five `vmm-perf` jobs.

NVX, at this head:

- **Pass on Windows:** `python scripts\nvx.py verify`, the link check, and `git diff --check`.
- **What `nvx-rs` copies from OpenVMM:** `openvmm_vectors -- --ignored` (3 tests) and `openvmm_cpu_profiles -- --ignored` (1 test) pass.
- **`test-microvm`** with OpenVMM built at the pin passes 57 of 57 scenario runs on each of KVM and MSHV (Azure Linux 3) and WHP: on WHP at this head, and on KVM and MSHV at `d3117e3b8` with the gitlink at the pin, which differs from this head only in the roadmap. On each host, `nvx-rs download` installed a release's OpenVMM first, and `build-openvmm` then replaced it, as its changed SHA-256 shows.
- **Not run locally:** AArch64 and macOS builds, which OpenVMM CI runs.
- **NVX CI on this head:** [run 42353813190](https://github.com/microsoft/nvx/actions/runs/42353813190) passed: 35 jobs passed, `Required status check`, `OpenVMM CI of the pinned revision`, and the performance regression gate among them, and the 8 that a pull request does not run were skipped.

## Landing order

1. Done: OpenVMM CI passed NVX's required jobs on `bced18bec` ([run 42353627227](https://github.com

author: quanttrinh
body:
## Summary

This PR fixes the published-package integration issues found while updating the UI libraries, and hardens the AI review workflow.

### 1. Published Panda preset no longer scans consumer source

`dist/panda/preset.mjs` previously called `createConfig(process.cwd())` at runtime and scanned `<consumer>/src/components`. That directory usually does not exist, so the published preset failed with `ENOENT` or silently missed undefined-content tags.

The preset now imports a generated static tag module. Tags are produced from component source with `oxc-parser` and refreshed by the Stencil styles plugin during `buildStart`. The generated module is committed so the synchronous Stencil/Panda bootstrap always has a valid import.

### 2. Published peer ranges are resolvable

`@quanttrinh/qui-server` and `@quanttrinh/qui-unplugin` shipped `"@quanttrinh/qui": "workspace:^"` literally. Bun does not rewrite that for peer dependencies, so consumers could not resolve a published release.

Both now use:

```json
"@quanttrinh/qui": "^0.7.0"
```

### 3. Hydrate package no longer carries an ignored `exports` field

Stencil emits a nested `dist/hydrate/package.json`. The file is still required so `dist/hydrate/index.js` resolves as CommonJS under the root `"type": "module"`, but nested `exports` fields are ignored by Node.

`postbuild` now removes only the `exports` field, so:

- `require("@quanttrinh/qui/hydrate")` and `import("@quanttrinh/qui/hydrate")` still work
- publint no longer reports the warning

### 4. Build scripts consolidated

`build:all` now runs the package build followed by `panda lib`; `prepublishOnly` uses it. The standalone `build:lib`/`build:release` scripts were removed.

### 5. AI review workflow hardened

- Added a dedicated `review` OpenCode agent with `steps: 8`.
- Denied `glob` for that agent.
- Added the changed-file list and explicit review scope to the prompt.
- Moved non-negotiable secret/source read denials into hard `tool.use` policies.
- Disabled session sharing, snapshots, and update checks for CI runs.
- Reduced tool output limits.
- Kept `AGENTS.md` and `node_modules` readable for the reviewer unless policy denies them.
- Suppressed the OpenCode CLI stream; only a bounded log tail is printed on failure.

## Implementation notes

- Replaced `@babel/parser` with `oxc-parser` for component declaration parsing.
- Removed hardcoded Oxc node-type strings in favor of a typed `NODE_TYPE` map.
- Added tests for marker ordering, non-exported components, parse failures, generated module sync, and hydrate package normalization.
- The generated tag module lives at `packages/qui/tooling/panda/generated/undefined-content-tags.ts`.

## Verification

- `bun run lint`
- `bun run fmt:check`
- `bun run --cwd packages/qui build`
- `bun run --cwd packages/qui build:all` (publint: **All good!**)
- `vitest --project unit`: **281 passed**
- Stale generated tags are repaired during `buildStart` and the emitted selector is correct.
- `require("@quanttrinh/qui/hydrate")`, `import("@quanttrinh/qui/hydrate")`, and `renderToString()` were verified through the public hydrate export.
- The hardened OpenCode config was validated against the pinned `2.2.6` binary with `debug agents --standalone`.

Note: this PR modifies `.github` workflows, but `pull_request_target` restores workflow files from the default branch. The bounded review configuration takes effect after merge.

author: trapsterdk
body:
Closes #9080. Stacked on #9084 (same wiring files; now merged). The rust_toolchain sysroot symlinks are split out to #9089, and upstreaming is tracked in #9091.

On windows_arm64, `atomic_helper_cc_library` (llvm 0.8.26 `compiler-rt/targets.bzl`) renamed `lse.S` to `lse_<pat>_<size>_<model>.S` with `copy_file(allow_symlink = True)`. It did this for each of the 125 outline atomic helpers in every aarch64 configuration, which came to 500 local `Symlink` actions per evidence run. The rename is needed because `cc_static_library` rejects duplicate `lse.o` members.

- New `patches/llvm/lse_atomic_sources.patch`:
  - The `(pat, size, model)` comprehension moves unchanged into `compiler-rt/lse_variants.bzl` as `LSE_ATOMIC_VARIANTS`, and `compiler-rt.BUILD.bazel` loops over it.
  - `targets.bzl` drops `copy_file` and compiles `lib/builtins/aarch64/lse_<...>.S` directly.
  - `write_llvm_project_files` reads `lse.S` (`watch = "no"`) and writes the 125 copies with `rctx.file` when `@llvm-project` is fetched. LLVM trees without `lse.S` are skipped.
  - Object names stay the same.
- Wired in the same way as e4d43a1ab and #9084: `MODULE.bazel`, `patches/llvm/BUILD.bazel`, `cli/adopt` (BUILD and `overrides.rs`), `patches/README.md`, and the rendered `families/*/third_party/rules_dx` copies (sorted the way `dx init --apply` renders them). No lockfile changed: `bazel mod deps --lockfile_mode=update` left `MODULE.bazel.lock` as it was, because the llvm extension is not recorded there.
- Test: `//patches/llvm:lse_atomic_sources_test` builds `@llvm-project//compiler-rt:clang_rt.builtins.static` for `@llvm//platforms:linux_aarch64` (through `platform_transition_filegroup`). This build runs the duplicate-member check. The test then asserts that the archive has 125 distinct `lse_*.pic.o` members. I changed the planned `cmp` against `lse.S` because neither `lse.S` nor the `@llvm` BUILD/bzl files are visible from rules_dx.

Local (Linux):
- `bazel aquery 'mnemonic("Symlink", deps(@llvm-project//compiler-rt:clang_rt.builtins.static))' --platforms=@llvm//platforms:linux_aarch64` finds 1 action, which is `@bazel_tools//tools/build_defs/build_info:cc_build_info`. The lse ones are gone, and the 125 `lse_*.o` compile actions remain.
- `bazel build --platforms=@llvm//platforms:linux_aarch64 @llvm-project//compiler-rt:clang_rt.builtins.static` passes, and `llvm-ar t` lists 125 `lse_*.o`.
- `bazel test //patches/llvm/... //cli/adopt/... //tools/workspace/...`: 8 of 8 pass.
- `//modules:families_test`: `moved_families_vendor_the_overrides_dx_renders` passes. `every_item_is_in_exactly_one_family` and `family_files_define_aspects_listed_in_families_json` fail with errors about aspects in `families.json` and `rust.bzl`. This change does not touch either file.
- Nested-Bazel and consumer tests were not run.

Evidence (`//cli/process/...`, windows_x86_64 + windows_arm64):
- First pair, cold for the branch: branch 42353775574, main 42353777599. All four jobs green.
- Warm pair 1: branch 42354092399, main 42354094336. All four jobs green.
- Warm pair 2: branch 42354309116, main 42354311286. All four jobs green.

| Pair | Platform | Run | Job time | Bazel elapsed (profile) | Symlink actions | of which compiler-rt |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| warm 1 | windows_arm64 | branch 42354092399 | 1m31s | 56.5s | 296 | 0 |
| warm 1 | windows_arm64 | main 42354094336 | 2m39s | 118.7s | 796 | 500 |
| warm 1 | windows_x86_64 | branch 42354092399 | 1m20s | 59.3s | 296 | 0 |
| warm 1 | windows_x86_64 | main 42354094336 | 2m02s | 105.4s | 296 | 0 |
| warm 2 | windows_arm64 | branch 42354309116 | 1m46s | 62.2s | 232 | 0 |
| warm 2 | windows_arm64 | main 42354311286 | 1m44s | 63.4s | 732 | 500 |
| warm 2 | windows_x86_64 | branch 42354309116 | 1m18s | 58.5s | 232 | 0 |
| warm 2 | windows_x86_64 | main 42354311286 | 1m02s | 45.2s | 232 | 0 |

- Result: arm64 drops by 500 Symlink actions (all compiler-rt) in both warm pairs, and x64 is unchanged. Wall time fell sharply in warm pair 1 but was flat in warm pair 2, where both sides were mostly cached, so runner noise is larger than the time saved there.

author: shiba4life
body:
The Mac app updater exits as soon as one installed receipt points to an unavailable or retired registry index. On a mixed fleet, that leaves apps later in the pass unprocessed.

Keep the existing signed registry and consent checks. Report receipt, index and install failures per app and reuse each index and channel result for the pass. The background job reports retired LastSecrets index receipts as blocked and retains their existing installation. Other errors still fail the pass after the remaining apps have been processed. An explicit upgrade can still name an eligible index.

The hosted app install smoke uses two actual signed installs in an isolated app root. With the first app's index unavailable and no cache for that pass, the CLI reported Brain red and processed LastSecrets with its inactive receipt intact. After the index was restored, the poll checked Brain again. The exact source run and its proof archive passed. https://github.com/EdgeVector/lastdb/actions/runs/42354012394

body:
## Outcome Delivery v1

- **Lane:** FAST
- **Related outcome issues:** #1390, #1391, #1392, #1393
- **Host/runtime effect:** NONE
- **Trust-boundary change:** NO
- **Native stacked PR:** NO

## Outcome

Refactor the required validation surface so the existing regression coverage is explicit, parallelizable and fail-closed while keeping security checks and Gitleaks history scanning intact.

## Coherent work items

1. Replace the flat Makefile test catalog with explicit command manifests split into 10 reviewable groups.
2. Run those regression groups in parallel and converge them into one required fail-closed `validate` aggregator.
3. Move GitHub API contract assertions and targeted legacy selection out of workflow YAML into focused scripts/tests.
4. Make `test-shell-syntax.sh` single-purpose and retain its prior regression coverage exactly once in the explicit manifest.
5. Pin Gitleaks 8.18.4 Linux x64/arm64 archives to reviewed in-repository SHA-256 values.

These changes belong in one delivery unit because the manifest is the shared compatibility boundary between local `make validate`, parallel CI execution, coverage-preservation tests and the final required gate.

## Scope

Source/test/workflow only. No repository settings, merge, LIVE, host/runtime, secrets or permission changes.

## Integrated validation

Exact-head CI must prove:
- all 10 regression groups pass;
- API contract and targeted legacy selection pass;
- tracked-source secret guard and public diff guard pass;
- Gitleaks full-history scan passes with repository-pinned archive digest;
- actionlint, zizmor and public automation baseline pass;
- final `validate` aggregator fails closed on any non-success dependency.

The manifest contains 286 explicit commands across 10 groups and rejects duplicate command entries. Regression scripts previously hidden inside `test-shell-syntax.sh` remain explicit exactly once.

author: cherry7435
body:
想给这个插件加一个在网页里管语录的面板，顺路修了两个我自己用出来的毛病。

**为什么要面板**

现在查语录只有聊天里的指令，翻到第几条、配图长什么样全靠记。表情包那个插件有页面，用顺手了就想着语录也来一个。

**长出来的东西**

- 「扩展功能 → 语录管理台」：普通池 / 涩图池两个 tab，按会话筛、按名字或正文搜，一页 12 条，每条带缩略图、时间、徽标（看图几、聊天记录还是纯文字），卡片上三个小按钮：预览 / 复制 / 删除。
- 卡片样式抽屉：背景色、文字色、字号百分比、宽高、字体、背景图（上传图片或填 URL），改一下右边就实时出一张预览，满意再保存。保存后的样式 QQ 那边发语录也用同一套。
- 删掉了 iframe 里必定失效的 `window.confirm()`，换成页面内确认框；顺手把语录配图内联进卡片模板（原来只有头像和文字，带图语录渲染出来是一对空「」）。
- 渲染这块加了点保险：失败重试一次，还不行就降级成文字语录，不再把整条指令带崩；单次渲染 45 秒超时（原来要等 aiohttp 默认 300 秒）。

**几处取舍**

- 个人号（aiocqhttp / NapCat）发不出可点的内联按钮，AstrBot 的 Button 组件目前只有 qqofficial 实现，所以删除走「语录列表 + 删除 编号」，没做按钮。
- 背景图和配图都在渲染前转成 base64 内联，因为远端渲染服务读不到本机路径，传 file:// 会被静默忽略。
- `image` 里新增的 `font_scale` / `bg_image` / `bg_image_overlay` 三个键已写进 `_conf_schema.json`，否则 AstrBot 加载配置时会把它们丢掉。

**怎么验的**

本地 AstrBot 4.29.4 + Python 3.12 + NapCat 实机跑，面板接口、删除、翻页、搜索、样式保存后重启是否还在、带图语录渲染都过了一遍；渲染失败的降级路径用假 renderer 强制抛异常验过。

**两个想听你意见的地方**

1. 页面上的删除目前完全走面板登录态，没校 `delete_permission`；要不要让页面里也按这个配置卡权限？
2. 列表默认带出正文前 40 字，涩图池那边可能你希望默认打码，现在没做，要不要加个开关。

author: karthiksubramanian07
body:
## Audit summary
I reviewed the Pages function, the rooms Worker and Durable Object, the Rust engine's message parsing and redaction, the client identity and the headers. It was already solid:
- The rooms Worker is reachable only through a service binding.
- Room codes and hello payloads are validated in Rust, and frames are capped at 2 KB and 24 sockets.
- The pid that reclaims a seat is never part of any player's view.
- The CSP, HSTS and frame headers are strict.
- `osv-scanner` and `cargo audit` report nothing.

## Changes
- **Flood limit:** every accepted socket message can trigger a broadcast and a Durable Object storage write, and nothing limited how fast one client could send. Each socket now gets a token bucket (a burst of 30, refilled at 10 per second), and excess messages are dropped silently. Normal play sends a few messages a second at most.
- **Predictable pid helper:** `makePid` defaulted to `Math.random`. It is not on the live path today (`browserId` already uses `crypto.randomUUID`), but it now defaults to `crypto.getRandomValues` so it cannot be misused later.
- **CI:** actions are pinned to SHAs and checkout runs without persisted credentials. zizmor and actionlint are clean.

## Verification
CI on this PR runs typecheck, lint, vitest and the Rust workflow.

author: 7empes7s
body:
Closes #185

## What changed
- **Who counts as trusted** (`shared/trust.ts`, pure): the repo owner, the office's own `gh` user, collaborators with write access (`repos/…/collaborators?permission=push`, checked again every 10 min), GitHub's `OWNER`/`MEMBER`/`COLLABORATOR` author associations, and a new per-floor **Trusted authors** allow-list (Manager's console → the floor). This applies to every floor, private or public.
- **Issues:** `listIssues` now uses one GraphQL query that also returns the author, the authorAssociation and who last added the `office-trusted` label. Each sync marks issues from anyone else `untrusted`. Untrusted issues:
  - are never picked by the scheduler;
  - are refused by `assign`, which covers the manager's Assign, stickies and the CEO's tools;
  - show as "🛡 Untrusted: not built · @author" on the Kanban, with a **Trust this issue** button (it asks for confirmation first).
  
  Trusting an issue adds `office-trusted` as the office's user, posts "🛡 … trusted #N by @author" in the office chat, and re-syncs. GitHub's timeline keeps the audit trail. The label only counts when a trusted user added it.
- **PRs:** a PR from a fork (`isCrossRepository`) or from an untrusted author is never queued for QA, QA'd, fixed, sent back, previewed or merged, either automatically or through the office's buttons. It shows as "🛡 From outside: review on GitHub" with a Review on GitHub ↗ link. The What's new strip and the PR channels leave it out, and its "Closes #N" no longer holds #N back.
- **CEO:** `company_status` marks untrusted issues and outside PRs.
- **Comments:** the office reads no GitHub comments as instructions. QA reports and fix notes already come only from its own QA records, so nothing needed to change there.
- **Demo:** pixel-todo has a stranger's issue ("Add my analytics snippet", @drive-by-dev) and a fork PR on a `swarm/` branch ("Fix typos in the README"), each with its badge.
- **Docs:** `docs/how-it-works.md` → Safety model → "Whose work the office takes (public repos)". It explains the rules and says: before making a floor's repo public, set GitHub → Settings → Moderation → Interaction limits to collaborators only until this is live.

## How I verified it
- New tests:
  - `shared/trust.test.ts`: the trust rules, including that the label only counts when a trusted user added it.
  - `server/github.test.ts`: who last added the label.
  - `server/trust.test.ts`: a demo office where the untrusted issue is never picked by the scheduler or assigned, and the fork PR (on a `swarm/` branch) is never queued for QA, can't be sent to QA, sent back, merged or previewed, and is not auto-merged even with a passed QA record. It also checks Trust this issue and the allow-list.
- Checked that the tests fail without the fix: with `scheduling.ts`, `agents.ts`, `qa.ts` and `merge.ts` reverted to main, 3 of the 5 tests in `server/trust.test.ts` fail.
- Ran `typecheck`, `test` (3416 passed), `lint` (no new findings), `build` and `node scripts/smoke-package.mjs`; all pass.
- Read the real repo with the new GraphQL issues query, the collaborators call and the PR fields: all three return the expected data.
- Booted a demo office (DEMO MODE, own SWARM_HOME, port 5660) and checked it in the lab browser. At 390 px on iPhone, both badges, Trust this issue and Review on GitHub show, with no sideways scroll and no console errors. The trust dialog renders, and at 1280 px the fork PR is gone from What's new. Screenshots are in .lab/ (not committed).

## Decisions I made
- Missing author or fork data counts as untrusted (fail-safe). The demo backend supplies these fields for its own issues and PRs.
- The manager's own Merge and Preview are refused for outside PRs too: they should review and merge on GitHub, because a merge on the office's floor updates the live office.
- `server/practices.test.ts`: its helper called `syncRepo` right after `connectRepo`, which returns at once while the first sync is still running. It only passed because that sync used to finish in a couple of ticks. The helper now waits for the first sync, as the new test does.
- I left out the unrelated "1 fixed since the baseline" lint note (`shared/journal.ts:compactMessage`), so `code-health.baseline.json` is unchanged.

Self-review: read the full diff against the issue and the QA brief. I found and fixed:
- the What's new strip and the PR channels still offered previews of outside PRs (now left out, with tests);
- an outsider's "Closes #N" could stall #N;
- the CEO couldn't see which issues were untrusted;
- a lint finding (an unused export);
- the trust lookups made the first sync slower (they now run in parallel).

author: flotob
body:
Amends design 0014 (the Colibri verifier process, merged as proposed in #274) for what has been found since it merged. Docs only. **Status stays proposed**; no user decision is taken here.

## Why

Since #274 merged, the reviews of solardev-xyz/freedom-browser#1048 and #1049 found that Colibri 3.0.3 doesn't prove some answers the design had the service serve:
- **Calls without proofs** (solardev-xyz/freedom-browser#1060, its comment of 7 November; High). In PAP mode (`privacy_mode: 'basic'`, which main always sets), `eth_call` and `eth_estimateGas` are `METHOD_LOCAL` (`eth_verify.c:228–235`).
  - The verifier runs them on contract code from one of the package's public `eth_rpc` hosts, never compared with the proven code hash (`call_ctx.c:245–260`, `eth_account.c:134–189`, `:165–168`).
  - A call that reads no storage or block context fetches no proof and is accepted (`verify_call.c:704–721`).
- **ENS through Colibri** (solardev-xyz/freedom-browser#1076; High). Forward, reverse and NameNFT resolution ran their `eth_call` that way, labelled verified, and send-to-name used the address.
- **Unbound reads** (solardev-xyz/freedom-browser#1060). Account reads at a number, a hash, `safe`, `finalized` or `justified`, or without their block, aren't tied to the requested block. `eth_getBlockByNumber` matches strings like `0X10` and `1x10` with any proven block, because 3.0.3's `check_hex` (`json_validate.c:184`) joins its two prefix tests with `&&`.
- **Private windows' store** (solardev-xyz/freedom-browser#1058). Colibri's disk store records which contracts and blocks were read, and private windows shared it.
- **Local proving** (solardev-xyz/freedom-browser#1059). The design already drops the fallback (deviation `no-local-proving`). This amendment keeps that, now for private processes too, and adopts the error contract of solardev-xyz/freedom-browser#1080 and #1081: a failed remote proof ends as `remote proof failed (no local proving): <the prover's error>`.

The core's side of these rules is #279 (`fc-chain`, chain data; merged at `372d2d8c`) and #286 (`fc-naming`, ENS; in review). This amendment cites them as the rules the service follows.

## What changes in `docs/design/0014-colibri-verifier.md`

- **Header and references:** an *Amended* note, plus the browser fixes and their heads: #1048 `a515f9a7`, #1049 merged, #1082 `0da2215b`, #1083 `528e91dc`, #1070 `038d27cb`, #1071 merged at `841bd5d4`, #1080 `a25305c5` and #1081 `5d0fcfa8`. It also cites #279 (merged at `372d2d8c`) and #286 at `2f873ce7`.
- **New facts:**
  - **F-11:** calls without proofs, ENS through them, and their fixes.
  - **F-12:** unbound reads, including the validator's `0X`/`1x` prefix bug and the 16-digit limit.
  - **F-1 and F-10:** their "being fixed" lines are updated.
- **Operations:** a new *What the service serves* section.
  - It lists the closed set: account reads at explicit or appended `latest`; `eth_getBlockByNumber` at `latest`, a canonical number, a 32-byte hash or no block; `eth_getBlockByHash` at a hash; `eth_blockNumber`; `eth_maxPriorityFeePerGas`; the two transaction lookups.
  - It gives #279's block rules exactly (positions, appended `latest`, refusal texts, non-string blocks, exact string matching).
  - The service never appends `latest` itself. An account read that reaches it without its block is refused. COL-4 runs #279's unit cases against the service's check.
- **Calls and ENS:** a new section that says why the service serves no `eth_call`, `eth_estimateGas`, ENS, reverse or NameNFT call, and what goes with them.
  - **Bringing them back is a condition, not a plan.** An upstream release must bind the code a call runs to the proven code hash, and prove every call it answers against the requested state, held to the freshness gate.
- **The fetch contract:**
  - `colibri_proofCall`, the header sub-proof and the storage and code reads leave the variant table.
  - So does the original-payload variant for odd-arity account reads, since those forms are now refused.
  - No variant has the `eth_rpc` type, so main's server table has no RPC hosts.
  - A form the service doesn't serve admits no fetch, the sync variants included.
  - The refusal and acceptance tests follow.
- **Private sessions:** a new section.
  - A private session's reads go to a private process per chain. Its store is in memory, it has no `--data-dir` and no lock, and it fails closed to memory. It ends with the session (`colibri.shutdown`, open requests as bystanders).
  - It counts toward the 3 persistent processes, and has no directory.
  - Main tells which reads are private the way #1071 does on integration. Spawn, How many, Confinement, the store, Budgets, Crashes, the WASM call map and COL-5 follow.
- **A failed remote proof:** a new section. The service stops at the step #1080/#1081 stop the WASM runtime at. It records a proofable context's remote proof, and on an error from main it runs no further step. It frees the context and replies `remote proof failed (no local proving): <text>`, whole. Main cuts the completed adapter message to 2,000 units after `createError`, as #1080's worker does, so both backends give byte-identical adapter messages at any length. The verifier-only build's own error is only a backstop. F-9, the verifier-only change, the `no-local-proving` row (parity against a reference with #1081), the F-9 vectors and COL-4/COL-5 follow.
- **The build:** a short *The call verifier* section. COL-2 tries `ETH_CALL=OFF`, which would drop evmone; 3.0.3 isn't known to build that way. The notices line follows.
- **Threat model:**
  - **The attacker** no longer picks EVM code, and a second attacker (a public RPC host or a lying prover whose answer isn't bound) is named.
  - **Two new rows:** unbound answers, and private windows' reads.
  - **The leak row** has no `eth_rpc` hosts.

author: derekadams
body:
## What

One device whose clock ran ahead (the resolver admits event times up to 300 s past the server clock) advanced the engine-wide DETECT watermark for every tenant. That fired other tenants' absence timers early and refused their windowed samples as late.

Each message now contributes `min(occurred, appendTime + lateness)` to the shared frontier, so the frontier can never pass the broker's append time. The clamp is `Engine.frontierInstant`, called from `ProcessReceived` and `ProcessReceivedMember`; the live loop and the replay preview both feed the engine through those, so they share it. The event keeps its own time, so a fast device's samples are still windowed at the instants it reported. A zero append time (the bare `ProcessResolved`/`ProcessEvent` entry points, tests only) is not clamped.

This is the fast-clock half of the finding only. A backlogged or store-and-forward device's samples can still be dropped as late (the frontier is still shared); that needs per-key time and is not part of this change.

## Snapshot frontier version

`snapshot.frontier` (omitted when 0). An engine built fresh writes 1. A restore from a snapshot without the field keeps 0, so re-snapshotting an old snapshot is still byte-identical (`TestTimersWindowsOldSnapshotRestores`). It moves to 1 the first time a clamped message carries the frontier past the restored value. The processor logs a warning when it restores version 0. A previous-release pod ignores the field and writes without it, so a rolling upgrade needs nothing.

## Tests

- `TestFastTenantClockDoesNotMoveAnotherTenantsTimersOrWindows` (negative control, message and envelope-member paths): tenant A at +290 s must not fire tenant B's absence timer or make B's windowed sample late. Fails on the old code.
- `TestPreviewFastDeviceClockDoesNotMakeOtherDevicesLate`, `TestProcessorClampsTheFrontierToTheBrokerAppendTime`: the preview and the live loop carry the append time into the engine.
- Frontier version round trip (single, sharded split/merge, legacy restore, healing).
- Envelope/applied-guard differential tests now store every message of the corpus after its newest event (`diffStored`). They hold batching equal to single messages; their old append times (an envelope stored at its first member's time) would have engaged the clamp. The timers/windows golden is regenerated for the new field; the old-engine snapshots are kept and the old tail hash moved to `oldTailHash`.

## Mutants (whole `internal/detect/core`, `internal/preview`, `processor` runs)

All killed: clamp removed; clamp on the message path only; clamp on the envelope-member path only; min/max swapped; lateness dropped from the bound; version not written; restore ignores the version; healing never fires; merge drops the version; `ReceiptOf` drops the append time.

## Gates

`event-processing`: gofmt clean, build, vet, `go test -p 2 -count=1 ./...` green except `TestStartsUnderItsDeclaredCatalog` at the module root, which fails the same way on an untouched `main` checkout on this Windows box (broker start under the catalog, then a nil `Stop`). No `go.mod`/`go.work.sum` change.

Codex (read-only) was run on the diff: no concrete findings. Its sandbox could not read the repo, so it judged from the diff alone.

## Upgrade note (v1.2)

author: vitaliilazebnyi
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #78 (`fix/git-copy-log-noise`), fixing the two leftovers its review accepted as non-blocking. Stacked on #78; merge that first.

`pkg/git/service.go` logs a failure to copy data between git and the client at debug when the client went away, and at error otherwise.

- **Windows disconnects:** `clientGone` only knew the Unix errors (`EPIPE`, `ECONNRESET`), which are made-up values on Windows. Real Windows failures are `WSAECONNRESET` (10054), `WSAECONNABORTED` (10053), `ERROR_BROKEN_PIPE` (109) and `ERROR_NO_DATA` (232), the last two being the codes Go's own `os/exec` treats as "the child exited" for pipe writes. They are now recognised on Windows only (`clientGoneOn(runtime.GOOS, err)`); the numbers are written out in shared code because `syscall` has no `ERROR_NO_DATA`, so the check builds and is tested on every platform.
- **stdin copy:** copying the client's input to git still logged at error when git exited first (broken pipe, `os.ErrClosed`) or the client disconnected. It now uses the same classification as stdout/stderr. Real failures stay at error, and a git failure itself is still reported through the service error path (`cmd.Wait`), so nothing is lost.

## Testing

- `TestClientGoneWindowsErrors` (all platforms): the four Windows codes, bare and wrapped in `*net.OpError`/`*fs.PathError`, count as a disconnect on Windows only; `WSAECONNREFUSED` never does.
- `TestGitServiceInputCopyErrorLevel`: real `git upload-pack` fed garbage exits and the stdin write failure is logged at debug; context cancelled, closed pipe, closed connection and connection reset are debug; any other failure stays at error.
- `TestGitGone` covers `os.ErrClosed`; `TestWindowsErrnosMatchSyscall` (windows build tag) checks the hard-coded numbers against `syscall`.
- Before the fix (base `service.go` with stubs keeping the old behaviour) the debug cases fail; after, all pass.
- `gofmt`, `go vet ./pkg/git ./pkg/ssh/... ./pkg/web`, `GOOS=windows go vet ./pkg/git`, `GOOS=windows go test -c ./pkg/git`, `go test -race ./pkg/git ./pkg/ssh/... ./pkg/web`. The independent reviewer also ran the stdin tests 450 times under `-race` with no failure. The windows-tagged test runs for the first time in the `windows-latest` CI job.

Approved by an independent reviewer in review round 1.

author: doobidoo
body:
Refs #1897. That RFC stays open, this PR is the groundwork it needs. ## What was wrong `Memory.__post_init__` turned every memory type it did not know into `observation`. The constructor also runs when storage hydrates a row (retrieve.py alone has nine call sites, plus cloudflare, milvus, remote_http, hybrid). On a node whose `MCP_CUSTOM_MEMORY_TYPES` differs from the writer's, which is normal since v12 synced nodes through the hub, the read returned `observation` and the next update wrote it back for good. Delta-sync itself applies events as raw SQL and keeps the type; the damage happened on the read-and-update round trip. Separately, `_get_merged_taxonomy()` did `merged = dict(TAXONOMY)` and then `.extend()`ed the subtype lists, which are the built-in lists. A custom subtype stayed valid after it was removed from the env var and `clear_ontology_caches()` ran. ## What changed - `Memory()` canonicalizes known types as before and leaves unknown ones alone. - New `coerce_memory_type()` in `models/ontology.py` does the old coercion and warning. It is called where a caller-supplied type enters a new memory: `MemoryService.store_memory` (MCP and REST both go through it), the code-execution API `store()`, and document ingestion via CLI, REST and MCP. Literal types (`"session"`, `"note"`, `"learning"`) need nothing. - The #843 warning in the MCP store response still fires; it now has a test. - The taxonomy merge copies the subtype lists. ## Tests New `tests/test_memory_type_coercion_store_path.py` plus a leak test in `tests/test_ontology.py`. The two bug tests fail on the unchanged `src` (`git stash push -- src`): ``` FAILED tests/test_memory_type_coercion_store_path.py::test_stored_unknown_type_survives_read FAILED tests/test_ontology.py::TestBurst21CustomMemoryTypeConfiguration::test_custom_subtypes_do_not_leak_into_builtin_taxonomy 2 failed, 2 passed, 53 deselected ``` Three existing tests asserted coercion in `Memory()` itself (#603, burst I1, the #1146 log-injection test). They now assert it on `coerce_memory_type()`, so the guarantees moved rather than disappeared. ``` .venv/bin/pytest tests/test_memory_type_coercion_store_path.py tests/models/test_memory_logging.py \ tests/test_issues_603_to_608.py tests/test_ontology.py tests/test_memory_ontology_integration.py 91 passed ``` ## pre_pr_check.sh Exits 1 with four failures, none introduced here: - Quality gate, complexity 9 on `ingest_document`, `handle_ingest_document`, `store_memory`. Each got one changed line. radon on origin/main vs this branch: A (3), C (18), E (40) in both. - Test suite: the eight `test_http_mcp_round_trip_with_read_scope` cases fail locally with `KeyError: 'result'` with this PR's `src` stashed as well. ci.yml is green on main at e74a66c4, so this looks like my local venv. CI here will tell. - Import ordering and debug code: whole-file scans hitting existing lines (`import tempfile` in operations.py:509, `import time` in handlers/documents.py, docstring `>>> print(...)` in operations.py). ## Not in scope Unknown types now survive into `get_parent_type()` (returns None) and `is_allowed_pair()` (a named type never matches None), so decay falls back to the default retention and typed inference skips them. Making those nodes actually know the type is #1897.

Confidence Score: 5/5

The PR appears safe to merge; the previous finding is fixed and no new actionable issues were found.

Summary

 Keeps unknown memory types intact when reading stored rows, while retaining coercion for caller-supplied types on new writes. - Unknown memory types survive reads but still get checked on new writes. - Custom subtypes no longer stick around in the built-in taxonomy.

body:
## Summary
Implements the **Photo EXIF/GPS Extractor & Spatio-Temporal Scene Matcher Engine** for the Anime Pilgrimage Travel Planner. When travelers shoot dozens or hundreds of photos during a pilgrimage or import a batch from their camera roll, this backend engine automatically matches each photo to its corresponding itinerary stop and anime reference image cut.

### Key Components
1. **\PhotoExifExtractor\ (\lib/features/camera/services/photo_exif_extractor.dart\)**:
   - Parses GPS coordinates (rational degrees/minutes/seconds to signed decimal degrees), timestamp (\DateTimeOriginal\), altitude, and orientation from in-memory byte buffers or disk files.
   - Resilient against corrupted or non-JPEG headers; gracefully falls back to file stat modification timestamps when needed.
2. **Models (\lib/features/camera/models/photo_exif_models.dart\)**:
   - \PhotoExifData\, \PhotoMatchCandidate\, \PhotoInput\, \PhotoMatchResult\.
   - Tracks spatial distance, confidence percentage, match reasons, and flags ambiguous closely-co-located stops.
3. **\PhotoSceneMatcherService\ (\lib/features/camera/services/photo_scene_matcher_service.dart\)**:
   - Blended spatio-temporal matching scoring:
     - Spatial distance decay: 100% within <=30m, decaying to 0% past 1000m.
     - Temporal itinerary alignment: 100% within scheduled visit window (+-15m buffer).
     - Combined confidence: .65 \\times S_{spatial} + 0.35 \\times S_{temporal}$.
   - Database operations:
     - \matchPhotosForTrip\: resolves scheduled day windows and matches photo batch.
     - \pplyPhotoMatches\: commits confirmed matches into \Photos\ table with foreign key validation (Rule 2) and atomic transaction.
4. **Riverpod Providers (\lib/features/camera/providers/photo_matcher_providers.dart\)**:
   - \photoSceneMatcherServiceProvider\, \	ripPhotoMatchesProvider\.

### Testing
- Full unit test suite in \	est/features/camera/photo_scene_matcher_test.dart\ (9/9 passed).
- Project-wide suite: 344/344 passed with zero regressions.

body:
## Problem

PBI 18 runs the factory locally on this repo's own board. Nothing yet tells the factory which board that is, because `config/sources.yml` doesn't exist. Nothing names a reviewer for factory PRs, because there's no CODEOWNERS. And starting it takes several manual steps: pull `main`, start Docker, set the AppHost's secrets for this checkout, rebuild `factory-cell:local`, then `aspire run`. The owner asked for the latest `main` and one simple command to run the factory.

Refs #22. This covers plan Task 18 Steps 1 and 2. Steps 3 to 6, the live run, the override tests, the restart and the runbook, stay with the owner.

## What changed

- `config/sources.yml` names Project 4 on `ricksu978` for this repo, through installation 179116800, with a board status for each of the 11 factory states.
- `.github/CODEOWNERS` is `* @ricksu978`, so each factory PR requests the owner's review.
- `npm run factory` runs `scripts/factory.ps1`:
  - It fast-forwards `main`, and only when the checkout is on `main`.
  - It starts Docker Desktop if `docker version` fails, then waits up to 3 minutes.
  - It asks for any AppHost parameter this checkout lacks.
  - It rebuilds `factory-cell:local`, then runs `aspire run`.
- `scripts/set-local-secrets.ps1` gains `-MissingOnly`. It exits 1 while a parameter is missing, and it writes `secrets.json` only when a value changed.
- Plan Task 18 Step 1 names the command.

## Board statuses

| Factory state | Board status |
|---|---|
| Eligible, NotReady | Backlog |
| Queued | Ready |
| InProgress, SignOff, NeedsInput | In progress |
| InReview, Accepted | In review |
| Done | Done |
| Failed, Abandoned | Backlog |

Failed and Abandoned go to Backlog, so the board never shows an item the factory stopped on as still in progress. The alternative is a dedicated "Failed" option on Project 4, which `src/e2e.ts` already expects. That's the owner's call, and it changes two lines here.

## Checks

- Both scripts parse with 0 errors.
- An end-to-end run of `factory.ps1` used `aspire` stubbed as a PowerShell function, against a throwaway `secrets.json` of dummy values.
  - With every parameter set, it reached `aspire run` without a prompt.
  - With one missing, it asked only for that one and stopped before the image build.
- A run that asks nothing left `secrets.json`'s write time and SHA-256 unchanged.
- `sources.yml` parses to the `Source` shape `migrate-cli.ts` reads, with all 11 states mapped to a Project 4 option.
- `npm run typecheck` exits 0. Unit tests: 421, 419 passed, 0 failed, 2 skipped, both opt-in (the GitHub contract and the live Haiku test).
- A real `npm run factory` from the main checkout hasn't run yet. It's the owner's first step of Step 3.

## Review

The local `self-reviewer` took 2 rounds. Round 1 found 3 issues: every start rewrote the live secrets file, a failed pull blamed a cause it couldn't know, and Failed and Abandoned left stale statuses on the board. All three are fixed in ff29e30, and round 2 answered APPROVED.

author: csoai-org
body:
#4043 merged a sentence that was true when it was written and is **not true now**. This corrects it forward.

**What landed:** *"The digest comparison needs the BUILT tree: the index hashes the bytes the site ships from, so without `--served-root dist/client` the digests are UNCHECKABLE, not clean."*

**Why it stopped being true.** The producer now asks **the injector** for the served HTML bytes when there is no built tree: `scripts/surface/served-html-digests.mjs` imports `scripts/inject-workspace-launcher.mjs` and calls its exported `injectLauncher` — **the same transform the build uses, imported rather than re-implemented**.

**MEASURED here, independently** (not taken on trust), on a committed page:

```
public/interop/art50-hub-queue-2026-09/index.html
  committed            4,379 B   sha256 cf697b2e783128ee7117268ab41a211382621f004c009ab3598419d908a795b9
  after injectLauncher        sha256 5e931d20d1cc99866cd86acda61e4521b68dec0e79c041fa7cf59826107271fe
  byte delta                  63 B
```

**4,379 + 63 = 4,442 B** — which is the built file's size. The transform reproduces the built bytes exactly, because the build applies exactly this transform. So **a check with no built tree is faithful for every row**, and the index matches whether it is compared against the built tree or against the injector.

`UNCHECKABLE` is now what the producer says **only if the injector itself cannot be run**.

## The change

Text only — no step, trigger, exit code or measurement changes. The repair instruction becomes:

```
python3 scripts/build-interop-file-index.py --check public/interop \
  public/interop/file-index.json scripts/deploy-exclusions.json
```

…with the explanation that the digests are of the bytes **as published**: without a built tree the producer asks the injector what it would write for each HTML page; with a built tree it reads the built file; either way the comparison is faithful.

## A note on the push

Pushed with `--no-verify`, using the escape hatch the hook itself names, because the pre-push `trigger-coupling` check is a **false positive on a correct tree** — the shell copy in `scripts/pre-push-gates.sh` does a literal `grep -qF` for `deploy.yml`'s raw name, while `workflow_run.workflows` takes **glob filters**, so the five followers correctly carry `Build \+ deploy site (…)` and the canonical checker CI runs (`scripts/workflow-trigger-coupling.mjs`) passes 5 of 5 where the shell copy fails 4. The fix for that is the DC lane's, in #4014, which is no longer a draft. **Once #4014 lands the gate is gone and this push needs no bypass.**

Refs: #4043, #4014.

author: aj0070
body:
### Problem description
`ttnn.experimental.isin(..., out=out)` checked only the dtype of the preallocated output. The writer always stores `logical_volume(elements)` uint32 values into `out` as one flat row-major row, so an `out` with fewer elements got the mask written past the end of its DRAM buffer, and an `out` with another shape or a TILE layout came back with wrong values. Nothing raised.

### What's changed
- `create_output_tensors` now requires the preallocated output to be uint32, have the flattened elements shape `[N]`, be ROW_MAJOR, interleaved, allocated and on device, and raises a clear TT_FATAL otherwise.
- New tests in `test_isin.py`: a correct preallocated output still gets the right mask, and a smaller output, a `[1, N]` output, an input-shaped `[2, 95]` output and a TILE output are rejected.

### Verification (Wormhole N150)
Main dbc10eb0a4c, Wormhole N150, the changed test files with the new tests, on main and with the change:
- `test_isin.py`: 4 failed, 10 passed on main; 14 passed with the change.

### Checklist
- [x] New/Existing tests provide coverage for changes

body:
The features for 1.3.10-rc.1, and the version bump.

**Icons follow Interface Text Size.** `--chrome-scale` (the text scale, ×1.15 in full screen on the Mac) sizes the title bar (`--window-bar-height`, which also replaces the 28px everywhere the layout clears the bar), the header row, icon buttons, the window's caption buttons, sidebar tabs and the tree's icons. Buttons are sized with `calc`, glyphs with `scale`, no `zoom`. The phone keeps scale 1.

**Sidebar new file/folder.** New Document and New Folder stay in the Files toolbar. The new item is named in place (a row with a field, prefilled with a free name: Untitled, Untitled 2…); Enter or clicking away makes it, Escape or an empty name doesn't. A double-click on the tree's blank space makes a document in the root, and an empty root says so. Right-click › New Document/New Folder use the same row. The toolbar's Open Project… button goes, to make room: it stays in File, on the start page, and as the "Open as Project" link under the toolbar.

**Clipboard History is a plugin.** The core's history (the sidebar tab, its Privacy section and setting, the capture listeners) is removed. Copy and cut in the editor, source mode, a code block's Copy button and Copy as Plain Text now call `tellCopied`, which the window passes to plugins as `textus.env.onDidCopy` (plugin API 1.3, the existing `clipboard` permission). The plugin is catvinci.clipboard-history (CatVinci-Studio/textus-plugins#34). Users who had history entries are offered it once on the suggestion card ("… is a plugin now"); the old entries aren't migrated.

body:
Closes #104.

## What
- **The card:** when a route has some, but not all, of its stops visited, a **Continue your walk** card appears above the routes. It shows the route, the progress ("Al-Muizz Street Route · 2 of 7 stops"), the next stop ("Next stop: Al-Aqmar Mosque"), and a **Continue** button.
- **Continue:** selects that route and opens walk mode. The walk starts at the first unvisited stop, the same stop the card names.
- **Which route:** the route on screen if it's part-way; otherwise the one with the most stops visited, then the first. The logic is `routeToContinue` in `src/lib/walk-summary.ts`, with tests.
- **Not now (×):** hides the card for the rest of the visit (sessionStorage). It comes back next time.
- **When it's hidden:** while walking, and while the finish screen is open.
- **Offline and languages:** it reads only the visited marks on the device, so it works offline, in all four languages. The Arabic count is written "المحطات: 2 من 7" to avoid number agreement. README updated.

## Checks
- Type check passes, and 592 tests pass, including 4 new ones:

author: hanzlamateen
body:
## Summary

A browser that used an app before the Hub's sign-in was put in front of it could stay stuck on the app's old cached page for good, Companion Memory's "Can't reach Memory" for example. The browser can't fetch the app's new service worker, because the sign-in turns that fetch away too. Now a signed-out browser gets a small worker from the Hub that removes the old one, so the next page load reaches the sign-in. Nothing of the app becomes reachable without signing in.

## Example

Open Memory in a browser, let the sign-in go on (or the session lapse), update Memory, then open it again while signed out.

Before, every visit shows Memory's cached page, served by its old worker:

![Before: the cached page, every visit](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d39f2025-103d-4739-8519-42f472502714)

After, the first visit goes to the Hub's sign-in. After signing in, Memory loads and registers its own worker again.

## Try it locally

```sh
pnpm install
pnpm --filter @ci-hub/common build
cd packages/backend
pnpm exec vitest run src/modules/docker src/modules/auth src/modules/apps src/tests/traefik-sw-reset-config.test.ts
```

To see it end to end you need Traefik in front of an app with the sign-in on: put the `ci-hub-sw-reset` middleware from `assets/traefik/dynamic/dynamic.yml` and the app's routers from `TraefikLabelsBuilder` (`exposureMode: 'cloudflare'`, `enableAuth: true`) in a Traefik v3.6 file config, with the forward auth pointing at a local Hub backend. Then `curl -H 'Service-Worker: script' http://<app host>/sw.js` signed out returns the reset worker, without the header it returns the sign-in redirect, and with a session it returns the app's own file.

## Detail

- **Endpoint:** `GET /api/auth/service-worker-reset.js` serves a fixed worker (`application/javascript`, `Cache-Control: no-store`). On install it calls `skipWaiting()`. On activate it unregisters itself and reloads the app's open pages. It fetches nothing, caches nothing and holds nothing of any app.
- **Forward auth:** a signed-out request that carries `Service-Worker: script` gets a 401 instead of the sign-in redirect. A browser refuses a redirect for a worker script anyway.
- **Middleware:** `ci-hub-sw-reset` in `dynamic.yml` is Traefik's `errors` middleware. It catches only that 401, serves the Hub's worker in its place and rewrites the status to 200 (`statusRewrites`, already used by `ci-hub-app-starting`). An app's own 302 or 403 for its `/sw.js` reaches the browser untouched; an app's own 401 there gets the reset worker too.
- **Routers:** for every app with the sign-in on its public routes, `TraefikLabelsBuilder` adds `<app>-sw-reset` (websecure) and `<app>-sw-reset-insecure` (web, the one the tunnel uses). Each matches the app's host rule plus `Path(/sw.js) && Header(Service-Worker, script)`, with the same chain as the app's router and the reset middleware in front of the forward auth. Service and TLS are the app's own. They set no priority: Traefik ranks them above the app router only because their rule is longer, and only for that one request.
- **Which apps:** apps on This machine only and on Tailscale have no Hub sign-in on their routes, so they get no reset routers and nothing changes for them (builder tests cover both). This applies to every app behind the sign-in, not just Memory, since all the worker can do is remove a worker for a signed-out visitor.
- **Names:** `ci-hub-sw-reset` and the `-sw-reset` router suffixes are reserved, so an app can't define them. The CLI's bundled copy of `dynamic.yml` is regenerated, and a test ties the middleware's query to the endpoint's route.

**Existing installs:** the middleware arrives with the Hub update, like the rest of `dynamic.yml`. The routers are labels on the app's containers, so an installed app gets them the next time its containers are recreated: an app update, a reinstall or a settings change that restarts it. Until then it behaves as before. A Memory update that ships the fix from Companion-Memory#3402 recreates Memory, so Memory picks this up with that release.

**What a signed-out request gets, through Traefik v3.6** with the branch's routers and middleware and the branch's backend:

| Request | Answer | Body |
|---|---|---|
| GET `/sw.js` with `Service-Worker: script` | 200 application/javascript | the Hub's reset worker |
| GET `/sw.js` without the header | 302 | the sign-in |
| HEAD `/sw.js` with the header | 200 | headers only |
| POST `/sw.js` with the header | 200 | the Hub's reset worker |
| `/sw.js?x=1` with the header | 200 | the Hub's reset worker |
| `/sw.js/x` (prefix) with the header | 401 | nothing |
| `/sw.jsx` with the header | 401 | nothing |
| `/%73w.js` (encoded) with the header | 200 | the Hub's reset worker (Traefik decodes it to `/sw.js`) |
| `/x/../sw.js` (dot segment) with the header | 200 | the Hub's reset worker (Traefik resolves it) |
| `/index.html`, `/api/graphql`, `/` with the header | 401 | nothing |
| signed in, GET `/sw.js` with the header | 200 text/javascript | the app's own `sw.js`, same sha256 as the app serves |

Without the reset routers the same signed-out requests all get the sign-in's refusal and no app content either. In no row does a signed-out request reach the app.

**In Chromium** (Memory's built files behind that Traefik, an old Memory worker installed, then signed out):

```
without the routers: visit 1 and 2 -> Memory's cached page, from the old worker
with the routers:    visit 1 -> the Hub's edge sign-in; visit 2 -> same, not from a worker
                     signed in -> Memory loads and its own worker is active
```

**Checks:** docker, auth and apps suites (2,840 tests), the new lock-step test, the common schema tests (519), `test:cli` (3,397), the backend typecheck, biome and `check:openapi`.

**Not covered:**
- **Manifest overrides:** an app whose manifest replaces its router rule through `extraLabels` (Kimai, IPFS) keeps the builder's host rule on the reset routers. A very long replacement rule could outrank them, so those apps may not get the reset.
- **Other worker paths:** a worker served from another path than `/sw.js` isn't covered.
- **Push subscriptions:** unregistering drops the worker's push subscriptions, which the app sets up again after sign-in.

Not tried: a real Hub with Traefik, the tunnel and an installed Memory.

Fixes #2324

author: mizzy
body:
Closes #4314

## Problem

#4310 made provider text opaque. Create and read take a typed partial-read reason (`PartialReadDiagnostic::<S>::new(reason: S::PartialReadReason, ..)`). `UpdateOutcome::partial_success` still took `reason: String`. A provider that holds the cause as a `ProviderError` / `ProviderFailure` cannot turn it into a `String`, because unbound provider text has no `Display`. So carina-provider-aws and carina-provider-awscc cannot bump to v0.12.0 without either dropping the AWS cause or stringifying provider text.

## Fix

- `UpdateOutcome<S>::partial_success(state, reason: S::PartialReadReason, missing)` now builds through `PartialReadDiagnostic::new`, the same path create and read use. For `Unbound`, `S::PartialReadReason` is `ProviderText`, so `reason.into()` works from an opaque `ProviderError` and from an authored string literal alike. The crate-private test helper `CreateOutcome::partial_success` gets the same shape.
- The protocol and WIT update decoders wrap the incoming reason as `ProviderText`, matching the create and resume decoders.
- The sweep of public entry points in carina-core, carina-plugin-sdk, carina-plugin-host and carina-provider-protocol found one more slot that could only take a string: the SDK's `CarinaProvider::validate_config` and `initialize` returned `Result<_, String>`. They now return the structured protocol `ProviderError`, like the CRUD methods. The guest carries it over the WIT `provider-error` record those exports already return (WIT unchanged).
- No plaintext accessor, no `From<ProviderError> for String`, and no `Display` on `Unbound` are added. The #4310 type table is unchanged, and its compile_fail doctests still pass.

The other String-taking constructors that were checked are fine. They take a new provider-authored message that becomes `Unbound` text (`ProviderError::api_error`, `ProviderText::from(String)`), or host-authored text, or protocol DTO fields. Each also has a typed path that carries an opaque cause.

## Tests (written failing first)

- A native provider builds an update partial-read reason from `ProviderError::api_error_caused_by` with a secret in the cause. Before the fix this did not compile (`String: From<ProviderFailure>`). Now it runs through `ProviderBoundary`, the real executor and CLI, and the local backend. The persisted `partial_read.pending.reason.detail` and stderr show the cause masked, exactly like the create twin test.
- compile_fail doctests (E0308) pin that the update reason and the SDK config/initialize errors cannot be `String`.
- SDK test: a typed config failure keeps every protocol field (kind, cause, status, code, request id).

## aws / awscc adaptation (for the v0.12.1 bump)

`partial_success` call sites. There are 5 calls: aws 1, awscc 4. 3 of them need edits.

| Repo | Site | Change |
|---|---|---|
| aws | `carina-provider-aws/src/provider.rs:3608` | `reason.to_string()` → `reason.into()` |
| awscc | `src/main.rs:1698` | none (`"arn omitted".into()` infers `ProviderText`) |
| awscc | `src/provider/operations.rs:2460` | `reason.to_string()` → `reason.into()` |
| awscc | `src/provider/operations.rs:3169` | `reason` → `reason.into()` |
| awscc | `src/provider/operations.rs:3525` | none (`"read failed".into()`) |

SDK `validate_config` / `initialize` implementations change their return type to `Result<_, proto::ProviderError>`:

- aws: `src/main.rs:590`, `:611`; `tests/guest_read_back_winterbaume.rs:366`, `:369`; `carina-aws-types/tests/elbv2_sdk_dispatch.rs:63`, `:67`.
- awscc: `src/main.rs:779`, `:798` and the `provider_config_decode_error` helper at `:90`; `tests/guest_read_back.rs:52`, `:55`.
- Two tests that expect an error message bind it first with `let err = err.message;` (aws `src/main.rs:1810`, awscc `src/main.rs:2000`). Their assertions stay the same.

body:
Implements roadmap items **1.8 Attributes and specifications** and **1.6 Variants** in the inventory service. Variants are represented as attributes such as size or color.

- Adds an optional, ordered list of key-value `attributes` to `Product`, the add/update commands and requests, `ProductResponse` and `ProductJpaEntity`
- `PUT /product` replaces the whole list, so omitting `attributes` clears it; a blank key or value returns 400; duplicate keys are allowed
- New `product_attribute` table in the initial `1.xml` changeset; seed data added for Laptop and Skirt
- Marks 1.6 and 1.8 as done in `.docs/domain-expansion.md`

**Avoiding N+1 queries on lists**

- Attributes are lazy, so `GET /product` and `GET /product/ids` no longer run a query per product
- Those two endpoints now return a new `ProductSummaryResponse` with no `attributes` field
- `GET /product/{id}` loads attributes with a single join query

**For reviewers**

- Products from `getProducts` and `getByIds` have an empty attribute list, so saving one deletes its attributes. Code that loads products in order to save them must use `getById` or `getByIdsWithAttributes`
- `UpdateProductQuantitiesCommandService` now uses `getByIdsWithAttributes` for this reason, with a test covering it
- `saveProducts` still merges each product separately, which was left as is because users can't easily spam the purchase flow

**Tests**

- Hibernate statistics confirm list queries load no attribute collections
- Attributes survive a purchase save
- Read, update, purchase and delete paths work without a surrounding transaction

`./gradlew check` passes locally.

body:
Connects the command lane to Discord and adds the first real command, `/config get`. After this, the bot registers its slash commands at startup and answers `/config get` for the owner.

## Changes
- Startup:
  - `prepare_database` now returns the open, migrated connection, and closes it itself only if migration fails.
  - `main()` passes the connection, the command registry and the config to `MaikaClient`.
  - `main()` closes the connection after the client stops, including after a crash or a rejected token.
- `bot.py`: `MaikaClient` has a command tree. `setup_hook` adds the `/config` group, installs `handle_tree_error`, and syncs once, logging "Synced N slash command(s)." A failed sync is logged and the bot keeps running.
- `slash_commands.py`: the `/config` group ("View and change settings (owner only)") with `get` and its `key` parameter. The callback calls `handle_command`.
- `config_commands.py`: `config_get` and the `config get` definition: key `config.get`, owner-only, category Owner, private reply.
- The reply has three lines:
  - `` `<key> = <value>` (default|changed) ``
  - the setting's description
  - `Type: …. Range: …. Default: ….`
- On the third line, a text setting with fixed choices shows `Choices: …` in place of Range, and a setting with neither leaves that part out.
- How values display:
  - bool as true or false, and None as none;
  - a time in its stored form (`04:00`);
  - a list as its items joined by ", ", or `empty list`;
  - a backtick as an apostrophe, so the code formatting holds.
- An unknown key returns NOT_FOUND: "I don't know a setting called `<key>`."
- `command_catalog.py`: `build_command_registry()` collects every command definition into one registry.
- `settings_store.py`: `lookup_value` returns the value and whether a stored row supplied it. `get_value` now uses it and behaves as before.
- `settings.py`: `describe_range` for display ("1 to 365", "at least 1", "at most 10").
- `discord_adapter.py`: `guild_id_from_interaction`, shared by the context builder and the callback.
- `command_runner.py`: docstring fix: only calls that reach a permission decision produce a usage

## Design edits
- 8 (Parking Lot): build one combined settings registry when the first feature adds settings; decide at friend-server go-live whether to hide owner-only commands from the picker with `default_member_permissions`.

## Tests
- `tests/db/test_config_commands.py`:
  - default and changed values, the server and global lookup, and an unknown key;
  - none, time, bool, list, empty-list and backtick values;
  - range, choices, and neither on the third line;
  - `display_value`, `describe_range` and `lookup_value`.
- `tests/db/test_config_get_command.py`:
  - the registry entry;
  - a non-owner refused at the owner-only step, at every level and through `handle_command`;
  - the tree after `setup_hook` (with a fake sync), the error handler, the sync log wording, and a failed sync;
  - the callback for the owner, an unknown key, a non-owner and a DM.
- `tests/unit/test_main.py`: the connection stays open while the bot runs and is closed after a normal exit, a crash, a failed migration and a rejected token.
- `tests/unit/test_bot_close.py`: updated for the new client arguments.

## Out of scope
`/config set`, `reset`, `list` and `channels`; key autocomplete; Discord log channels; `/perm` and `/block`; the daily backup task; signal handling; and the message handler.

author: cshum
body:
## What

`IMAGOR_AUTO_JXL` / `-imagor-auto-jxl` / `WithAutoJXL`, the JPEG XL counterpart of `IMAGOR_AUTO_WEBP`, `IMAGOR_AUTO_AVIF` and `IMAGOR_AUTO_JPEG`. A request that asks for no format is served JPEG XL when the client sends `Accept: image/jxl`.

Closes #872.

## Negotiation

JPEG XL ranks above AVIF, WebP and JPEG. When the client accepts more than one of them the response carries a `fallback_format` for the next one down, so a build whose libvips has no libjxl answers AVIF or WebP instead of failing:

| Accept | filters applied |
| --- | --- |
| `image/jxl,image/avif,image/webp` | `format(jxl):fallback_format(webp)` |
| `image/jxl,image/avif` | `format(jxl):fallback_format(avif)` |
| `image/jxl` | `format(jxl)` |
| `image/avif,image/webp` | unchanged: `format(avif):fallback_format(webp)` |

WebP is the fallback whenever the client accepts it. It animates, so an animated source keeps moving rather than flattening to a still JPEG XL; a libvips without libjxl lands on it too.

Explicit `format()` still wins over all of it, and `Vary: Accept` comes from the existing `Imagor-Auto-Format` marker.

## Encoding

libvips encodes JPEG XL at effort 7. The encoder now uses **effort 5**: on a 1600x1067 photo at Q80, 54 ms and 104,458 bytes against 107 ms and 105,164 bytes at effort 7. Effort 4 is 26 ms but 116,330 bytes.

Quality is untouched: it stays the libvips default (75) and `quality()` decides it when the URL asks for one.

## Docs

- `configuration.md` — a `### Auto format` subsection under `## imagor Core`: the `Accept` to output mapping, the WebP fallback, and that `q` values are not read, `Vary: Accept` is set and each format is cached under its own key.
- `image-endpoint.md` — the `## Image Formats` paragraph links it, so a reader asking "how do I get AVIF" finds it from the URL page.
- `security.mdx` — the list of auto formats is gone from the SVG pass-through section. Which encoder renders the SVG does not change whether a script in it runs, and the list went stale with every format added.

## Tests

- `TestAutoJXL`, and `TestAutoFormatPrecedence` extended to the four formats, covering precedence, the fall-through when JXL is not accepted, and both fallbacks.
- `TestProcessor/vips_jxl_keeps_the_libvips_quality`: no `quality()` leaves the encoder at the libvips default, and `quality(90)` grows the file.
- Config flag parsing.

`go test . ./imagorpath/ ./svg/ ./config/...` passes. The `vipsprocessor` package fails 59 golden tests locally, the same 59 on `master` (fonts and animation goldens), compared by parsing `go test -json` on both trees rather than by grepping the output.
