## Summary

- Show pricing-table changes in the menu and offer an explicit, confirmed asynchronous **Rebuild last 180 days** action. Retain progress across menu dismissal, prevent duplicate clicks/manual refresh, reconcile after failures, and never retry automatically.
- Replace the bar chart with a GitHub-style 180-local-day token heatmap: green intensity, date/token/estimated-cost tooltips, distinct missing versus zero cells, calendar/DST handling, and accessibility labels. Today/7-day/30-day summary totals and rankings remain unchanged.
- Extend the collector's daily snapshot and explicit rebuild limit to 180 days; include package changesets and documentation.

Closes #37.

Consolidates #52 at the owner's request: retire Plan 0001, preserve its Git history, and move current architecture, validation limits and backup-first backend recovery guidance into maintained documentation. The recovery guide explicitly warns that re-pairing clears cached remote history and complete recovery requires every device's own retained data or verified backups. #50 continues to track deferred signing verification.

## Spec

The heatmap reads stored aggregate buckets only, without scanning source logs. It anchors 180 local dates to the snapshot's timestamp and timezone. Summary totals retain their original windows. An old snapshot with only 30 daily entries shows earlier dates as missing, not zero.

Rebuild uses the existing atomic replace-and-rescan transaction. Deleted source logs cannot be recovered, and their old usage is zeroed, including after sync to other devices; the destructive confirmation states this before execution. Uploads replace each device/hour/agent/model bucket rather than incrementing it. No synchronization redesign or automatic rebuild is introduced.

## Plan

1. Add pricing-state and asynchronous confirmed rebuild UI with fake process-runner tests.
2. Expand the supported rebuild range and snapshot daily history independently from summary windows.
3. Add the calendar heatmap and generated-data tests for boundaries, DST, missing days, tooltips, repeated rebuilds, and sync retries.
4. Retire the accepted plan and consolidate current guides, preserving the 180-day feature behavior and recovery prerequisites.
5. Validate repository and native builds; leave this PR unmerged for review. No real agent session files or production rebuilds are used.

## Validation

- `corepack pnpm run check`: passed (format/build/lint/typecheck; collector 347, protocol 17, worker 63, scripts 14 tests).
- Isolated temporary-HOME `swift test --package-path apps/macos/SnorlaxKit`: 98 tests passed.

- Synthetic 180-day rebuild repeated twice preserves counts; older out-of-window buckets stay unchanged; deleted synthetic logs explicitly zero their buckets. Existing paired-sync retry/reset test now exercises the 180-day rebuild; server absolute-upsert tests pass.
- After integrating #52: `corepack pnpm run check`, repository checks, Markdown local-link validation and `git diff --check` passed. The integration only changes documentation; prior native 98-test results remain applicable.
- Light/dark native SwiftUI renders with synthetic data were visually inspected; token and price columns are individually aligned. This is not a production app run.
- Heatmap adds a bounded 180-cell model and no additional ledger query or source-log scan. Real-data performance and production interactive UI were not measured; no production app was launched.
- Repository/title/body checks and `git diff --check` run before push. GitHub CI is checked separately after push.

body:
Hoort bij thewally/ontwikkelstraat#54

## Samenvatting
Frontend-deel van de Auth0-login, achter de build-vlag `VITE_AUTH_PROVIDER` (standaard `supabase`, dan verandert er niets).

- `@auth0/auth0-react` 2.x, `Auth0AuthProvider` (`src/context/Auth0AuthContext.jsx`) vult dezelfde `AuthContext` (`user`, `profile`, `loading`, `signIn`, `signOut`, `userRoles`, `hasRole`, `hasAnyRole`); `useAuth` en `ProtectedRoute` blijven ongewijzigd.
- Rollen uit claim `https://vvz49.nl/roles` van het access token, met terugval op het ID-token; `admin` komt overal bij.
- `LoginPage`: in Auth0-modus redirect naar Universal Login, `returnTo` gevalideerd (geen open redirect); mislukte terugkeer (bijv. `access_denied`) toont een Nederlandse melding (`AuthFoutMelding`, plus op `/login`).
- `/wachtwoord-vergeten` roept in Auth0-modus `POST https://<domein>/dbconnections/change_password` aan en toont altijd de neutrale melding (alleen een netwerkfout is een fout).
- `getAccessToken()` in `src/services/auth0Token.js` voor #60/#62.
- `VerslagEditPage`: `author_id` alleen bij een UUID.
- In Auth0-modus redirecten `/wachtwoord-instellen`, `/wachtwoord-resetten` en `/email-bevestigd` naar `/login`.
- Ontbrekende `VITE_AUTH0_DOMAIN` of `VITE_AUTH0_CLIENT_ID` in Auth0-modus geeft een configuratiefout via de error boundary.

## Hoe te testen
- `npm test` (nieuw: `tests/auth0.test.mjs`: rollen uit claim, returnTo, resetaanroep, UUID) en `npm run build`.
- Auth0-modus: zet in `.env.local` `VITE_AUTH_PROVIDER=auth0`, `VITE_AUTH0_DOMAIN`, `VITE_AUTH0_CLIENT_ID`, `VITE_AUTH0_AUDIENCE` en draai `npm run dev` (`http://localhost:5173/vvz-toolbox/`). Vereist een Auth0 SPA-applicatie met callback-URL voor localhost (zie README).
- Regressie: zonder vlag inloggen met een Supabase-account en `/beheer` openen.

## Configuratie
Nieuwe publieke variabelen `VITE_AUTH_PROVIDER`, `VITE_AUTH0_DOMAIN`, `VITE_AUTH0_CLIENT_ID`, `VITE_AUTH0_AUDIENCE`, `VITE_AUTH0_CONNECTION` (README, `.env.example`, `deploy.yml` via GitHub Actions-variabelen `AUTH_PROVIDER` enz.). Leeg laten bij mergen; omschakelen pas als #55, #42 en #60/#62 klaar zijn. Geen migraties.

Terugdraaien: vlag leegmaken en opnieuw deployen, of de PR reverten.

author: voodoomods
body:
A `checked` on a claim that cites a lesser source is refused until the reviewer has opened the better source the record holds.

## What happened
K1 (the Ashby archive), two consecutive full rounds of main (ho1, ho2, 2026-11-07): Q3 "who formally opened the footbridge" settled on "formally opened by the Mayor in 1889", citing the 2004 visitor guide (kind tertiary), review note "the source is tertiary but provides direct evidence … no contradictory source found". The record cites the 1887 council minutes (primary) on Q1, and they say "opened to the public on … 14 June 1887 … without ceremony beyond a short address"; the 1962 society history agrees. The telemetry shows what the fact checker read before checking: ho2 the guide and RETRACTIONS.md; ho1 the guide and two `find`s. Never the minutes. The knowledge brief already says a primary source outranks a later summary and to list what else is there before relying on a source; the model doesn't do it unprompted. Over all 25 K1 records on disk, Q3 settled 22 times, 19 right and 3 on the Mayor (base3, ho1, ho2) — and every time a reviewer looked at the Mayor claim, it was checked (3 of 3).

## The gate
`review(verdict="checked")` on a claim with `cites` links: for every live source node in the investigation whose kind outranks the worst kind the claim cites (primary < secondary < tertiary; unknown counts as secondary), that is a file the seat can open (`file:…` or a bare relative path), is not withdrawn, and is not in the order's `read` list — refuse, naming it: "CL3 cites a tertiary source, and the record holds a primary one you haven't read: S1 (archive/council-minutes-1887.md). A primary source outranks a later summary of it, and a check that never opened it can't say they agree. read_file('archive/council-minutes-1887.md'), then give your verdict from both." After the read, checked or objection is recorded. Never on an objection; nothing outside the worker loop (`state["read"] is None`).

## Measured
- **Replay of the two recorded failures.** On copies of the ho1 and ho2 records, with the checker's read list set to what the telemetry shows (ho2: guide + RETRACTIONS.md; ho1: guide), `review(CL3/CL2, checked, …)` is refused and names S1 (archive/council-minutes-1887.md); with the minutes added to the list, the objection is recorded and the claim goes contested.
- **Four live K1 runs on the box with the gate (sr1–sr4, gpt-oss-20b, 160 calls):** Q3 settled right 4 of 4, 63 / 63 / 82 / 117 calls. The gate never fired: no claim cited the guide, so the 4 of 4 is the base rate, not the gate. No cost seen.
- **A fresh knowledge challenge, K3 (`studies/challenges/k3_lighthouse`, written before any run):** same trap shape, new content, bait set higher — the tertiary leaflet sorts first in `archive/` and answers every question with a ducal inauguration; the keeper's log (primary) says "No ceremony … no other person". **Eight runs on this branch and eight on main** (a worktree without the gate), alternating, same model and budget. Q1 and Q2 right in all sixteen. Q3:

  | arm | right | wrong | unsettled | runs that filed the Duke claim |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | gate (g1–g8) | 3 | 1 | 4 | 3 of 8 (g4, g6, g8) |
  | main (m1–m8) | 6 | 0 | 2 | 1 of 8 (m2) |

  **The gate arm did not beat main.** The difference sits in which runs took the bait: the researcher files the Duke claim before any review exists, so the gate can't have caused 3 of 8 against 1 of 8 (that is chance), and a run that files it spends its reviews on it — g6 and g8 ran out of budget (140, 147 calls) with every Duke claim objected to and the right answer unchecked or unwritten. Inside those runs the gate did what it says: of 9 reviews of a Duke claim, each refused until the reviewer had opened the log, **8 were objections and 1 a check** (k3g4 CL9, after reading the log and the certificate: "Primary sources provide context but do not refute the claim. Tertiary source confirms it"; Q3 settled on it). On main the one Duke claim (k3m2) never reached a reviewer, so there is no same-challenge number for the decision without the gate; the nearest is K1 on main, where every reviewed Mayor claim was checked (3 of 3). K3's log is blunter than K1's minutes ("no other person"), so that comparison flatters the gate.
- Verbatim re-filing of an objected claim, which is how k3g4 got four draws at a reviewer: 5 copies across all 387 records on disk before K3, 2 of them later checked. Rare; not built here.

So: the gate turns a check-without-reading into a read, and after the read this model objects 8 times in 9. It does not raise the settle rate, it costs calls in the runs that need it, and one reviewer in nine checks over the primary it just read.

## Checks
- 338 tests pass (7 new in `tests/test_source_rank.py`), ruff clean.
- Not changed: the writer's side (the researcher who cites the guide), the trading and software profiles, the re-filing of an objected claim.

author: cjcormack
body:
Session 1 of the [FX speed plan](docs/plans/fx-speed-plan.md): *Seconds* becomes **Own tempo**.

A beat FX on Seconds read its `cycle` as seconds and followed no master. That made "slow and independent of the tempo" a different unit from every other FX, and the next sessions want one Speed slider and a Tap that work the same on a master and off one. So a beat FX now runs on a speed master or on its own tempo, `ownBpm` (20–300), with `cycle` still in beats at that tempo. A wall-clock FX keeps its cycle in seconds and runs on a rate master or *Natural* (no rate master), and never takes an Own tempo.

What changed:

- **Engine.** An Own-tempo FX runs on the wall-clock loop as Seconds did, its accumulator advancing at `ownBpm / 60` over the stored beats. A new tempo is written in place and moves only the rate, so the phase is kept. Moving between a master and Own tempo is still a swap that restarts the phase. The engine's wall-clock pass, the sampler and the preview's clock each read the Own tempo as the rate; missing any one of them would run an Own FX at 120.
- **Storage and sync.** `own_bpm` replaces `seconds` on `look_fx`, `cue_ad_hoc_fx` and `palette_fx`. Database step 12 (`OwnTempoMigration`) rewrites every Seconds FX as Own tempo 120 at twice its cycle, which runs to the same bytes (`OwnTempoEquivalenceTest` runs both over a grid of cycles, offsets, directions and runs). A wall-clock FX on Seconds becomes Natural. Then the step drops the columns, taking a backup first when it changes anything. Sync goes to `formatVersion` 49 with `minReader` 49, because a v48 reader would run an Own FX on master 1. The importer reads an older archive's `seconds` by the same rule.
- **Wire and MCP.** The FX routes, `updateFx`, the stored-FX writes and the MCP tools take `ownBpm` and `natural`. They still read `seconds`: given a cycle, it converts as the migration does; without one, the FX goes onto Own tempo at the tempo of the master it would have followed, keeping its speed. Reports carry `ownBpm` and `natural` in place of `seconds`.
- **Client.** The timing chip's *Seconds* is now *Own tempo* with a BPM field, and *Natural* on a wall-clock FX. Moving onto Own tempo starts it at the master's running tempo, so the speed doesn't change. Labels read `Own 96` where they read `4 s`. The Speed slider itself is session 3.

Two decisions the plan left to this session.

- **Telling wall-clock FX apart.** With no registry at database init, the step identifies a wall-clock FX by name, normalised the way the registry resolves names: a built-in, or one of the project's own FX definitions on the wall clock. An FX registered by a script can't be seen there, so the step reads it as a beat FX. It still runs at the seconds it meant: the spawn reads an Own tempo on a wall-clock FX as Natural at the equivalent cycle, and a stored write keeps it that way instead of refusing it. Every other wall-clock FX is refused an Own tempo (D4).
- **Masters on rewritten FX.** The rewrite drops the masters of every FX it touches, a wall-clock one's rate master included. Seconds already ignored them on spawn, and keeping them would change the output.

One accepted exception to "no output moves": a user wall-clock FX that reads its phase and was on Seconds ignored a layer's cycle and rate-master overrides. On Natural it takes them. Neither built-in reads either, and the plan's "As built" note records it.

---

author: himacharan128
body:
Refs #256

Fixes the iPhone flake in `e2e/support/motion.ts` (`holdTabChange` timing out on `waitForLoadState("networkidle")`). The cause is the mock worker, not the motion code.

**Cause**
MSW 2.15 reloads the page whenever no worker controls it and a mock registration exists, and it counts an installing or waiting worker as one (`get-worker-instance.ts`, `get-worker-by-registration.ts`). A test that leaves `/` while the first install is still running hands the next page exactly that. On WebKit the install appears never to finish, so every load reloads: CI run 42359607335 logged 112 commits for one test, and its retry passed. The WebKit stall itself is inferred from those logs.

**What changes**
- `mocks/start-browser.ts`: `dropStalledMockWorker()` runs before `worker.start`. It does nothing while a worker controls the page. Otherwise it unregisters only a registration with no active worker whose installing or waiting script is `/mockServiceWorker.js`. MSW then takes its first-visit path and registers again. A hard reload (no controller, an active worker) is left to MSW's own reload.
- `src/lib/dev/msw-start.test.ts`: four cases. A stalled worker is unregistered before `worker.start`, an active one is left alone, nothing is read while a worker controls the page, and the app's own `/sw.js` is left alone.
- Reached only when mocking is on: both callers (`msw-provider.tsx`, `client.ts` `awaitMocks`) check `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_MOCKING` first.

**How it was checked**
- Branched off origin/dev da99da5. 7aec59e is the fix; 2738080 is a plain merge of `dev` 3ba81d3e (app#305), which touches none of these files.
- Each head was reviewed and passed by the decider lane (prettier and tsc clean on the archived head).
- The server pre-push verify on this head: green on 2738080 (unit 364 files, 4,225 tests; contract matches yuvoy-api 84988635dfc0; prerender manifest matches, 31 routes; e2e 976 passed, 51 skipped, 0 failed, 0 flaky).
- The iPhone motion spec at `--repeat-each=5` on this head: green on 2738080, on the server: `e2e/motion-webkit.spec.ts --project=iphone --repeat-each=5 --retries=0`, 270 tests, 255 passed, 15 skipped, 0 failed, 0 flaky. The flaky test ("over a reel the pill is solid while the change runs, frosted after") passed all 5 times. With no retries, a flake would have shown as a failure.

## Summary

Implements the bounded F4.5.2 slice tracked by #319.

- Compiles valid closed Flow v1 definitions into immutable execution plans with stable heap-based topological ordering and SHA-256 plan identity.
- Stores a canonicalized FlowDefinition in each plan so equivalent node/edge tuple orderings produce equal plan values.
- Revalidates and canonically recompiles a supplied plan before evaluation so a fabricated or altered plan cannot bypass graph validation.
- Evaluates all 21 closed v1 node kinds against the existing immutable StrategyContext, returning existing StrategyResult / StrategySignal / passive TradeIntent values.
- Pins and versions Decimal semantics (precision 34, ROUND_HALF_EVEN, Emin/Emax, and explicit trap flags) independently of ambient context.

author: pr-minder[bot]
body:
## Summary

Moves the model catalog fetch off the blocking pool and adds structured `unified_log` warnings around the fetch path so startup catalog/session-model timing issues are visible in `~/.grok/logs/unified.jsonl`.

- `oai.rs`: splits `OaiModelSource::fetch` into shared helpers (`request_auth`, `parse_response`, `etag_of`) and adds `fetch_async`, which sends the same request on the async client with `STARTUP_FETCH_TIMEOUT`. Adds a test asserting the async fetch returns the same models as the blocking fetch.
- `model_source.rs` / `remote/mod.rs`: expose `fetch_active_models_async`.
- `fetch.rs`: adds `prefetch_models_async` (cache check, remote-fetch gate, async fetch, then commit) sharing result handling with the blocking path via `prefetch_from_result`. Logs a warning when the models listing is empty (with `url`) and when the models fetch fails (with `url`, `error`, `elapsed_ms`).
- `endpoint.rs`: `fetch_models_async` now calls `prefetch_models_async` directly instead of wrapping the blocking fetch in `spawn_blocking`, so a saturated blocking pool cannot stall the catalog.
- `manager/mod.rs`: logs a warning when the startup auth refresh times out (with `timeout_secs`) and when the catalog fetch times out (with `timeout_secs` and `has_auth`).

## Test notes

- New test `async_fetch_matches_blocking_fetch` verifies the async and blocking fetches return the same model IDs against a mock server.
- To inspect the new log output, run the pager and check `~/.grok/logs/unified.jsonl` for `model catalog:` entries.

## Risk

Low-to-moderate: the fetch path now runs on the async client rather than a blocking thread, which is the intended behavior change; request construction and response parsing are shared between both paths to keep them consistent. The added logging is diagnostic-only and does not change return values.

author: ersinkoc
body:
One I/O thread per terminal: PTY reader → bounded channel → actor → VT feed → `Snapshot`. The actor drains the command channel (input, resize, kill) before every output chunk, so input outranks output. API: `TerminalHandle::{start,send_input,resize,kill,snapshot,wait_change}`.

Also: `AlacrittyTerminal::with_scrollback` (agora-vt, additive) so the scrollback cap is configurable.

Tests (Unix): fake agent screen visible in snapshots and exit recorded; input + resize; a flooding terminal does not delay input to another terminal; scrollback cap.

Not in this PR: raw output fan-out to clients (needs the hub transport design), hot-path benchmark (P2-04).

author: gillesgoetsch
body:
After #728 (branched from rc-3.4.0 02e3a4e4; to be rebased once v3.4.0 is on main). See #727.

## What happens

With Omanotch on, the bar on the built-in display is parked while the notch strip shows: its window stays mapped, 1 px tall at y -1 (fully off screen), and reserves nothing. On clones of an Omarchy 4.0.3rc4 test VM on the M1 Max (hidden start, the test app's HDR on), the bar did not come back after the unpark in 4 of 4 runs (bar patch v36 and v37, 2026-11-06): Hyprland kept the layer at `0,-1 1120x1` with reserved top 0 for 20 s; `omarchy-toggle-bar` twice brought it back.

What the Mac mini's protocol trace shows (Qt's Wayland logging + `WAYLAND_DEBUG=client`, run r6, Omarchy 4.0, OmacVM's virtio-gpu driver at 8-bit):
- The parked bar's last frame (a 1320x1 buffer) is committed; Hyprland does not answer its frame callback for 3.1 s and Qt logs "Didn't receive frame callback in time, window should now be inexposed".
- At the unpark, Qt sends the new `set_size(0, 26)` / `set_margin(0, 0, 0, 0)` only after that callback is answered. On the mini it was answered 2.5 ms after the notifications layer (another surface of the shell on the same output) committed a frame at the unpark, so Hyprland drew that output again. The bar was back after 331-364 ms.
- So the parked bar's new size waits for the output to be drawn again for some other reason. If nothing else draws on it at that moment, the bar stays parked. That fits the M1 picture. It is shown on the mini's working path only. The M1 trace that would show the failing path is still owed (see below).

## Change

`src/omanotch/guest/bar/apply-patch.py`, bar patch v37 -> v38, in the window code that both forms (4.0 and 4.5) share: the existing `notchRemap` item now also unmaps the window for 100 ms when its role leaves `"parked"`, i.e. when the notch park ends (`notchParkEnd`, previous role stored, run at start and on `notchRoleChanged`). A new map does not wait for a frame callback, and it maps at the unparked size and margin. This is narrower than a remap on every `parked` change: Omarchy's own bar toggle (`barHidden`) does not change the role, and the NOTCH and FullPanel bars never have the parked role. So those keep Omarchy's fast path (margins only, the reason Omarchy 4.5 parks instead of unmapping). The new function is one of the patch's required pieces, so a v37 copy is patched again by Update VM (copies.py's three-way merge).

Docs: CHANGELOG under 3.4.1, a troubleshooting row in Omanotch's README, the v38 note in AGENTS.md.

## Tests

Offline (`src/omanotch/guest/tests/test.sh`): test_bar_patch.py 125 ok, test_copies.py 32 ok, start-limit and fullpanel-skip ok. New `ParkEnd` (5 tests) runs the patch's own `notchRoleFor` and `notchParkEnd` in node per window as QML runs them:
- the notch unpark remaps the parked window (2 cycles: 2 remaps), and so does a bar that started parked;
- no remap on Omarchy's bar toggle (4 toggles, 3 windows: 0), nor on the NOTCH or FullPanel bars;
- wired to `notchRoleChanged` in all three real shells (omarchy-mac ba546a61 = 4.0, a06ec133, ac2690cd = 4.5.0), and no `onParkedChanged`.

On 02e3a4e4 (v37) ParkEnd gives 4 ERROR + 1 FAIL (x3 shells); with this change 0.

Hidden VM rows on the Mac mini (one park/unpark per cycle; Hyprland's layer and reserved top read every 0.25 s):

| Run | Guest | Driver | Bar copy | Cycles stuck | Back after |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| r5 | 4.0.3rc4 clone of M-bb, 10 vCPUs | stock | v37 | 0 of 5 | 356-375 ms |
| r6 | same, "Draw only what changed" on | OmacVM's, 8-bit | v37 | 0 of 5 | 331-364 ms |
| r6 | same VM, Update VM to this branch (copy merged v37 -> v38) | OmacVM's, 8-bit | v38 | 0 of 3 | 335-343 ms |
| r7 | new Omarchy 4.5.0-3 VM (rc's create-vm.sh) | stock | v38 | 0 of 3 | 372-439 ms |

r6 v38 also ran the 3.4.0 kit's whole bar sequence (kit2): 27 ok, 0 FAIL, 4 info, incl. toasts under the parked bar and the FullPanel toast, NOTCH strip, clicks and hover, unpark 569 ms, 0 shell error lines. On Omarchy 4.5.0-3 (r7, new VM, v38) the same sequence: 26 ok, 2 FAIL, 3 info. The two FAILs (pick, twins-pick: a click at x 1217.5 in the strip, where a 4.5.0-3 tray icon `superwhisper.panel` and `omarchy.agents` overlap, lands on the other one) are not from this change: r8, a second new 4.5.0-3 VM, gives the same 26 ok, 2 FAIL with v37 (rc) and then with v38 applied over it (unpark 553 ms and 582 ms). Left for its own issue.

Packages on both mini guests: qt6-base 6.12.0-3, qt6-wayland 6.12.0-1, qt6-declarative 6.12.0-1, hyprland 0.56.2-7, mesa 26.2.5-1, linux-aarch64 7.2.11-1; quickshell 0.3.2-1 (4.0) and 0.3.2.r7.g2b4501a-1 (4.5). The bug never showed on the mini: 0 of 66 v37 cycles on 4.0 today (56 in the plan stage, 10 here), with or without OmacVM's driver at 8-bit. So the driver alone is not the trigger there. What is left is the M1's 10-bit HDR path on an M1 GPU.

## M1 Max rows (2026-11-07, lane rcm1-owed)

Hidden clones of the Omarchy 4.0.3rc4 test VM M1-td2 (10 vCPU, 3 GB, Virtual-1 2240x1240 at 120 Hz, scale 2), started by the test identity at rc-3.4.0; v37 = rc 02e3a4e4, v38 = bf5eb2f5 applied over it by `omacvm apply` (the Update VM path). Kits `work/open-1107/i727/kit/m1run5.sh` (m1b, 14:34-14:42), `work/rc-on-m1/owed/kit/i727/m1run6.sh` (m1c, 19:38-19:47; guest6.sh = guest5.sh with a working damage nudge) and `m1kit2.sh` (m1d, 19:51-19:58). Raw: `work/rc-on-m1/owed/raw/m1-727/` and `.../m1-fetch/i727/out/`.

| Row | Result |
|---|---|
| Packages (REQUIRED 1) | the mini's: qt6-base 6.12.0-3, qt6-wayland 6.12.0-1, qt6-declarative 6.12.0-2, quickshell 0.3.2-1, hyprland 0.56.2-7, mesa 26.2.5-1, linux-aarch64 7.2.11-1 |
| v37, HDR on (`/run/omacvm/virtio-gpu` = omacvm, XRGB2101010, cm hdr) | m1c: stuck 4 of 4 (`0,-1 1120x1`, reserved 0 for 15 s); m1b: stuck 3 of 7 (one more back only after 9.4 s) |
| v37, HDR off (no `/run/omacvm/virtio-gpu` = stock driver, XRGB8888, cm srgb) | m1c: stuck 4 of 4. So neither OmacVM's driver nor 10-bit is the trigger |
| Damage only (REQUIRED 2), each stuck m1c cycle: foot opened on Virtual-1 | foot mapped on Virtual-1 (`hyprctl clients`: monitor 0, mapped), its own 3 frame callbacks answered within 4 s, and the bar came back in 8 of 8 stuck cycles. (m1b's nudge was void: foot exited at once, its cwd /root was denied, no window; its "answered" counts were `wl_display.sync` callbacks.) |
| Trace of the failing path (m1b, debug shell) | the parked bar's frame callbacks were answered 2.4 s and 10.0 s after the request; Qt sent `set_size(0, 26)` 0.2 ms after the late answer (back after 9.4 s) |
| v38 over v37 (REQUIRED 4) | back 3 of 3 with HDR on (m1b, 349-355 ms) and 3 of 3 with HDR off (m1c, 343-350 ms); `notchParkEnd` in the copy, 0 shell error lines; kit2 (the 3.4.0 kit's bar sequence) on the M1 clone, m1d 19:51-19:58, HDR on: v37 26 ok, 1 FAIL (`unpark-time`: reserved top 0 for 20 s, the bug), 5 info; v38 over it 27 ok, 0 FAIL, twice (unpark 549 and 548 ms, toasts, `fullpanel-toast` 37 px under the 37 px strip, NOTCH strip, clicks, hover, 0 shell error lines). m1b's one `fullpanel-toast` FAIL with v38 (32 px) did not come back in these two runs |

What this shows: the M1 output is drawn when something on it changes, and other clients get their frame callbacks. The parked bar gets its callback only when the output is drawn again for something else; at the unpark nothing else draws on the M1 (on the mini the notifications layer does), so v37 waits. A redraw alone frees the bar, which is REQUIRED 2's condition for a display-path issue in its literal form. Not shown: why the mini redraws at the unpark and the M1 does not. Whether that gets its own issue is open; v38 does not depend on it (a new map does not wait for the callback).

## What is owed / needs a person

- **On screen:** every row here is a hidden start with the park driven over the bar's IPC, never a real exit from full screen in a window on screen. The on-screen check on the M1 (notch, HDR) is owed: VM in full screen including the

author: laurendarrah
body:
Closes #221

## What changed

The Backups page's encrypted download and restore now work at any size up to well past 10,000 families. The Worker streams the backup as lines of JSON, one batch at a time. The browser gzip-compresses and encrypts them into one file. A restore uploads the file in checked parts and applies them in one D1 batch. Files saved by the old page still open and restore.

## Why

At about 1,500 families the download refused, because the whole backup had to fit in one 12 MB response. Restore had the same limit: the old page also capped files at 9 MB. At 10,000 families the records come to about 99 MB, which would not fit in a Worker's 128 MB memory even without a response cap.

### Options considered

- **Compression alone** shrinks the file about 4.6 times, but the Worker would still build the whole backup in memory and the restore would still send the whole backup in one request. That works at 3,000 families (30 MB) but not at 10,000 (99 MB).
- **Numbered part files** means several downloads to keep together, and restore still has to send everything to the Worker.
- **R2** isn't set up, and it would still leave the restore problem.
- **Chosen: stream the export, compress and encrypt in the browser, restore in parts.** This keeps one file and one passphrase, and every protection the restore had: all or nothing, a recovery snapshot first, a check for changes since the preview, and existing records never overwritten. No new service is needed. Compression is part of it because it keeps the file at about a fifth of the size.

### How it works

- **Download.** `GET /api/backups?mode=lines` streams `lib/backup-records.ts` `backupLines()`: a header line (version 3, project, time, academy settings), then sections of up to 1,000 rows, or 250 for tables with long text. The last line has every section's row count. It is sent only after every row, so the page never saves a file that was cut short. If the export fails part way, the last line is `{"error": ...}` instead. Rows are read with the same keyset batches as before, and the Worker holds one batch at a time.
- **File format v2** (`public/security-backup.js`):
  - The file starts with one JSON line: `savage-encrypted-backup-v2`, the project, `AES-256-GCM`, `PBKDF2-SHA256`, 600,000 iterations, a random 16-byte salt and 12-byte IV, and `gzip`. The ciphertext follows that line.
  - The key derivation and cipher are the same as v1. The whole first line is the AES-GCM authenticated data, so changing any byte of it, even in a way that keeps its meaning, makes the file refuse to open.
  - The passphrase still never leaves the browser.
  - Compressing before encrypting is safe here: it is the owner's own records in the owner's own browser, with nothing an attacker controls in the same stream.
  - Details are in SECURITY.md.
- **Restore.** `openBackup()` reads both formats:
  - v1 is the JSON envelope, with version 1, 2 or 3 contents. v2 is the new line file.
  - It reads every line once to check it and builds the preview from the end line's counts. Only the compressed data stays in browser memory.
  - `restoreLines()` then sends `begin`, then `stage` requests of up to about 4 MB, then `commit`.
  - The server checks every part as it arrives, with the same row checks as `validBackup`, which is now built from a shared `validRows()`. It saves each part, under 1.5 MB, in a new `restore_staging` table.
  - At commit, the server checks that every expected section arrived whole (it compares counts with the end line) and that no key appears twice across parts. It also runs the version rules: v1 is core only, v2 has six tables, v3 has every table plus the later optional ones.
  - Then the same `applyRestore()` used by the one-request restore runs one batch. That batch writes the recovery snapshot, then reads each part from `restore_staging` inside D1. It deletes the parts in the same transaction.
  - An upload belongs to the session that began it. It is replaced when that owner begins another, deleted on any failure, and removed by the daily job after a day.
- **Unchanged.** `GET /api/backups` without a mode, and `POST {action:'restore', backup}`, still work for files up to 12 MB. The checks and the walkthrough use them. They now share the new validation and restore code.

### Sizes and timings

Measured by `tests/load-check.mjs`, now end to end through the real route and the page's module. Times are on the local D1 stand-in.

| | 3,000 families | 10,000 families |
|---|---:|---:|
| Records (JSON) | 30.1 MB | 99.0 MB |
| Encrypted file (gzip, then AES-GCM) | 6.5 MB | 21.6 MB |
| Largest single line or batch in the Worker | 1.1 MB | 1.1 MB |
| Download: stream, compress, encrypt | 1.8 s | 5.2 s |
| D1 queries in the download Worker run | 97 | 253 (limit 1,000) |
| Unlock and check the file | 0.4 s | 1.5 s |
| Restore: upload and apply | 1.9 s | 6.4 s |
| Restore requests (largest) | 10 (4.0 MB) | 27 (4.0 MB) |
| Statements in the one restore batch | 36 | 88 |

Every bound value stays under D1's 2 MB limit and every statement under 100 KB; the test fixture enforces both. In the load check, each wrestler's drawn signature is now slightly different. With identical signatures, compression looked far better than it would be with real ones.

### Limits

- Families and openings stay at 20,000 rows each, because every restore first saves them in a recovery snapshot.
- Each other table may have up to 500,000 rows.
- One restore may upload up to 400 MB in 700 parts.
- Anything larger is refused with a clear message, never saved as a partial file.
- About 250 D1 queries for one download at 10,000 families needs Workers Paid. The free plan allows 50 per run, which the old one-object export also reached at 3,000 families.
- Attendance history is what will grow most over the years.

## How it was tested

- [x] `pnpm test` (93/93)
- [x] `pnpm typecheck`
- [x] `pnpm build`
- [x] New or changed behavior has a test in `tests/`
- [x] Checked in a browser, if a page changed. I ran the walkthrough locally on other ports (`E2E_PORT=8871 E2E_AUTH_PORT=54871 E2E_USAW_PORT=54881`): 53 steps passed.

New and changed tests:

- **`tests/backup-files.mjs`** (new):
  - Three files saved by the old page, made with the code on `main` at 90c4179 (v1 format with version 3, 2 and 1 contents), open and restore through the new restore in parts. They give the same database as the one-request restore.
  - A new file restores every table exactly. The new format refuses a wrong passphrase, a changed first line, salt or data, and a file that was cut short.
  - An unfinished download (no end line, an error line from the route, or counts that don't match) never becomes a file.
  - The restore in parts refuses: a bad row, a missing or extra section, wrong counts, a key repeated across parts, another site's file, records changed after the preview, and another session's upload. An upload expires after a day.
  - A change while the batch runs rolls back everything, including the snapshot. The daily cleanup is covered too.
- **`tests/load-check.mjs`**:
  - Now runs the full download and restore at 3,000 families and checks every table row for row. `LOAD_FAMILIES=10000 node tests/load-check.mjs` runs the whole load check at 10,000.
  - The seed's academy settings are now ones a backup accepts. The old two-program stand-in failed `validState`.
- **`tests/site-health.mjs`**: the daily job clears stale uploads, and a failure is recorded.
- **`tests/backup-coverage.mjs`**: lists `restore_staging` with the tables backups leave out.
- **Walkthrough** (`scripts/e2e/journey.mjs`): the backup step matched "restored" in the page's static text, so it moved on before the restore finished. It now waits for the status line, expects "Backup restored.", and checks that the file is the v2 format. The server log confirmed the page's begin, stage and commit requests.

author: markusjura
body:
About one in ten Capture Area and Record Area selections started without the crosshair: the cursor stayed the frontmost app's arrow until the pointer moved. Shotty set the cursor before the window server had the new surface under the pointer, and that set was lost. Stopping just past the edge of another display left the arrow the same way, because a surface can set the cursor only once the window server has made it key.

Now a selection sets the cursor again every 50 ms, for up to half a second, until the system shows it, both as the surfaces appear and as the pointer enters another display's surface.

- A Shotty that had run for days lost the crosshair to the arrow on every mouse move until a drag began, and a relaunch cleared it. A selection now logs one line when another cursor keeps replacing the crosshair, with the frontmost app, the key window, Shotty's visible windows, and its uptime, so the next occurrence shows the cause. Nothing appears in the app.

## Proof

- Capture Area opened with a resting pointer: the crosshair showed in 100 of 100 starts, against about 1 in 10 failures before (sampled through the system cursor).
- Record Area opened with a resting pointer: the crosshair showed in 40 of 40 starts.
- Moving onto a second display and stopping just past its edge: the crosshair returns about 40 ms after the crossing in 6 of 6 runs; before, the arrow could stay until the next move.
- The diagnostic logged nothing across normal starts, display crossings and sweeps, and logged one line when another app kept setting the I-beam during a selection.
- Area captures on both displays still copy the expected 600×400 px image for a 300×200 pt drag.
- `Scripts/test.sh` passed.

## Scope

APP-POLISH-007 (#333) saw 3 failures it said also fail on main: `test_session_skills.test_scenario_and_unsent_cast`, `test_session_combat.test_fight_frames_and_plaintext_attack_encrypted_cast_unsent` and `test_fixture_scenarios.test_every_discovered_scenario_runs_in_make_test` ("undecodable/unsent counts").

Four scenarios (skills-state, combat-fight, quest-progress, quest-routes) name their tables repository-relative (`native/fixture/scenarios/{skills,quest}-tables`). The harness started `mu-session` in the caller's cwd. The tests pass from the repo root (the gate, `cwd=ROOT`) in both portable and private mode, and fail from `native/`. `test_session_quest.test_quest_journals_have_no_host_pointer_differences` fails the same way; the lane didn't list it. The result is the same on `c5ed13dd`, `ae5e6f36` (#333) and `f2370871` (#334).

- skills-state: `aef79e57` (#204)
- combat-fight: `e72517ba` (#197)
- quest-progress and quest-routes: `2a916b52` (#179)

## Purpose
Owner-approved permanent policy: **every future KAS Core release candidate gets a pinned read-only main/stable runtime-drift report before QEMU release gates**. Reuses the existing Core Sync Guard instead of creating a new checker.

## Narrow scope
- `.github/workflows/stable-release-gate.yml`: lightweight prerequisite job, runs for every existing manual native scenario; verifies full candidate SHA; compares root shell blobs from `main` against exact candidate with Core Sync Guard; separately compares `S00ubifs`; archives `report.json`, `report.md`, `identity.json` and prints to step summary. Native gates depend on successful report generation. No new native matrices, no changes to router runtime.

`provider.m6` mirrors `provider.tf1` on the generic `CatalogueIndex` from #28:
- `M6Http`: platform `m6group_web`, `x-customer-name: m6web` and the browser UA on every call. It returns the body plus `x-rest-collection-count`.
- `m6CatalogueIndex`: 100 per page, item offset, stops at the count header. One crawl is shared by the 5 Chaînes (M6, W9, 6ter, Gulli, M6+).
- `M6Parsers` / `M6Genres` / `M6Channels`: tested on fixtures trimmed from the 2026-11-07 captures.
- `M6Provider`: Saisons and Épisodes come from all `vi` pages (cached per Programme, cap 1000). Search is local only. `manifestUrl()` is anonymous. `stream()` raises the existing account-required `StreamResolutionException` when there is no DRM token provider. With a token provider it returns DASH + drmtoday + `x-dt-auth-token`; unwrapping the licence response is step 4b.
- Anonymous health-check probe `m6`: `shows` → `seasons` → `episodes` → `manifest`. `m6` is added to `KNOWN_PROVIDERS` in the status script and to the `simulate_failure` choices.
- SPEC: new §Provider M6+, and §Health-check updated (« `m6` en V2 » removed).

M6 is **not wired into `Providers`, `ProviderGroups` or any UI**: the DRM spike with Arnaud's credentials decides that. No box check is needed, because nothing changes in the UI.

## Decisions and deviations from the plan
- **Images**: the M6 `images[]` carry only `external_key`. I measured `https://images.6play.fr/v2/images/{key}/raw` (200, anonymous). Resized variants need a signed `hash` and return 403 without it, so raw files are used: portrait 1000×1500 (falls back to cover 750×1000), backdrop `jumbotron` 2732×1536 (no title, unlike `vignette`). Raw files run 120–400 KB each.
- **Manifest step stops at the signed URL**, like France TV's `signature` step. `full_physical_path` carries `countries=AD|FR|GP|…|WF`, so a US runner would most likely be refused. The step checks https, `.mpd`, `token=` and a future `expiration`.
- Saisons: newest first, as in TF1. Videos without a season number go into an unnumbered « Épisodes » Saison (the plan's title; TF1/FTV use « Divers »). It is placed last when numbered Saisons exist too, so no Épisode is lost. Inside a Saison: episode, then part, ascending (the API order is not sorted).
- Genres: union of category and type. Explicitly mapped: `serie-realite` → Divertissement only; `film`/`long-metrage` category → Films. Unmapped `serie*`/`telefilm*`/`telenovela` → Séries. `action` (54 Programmes) has no Genre of its own.
- Asset tokens in fixtures are replaced by `trimmed`.

- `node --test .github/scripts/healthcheck-status.test.js`: 8 pass.

author: ceronos
body:
## M1.3 — Model providers, witnessed inference, credential custody

Stacked on #1 (base `claude/m0-substrate`).

### Providers (raw HTTP, no vendor SDKs)
Native codecs: **Anthropic**, **OpenAI**, **Gemini**, **Ollama**. Through the OpenAI-compatible codec: **LM Studio**, **vLLM**, **llama.cpp**, OpenRouter, Groq, DeepSeek, xAI, Mistral, Together, Fireworks, Cerebras, Nous.
We use raw HTTP so the exact bytes sent and received can be hashed. An SDK hides those bytes.

### InferenceReceipts (AF-REMEDY-V1 §1.1)
Every call becomes a host-signed `inference.receipt` ledger event. The raw request and response are stored content-addressed. `verify_receipt` re-decodes the stored bytes and rejects any claim that doesn't match. Fixture providers record `provider_kind: fixture` inside the signed receipt, and production hives refuse them before they run.

### Credentials
Keys are never in the repo. Lookup order is env → OS keyring → owner-only `secrets.env`, and that file is refused if it sits inside a git worktree. Receipts store fingerprints only. Every tracked file is scanned for credential shapes in CI. Vendor `*_BASE_URL` variables are not inherited. See `docs/SECRETS.md`.

### Live CI
- `live / ollama`: a **real** 0.5B model answers in a production hive, then its receipt is re-derived and the chain verified. No keys needed.
- `live / hosted APIs`: runs only when `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` / `OPENAI_API_KEY` / `GEMINI_API_KEY` repository secrets exist. A missing key is reported **skipped**.

### Red Team notes
- Two-arm: fixture in production, a key echoed back by a provider, a forged completion hash, corrupted raw bytes, a test-mode receipt in a hive that has become production, a secrets file inside a git repo, a group-readable secrets file, attacker-set `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`.
- Known gaps: no streaming or tool-calling yet (M1.5), and the Ollama version in CI is unpinned.

author: robobun
body:
### Problem

- `bun build --react-compiler` prints `break loop` as a bare `break;` when only a `switch` stands between it and its loop: `loop: while (true) { switch (i) { case 2: break loop; } }`. That `break` leaves only the `switch`. The build exits 0.
- 1.4.0 to 1.4.4 have it. Main also has it for a `for` without an init or a test (9e76acc6fb, in no release).
- The cause is `get_break_target` (`src/react_compiler/reactive_scopes/build_reactive_function.rs:256`). It asks for a label only past another loop. babel-plugin-react-compiler 1.0.0 does the same.

### Fix

- `Context::open_switch_depth` records the stack depth at the innermost open `switch`. A `break` to a loop frame below it gets the label, because an unlabeled `break` goes to the nearest loop or `switch`.
- The transpiler cache version goes from 51 to 52: the output changes.
- Verified: three new tests in `test/bundler/transpiler/react-compiler.test.ts` (20 of 23 rows fail on main).
- Self-reviewed: 6 concerns raised, 4 addressed (see Notes).

### Background

- `BuildReactiveFunction` turns the control flow graph back into nested statements. Its stack has a frame for each `break` target.
- Considered: count the `switch` and case frames. The stack has none during the last case of a `switch` that nothing falls out of.

### Downsides

- The next run transpiles each cached file again.
- CI's release binaries keep their size on 11 of 12 targets (windows-aarch64: +512 B). `Context` grows from 168 to 176 B.
- Each upstream sync carries 5 more local hunks.

<details><summary>Notes</summary>

**Where the report came from.** A fuzz run, with a script of 19 rows (kinds of loop, places of the `break`, neighbours, controls). No user reported it, and no GitHub issue exists for it.

**Which `for` loops, on which build.** Each is `loop: for (HEAD) { switch (i) { case 2: break loop; } ... }`. The plain build prints `0,1`.

| Head | 1.4.3 canary | main b1305ddc7c | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| init and test (`let k = 0; k < 9; k++`, `let k = 0; k < 9;`) | `0,1,2,3` | not run | `0,1` |
| `;;`, `; t;`, `; t; u` | `0,1`, not compiled | `0,1,2,3` | `0,1` |
| `; ; u`, `init; ;`, `init; ; u`, `init; true; u` | `0,1`, not compiled | not run | `0,1` |

9e76acc6fb made the compiler take a `for` without an init or a test. No release has that commit, so a merge before the next release keeps the wider form out of every release.

**More shapes than the report has.** All are wrong on main and right with this change.

- The source needs no label. `for (const x of xs) { const v = (() => { switch (x) { default: return x; } })(); if (v >= 2) break; out.push(v); }` prints `0,1,0,1` for `[0, 1, 2, 0, 1]`, the plain build `0,1`. The compiler inlines the call, and what follows it lands in the case that returns.
- The source can have a loop between the two. `case 2: do { break loop; } while (n > 100);`: the compiler removes a `do...while` whose test is never reached.
- When every case leaves the `switch` another way, the loop never ends (`switch (i) { case 0: case 1: ...; continue loop; default: break loop; }`). This is the shape that has no frame for the `switch`.
- Nested functions: an arrow function, an object method, and a function that the compiler moves out of the component.

**Not changed.**

- A `break` of a `do...while` that the compiler removes, in a case that is not the last one: `switch (n) { case 4: do { if (c) { ...; break; } return x; } while (n > 100); default: ... }`. The output has `break bb3;` and no `bb3:`, and it does not load (`There is no containing label named "bb3"`). It is the same on the 1.4.3 canary, with this change, and in babel-plugin-react-compiler 1.0.0. The cause is another one: `remove_dead_do_while_statements` (`src/react_compiler/hir/cfg_utils.rs:158`) leaves the `break` with the next case as its target, and a case has no label to print. The `todo` test `DoWhileWhoseTestIsUnreachableKeepsWhatFollowsIt` in #43603 is about the same pass. No issue tracks it.
- Upstream. `getBreakTarget` is the same in `BuildReactiveFunction.ts` and in the Rust crate, at the ported commit 560db514 and at upstream main. The upstream fixture `reactive-control-dependency-reactive-after-fixpoint` has the shape, and its expected output has the bare `break;`. I found no upstream issue for it and filed none. The same change applies to upstream's Rust crate. The new lines have `Not in upstream` comments.
- `get_continue_target`: no `switch` takes a `continue`.
- The expected output of that upstream fixture: the suite compares slot counts, and Bun does not compile the function in `infer` mode.

**Self-review.** Done: the `for` loops of main are in Problem, each new comment is one line, the field has a name that says what it holds, and the report's origin is stated. Not done: an issue for the `do...while` shape and an issue at react/react. Both are under "Not changed".

**Why no check of the output.** `get_break_target` is the one place that gives a `break` the kind `Unlabeled`. The other maker of a `break`, `propagate_early_returns.rs`, always writes `Labeled`. A second check in the printer would run for each printed statement, and no test could reach it.

**Measurements.** Base is main b1305ddc7c. Debug builds, unless a line says another thing.

- The 19 rows of the report: rows that differ from the plain build 12 -> 0 (9 on the 1.4.3 canary).
- New tests on main: 20 of 23 rows are wrong in the client test and in the ssr test, and the label test fails.
- Variants of the fix that pass the new tests: 0 of 5. Without the new clause: 20 rows. With the record only when the `switch` has a frame: `InTheLastCaseOfASwitchThatNothingFallsOutOf`, `InTheFirstCaseOfASwitchThatNothingFallsOutOf`, `AfterACallThatTheCompilerInlines`. With a reset to 0 after a `switch`: `AfterASwitchInTheCase`. With no reset, and with `>=` for `>`: the label test.
- Upstream fixtures (1,807 inputs, the options of `react-compiler-fixtures.test.ts`): outputs that differ from main 0, memo caches 593 -> 593.
- How often the new code runs, from temporary counters: fixtures: 2,360 builder contexts, 18 `switch` statements, 4 of 4,859 `break`s go to a loop, 0 get the new label. A file of 2,000 components, each with a loop, a closed `switch` and a plain `break`: 2,000 / 2,000 / 2,000 of 8,000, 0 labels in the output.
- Binary size, from the release builds of CI (build 138266 for this PR, build 137822 for the merge base b1305ddc7c): the same number of bytes on 11 of 12 targets (linux-x64 140,680,448, darwin-aarch64 123,684,959), and 133,804,544 -> 133,805,056 B on windows-aarch64.
- Code size of the crate alone: the release bitcode of the crate (the `rustc bun_react_compiler` step of the release build), made into machine code with `opt -passes='thinlto<O2>'` and `llc -O2` of LLVM 23. `Driver::visit_block` 14,396 -> 14,430 B, `Driver::visit_break` 455 -> 484 B, `build_reactive_function` 1,074 -> 1,081 B. `.text` +70 B, `.rodata` +0 B, 0 new symbols, no other symbol changes size.
- Instructions, same objects: per compiled function +1 (a store), per `switch` +5 and no branch, per `break` to a loop +5 with 1 conditional branch. Calls added 0, allocations added 0.
- `Context`: 168 -> 176 B (a `const` assertion on `size_of` with `cargo check -p bun_react_compiler`).
- Cache: `bun test --react-compiler` on 2 components writes 2 entries and rewrites 0 in the next run. With the version of both entries set to 51 by hand, the next run rewrites 2 of 2, and the run after it 0.
- `build_reactive_function.rs` against upstream's Rust crate at 560db514: 63 -> 68 diff hunks.
- `--minify`, `--target=node`, `--target=bun` and `bun test --react-compiler` print `0,1` for the example. `bun lint` with `react/invariant` and `react/todo` as errors finds no problem in it.

**Suites on the PR build.** `react-compiler.test.ts`: 148 pass, 1 skip, 1 todo. `react-compiler-fixtures.test.ts`: 3,293 pass, 320 skip. `react-compiler-fixtures-run.test.ts`: 849 pass.

</details>

author: alexshpunt-clanker[bot]
body:
Task: [LPT-1220](https://linear.app/alexshpunt/issue/LPT-1220/pi-sessions-on-one-machine-share-language-servers)

## Problem

Every Pi process starts its own language servers. Six agents in one directory run six clangd processes that each hold the same file (LPT-1214: 2,160 MiB versus 429 MiB for one server). This applies to every language server the IDE starts locally.

## Change

Pi sessions on one machine now share a local language server when they use the same server configuration: server ID, command, configured environment, project root, initialization options and settings.

- `shared-server-host.mjs` is a detached host process that runs one language server. The first session that needs the server starts the host; later sessions connect to its socket. Sockets live in `$TMPDIR/pi-agent-ide-lsp-<uid>` (mode 0700, owner checked) or a per-user named pipe on Windows. The host is plain JavaScript with `// @ts-check`, because Node cannot run the package's TypeScript sources from `node_modules`. It runs on Pi's own Node, as `BUN_BE_BUN=1` under a Bun binary, or on `node` from PATH under a single-executable Pi.
- `LspSharedServers` (`shared-servers.ts`) connects a session. One JSON line carries the configuration and the session's initialize parameters; the reply carries the server PID once the server is initialized. After that the socket carries ordinary LSP, so `LspClient` keeps its protocol code and only gets its stdio from the host.
- The host initializes the server once and answers server requests itself: `workspace/configuration`, file-watcher registration, workspace folders and progress tokens. `LspFileWatchers` and the configuration lookup moved to `server-request-handlers.mjs`, so the client and the host share them.
- The host keeps one server copy of each document open while any session has it open. It keeps each session's text and version, gives the server the requesting session's text before a request, sends push diagnostics only to sessions whose text the server has (under their own version), replays cached diagnostics to sessions that reach that text, and translates versioned identifiers in results such as rename edits. When a newer text replaced one that a session still waits on, the host switches the server back to that session's text after the next publication; clangd publishes nothing for replaced versions.
- The host stops the server `lsp.idle-timeout` (default 10 minutes) after its last session disconnects. A session's idle stop now disconnects it. A server crash disconnects all sessions; their clients restart on a new host.
- If attaching fails for any reason, the session starts its own server as before. Servers on SSH owners are not shared.

## Verification

- `shared-servers.test.ts` (fake server, several `LspClient` sessions, real host processes): one server per configuration, another for different settings; per-session diagnostics versions and replay; per-session diagnostics when another session's text replaced its own; requests answered on the requester's text with its rename versions; host-served `workspace/configuration` and file watching; a session leaving keeps the others working; the server survives a reconnect within the linger time and stops after it; a crashed server is replaced on restart; fallback to an own process when the socket directory is not private. Disabling each routing rule in the host fails at least one test.
- LSP plugin unit suite, lint, type check, `check:boundaries`, `check:capabilities` pass. The packed tarball contains the host, and its imports resolve in an installed copy.
- Targeted integration tests (LSP post-edit and read diagnostics, TypeScript push diagnostics, semantic rename, diagnostic readiness, linked diagnostics, local config cancellation, symbol delete, module settings) pass.
- Six real Pi sessions editing the LPT-1214 `main.cpp` in one directory with clangd 18: develop ran 6 clangd processes peaking at 3,115 MiB; this branch ran one at 515 MiB. All six sessions' diagnostics reads reported their own inserted error (4 of 6 on develop). The shared clangd stopped 29 s after the last session with a 30 s idle timeout. Measurements are attached to the task.

## W02-F08 — RED→GREEN candidate for SERVER replay window, NOT ready for production

**Baseline RED (real PG16):** [test-only PR #1298](https://github.com/hraaaaf/IAMINA-MVP/pull/1298), original test-only SHA `c2b4f498005ccdc991de4876466abc333c52045d`, [PostgreSQL CI #42368386293](https://github.com/hraaaaf/IAMINA-MVP/actions/runs/42368386293): **2926 PASS, 1 FAIL** at `test_w02_f08_candidate_15min_absolute_bearer_limit_rejects_replay` — protected GET `/api/v1/logs` with a 16-minute-old signed native bearer returned **HTTP 200** instead of the PROPOSED HTTP 401. Distinct synthetic HTTP proof PASS that if `/auth/logout` never reaches Django, the same bearer is still accepted immediately and auth_token_version remains unchanged. Source default was 30 DAYS. The test-only branch has since added one more independent oracle: a runtime setting must not override the new ceiling back to 30 days. No previous adversarial tests changed.

**This candidate code (exact parent test-only branch `test/w02-f08-offline-server-token-replay-20261107@2b940d3d20f8743138e926d6954de77c887f1099`):** ONE production file `backend/core/native_auth.py` changes default native bearer absolute max age from 30 days to 900 seconds, and prevents `settings.NATIVE_AUTH_TOKEN_MAX_AGE_SECONDS` from extending above that ceiling; invalid security setting fails closed. Existing version-based revocation, login, logout, protected router and patient data untouched. Temporary base main for CI only, restore stacked base after exact-SHA evidence. Draft, unmerged, no Vercel.

**MAJOR ARCHITECTURE/HUMAN GATE:** 900 seconds is a policy PROPOSAL and remains **BLOCKED FOR MERGE**. Current native Flutter auth does not implement a secure rotating refresh/reauth protocol: enforcing a 15-minute cap can interrupt clinical work and force frequent login. More importantly, when logout HTTP is offline, a copied token can still be replayed until its expiry. This patch only BOUNDS the window, does not guarantee instant remote revocation, nor verify any real deployment's runtime config. Needs independent reviewer approval, explicit security/UX decision and client renewal tests before production. A separate Draft [PR #1290](https://github.com/hraaaaf/IAMINA-MVP/pull/1290) fixes `/auth/me` bearer verification but is not part of the current F07 stack, so eventual integration is another gate.

**Accept narrowly:** real PG16 test after 16min gets 401 with no config and with oversized config; immediate offline replay evidence still 200; existing all Django tests, schema, OpenAPI and W01 synthetic auth tests PASS; client F05B old physically-impossible deletion test stays RED and W02 remains **SECURITY_NO_GO / patients NO-GO**. No merge, Vercel preview or prod deployment, Neon, PHI.

author: haseenesss
body:
## What and why

Minecraft (Bedrock Edition, 1.21.120) crashed right after start in its `NetherNet Network` thread: `CRASH sig=10` at `main+0x18b2ae8`, `x0=0x4000`, a load from its own stack. The host numbered its event descriptors from `0x4000`. NetherNet puts its event descriptor in an `fd_set` on the stack for `Select` (1024 bits, as the bsd service's descriptors are small numbers), and `FD_SET(0x4000)` read and wrote 2 KB past the set. `Select` also failed as soon as a descriptor was set, so it could never wait on one.

The change (`dm/host/hle_net.c`):
- The event descriptors are 960-1023, inside an `fd_set`.
- `Select` (`dm_sk_select`, both overloads) waits on the event descriptors in its sets as `Poll` does and returns the ready ones in the sets. With only descriptors the host never made it fails as before, with none it waits out the timeout.

author: dotcoocoo
body:
## What and why

In `vendor/linesweeper/docs/sweep.typ`, the crossing-height lemma (`lem-intersection-height-error`) defined `t` as the ending gap `alpha(y_1) - beta(y_1)` divided by the sum of both gaps. The gap between the two segments is `D0 (1 - t) - D1 t`, with `D0 = beta(y_0) - alpha(y_0)` and `D1 = alpha(y_1) - beta(y_1)`, so it is zero at `t = D0 / (D0 + D1)`. With `D0 = 1` and `D1 = 3`, the old formula gave `t = 0.75`, while the segments cross at `t = 0.25`. `intersect_lines` in `src/curve/line.rs:52-53` already divides the starting gap `dx0` by `dx0 - dx1`.

The lemma and its proof now use the starting gap `beta(y_0) - alpha(y_0)` as the numerator `c`. This matches the proof's later line `alpha(y) - beta(y) = -c + (y - y_0) / (y_1 - y_0) d`, which is zero at `t = c / d`. The same proof's last step divided `d` by `y_1 - y_1`, which is zero; it now divides by `y_1 - y_0`, the difference of the inverse slopes.

`SOURCE.json` lists the change in `local_patches` and gives the new `sha256` of `docs/sweep.typ`; its `source_sha256` stays the package's hash. `README.craft.md` and `NOTICE` now say one file of the package is changed.

The change is to documentation only, and no code or build reads `docs/sweep.typ`, so there is no test for it.

## How it was tested

- Every `sha256` in `SOURCE.json` matches the file in this commit (71 files, no mismatch); `docs/sweep.typ` is the one file whose `sha256` differs from `source_sha256`.

```sh
cargo test --locked --lib --test regression   # in a copy of vendor/linesweeper: 63 lib + 10 regression passed
cargo test --locked --doc                     # 1 passed
cargo fmt --all -- --check                    # clean
cargo clippy -p craft-prepress --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings  # exit 0
cargo test -p craft-prepress --all-features   # 102 passed, 3 ignored
```

body:
## Summary
This is the F2 follow-up from the grader. A .csv or .xls that holds a column of dates and a column of amounts, under names Clicky doesn't know, is no longer left out. Clicky asks about it before the receipt.

**The question**
- `sources.guess_columns` judges columns by content:
  - a date column needs 4 in 5 of its digit-bearing cells to read as dates;
  - amounts rank by how often they read, then by size, so a line total comes before a fee or a quantity.
- Each role gets at most 3 options. Each question is one card with buttons ("Cột Giá trị", "Cột Phí", "Cột SL", "Không phải đơn hàng"). The card names the file, and like any choice card it sits bottom-right, away from figures.
- When there is exactly one date column and one amount column, a single question confirms both: "Em hiểu cột "Thời điểm" là ngày bán, cột "Giá trị" là số tiền. Đúng không chị?"
- Nothing is read or written until chị answers. Each question is logged as the scene event `column_question`, and the answer as `column_answer`.

**Remembered per header ("nhớ cho tháng sau")**
- The answer is stored as header signature → column keys in `cot_da_nho.json` in Clicky's data folder. It holds header names only, never a file name.
- "Không phải đơn hàng" is remembered too, and the receipt names the file with that reason.
- `sources.columns_of` uses a remembered column only when the names give no date or no amount.
- The per-file query (C1) carries the same signatures, for this folder's files only, so no other company's column names end up in the workbook. It resolves them the same way.
- `needs_reader` picks the per-file query for these files.

**Biên bản and receipt**
- The Biên bản gets "Chọn cột: <file>" with what chị chose, and "Cột đã nhớ: <file>" when a later month reuses the answer.
- The receipt's sales line says "cột ngày, số tiền theo chị đã chỉ".

## Type of change
- [x] New feature (rule 4: never leave an order-like file out in silence)

## How to test
```bash
QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen python -m pytest tests -q
```
New tests in `tests/test_order_exports.py`:
- guessing ranks columns best first;
- the full run: question → answer → remembered on disk → receipt reads the file → per-file query has the signature → "Excel khớp" → Biên bản row. Next month: no question, and the receipt says so;
- one-question confirm;
- "Không phải đơn hàng" is remembered and named;
- the M signature matches the engine's.

- Case 01 and BHC engine snapshot: identical.

author: bobocman
body:
## Summary
This PR audits every path that grants, spends or bypasses credits. After it, the free tier is one tale at signup and then pay. Nothing refreshes automatically.

### Credit leaks fixed
- **Users could set their own balance.** The `users_update_own` RLS policy let any signed-in user update their own `users` row with the public anon key. That includes `purchased_credits`, `free_credits`, `subscription_tier` and `is_admin`. A new trigger, `protect_user_billing_columns`, keeps the stored values of those columns for any write made as `anon` or `authenticated`. A row a client inserts always starts with 1 free tale and nothing else.
- **`deduct_credit_atomic` was executable by `anon` and `authenticated`** and took any user id, so anyone could drain other users' tales. It is now service-role only.
- **The credit ledger** (`credit_transactions`) is now read-only to users, who can still read their own rows.
- **Removed the monthly free tale.** The cron route `api/cron/weekly-credits`, the Vercel cron, `grantWeeklyCredit` and the `FREE_TIER.monthly*` values are gone.
- **Removed the legacy client-side credit helpers** (`lib/credits/operations.ts` and `operations-server.ts`, which granted 3 welcome credits) and the public `/test-credits` page.
- **Plans:** when a subscription ends (`canceled` or `unpaid`), the unused plan tales are cleared. Events for an old subscription can no longer overwrite a newer active one.

### Cost leaks fixed (unauthenticated routes that spent money)
- `api/tts/generate` accepted any `text` and `entryId` from anyone. That ran ElevenLabs on your bill and could overwrite a public tale's narration.
- `api/video/compress` accepted any `videoUrl` and `entryId`. That ran Cloudinary on your bill and could overwrite a tale's video.
- `api/cloudinary/merged-video` and `api/n8n-webhook` had no auth either.
- All four now require `X-Internal-Secret`. The value is `INTERNAL_API_SECRET`, falling back to the existing `N8N_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, so no new environment variable is needed. Every internal caller now sends the header.
- `api/captions/status` listed every entry with its transcript publicly. It is now admin only.

### Rate limits and refunds
- The upload API's in-memory limiter (per serverless instance, so it didn't hold) is replaced with the existing Upstash Redis limiter: 20 an hour per user, keyed separately from the 3-an-hour pre-check.
- An upload now refunds its tale only when n8n clearly never got the job: unreachable, 404, 502 or 503. The refund goes through a new service-role `refund_credit_atomic` RPC.
- `stripe_customer_id` is now saved with the service role, because the column is locked.

### Not changed, needs a decision
- **Multiple accounts.** Email confirmation appears to be off: signup signs the user in straight away. Each throwaway email therefore gets a free tale.
- **Redis fails open.** If Upstash is down, uploads aren't limited. Credits still gate them.

## Setup after merge
Run `supabase/migrations/20261107000000_lock_credit_columns.sql` in the Supabase SQL editor.

## Test plan
- [ ] `tsc` shows no new errors (122 before, 114 after, from the deleted files).
- [ ] After running the SQL, a new signup gets 1 tale.
- [ ] Running `supabase.from("users").update({purchased_credits: 99})` in the browser console leaves the balance unchanged.
- [ ] Upload a tale end to end: TTS, compress and merge still run.
- [ ] Subscribe to Pet Parent and confirm 10 tales; the billing portal opens.

author: kylejune
body:
## Summary

Fixes four session-state bugs in `DirectClient` and `<OAuth2Provider>`, all of which show up in browser apps that share refresh-token storage across tabs or keep the access token in memory.

## Changes

- **A reload no longer signs out when the refresh token survived.** `DirectClient.getSession` used to return signed out as soon as the token bundle was empty. It never got to the "a stored refresh token can revive this" check, which only ran for an expired bundle. So `IndexedDBRefreshTokenStorage` with an in-memory access token, which the storage docs recommend for surviving a reload, signed the user out on every reload. Now an empty bundle with a stored refresh token reads as `{ isAuthenticated: true, user: null, sessionExpiresIn: 0 }`, the same shape as an expired-but-revivable bundle, so the provider renews. A refresh that starts from an empty bundle emits `authenticated` after `token_refreshed`, because it is the first time this client holds the user's claims. Without that, an on-demand `getAccessToken()` before the provider's own renew would emit only `token_refreshed`, the renew timer would re-arm for the token lifetime, and `user` would stay null until then. A refresh over an existing bundle still emits only `token_refreshed`. `OAuth2State.user` now documents that it can be null while authenticated, until the claims load.
- **The tab that loses a cross-tab refresh race no longer deletes the winner's token.** Before, when a refresh failed with `invalid_grant`, the client cleared the shared refresh-token storage unconditionally. If another client sharing that storage had already rotated in a newer token, that token was wiped. Now the clear happens only when storage still holds the token this refresh presented (compare-and-clear, serialized with the client's other session writes). When storage holds a different token, it is left alone and the refresh retries once with the newer token, so `refresh()` keeps its contract that `InvalidGrantError` means the stored token is dead. If the retry also gets `invalid_grant` and storage now holds that token, the session clears as before. A store that cannot be re-read for the comparison falls back to clearing. If the session version moved while that re-read was in flight (a sign-in, callback or device poll started), the clear and its version bump are skipped and the refresh rejects with "session changed during refresh", so the new sign-in's tokens are kept rather than failing after its code is spent.
- **`logout` revokes even when the local clear fails.** Before, the revocation ran only after `#clearSession` resolved, so a storage clear that threw (an IndexedDB failure, say) left the refresh token unrevoked. The revocation now runs in a `finally` after the clear. `logout` still rejects with the storage error and emits nothing in that case, and the success path is unchanged: clear, emit `logged_out`, then revoke.
- **The provider drops stale user claims.** The `authenticated` handler set `user` from `client.getUser()` without checking whether the session had moved on. A `getUser()` that resolved after a `logged_out`, or after a newer sign-in, wrote the old claims onto the state. Each lookup now records which sign-in it belongs to and is dropped if a later `authenticated` or `logged_out` has arrived.

## Testing

Each regression test was run against the unfixed code first and failed at its behavioral assertion:

- `reports signed in after a reload when only the refresh token survived, and renews from it`: got `isAuthenticated: false`.
- `keeps a refresh token another tab rotated in while this refresh lost the race, and refreshes with it`: `refresh()` rejected with `invalid_grant`.
- `retries a lost refresh race once, leaving a token rotated again in place`: shared storage was `null` (wiped).
- `revokes the refresh token even when clearing local storage fails`: revoked `[]`, expected `["rt-seed"]`.
- `drops claims that resolve after the session signed out`: user `u-stale`, expected none.
- `keeps the newer sign-in's claims when an older lookup resolves last`: user `u-old`, expected `u-new`.
- `shows the user once an on-demand refresh revives a reloaded session` (real `DirectClient`, empty `MemoryTokenStorage`, seeded refresh store, token response with an `id_token`): user stayed `none` after `await client.getAccessToken()`.
- `leaves a sign-in that starts while a dead refresh re-reads storage intact`: the sign-in failed with "session changed during token exchange".

These also pin the paths around them: `reports signed out with no token bundle and no stored refresh token`, `clears the session when the newer refresh token another tab stored is dead too`, and `clears the session on invalid_grant when the store cannot be re-read to compare`. Two guards were proved by mutation instead:

- `keeps the newer sign-in's claims when a second sign-in follows with no sign-out` fails when the provider counts only `logged_out`.
- The `deduplicates concurrent refreshes` test now asserts that no `authenticated` is emitted, and fails when the empty-bundle condition is dropped.

I changed two existing assertions on purpose. The cross-tab retry test starts with no bundle, so it now expects `token_refreshed` then `authenticated`. `refuses a 200 carrying no access_token rather than persisting one` checked `getSession().isAuthenticated` as a stand-in for "nothing persisted". Its seeded refresh store still holds a token, which the reload fix now correctly reads as revivable. It now asserts that the token store is empty, which is what its message says.

`pnpm check` and `pnpm test:coverage` pass locally (150 files, 4573 tests).

Known limit: across tabs, the compare-and-clear is a read followed by a clear on the storage. `RefreshTokenStorage` has no atomic compare-and-delete, so a rotation that lands between those two calls can still be cleared. The window is much narrower than before (one storage round trip instead of a whole token request).

## Related Issues

None.

author: madbomber
body:
## Why

`imbibler.rb` can't run on any Ruby since 3.0 (brain finding F-4 for scripts, re-confirmed by the #14 review):

- `URI.escape` and the open-uri `Kernel#open(url)` form were removed in Ruby 3.0. Every run dies with `undefined method 'escape' for module URI (NoMethodError)` at `ReadIndex`.
- `Pathname#realpath` on the OUTPUT argument raises `Errno::ENOENT` when the CSV doesn't exist yet. That's the normal case, so a first run fails before it fetches anything.

## What changed

- `URI.escape(url)` becomes `URI::RFC2396_PARSER.escape(url)`. This is the same RFC 2396 parser `URI.escape` used, so escaping behaves exactly as before. `open(...)` becomes `URI.open(...)`, using the block form so each fetched page's IO is closed.
- The fetch-and-parse step is extracted into `fetch_page(url)` and used by both `ReadIndex` and `ReadBookChapter`. Main is skipped when the file is loaded instead of run (`return unless $PROGRAM_NAME == __FILE__`), so the edited methods can be tested in isolation.
- `realpath` becomes `expand_path` for the output path.
- README: imbibler.rb was described as a "Drinking game or beverage tracker". It now says what the script does.

## Proof

There's no `test/` directory, so the proof is a throwaway harness. It serves stub HTML from a `TCPServer` on 127.0.0.1 and runs the script in a temp dir, with no external network. The stub chapter URL contains a space, so the escape path is exercised.

develop (Ruby 4.1.0-preview1):
```
== CLI: imbibler.rb niv.csv http://127.0.0.1:<port>/index/
imbibler.rb:161:in 'Pathname#realpath': No such file or directory ... niv.csv (Errno::ENOENT)
exit: false, files: []
# with niv.csv pre-created:
imbibler.rb:113:in 'Object#ReadIndex': undefined method 'escape' for module URI (NoMethodError)
exit: false
```

branch (same result on 4.1.0-preview1 and 4.0.9):
```
== CLI: imbibler.rb niv.csv http://127.0.0.1:<port>/index/
exit: true, files: ["niv.csv"]
== ReadBookChapter against the stub chapter page
Genesis,1,1,In the beginning.
Genesis,1,2,The earth was formless.
exit: true, chapter file: "In the beginning.\nThe earth was formless.\n"
== isolation: load without running main, stub fetch_page (no network)
ReadIndex ran with stubbed fetch_page; rows=[]
exit: true
```

`ruby -wc imbibler.rb` reports Syntax OK on both Rubies. The script was not run against biblegateway.com.

## Review

- `/simplify` (done inline): nothing trimmed.
- `/code-review medium` round 1 (10 findings): fixed one, that the edited methods couldn't be tested in isolation and the fetch expression was duplicated, by extracting `fetch_page` and adding the main guard. The other 9 are in code this PR doesn't change (double-encoding of `%` that the old `URI.escape` also did, missing nil guards, the lazy verse regex, octal parsing in `format('%03d', '08')`, `succ!` on a string literal, the hard-coded biblegateway prefix, usage text that disagrees with where files are written, and `expand_path` not resolving a symlinked OUTPUT). They're recorded in brain as findings, not fixed here, to keep this PR to the Ruby 3 fix.
- Round 2 (6 findings): fixed the IO that was never closed (block form of `URI.open`). Rejected:
  - a wrapper script that `load`s the file would skip main. This is the standard `__FILE__ == $0` idiom, and nothing in the repo wraps it.
  - namespacing `fetch_page` and injecting a fetcher: more structure than a standalone script needs.
  - the existing `puts` progress line: it's user-facing output, not debugging.
- Round 3 (4 findings): no defects in the changes. Non-block `CSV.open`, charset passthrough, the local-path fallback and timeouts are all already-present behaviors or enhancements, recorded in brain. The loop converged within the 3-round cap.

## Risk and rollback

The change is limited to one standalone script and one README line. Escaping is unchanged. Revert the PR to roll back.

body:
events_log gets two columns filled when the row is written:

- `mentions Array(String)`: the @usernames typed, lowercased, without the @
- `mentioned_user_ids Array(UInt64)`: the accounts linked by a text mention

They are filled on send and edit rows by `entities::mentions`, which slices the text in UTF-16 units the way Telegram counts offsets. Unit tests cover an emoji before the mention, duplicates, and an entity that runs past the text.

`migrations/057_mentions.sql` is applied by the bot's startup migration runner on deploy. It recreates the Buffer around the ALTER, then backfills old rows from `entities` as an async mutation (`ALTER … UPDATE`), so startup does not wait for it. The backfill slices by code points, so a mention after an emoji can come out shifted on old rows. All statements pass `EXPLAIN AST`, and the backfill expressions were dry-run against live data.
