author: mimelyc
body:
## ELI5

If you quit an agent and go back to the shell, the sidebar should stop counting it. Sometimes it kept a "Done" row for that pane, so a tab with one real agent showed two. Now, once Orca confirms the pane is back at the shell, the leftover row goes away and doesn't come back.

## What Changed

**Before:** split a tab into two panes, finish and exit the agent on the left, and keep the right one running. The worktree card lists two agents: a retained Done row for the left pane plus the live right pane. `orca worktree ps` reports one.

**After:** the card lists only the live agent. Done rows for panes whose agent process is still alive are unchanged.

**Mechanism:** the Done status can disappear before the async foreground read confirms the shell has returned. In that window, retention saves it as a retained row. The confirmed-shell callback then cleared the title and launch identity. Its same-turn drop returned early because the live row was already gone, so the retained row survived.

- `retireConfirmedShellAgent` runs in the existing non-hibernation confirmed-shell branch of `pane-agent-identity.ts`. When the pane has no live status row, it drops the renderer-side row and suppresses the pending retention snapshot. A live row returns early, and generic program results are kept.
- `dropAgentStatus` gains two explicit options:
  - `suppressRetention` writes the existing `retentionSuppressedPaneKeys` marker even when no live row remains, so the next retention sync can't re-create the row. The collector already consumes this marker.
  - `rendererOnly` skips the main-process `drop` IPC. A lagging renderer then can't delete a newer host-owned row or a moved PTY's owner alias.
- No Pi-specific checks. This uses the existing confirmed-shell, drop and suppressor paths.

## Why

The retained branch had no way to tell "finished history" from "pane still occupied" once the live row was gone. Fixing it at the confirmed-shell point reuses the existing suppressor that retention already honors. I tried retiring the pane's authority instead, but that interfered with the next generic OSC program in the same pane, so I dropped it. Keeping the new path renderer-only leaves host state, aliases and existing live-row confirmation paths untouched.

## Linked Issue

Fixes #39499

Related: #31044 (retained Done rows for tabs that no longer exist), #20738 (agent identity kept after exit in the CLI/RPC layer). Both involve stale agent rows but go through different paths.

## Visual Proof

Hidden Electron at 1440 × 900 on an isolated profile, with real PTYs and a Pi hook fixture. Both images show the sidebar and both panes in the same terminal tab. These are fixture runs, not model-backed Pi sessions.

In both captures, the left pane has exited Pi (`PI_FIXTURE_EXIT`), printed `SHELL_RETURNED`, and returned to a shell prompt. The right pane's Pi fixture has finished a turn but its process remains alive.

**Before:** the sidebar incorrectly lists two Pi rows even though the left pane is back at the shell.

![Before: sidebar shows two Pi rows; left pane shows PI_FIXTURE_EXIT and SHELL_RETURNED at a shell prompt, while the right Pi fixture remains alive](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9b0f4aff-7016-489e-9ea4-4e196a306682)

**After:** the sidebar lists only the right pane's Pi; the left pane is still at the shell.

![After: sidebar shows one Pi row corresponding to the right pane; left pane shows PI_FIXTURE_EXIT and SHELL_RETURNED at a shell prompt](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/279dddd3-6f10-4311-9111-e25e7b6e763e)

Gray rectangles redact identifying setup output, shell prompt prefixes, and project labels. The bottom callouts are annotations; the sidebar rows and relevant terminal output are from the original captures.

## Testing

macOS, Node 24.22.1 (repository pin), pnpm 12.14.0. All test and app processes use `ORCA_BACKGROUND_LAUNCH=1`; browser checks run headless. The validated commit matches this PR's head. No tracked source or test files changed during validation.

| Command | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `pnpm lint --maxWorkers=2 --timings` | **Passed**: all 41 lint steps. Code-quality comparisons use the PR base via `ORCA_CODE_QUALITY_BASE=upstream/main`. |
| `pnpm typecheck` | **Passed**: the complete repository typecheck. |
| `pnpm test --maxWorkers=2` | **Failed** after approximately 60 minutes: 10,057 files passed, 38 failed, 124 skipped; 65,023 tests passed, 22 failed, 3 expected failures, 1,392 skipped, 2 todo. |
| `pnpm build` | **Passed**: desktop assets and macOS native builds. |

**Follow-up on the full-suite failures:**

- The initial run was missing matching Playwright Chromium/WebKit binaries, cloud dependencies/build outputs, and release tags required by cross-version fixtures. These prerequisites were installed or fetched before focused reruns. The reruns also use a short canonical temporary directory and an isolated Git configuration for fixtures.
- Rerunning the original 38 failed files with the default test runtime and one worker produced **31 passed / 7 failed**, with **209 tests passed / 9 failed**.
- Running those same 38 files with `pnpm test:node ... --maxWorkers=1` produced **34 passed / 4 failed**, with **213 tests passed / 5 failed**.
- One remaining import failure in both reruns was a missing cloud contract build output. After running the cloud relay's declared `pretest` build, `pnpm test tests/e2e/relay-region-correction.unit.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` **passed all 3 tests**.

The following failures remain after preparation and reruns:

| Area | Default runtime | Node control |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PTY navigation readiness: shell environment not returned within the wait | Failed | Failed |
| WSL deployment store: unreadable records expose extra environments | Failed | Failed |
| Terminal font rendering: fallback glyph does not repaint after the font arrives | Failed | Failed |
| Read-only generated-directory cleanup | Failed | Passed |
| Source-control shell preparation / pipe-close assertion | Failed | Passed |
| Persisted profile-state fixture database reads | Failed | Passed |

These failing test files are outside the four changed renderer files. **The complete test gate remains failing; the checklist below is intentionally unchecked.** The focused reruns do not replace a passing full-suite run.

Earlier focused lifecycle validation:

- 171 existing tests across 10 files passed: foreground tracking, same-turn/late Done, no-OSC exits and host verification, hibernation, pane authority, retention and store drop. No unit tests were added.
- Hidden Electron on an isolated profile with real PTYs and a Pi hook fixture passed both deliberately staged status-clear-before-shell ordering and natural exit. It covers removal of the exited pane, sibling Done preservation, another retention sync, ordinary OSC program results, Pi relaunch in the same pane, and sibling close.
- The existing hidden sleep/wake E2E passed.
- `pnpm check:changed --base=upstream/main` previously passed 24/25 checks; its format failure was on untracked local diagnostics outside this diff. Formatting of all four committed source files passed separately.

Not exercised: a model-backed Pi session, remote/SSH panes rendered end to end, Linux or Windows.

## Risk

**Level:** Low

- The new path runs only on a confirmed shell return with no live status row, and only touches renderer state.
- Worst case: a pane that just returned to the shell loses a Done row the user wanted to keep, or the suppressor hides one stale retained snapshot.
- Known limitations:
  - If a live Done row still exists when the shell is confirmed, this path skips it. If that row is later removed through `removeAgentStatus` (no suppressor), the ghost can still return.
  - On `command-finished` confirmed-shell events, the drop also clears the pane's launch config and acknowledgement. Before this change, only `visible-pty` and `process-exit` did.
  - Suppressor markers set after retention has

author: businessappwithai
body:
Phase 5 of `docs/errorhandlingandlogging.md`: the sweep that makes the phase 4 core cover the whole platform. It is large because it is mechanical; the changes fall into five groups.

**API routes (80 files)**
- Every route is wrapped in `withApiHandler` (the voice WebSocket upgrade is the one exception, since it answers 101 and keeps the connection). Each request now gets one log line at its category's level, a request id, and, for a thrown error, the standard envelope.
- The hand-built `catch { return json(…500) }` blocks now `throw serverFailure(error, "what failed")` (the route's own plain message is shown, the cause is logged with its stack) or call `recordFailure(error, label)`, so the cause is on the request's single line instead of a stray `console.error`. 43 routes no longer send `error.message` to the caller.

**`console.*` (347 calls, 79 files)**
- Now `getLogger(channel).note(level, …)`. `console.log` becomes `debug`, so a production install stops printing it; each channel can be turned up with `LOG_LEVEL_<CHANNEL>`. Pool errors are `db.pool.error` events. Data source tests, schema inspection, audit failures, voice and embedding failures have events of their own. Migrations, seeds and sample-data scripts keep their console report.

**Browser**
- The logger runs in the browser (Pino's browser build). Warnings and errors go to the bounded `POST /api/logs` (20 a minute, one per message per minute, never throws). A render error was previously logged in development only, so in production it never left the browser.
- The database sink no longer imports the database: that import dragged the server's connection code and `crypto` into the client bundle (the first production build after the sweep failed on it). The database module registers the writer instead.

**System Logs**
- `logs` gains `category` and `code` columns and an index on `request_id`. `GET /api/logs` filters by `requestId`, `category` and `code`; an administrator can look a request up by the reference an error showed. The viewer has a kind filter and a reference box.

**Tests**
- New `no-stray-logging` test: no `console.*` outside the logger and scripts, every route wrapped, no `error.message` in a route's response body.

**Verified:** `bun run typecheck`; `bun test src` (288 pass, also with `AUTH_SECRET` unset); `vite build` (`routeTree.gen.ts` unchanged). In a real browser, sign-in and six pages (dashboard, SQL editor, data sources, logs, reports, settings) load with no page errors. Against a running instance, a query typo's reference finds both its request line and its `sql.query.failed` row in the table with category and code, and a browser-style report is accepted.

**Not done:** the remaining `note()` calls are free text and should be given events of their own as the code is touched; `GET /api/logs` still shows an ordinary user only their own rows.

author: verigence-admin
body:
## Root cause (reproduced)

`src/services/security/rememberSession.ts` (origin/dev, lines 56-70):

```ts
async function secureStorage() {
  ...
  const { SecureStorage } = await import('@aparajita/capacitor-secure-storage');
  return SecureStorage;          // <- resolves a promise with a Capacitor plugin Proxy
}
```

A Capacitor plugin is a `Proxy` whose `get` trap returns a native-method wrapper for **every** property, `then` included (`@capacitor/core` 8.5.3, `registerPlugin`, `default: return createPluginMethodWrapper(prop)`). Resolving a promise with it makes JavaScript treat it as a thenable and call `SecureStorage.then(resolve, reject)`. That native method does not exist. The wrapper's own promise rejects (`"SecureStorage.then()" is not implemented on android`, an unhandled rejection), and `resolve`/`reject` are never called. So **`await secureStorage()` never settles on Android**:

- `enableRememberedSession`: `/auth/remember` returns 200, then `storeNativeRememberCredential` hangs. The credential is never stored and `setRememberSessionHint(true)` is never reached, so no failure path runs either (no `/auth/logout`).
- Cold start: `SessionBootstrapGate` sees no hint, becomes ready at once, and calls nothing. In-app expiry: `SessionRenewalGate.resumeOrEnd` sees no hint and signs out to the login page. **`/auth/resume` is never called.**
- Sign out: the hint is cleared synchronously, then `readNativeRememberCredential` hangs, so `/auth/logout` is never sent.

Web never reaches the plugin (`!Capacitor.isNativePlatform()` returns before the import), which is why Web works. This matches the DEV evidence exactly: 552 MOBILE remembered sessions with none ever resumed, `/auth/remember` 200 from the WebView several times a day, zero `/auth/resume` and zero `/auth/logout` from the WebView.

**Reproduction:**
1. Node, with the real `@capacitor/core` + `@aparajita/capacitor-secure-storage` and an emulated `androidBridge`: the old pattern never settles; the plugin works when used directly.
2. Both bundles built with `vite build --mode native-dev`, run in Chrome via Playwright with an emulated Android bridge (in-memory Keystore, WebView user agent) and Security stubbed in the browser. No DEV traffic.

| | after sign-in | cold start | cold start, hint removed |
|---|---|---|---|
| origin/dev | hint `null`, keystore empty, console: `"SecureStorage.then()" is not implemented on android` | `/login`, **no** `/auth/resume` | `/login`, no call |
| this PR | hint `1`, credential stored | `/home`, `/auth/resume` with the stored credential | `/home`, `/auth/resume` (credential decides) |

In-app renewal refused: with `SESSION_SUPERSEDED` (401) the app calls `/auth/resume`, gets 401, clears the credential and sends `/auth/logout`. With `ACCESS_BLOCKED` (403) the app calls `/auth/resume`, gets 403, and **keeps** the credential.

The Android project itself was checked: `capacitor.config.ts` serves the bundled `dist` (no `server.url`), `hostname: localhost` / `androidScheme: https`, and the project is generated by `cap add android` in CI with nothing that clears WebView data. localStorage persists across launches, as the stable `device_id` on DEV confirms: 552 revocations were by a new sign-in on the *same* device.

## What changed
- **`rememberSession.ts`**: `withSecureStorage(name, op)` uses the plugin only inside the call and never hands the Proxy out of an async scope. It has an 8 s timeout, so a stuck bridge can no longer hold sign-in or resume. `storeNativeRememberCredential` returns true only if the value reads back.
- **`rememberSessionLifecycle.ts`**: on MOBILE the stored credential is the source of truth (hint ignored). With no credential there is no network call and nothing is revoked (the old path called `/auth/logout`). Only a **401** from `/auth/resume` clears the credential. 403/426 (paused, inactive, app update) give a new `refused` outcome that keeps it. New `mayHaveRememberedSession()` (native → always try; Web → hint).
- **`SessionBootstrapGate`**: in the app it always looks for the credential on cold start. When none is stored this costs one local secure-storage read and no network call.
- **`SessionRenewalGate`**: always tries the resume (no hint check). Every automatic ending uses `signOut('SESSION_ENDED')`. A refresh refused with 401/403/426 now goes to `/auth/resume`, where Security decides about the credential. Before, it did `signOut()`, which forgot "Keep me signed in".
- **`sessionStore.signOut(reason: 'USER' | 'SESSION_ENDED')`** is required, so no caller can forget the device by default. `USER` is used only behind the Sign out buttons (AppShell, Maintenance page, assignment-gate screens). A test fails if any other file starts using it.
- **Diagnostics**: in the app the remember/resume/renewal/sign-out steps are always kept on the phone, in a 100-entry ring buffer of step names, outcomes and status codes, no secrets. They are uploaded through the existing `/me/client-diagnostics/logs` **only when** the server switch is on; who can switch it is unchanged. With the switch off the buffer is no longer wiped. Web keeps the previous behaviour.
- CHANGELOG under Unreleased.

Companion Security PR (one session and one remembered sign-in per user **per device type**, so the PC no longer knocks the phone out): verigence/verigence-security#130.

## Tests
- `npm run typecheck`: pass. `npm run ui:governance`: pass. `npx vitest run`: 99 files, **655 passed**.
- New `nativeRememberStorage.test.ts`: real Capacitor core + plugin with an emulated Android bridge. Store/read/clear round-trip and settle. **Fails on origin/dev with "never settled".**

author: brgv-code
body:
## Summary
Google Docs draws its text on a canvas, so saving a doc kept only the title and nothing could be highlighted on docs.google.com.

**Saving**
- A doc saves from Google's markdown export (`/export?format=md`), turned into HTML with marked. Readability is skipped because the export is already clean, and Readability drops short docs.
- The extension fetches the export with the browser's cookies, so private docs work. "Save a link" on the web fetches it on the server, which works for docs shared with anyone who has the link; private ones still save as a bookmark.
- `?tab=`, `/view`, `/u/1/` and `#heading` links all map to one canonical item (`googleDocUrl` in core, used by both `pageKey` and `normalizeUrl`).
- Saving a doc again refreshes its content, so existing empty doc items fill in. Other pages still keep their first save.
- For doc URLs the server ignores page HTML, so extensions already in the store (which send the canvas shell) get the export too.
- Docs inlines images as base64; the largest are dropped until the doc fits the existing 1.5 MB content cap.

**Reading**
- On `docs.google.com/document/*` a **✦ Read with Lumen** pill saves or refreshes the doc and opens `/app/read/<id>` in a new tab. If you are not connected it opens settings. ✕ hides it for the tab. Free on every plan.

Why markdown over the HTML export: through the same extractor, the HTML export lost about 90 words, got the title "docs.google.com" and wrapped links in `google.com/url` redirects. Markdown only loses merged table cells (they become blank cells).

## Testing
- Core: 71 of 71 tests pass, including new Docs URL tests (needs Node 22+ for `--experimental-strip-types`).
- Extractor checked against a real export: all 654 words, 2 tables, 3 headings, clean links, title from the download header, oversized images dropped, empty export saved as a bookmark.
- Local worker with D1: an old extension's page shell saves the full doc, a second link refreshes the same item, three URL variants resolve to one item, an inaccessible doc saves as a bookmark, and an ordinary page re-saved stays as first saved.
- Extension and web typecheck and build pass. Pill screenshotted on a Docs-like page.
- Not yet tested in a browser: the pill on real docs.google.com, a private doc through the extension, and a doc with large images.

New copy: "✦ Read with Lumen", "Opening…", "Hide", "Connect Lumen first, then read this doc in Lumen.", "Could not open this doc in Lumen".

author: lmolotii
body:
## Description

Phase 6, step 2 of the deprecated-dependency plan, following #71.

**@database without dbinfoz:**
- The provider now gets table schemas from `core/context/providers/database/`: one module each for Postgres (`pg`), MySQL (`mysql2`), MSSQL (`mssql`), and SQLite through core's `node:sqlite` wrapper from #71.
- Each module runs dbinfoz 0.14.0's queries and returns the same shapes, so context items don't change.
- Existing `connection` configs are passed to the drivers unchanged, as before.
- Two fixes along the way:
  - every lookup now closes its connection (dbinfoz opened a pool per lookup and never closed it);
  - a failed MSSQL connection now surfaces as an error instead of an unhandled rejection.

**`sqlite3` is gone:**
- **Dependencies:** core and the extension drop `sqlite3`, `dbinfoz` and their install chain (`node-gyp`, `prebuild-install`). The extension also had an unused direct `dbinfoz` dependency, now removed. Together that's about 100 packages fewer in the extension's lockfile.
- **Packaging and release:**
  - packaging no longer downloads or copies `node_sqlite3.node` (`download-copy-sqlite.js` is removed);
  - `publish-vscode.yaml` no longer builds `sqlite3` from source for win32-arm64 (file contents only, not renamed).
  - The darwin-arm64 VSIX goes from 28.3 MB to 26.3 MB. Its only `.node` files are `win-ca`'s Windows `crypt32` helpers, which aren't loaded under Electron.
- **Windows ARM64:** the "not supported due to missing native dependencies (sqlite3)" warning is removed, since no native dependency blocks that platform any more. win32-arm64 VSIXes were already being published.
- **Docs:** the Python pin in the build action stays for optional certificate addons, with an updated comment, and CONTRIBUTING's native-build section is updated.

**Deprecations:** `prebuild-install@7.1.3` remains only in `docs/` dev tooling (`mintlify` → `@mintlify/cli` → `keytar` 7.9.0, still present in mintlify 4.3.5). Nothing that ships has a deprecated package left.

**Review follow-ups for the `node:sqlite` move (#71)**, in the last commit:
- **Errors keep `sqlite3`'s format.** Errors now read `SQLITE_<NAME>: ...` and carry `code` and `errno`, so the indexer can tell a corrupt or full index (offer "Rebuild codebase index") from a busy one (don't). The chunk-insert error now keeps the SQLite message, and `SQLITE_NOTADB` also offers a rebuild.
- **Index corruption is no longer reported as a warning:**
  - directory indexing fails the run instead of finishing as a warning (that was true with `sqlite3` too);
  - a corrupt `index.sqlite` while taking the index lock is reported instead of escaping as an unhandled rejection;
  - the outer error handler sets `shouldClearIndexes`.
- **A failed COMMIT now rolls back**, so the connection is never left inside a transaction.
- **The event loop gets a turn in every case.** All calls share one queue that checks the time right before each statement, which also covers `Promise.all`. Chunk inserts run in ~15 ms transactions at file boundaries, and each marks its own files complete.
- **Values bind as `sqlite3` 6.0.1 bound them** (recorded): int32 integers as INTEGER, larger integers and Dates as REAL.

Indexing the opencode repo still takes ~150 s and builds the same index (p99 event-loop delay 42 ms, worst stall 323 ms).

## Checklist

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/nextcli-dev/nextcli/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] I have read and agree to the [Contributor License Agreement](https://github.com/nextcli-dev/nextcli/blob/main/CLA.md)
- [x] The relevant docs, if any, have been updated or created
- [x] The relevant tests, if any, have been updated or created

## Screen recording or screenshot

N/A

## Tests

- `core/context/providers/database/database.vitest.ts` checks against the output recorded with dbinfoz (`core/test/fixtures/regression/database/golden.json`):
  - **SQLite (always):** the database is rebuilt from the recorded schema SQL; tables, schemas and context items are byte-identical.
  - **Postgres and MySQL** (`NEXTCLI_DB_TESTS=1`): byte-identical to the recording. With `DBINFOZ_DIR` set, also identical to dbinfoz's live output on the same server. Both passed locally with `scripts/regression/database/compose.yaml`.
  - **MSSQL:** compared with live dbinfoz only. It has no recording because its image doesn't run on Apple Silicon.
- New workflow `database-regression.yml` runs that test on Postgres, MySQL and MSSQL service containers on x86 Linux. It's the first check of MSSQL.
- `core/util/sqlite.vitest.ts`:
  - binding types match a table recorded with `sqlite3` 6.0.1;
  - errors come back as `SQLITE_CONSTRAINT` and `SQLITE_NOTADB`;
  - a COMMIT failed by a reader's lock rolls back, and the next transaction works;
  - `Promise.all` yields.

  Each of these fails on the previous wrapper.
- `core/indexing/sqliteErrors.vitest.ts`:
  - a corrupt `index.sqlite` fails indexing with `shouldClearIndexes`, both during the directory scan and when taking the lock (both fail on the previous indexer);
  - a busy database doesn't fail the batch;
  - sliced chunk inserts let a timer run and mark every file once.
- `extensions/vscode/src/util/util.vitest.ts`: Windows ARM64 is no longer flagged as unsupported.
- A packaged darwin-arm64 VSIX builds, and `validateFilesPresent` passes without `node_sqlite3.node`.
- Local runs from a clean `npm ci`:

  | Area | Typecheck | Lint | Tests |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | core | clean | clean | Jest 816 passed; Vitest 1,914 passed |
  | vscode | clean | clean | 138 passed; bundles |
  | gui | clean | — | — |
  | cli | clean | clean | 1,896 passed |

  `check-deprecations --strict` and prettier also pass.

author: watson1978
body:
`locking_intern` took a slot from the reuse list or allocated one before it called the cache's `form` function. If `form` raised, the slot leaked. Invalid UTF-8 in a Symbol key or an object mode attribute name raises there. On develop, 300,000 calls of `Oj.load(%({"\xFFab":1}).b, mode: :strict, symbol_keys: true)` grew RSS by about 25 MB, and Valgrind reported 64 bytes definitely lost per call.

This change calls `form` first, as `lockless_intern` does, and takes the slot after it locks again. `OJ_CALLOC` doesn't call into Ruby, so allocating while holding the lock can't trigger GC. It also removes `test/valgrind/ruby.supp` and the Rakefile setting that pointed to it. Its only entry suppressed reports from `locking_intern` and hid this leak. The global caches are freed at exit, so `rake test:valgrind` passes without it.

Note: TruffleRuby 40.0.0 hits an internal error and exits inside `rb_check_symbol_cstr` when it gets a String that is not valid UTF-8. CRuby raises `EncodingError` there. So `test_symbol_keys_invalid_utf8` is skipped on TruffleRuby. The object mode attribute name test still runs there.

author: lopeselio
body:
## Bug
Compare on a run prepared without a system prompt (\`my-voice-2\`, 5 spoken answers) showed **empty answers for both base and tuned**.

**Cause:** with no short-answer system prompt, Qwen3 "thinks" for the entire 256-token reply budget and never closes its \`<think>\` block. Pocket Tune hides thinking, so nothing visible was left. I confirmed it from the raw output: 1,294 characters of thinking, never closed.

## Fix
- **Retry with thinking off:** \`reply()\` checks whether the reply ended still inside a think block with no visible text. If so, it asks once more with Qwen3's documented \`/no_think\` switch added to the system message, or as a new system message. The mobile app gets the same fix.
- **Demo answers unchanged:** replies whose think block closes, like the pirate demo runs, never retry. Verified on \`demo-small\`: identical output.
- **UI:** shows "No answer…" instead of a blank box, and comparisons where both answers are empty are no longer saved or shown.

## Testing
- \`npm test\`: 83 pass. New tests:
  - a reply stuck thinking retries with \`/no_think\`, and the hidden thinking never streams
  - a reply with a closed think block makes only one call
  - \`withNoThink\` appends to an existing system prompt
- **Real QVAC:**
  - \`compare runs/my-voice-2\` now returns answers.
  - \`compare runs/demo-small\` gives the same answers as before.

author: prabal-singh
body:
## What the person sees

A video arrives: the agent shows typing within the time of one typing call (on WhatsApp the blue ticks too, as Flow Messaging sends read with typing), kept up every 20 s while the video is downloaded and described, then the reply. Before this, on 0.17.0, nothing showed until the description was back (3.7 s for one video, 4 to 25 s with six at once).

## Why it was silent

Since 0.17.0 (#237, the two-runner fix), typing for a message with the platform's id waits for this runner's store write, so only the runner that has the message types. For a message with files that write comes after `readFiles`, so typing waited on `describeVideo` (and on `transcribe` for a voice note). Every Flow Messaging message has an id; the simulators and `flow test` give none, so they always typed at once.

## Change

- `Conversation.receive`: a message with files types at once, before they are downloaded and read. That covers the slow steps before the model runs: video description, voice note transcription, and the download of any file (photos and PDFs go to the model as they are, with no description step). The typing call is not awaited, so a failing or hanging one never holds up reading or the reply; failures keep today's handling (outside_window waits for the next message, anything else ends typing for the turn with a warning).
- Kept up by the existing `typingLastsMs` timer while the description runs; no double send when the store write lands (typing already showing is not sent again).
- Default on, no new option: `typing: false` / `disable: ["typing"]` still turn it off. Agents have no typing call of their own, so nothing double-sends.
- Two runners given one message with files now both type while they read it; it is still answered once, and neither is left typing (test).

## Tests

- `test/attachments.test.ts`: typing goes out before the download and the describer (and the transcriber) are called, and again at 80% of `typingLastsMs` while the description runs; a typing call that hangs and then fails neither holds up the description nor stops the reply. The first fails on main.
- `test/store.test.ts`: the two-runner race, now shared by a text and a video case.
- `simulators/test/server.test.ts`: the playground shows typing while a video is still being described.
- Local: root 733 (732 pass, 1 skipped), simulators 31, flow-messaging 53, conformance 80, typecheck (root, build, widget, simulators, flow-messaging): all green. GitHub Actions is billing-locked, so PR checks fail at once with no steps.

## Docs

`docs/guarantees.md`, `docs/channels.md` (`typingLastsMs`), `docs/agents.md` (Videos people send), `coding-agents/build-agent-skill.md`, CHANGELOG "Unreleased". No version bump. The public docs repository (flow-engineer/docs) is not changed here.

author: trinh-cloud
body:
## Điểm cần review

Các tiêu chí hợp lệ của một lượt và giao diện `requests.csv` được chốt trước V2 (14–15/11), vì dữ liệu V2 ghi theo định dạng lúc đó, và sau 22/11 không đo lại được. Ngưỡng nằm ở Môi trường §17, cùng chỗ với các ngưỡng hợp lệ đã có (50 ms, 70 %, 15 s).

- **`throttle_ok` theo tỷ lệ thời gian** (thay cho `nr_throttled == 0`): `throttled_usec` ÷ thời gian giữa hai lần đọc `cpu.stat` < 0,1 %.
  - Lý do: ở ĐG1-mini 05/11, một chu kỳ throttle 1,4–4,4 ms trong mức đo khoảng 3 phút (≤ 0,0025 %) đã loại cả lượt, trong khi lệch lịch p99 chỉ 2 ms. Lượt 20 req/s trên kind dưới đây cũng có đúng 1 chu kỳ 4,7 ms.
  - Kernel cộng `throttled_usec` theo từng CPU, nên tỷ lệ này là cận trên, tức tiêu chí chỉ chặt hơn. Không tính được tỷ lệ thì quay về `nr_throttled == 0`.
  - Phương án không chọn: bỏ hẳn kiểm throttle. Thiết kế đòi kiểm, còn lệch lịch và event loop chỉ bắt được gián tiếp.
- **Event loop có ngưỡng số** (trước đây chỉ báo cáo): p99 < 50 ms và max < 500 ms.
  - p99 dùng cùng ngưỡng với lệch lịch gửi, vì hai kiểm này đo cùng một sai số, một lúc gửi, một lúc nhận chunk.
  - Max bắt một lần nghẽn dài mà p99 không thấy (1 % của lượt 25 phút là 15 s); 500 ms là 20 % ngưỡng TTFT.
  - Số đo trên kind (bảng dưới): p99 ≤ 4,9 ms, max ≤ 56 ms, ngay cả khi CPU lên 87 %. Hai ngưỡng còn dư ít nhất 9 lần.
- **Khoảng trống scrape chỉ tính `up == 1`.** Prometheus ghi `up = 0` mỗi lần scrape lỗi, nên trước đây một pod bị scrape lỗi liên tục không để lại khoảng trống nào (phát hiện khi soát PR #19).
  - Mép cửa sổ tính theo pod: pod có từ đầu lượt tính từ đầu pha chính; pod còn sống, không đang bị xoá, ở cuối thì tính tới cuối pha.
  - Pod mới đang cold start và pod đang drain không bị tính phần chưa có hoặc đã hết `/metrics`.
  - Pod sống suốt lượt mà không scrape được lần nào, hoặc không có chuỗi `up` nào, thì khoảng trống là cả cửa sổ.
  - `session.py` truyền tên pod từ `pods_start` và `pods_end` vào.
- **Giao diện `requests.csv`** (Môi trường §14.2): giữ cột `id`, `n_in_target` và file `loadgen.json` mà runner và `capacity.py` đang dùng. Một request thành công khi và chỉ khi cột `error` rỗng; `status` chỉ là mã HTTP ở phần đầu câu trả lời, nên stream bị cắt giữa chừng vẫn có `status` 200. `capacity.py` đã lọc theo `error`, không phải sửa.
- **Vận hành §3.2** khớp lại với `observability/alerts/llm.yaml`: `LLMErrorRateHigh` có `for: 1m`; `KedaScalerErrors` dùng `keda_scaler_detail_errors_total` (tên của KEDA 2.21), `for: 1m`.

Phần cần đọc kỹ: `scrape_gaps` trong `collect.py`, `summarize` trong `loadgen/checks.py`, Môi trường §17. Phần lướt: test, các mục tài liệu khác.

## Thay đổi

- `loadgen/checks.py`: thêm `loop_lag_ok` và `throttled_pct`; `throttle_ok` theo tỷ lệ thời gian. `loadgen/__main__.py` đo thời gian giữa hai lần đọc `cpu.stat`.
- `experiments/runner/checks.py`: lý do trượt liệt kê mọi khoá `*_ok` bằng False của `loadgen`, nên tiêu chí mới tự hiện ra.
- `experiments/runner/collect.py`, `session.py`: `scrape_gaps` như trên. Range selector làm tròn lên, như `signal_gap`.
- Môi trường §3.6, §9, §14.2, §15, §17; Vận hành §3.2.

## Kiểm tra

- pytest `loadgen` 47 passed; `experiments` 79 passed, 1 skipped (cần `fcntl`, không đổi trong PR này); trên Python 3.15 và 3.11. ruff check, ruff format --check, lychee (0 lỗi) đều đạt.
- Đo event loop trên kind: simulator patch tạm (mỗi stream 100 chunk/s), 3 replica tĩnh, pod `loadgen` 1 CPU. Runner nạp code `loadgen` ở mỗi lượt: lượt 10 req/s chạy code `main`, lượt 20 req/s chạy code của nhánh này:

  | λ | Chunk/s | CPU tối đa | Event loop p99 / max | Lệch lịch p99 | Throttle | TTFT p50 / p99 (sim đặt 200 ms) | Kết quả |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | 10 req/s | ~2.500 | 53,1 % | 2,6 / 36,5 ms | 3,2 ms | 0 | 207 / 214 ms | hợp lệ |
  | 20 req/s | ~5.100 | 86,6 % | 4,9 / 56,0 ms | 6,1 ms | 1 chu kỳ, 4,7 ms (0,0026 %): luật mới đạt, luật cũ sẽ loại | 210 / 235 ms | invalid (`cpu_ok`) |

- `experiments/matrix-sim.yaml` (S1 rồi A2) chạy bằng nhánh này trên kind, 2 lượt liền, không can thiệp tay (mốc 10/11 của Kế hoạch §1.1):
  - `S1-CONST2-1`: hợp lệ; event loop p99 2,1 / max 17,0 ms; CPU 13,0 %; `throttled_pct` 0; khoảng trống scrape 5 s.
  - `A2-CONST2-1`: hợp lệ; scale 1 → 3 replica, về 1 replica sau 357 s; 357/357 request, 0 lỗi; event loop p99 1,9 / max 16,9 ms; CPU 20,7 %; tín hiệu scale có 3 chuỗi, khoảng trống 5 s.
  - Phiên chạy với `scrape_gaps` trước khi thêm mép theo pod (sửa sau soát). Chạy lại bản cuối trên Prometheus của kind, cùng cửa sổ, chỉ đọc: cả 3 pod của A2 (1 pod có từ đầu, 2 pod mới) và pod của S1 đều 5 s, tức mép theo pod không loại nhầm pod mới.
- `/code-review high`: 8 phát hiện, sửa 6. Không sửa: chép ngưỡng sang `00-thong-so.md` (lý do ở đầu mô tả).

## Chưa làm

- CPU của `loadgen` tăng theo số chunk/s: khoảng 0,2 ms mỗi chunk trên laptop chạy kind. Ở nhà, ĐG1-mini λ = 10 cũng khoảng 2.500 chunk/s nhưng tốn 25,5 %. Event loop chạy một luồng, nên thêm lõi cho pod không giúp. Nếu CPU của VM thuê chậm như laptop, các lượt KB3 của V2 có thể bị loại vì `cpu_ok` (đỉnh 3C; với C ước 4–6 req/s là 12–18 req/s, khoảng 3.000–4.600 chunk/s). Việc tiếp theo, trước V2: `loadgen` chạy nhiều tiến trình, chia lịch gửi theo `id`.
- Đối chiếu TTFT phía client với histogram TTFT của server (Môi trường §9): để cho `build_tables.py`.

author: ijjs
body:
## 요약
- #199 수정(상위: QLink-Bookmarks/alink-channel#79에서 발견)
- 링크 제목 정렬(`orderKey=title`, 기존 `order=laxico`)과 폴더 `order=laxico`가 앱 전용 ICU collation `app_sort` 하나를 따른다. 한글은 가나다순이고, 한글·라틴이 섞인 제목도 첫 글자부터 비교한다. 라틴 문자는 대소문자와 상관없이 알파벳순이다(대소문자만 다르면 서로 붙는다). 문자 종류 순서는 기호 → 숫자 → 한글 → 라틴 → 일본어 가나 → 한자 → 그 밖(키릴 등)이고, 숫자는 숫자로 비교한다(`파일2` < `파일10`).
- 사용자 로케일은 받지 않는다. 앱 전체가 이 규칙 하나를 쓴다.
- 내림차순은 오름차순을 정확히 뒤집은 것이고, 같은 제목이면 지금처럼 `id`로 이어 정렬한다. API 계약(파라미터, 응답, 커서 형식, ErrorCode)은 바뀌지 않는다.

## 원인
- 제목·폴더 이름 정렬과 keyset 비교가 collation 없이 컬럼을 비교해 DB 기본 collation을 따랐다. 마이그레이션에도 collation 지정이 없다.
- dev·운영(RDS for PostgreSQL 18)의 기본 collation은 glibc 계열이다. AWS 문서상 RDS 기본 collation 라이브러리는 glibc 2.26과 호환된다. glibc 2.26 `en_US.UTF-8`은 한글 음절을 1차 비교에서 무시한다. 그래서 한글만 있는 제목은 가나다와 무관한 순서로 맨 앞에 모이고, `이벤터스(Event-us)`·`네이버(NAVER)`처럼 섞인 제목은 라틴 문자 자리로 정렬됐다. glibc 2.26 환경(Amazon Linux 2)에서 같은 제목을 정렬해 dev와 같은 순서를 재현했다.
- 로컬과 테스트 컨테이너(musl 기반 PostgreSQL 이미지)는 바이트 순서로 정렬한다. 한글은 가나다로 나와서 기존 테스트가 이 결함을 잡지 못했다. 대신 라틴이 한글보다 앞에 오고 대문자가 소문자보다 앞에 오는, dev와도 다른 순서였다.

## 바뀐 점
- 마이그레이션(새): `V17__app_sort_collation.sql` — `CREATE COLLATION IF NOT EXISTS app_sort (provider = icu, locale = 'und-u-kn-kr-hang-latn-kana-hani');`. deterministic(기본값)이라 같은 제목의 `=` 비교와 `id` 이음은 그대로 맞는다. 테이블·컬럼·인덱스 변경은 없다.
  - locale은 PostgreSQL이 쓰는 BCP 47 표준형이다(키 순서만 다른 `und-u-kr-hang-latn-kana-hani-kn`과 같은 규칙이고, 표준형을 쓰면 `using standard form` NOTICE가 나지 않는다).
  - `kn`: 숫자를 숫자로 비교한다.
  - `kr-hang-latn-kana-hani`: 문자 종류 순서. `kana` 하나로 히라가나·가타카나를 함께 둔다(`hira`와 같이 쓰면 ICU가 거부한다). 나열하지 않은 문자 종류는 그 뒤에 온다.
  - 다른 테이블·스키마 객체처럼 Flyway 스키마에 만들고, 쿼리는 같은 `currentSchema`에서 이름으로 찾는다.
- 공통: `common/search/KoreanCollated.kt` → `SortCollated.kt` — `(<expr> COLLATE app_sort)` 표현식. 한국어 전용 규칙이 아니라서 이름을 바꿨다.
- 링크: `DbLinkRepository.sortKeys`의 `TITLE` 정렬 키가 `SortCollated(Links.title)`이다. `ORDER BY`와 keyset 비교(`>`·`<`·`=`)가 같은 정렬 키 표현식을 쓰므로 정렬과 커서 이어 받기가 같은 규칙이다. 검색어(`query`)와 함께 제목으로 정렬하는 경로도 같다.
- 폴더: `DbFolderRepository`의 `LAXICO` `orderBy`와 커서 조건이 `SortCollated(Folders.name)`이다.
- 도메인·ErrorCode 변경 없음. `links.title`·`folders.name`에는 원래 인덱스가 없어 실행 계획도 같다(정렬 비교 함수만 바뀜).

## 배포·롤백
- 앱 시작 때 Flyway가 V17을 적용한다. RDS for PostgreSQL 18은 ICU를 포함하므로 만들어질 것으로 보지만, collation을 만들지 못하면 **앱 시작(배포)이 실패**한다. 배포 직후 아래 스모크로 확인한다.
- 권한: `CREATE COLLATION`은 대상 스키마의 `CREATE` 권한만 필요하다. 앱 DB 사용자가 이미 같은 스키마에 테이블·인덱스를 만들어 온 사용자이므로 새 권한은 없다(슈퍼유저 불필요).
- ICU 버전: PostgreSQL은 collation을 만들 때 ICU 버전(`collversion`)을 기록한다. 이후 엔진 업그레이드로 ICU 버전이 바뀌어 `collation "app_sort" has version mismatch` 경고가 나면, 정렬 순서가 미세하게 달라질 수 있다는 뜻이다. 이 collation을 쓰는 인덱스는 없으므로 다시 만들 것 없이 `ALTER COLLATION app_sort REFRESH VERSION;`으로 기록만 갱신하면 된다.
- 배포 순간 앱이 들고 있던 제목·`laxico` 커서는 옛 순서 기준 값이다. 그래서 배포 직후 다음 한 페이지에서 경계가 한 번 어긋날(빠지거나 겹칠) 수 있다. 그 뒤 커서는 새 순서로 이어지므로 일시적이다.
- 롤백: **코드만 되돌려도 안전하다.**
  - 이전 빌드에는 V17이 없다. Flyway는 기본값(`ignoreMigrationPatterns = *:future`)으로 빌드보다 새 버전의 적용된 마이그레이션을 무시하므로, V17 기록이 남아 있어도 이전 빌드가 정상 시작한다.
  - `app_sort`는 남아 있어도 쓰는 객체(컬럼·인덱스·뷰)가 없어 영향이 없다.
  - collation까지 지우려면(선택) 앱 스키마에서 둘을 함께 실행한다. 기록만 남기고 collation만 지우면 다시 배포할 때 V17이 적용되지 않아 제목 정렬이 500이 된다.
    ```sql
    DROP COLLATION IF EXISTS <앱 스키마>.app_sort;
    DELETE FROM <앱 스키마>.flyway_schema_history WHERE version = '17';
    ```

## dev 배포 후 스모크 확인
1. DB 권한이 있으면 dev DB에서(앱 스키마가 `search_path`에 있을 때):
   ```sql
   SELECT collname, collprovider, colllocale, collisdeterministic FROM pg_collation WHERE collname = 'app_sort';
   SELECT string_agg(t, ' | ' ORDER BY t COLLATE app_sort)
   FROM (VALUES ('Zebra'), ('파일10'), ('東京タワー'), ('apple'), ('トマト'), ('파일2'), ('가나다'), ('Москва')) AS v(t);
   -- 가나다 | 파일2 | 파일10 | apple | Zebra | トマト | 東京タワー | Москва
   ```
2. API로(`Alink-Requester` 헤더 포함):
   - `GET /api/links?orderKey=title&order=asc`가 200이다. 한글 → 라틴 → 가나 → 한자 → 그 밖 순이다. `네이버(NAVER) - …`는 `네이버` 근처, `이벤터스(Event-us)`는 `이기적 …` 뒤에 있다.
   - `order=desc`는 정확한 역순이다. `nextCursor`로 끝까지 받아도 겹치거나 빠지는 링크가 없다.
   - `order=laxico`는 `orderKey=title&order=asc`와 같은 순서다.
   - `GET /api/folders?order=laxico`가 200이고 이름이 같은 규칙으로 정렬된다.

## 테스트 결과
- 전체 `./gradlew spotlessApply build`(CI와 같음, `lambda/link-fetch` Lambda ZIP 있음): **BUILD SUCCESSFUL**, 132 suites, **1241 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors, 0 skipped**. `spotlessCheck`·`test`·`jacocoTestCoverageVerification`·`check` 포함.
- 그 뒤 locale 문자열만 표준형으로 바꾸고(규칙 동일) 대상 spec을 다시 돌렸다: `GetLinksServiceTest` 61, `GetFoldersServiceTest` 44, 모두 통과.
- 테스트 컨테이너도 Flyway로 V17을 적용하고 그 collation으로 돈다. 기대 순서가 `ko-x-icu`·바이트 순서 어느 쪽과도 다르므로(아래), 테스트가 통과한 것 자체가 `app_sort`로 정렬했다는 확인이다.
- 테스트 제목 집합(기대 오름차순): `㈜아이센스, 1인 앱 개발, 2026 회고, 가나다, 네이버, 네이버(NAVER) 검색, 이기적 영진닷컴, 이벤터스(Event-us), 파일2, 파일10, 하네스, apple, Apple Developer, Banana, cherry, Zebra, とうきょう, トマト, 北京, 東京タワー, Москва`(+ 대소문자 쌍용 `APPLE`). 폴더는 `3월 여행, 10월 여행, 가계부, 업무, 하루, Alpha, beta, zoo 폴더, ノート, 旅行, Москва`. 넣는 순서와 저장일은 무작위다. 페이지 테스트는 같은 제목 세 쌍(`네이버`·`apple`·`北京`)을 넣고 페이지 크기 1·2·3으로 끝까지 받는다. 기대 순서는 로컬 PostgreSQL 18에서 같은 ICU locale로 먼저 확인했다.

### 수정 전 코드에서 실패 확인
- `main`(d575228) 임시 worktree에 이 PR의 테스트 파일 2개만 얹어 두 spec을 실행했다 → **105개 중 9개 실패. 새 케이스 9개가 모두 실패했고 기존 96개는 통과했다.**
  - 예: 폴더는 기대 `[3월 여행, 10월 여행, 가계부, 업무, 하루, Alpha, beta, zoo 폴더, ノート, 旅行, Москва]`인데 실제 `[10월 여행, 3월 여행, Alpha, beta, zoo 폴더, Москва, ノート, 旅行, 가계부, 업무, 하루]`였다.
- 참고로 이 PR의 첫 커밋(`ko-x-icu`, 83007e8)에서도 돌렸다 → **105개 중 8개 실패**(대소문자 쌍 케이스만 통과). `ko-x-icu`는 한자를 한글 바로 뒤에 두고(`네이버(NAVER) 검색, 東京タワー, 北京, 이기적 …`) 숫자를 글자로 비교한다(`파일10` < `파일2`).
- 한계: dev의 "한글을 무시하는" 순서 자체는 musl 테스트 컨테이너에서 재현되지 않는다. 수정 뒤에는 쿼리에 collation을 명시하므로 DB 기본 collation과 무관하게 테스트와 같은 순서가 나온다.

## 테스트 기준 (#199 §4)
### Service — GetLinksService
- Given 한글만 있는 제목, 한글 뒤에 괄호 속 라틴 문자가 붙은 제목, 대소문자가 섞인 라틴 제목, 숫자로 시작하는 제목, 기호로 시작하는 제목의 링크들
  - [x] `getLinks` When 제목 오름차순으로 조회하면 → Then 한국어 사전순이다: 한글 제목은 가나다순이고, 한글·라틴이 섞인 제목은 첫 글자부터 비교한 자리에 있고, 라틴 제목은 대소문자와 상관없이 알파벳순이고, 문자 종류는 기호 → 숫자 → 한글 → 라틴 → 가나 → 한자 → 그 밖 순이고, 숫자는 숫자로 비교한다 (회귀) — 대소문자만 다른 제목 쌍이 붙는 것은 별도 케이스로도 고정
  - [x] `getLinks` When 제목 내림차순으로 조회하면 → Then 제목 오름차순의 정확한 역순이다 (회귀)
  - [x] `getLinks` When 기존 `laxico`로 조회하면 → Then 제목 오름차순과 같은 순서다 (회귀)
  - [x] `getLinks` When 검색어와 함께 제목 오름차순으로 조회하면 → Then 메타데이터가 일치한 링크가 먼저 오고 그 안에서 한국어 사전순이다

author: paulm981
body:
Part of #127

## What changes

**Going into Broadcast or a Wall with many servers no longer freezes the window.** Before, every terminal fitted itself to its tile at the same moment, which held the window for seconds with 36 servers. Now they settle a few at a time: the window keeps answering, and the tiles fill in, usually within a second.

For the reviewer:
- **The cause, measured.** A Chromium benchmark with 36 xterm terminals did what the app does when a Wall opens: move every terminal into its tile, then refit, redraw and set up the GPU for each, all in one frame.
  - A refit re-wraps the whole scrollback (10,000 lines by default), so that one frame took 170 ms with empty terminals and **about 1 s with full ones**. On a real machine, with real sessions and the servers redrawing after the resize, that's the 3–4 s seen in the test on fork.26.
  - Closing 34 terminals took under 10 ms, so the freezes came from the switches, not the closes.
- **The fix**, all in the fork's own code:
  - `terminalDock.ts` gets `settleAfterMove`. It runs each moved terminal's refit, redraw and GPU step in the order they moved, within 8 ms of each frame.
  - A newer move replaces a job still waiting, and a closed terminal's job never runs.
  - `TerminalView`'s `moved` hands its work to the queue instead of one `requestAnimationFrame` each.
  - A terminal opening for the first time goes through the queue too, so opening many tabs at once is spread out as well.
- **Measured with the fix** (same benchmark, full terminals):

  | | Before | After |
  |---|---|---|
  | Longest the window couldn't answer | 870–1,020 ms | **116–121 ms** |
  | All tiles settled | 1.0–1.1 s | 1.3 s |

  The 120 ms left is one terminal's own work, mostly the software GPU set-up of the headless browser; a real GPU is faster.
- **The queue's own rules, checked by bundling `terminalDock.ts` with a stand-in frame clock:** the order the terminals moved, the 8 ms budget, a newer move replacing a waiting job, a closed terminal skipped, and stopping when empty. There's no frontend test runner yet (#61), so this check isn't in CI.
- **Checks:** `npm run typecheck` and `npm run build` pass. No Rust file changed.
- **Not done here:** #127's other parts, typing lag in a 36-server Broadcast and the freeze after reconnecting. This pull request doesn't close it.

## Checklist

- [x] CHANGELOG.md has a line for it under `## Next release`, ending with the issue's link. #42's lines, which shipped in v0.4.0-fork.23, now have that heading.
- [x] If the original project does this differently, FORK.md says so in "Where it behaves differently". Walls are the fork's own.
- [ ] It was tested in the app, not only by the tests. **Not tried in the app yet.** Please repeat the 36-server test on Windows:
  - go into Broadcast or a Wall and back to tabs a few times: the window should keep answering, and the tiles fill in within about a second;
  - **Copy diagnostics** afterwards: the "freeze(s) this session" count should stay at 0 or be well under a second.

## Giving back

No. Walls are the fork's own.

author: johnschettini-ship-it
body:
## Problem

The mission title showed app-injected text instead of the prompt. Seen live in the `crew_status` log: the person typed "hi", and Reception logged

```
Reception logged a new request: "<system-reminder> The user started this session without c...".
```

The next prompt had no reminder in front of it and was titled correctly.

## Cause

The `prompt.submit` hook in `hooks/register.tsx` passed the raw `e.text` to `startMission`. The app sometimes puts `<system-reminder>...</system-reminder>` blocks ahead of the person's words, and `cleanTitle` only trims whitespace and cuts the text to 60 characters.

## Fix

- `hooks/register.tsx`: remove `<system-reminder>` blocks (multiline, non-greedy) from the prompt before calling `startMission`. If nothing is left, it passes an empty string, so the title falls back to "Untitled task".
- The fix is in the hooks module, not `hooks/world.ts`, which `source/build_world.py` regenerates from `source/agent-boardroom.html`.

## Test

- New case `2b` in `tests/workplace.test.tsx`: submits `"<system-reminder>\nfoo\n</system-reminder>\nhi"` and checks that the phase line and the Reception log read `"hi"`.
- Without the fix, `2b` fails with the reported symptom (title `"<system-reminder> foo </system-reminder> hi"`).
- With the fix, `claude plugin test .` passes 19 of 19, and `claude plugin validate .` passes.

body:
## Intent

делать первый пункт.

Первый пункт из разбора памяти: убрать ежесекундный опрос `widgets.list` и `layout.get`, который в главном процессе каждый раз заново транслирует все виджеты. Вместо опроса держать кэш и сообщать окнам, когда файлы виджетов реально изменились. Повторный список без изменений на диске не должен транслировать виджеты. Горячая подмена виджета после правки файла должна остаться. Публичные контракты расширений не менять.

## What Changed

- The main process caches widget and layout descriptors and returns that cache from `widgets.list` and `layout.get` when the extension tree fingerprint is unchanged, so those calls do not recompile modules.
- Renderers no longer poll discovery every second. The popover and pinned windows reload widgets and the layout when the main process emits `baby-menu:widgets:modules-changed`, after a debounced `fs.watch` or a 45-second mtime/size walk sees a real file change.
- The new `widgets.onModulesChanged` hook is host-only on `BabyMenuApi`. Extension-facing contracts are unchanged.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The catalog publishes a snapshot only when the tree fingerprint is unchanged across compile, and an exhausted race leaves the cache empty and notifies renderers so the next list reloads.

The Test agent exceeded its invocation budget before live validation completed; no evidence was gathered for this head.

author: gnoviawan
body:
## Summary

People who update from Termul 0.4.x to Troupe 0.5.0 open an app with a new name and could think they installed something else or lost their data. This PR shows them one calm notice, once per device or browser: "Termul is now Troupe", one line saying it is the same app and their projects, chats, settings and sign-ins are unchanged, and a single "Got it" button. A fresh Troupe install never sees it.

## Related Issue

No related issue. This is part of the Troupe rebrand plan (`_bmad-output/planning-artifacts/research/technical-troupe-rebrand-2026-11-03/plan.md`, §3 step 6).

## Type of Change

- [x] feat: new feature

## What Changed

- `src/renderer/lib/rename-notice.ts` decides "updated vs fresh" from evidence a 0.4.x install already left behind. Since v0.4.50 both renderer roots write `termul.deviceId` to `localStorage` on every launch, so any other key starting with `termul` (0.4.x wrote `termul.`, `termul-` and `termul:` keys) means this device ran an earlier version. Keys from other apps on a shared origin do not count. The check runs at module load, before React mounts and before `ensureClientIdentity` mints the device id, so a fresh install's own writes never count. A fresh install is recorded as `fresh` right away; dismissing records `dismissed`. Both live under the new key `termul.renameNotice` (internal storage keys keep the `termul.` prefix per the rebrand's keep-forever list). When storage is unavailable or the device jumped from before 0.4.50 with an empty origin, the notice stays hidden, which is the safe way to be wrong.
- `src/renderer/hooks/use-rename-notice.ts` reuses the app's existing sonner toast (the same one `useUpdateToast` uses). It stays until dismissed: "Got it" or a swipe records it; closing the app first shows it again next launch.
- Both roots (`App.tsx` for the web client and phone UI, `TauriApp.tsx` for desktop and shared-live remote) mount the hook in `AppEffects`, next to `useUpdateToast`.
- `scripts/rebrand/rules.ts` gets a `rename-notice` keep entry scoped to the notice file and its test, so `bun run rebrand --check` and future codemod runs leave the old name in the title. `rules.test.ts` asserts it is kept in those files and renamed anywhere else.

## How It Was Tested

- [x] `npx biome ci --diagnostic-level=error` on the 7 changed files
- [x] `bun run typecheck:web` and `bun run typecheck:test`
- [x] `npx vitest run src/renderer/hooks/use-rename-notice.test.tsx scripts/rebrand src/renderer/App.test.tsx src/renderer/TauriApp.test.tsx src/renderer/main.web-bundle.test.ts`: 7 files, 149 passed, 1 skipped. The hook test renders the real `Toaster` and asserts the literal title, description and button text for an updated device (one case per 0.4.x key form), no notice on a fresh install (also after the app writes its own device id), none after "Got it", the notice again after a launch with no dismiss, none when only another app's key is stored, and none when storage throws.
- [x] `bun run rebrand --check --paths <file>` on every changed renderer file: `No "Termul" left.`
- [x] Manual verification completed: Playwright against an isolated `termul-server` on loopback. Each profile first loaded the Nov 5 pre-rebrand web build (it wrote only `termul.deviceId`), then this branch's build in the same profile:

```
desktop old build: notice=0 storage={"notice":null,"deviceId":true,"keys":1}
desktop after update: notice=1 storage={"notice":null,"deviceId":true,"keys":2}
desktop after Got it: notice=0 storage={"notice":"dismissed","deviceId":true,"keys":3}
desktop reload after Got it: notice=0
phone old build: notice=0 storage={"notice":null,"deviceId":true,"keys":1}
phone after update: notice=1 storage={"notice":null,"deviceId":true,"keys":2}
phone after Got it: notice=0 storage={"notice":"dismissed","deviceId":true,"keys":3}
phone reload after Got it: notice=0
desktop fresh first launch: notice=0 storage={"notice":"fresh","deviceId":true,"keys":2}
desktop fresh second launch: notice=0 storage={"notice":"fresh","deviceId":true,"keys":3}
phone fresh first launch: notice=0 storage={"notice":"fresh","deviceId":true,"keys":2}
phone fresh second launch: notice=0 storage={"notice":"fresh","deviceId":true,"keys":3}
```

Not run here: the Tauri desktop app itself. Desktop `localStorage` survives the update because the Tauri identifier `com.termul-manager.app` (which names the webview data dir) never changes.

## Screenshots or Recordings

Captured at 1440x900 and 390x844 from the running web client. The notice is a bottom-right toast on desktop and a full-width toast at the bottom on phone, using the stock toast styling (neutral card, default button). Screenshots are kept with the rebrand program's evidence, not uploaded here.

author: baaaaaaaka
body:
## Why

A Windows helper (still running v0.1.20 from `cxp.exe`, install record naming `codex-proxy.exe` at rc.66) could not update to rc.68:

```
candidate-owned update failed: exit status 1: candidate update: inspect managed stable cxp entry:
stable entry target …\.local\bin\cxp.exe does not match the running runtime and is not a recorded managed helper
```

`install.ps1` writes `cxp.exe` as a **copy** of the recorded `codex-proxy.exe` (on Linux/macOS `cxp` is a symlink that resolves to the recorded file). When a candidate-owned update cannot replace that copy because the Teams service holds it, the deferred repair gives up after its wait and `cxp.exe` keeps an older helper while the active runtime moves on. The ownership check only accepted the recorded `codex-proxy.exe` itself, so the next update refused `cxp.exe`, and every later one would too.

Nothing was renamed: the `codex-proxy.exe` + `cxp.exe` layout dates from c443e99f (2026-06-29), and the update code had not changed since rc.66. Processes already run as `cxp`/`cxp.exe` (the Teams service prefers the `cxp` entry; runtimes live at `.cxp-runtime/versions/<v>/cxp(.exe)`).

## What changed

- `candidateupdate.recordOwnsStableEntry`: the install record owns the recorded `codex-proxy` and the `cxp` beside it. A managed record and a verified helper build are still required; anything else is refused as before.

## Validation

- Unit: the ownership rule (Linux and Windows names; explicit or missing records refuse); the update from the field state succeeds and refreshes `cxp`, and without a record it still refuses. The update test fails without the fix with the field error.
- Windows smoke `scripts/ci/windows_stale_cxp_entry_smoke.ps1` (nightly and release): builds v0.1.20, rc.66 and rc.69 helpers from source, lays out the field state, runs the real candidate-owned update with and without the install record, then runs the refreshed `cxp.exe`.

body:
## Add the `transfer` (havaleh) market

[tgju.org/transfer](https://www.tgju.org/transfer) publishes foreign currency remittance rates using the same server-rendered `market-table` markup as `/currency`, `/gold-chart` and `/coin`. The existing scraper reads it unchanged, so this PR registers it as a new market, following `wiki/Adding-a-Market.md`.

### Changes
- **`market.go`**: `Transfer` market at `/transfer`, with the aliases `transfers`, `remittance`, `havaleh`, `havale` and `حواله`
- **`client.go`**: `Client.Transfer(ctx)` shortcut
- **Fixture**: `testdata/transfer.html`, taken from the live page on 2026-11-07 and trimmed the same way `make fixtures` trims the others. The fixtures tool is registered for it too.
- **Tests**: `TestFetchParsesEveryBoard`, `TestItem…`, `TestMarkets`, `TestParseMarket`, `TestTablesOnSavedPages`, `/v1/markets/transfer`, `/v1/items/transfer_usd`
- **Docs**: OpenAPI `Market` enum, README, docs site, wiki (Instrument Keys, Running the Service), CHANGELOG, CLI help

`/v1/markets`, `/v1/items/{key}`, `FetchAll`, `Item` and the CLI pick the board up through the registry. The legacy `/api/price/*` routes are unchanged, as the guide recommends.

### Example

author: luizfsantos-alt
body:
Implementa a `docs/SPEC_v3.1.md`, que saiu da crítica de mecânicas, e troca o logo do menu.

## O que muda no jogo
- **Mexidas:** 13 magias novas que mudam os seus próprios dados durante a alocação e devolvem o dado à mão para outra magia. Cada personagem jogável começa com uma: Segunda Chance, Ajuste Fino, Pico, Sangria ou Virar.
  - Quando resolve, o cartão sai do palco. As magias sem uso disponível também somem do palco.
  - As mexidas determinísticas podem ser desfeitas. As aleatórias (Segunda Chance e Tudo ou Nada) são definitivas.
- **Imitação Barata:** acabou a corrente exponencial. As cópias não alimentam Imitação, Sacrifício nem Transfusão.
- **Dado mudado:** quando algo muda o valor de um dado (mexida, Alquimista, Mercúrio etc.), ele mostra o valor original riscado e o selo da causa.
- **Portas:** cada porta mostra o arquétipo do inimigo. As moedas passam a 3/7/12/20 e a recompensa a 2/3/3/4 opções.
- **Desgaste:** cada vitória comum recupera 10% da vida máxima; a parada de Cura recupera 35%.
- **Mestres:** kit fixo, montado para combinar com a regra de cada um, e vida ×2,6.
- **Escala do inimigo:** depois do andar 10, ele ganha 0,35 melhoria por andar, e os adesivos dele acumulam.
- **Assassino:** a Esquiva Melhorada passa a 2× por luta. Combinada com o Ajuste Fino, estava forte demais (andar 10 em 50%).
- **Logo do menu:** imagem nova, com o fundo magenta recortado.

## Ferramentas
- **Bot novo do simulador** (`sim/bot.gd`, `--bot=old` para o antigo): escolhe porta, recompensa e parada por pontuação. Relatório com meios-turnos, chance por posição no bloco e uso de cada magia.
- **Telemetria local:** grava as últimas 50 jornadas no aparelho. O menu ganha o botão "Copiar dados das jornadas", e `sim/telemetria.gd` resume o arquivo.

## Verificação
- 228 testes do GUT passam; `sim/check.gd` não acusa nenhum script com erro.
- **Calibração** (bot novo, 500 jornadas por personagem): o andar 10 fica entre 27% e 33% para os cinco jogáveis, e o Mestre é a luta mais difícil de cada ato. Tabela completa em `docs/SPEC_v3.1.md` §12.
- **Critérios que não fecharam:**
  - O uso da mexida inicial fica abaixo de 60% dos turnos no Vampiro e no Bárbaro.
  - O limite de 40% de uso por mexida estava mal definido: todas as mexidas novas passam dele.
- **Capturas conferidas:** menu, portas e mexida.

author: robinnorberg
body:
## Lane A of F1-F15: the local (offline) forge adapter and config

Addresses **F1** (no local or offline forge) for the forge layer: adapter, types and config. Lanes B (engine) and C (setup/check/board/enqueue/poll) wire it in.

### What it adds
- `ForgeKind` `'local'`, the `{ type: 'local-backlog'; label? }` intake source, `LocalForgeConfig`, `ResolvedForgeConfig.local`, `ForgeOptions.local` (`baseSha()` getter, `workingTree`), `ForgeItem.uncommitted`, and an optional `Forge.limitations()`.
- `src/forge/local/`:
  - `backlog.ts` parses `.copilot/backlog/<id>-<slug>.md` with a strict frontmatter. A malformed file gets an error that names it.
  - `tracker.ts`: a run reads items at the base sha with `git ls-tree` and `git show`, so they are trusted. check, board and enqueue can also read the working tree, where an uncommitted item is untrusted. Comments and progress go to `.omg/factory/local/items/<id>/`. The enqueue writes `createItem`, `updateItem` and `addMarker` change backlog files.
  - `store.ts` is the JSON PR store under the engine-owned stateDir, with a lock directory and atomic rename.
  - `reviews.ts` reads PR heads and bases from the bare mirror's refs. A PR becomes MERGED once its head is an ancestor of the mirror base.
  - `checks.ts` reads back the engine-written `local-gate` record for the exact head. `rerun` removes the record.
  - `merge.ts` returns the human's `git -C <root> merge --no-ff <sha>` command. `mirror.ts` holds the paths, the repo id and the argv builders, all pure.
- `config.ts` (D1): `kind: "local"` overrides a GitHub or ADO origin only when it comes from the user config or the base-committed file. With no parseable origin, any layer may set it. `local.gate` is read from the trusted layers only. `backlogDir` and `gateTimeoutMinutes` may come from any layer. `resolveForgeConfig(..., originUrl: string | undefined, context?: { root, stateDir })`.

### Tests
Unit tests per module, a D1 trust test, and the no-spawn test extended to local: the adapter only ever runs git, and never gh, az or copilot.

### Outside lane A's files (approved by the lead)
`src/factory/setup/intake-pick.ts` gets the two minimal `local-backlog` cases that its exhaustive `IntakeSource` switches need: format returns `local-backlog[:<label>]`, and validate makes no server call. A test covers them. Lane C owns any further change to that file.

### Mirror footprint
The first push of OMC's dev history (6383 commits, 108k objects) makes a 93.5 MiB bare mirror and takes 43 s. The dogfood repo's mirror is 131 KB. Later pushes are incremental.

author: saltnpepper97
body:
When a client destroys and recreates its DRM synchronization object on the same surface, upstream's stored object association can remain empty. Halley then selected implicit synchronization despite a pending explicit acquire point, allowing unfinished client buffers into renderer state.

Honor each commit's pending acquire point through the public Smithay API, skip implicit waits when it is present, and preserve fatal rejection when its event source cannot be registered. Keep the current official Smithay pin and buffer-release policy unchanged. Update the changelog and testing guide.

Validation: the real-DRM protocol regressions failed with the previous association gate and pass with this change. They cover initial creation, repeated recreation, unrelated-surface progress, subsequent bufferless commits, and registration failure. The workspace suite passed 1,409 tests (118 ignored), strict all-feature Clippy and Rustdoc passed, and the release workspace build and CLI smoke checks passed. All nine PR checks passed, including the default/minimal/dinit Rust matrix, both Nix architectures, headless XWayland regressions, and the upstream-source guard.

Related to #264. The protocol defect is reproduced locally; resolution of the reporter's visible Intel flicker still needs confirmation.

body:
## EKODI AI-ROUTE-FAMILY-006 — dormant local consent broker and durable replay prevention (#8714)

User-authorized continuation under EKODI Orchestrator, parent #7796. **No live node enrollment, no credential/authority expansion, no production feature activation.**

### Implementation
- `ai-family-consent-issuer.mjs`: fail-closed, explicitly enabled but **default OFF**, OS user-presence approval and proof verification, signer via external protected user key (never embedded), exact claim/device/provider/request-hash binding, read-only OAuth-only subscription runtime, max 10-minute expiration bounded by job deadline, no raw prompts or private keys.
- `ai-family-durable-nonce.mjs`: SQLite/D1-compatible atomic consume-once contract; global UNIQUE nonce and UNIQUE job ID to forbid duplicate job execution with a new nonce; external durable DB required and no in-memory production fallback. Optional 24h-expiration pruning remains dormant; no implicit migration.
- `ai-family-consent-broker.mjs`: connects issuer + Ed25519 verifier + durable nonce consumer to existing user-mode runner's `getSignedConsent`/`verifySignedConsent` interface; fails closed when OS broker/public key/store absent.
- Tests: genuine ephemeral Ed25519 keypair, expiry/tampering/replay/race/restart/independent DB failures, optional real `node:sqlite` UNIQUE + ON CONFLICT and broker contract; documentation of operational approval gates.

### Important limitations
- No production secret/key, OAuth flow, OS attestation user UI, durable D1 migration or privileged Device Agent changes performed. This is an opt-in, inert contract; **not** an actual installed Windows user-session runner or verified operating consent UI.
- Automated GPT/Claude routing `AI_ROUTE_FAMILY_AUTO_DISPATCH` remains **false** by default. No paid APIs and no consumer-web automation.
- Real Windows user2/user3 CLI authentication and signed end-to-end execution, scoped queue token, Web/Cloudflare telemetry and consent need separate verified tests and explicit delegated authority. No self-merge or production deployment.
- Full GitHub CI, Constitution/AI Orchestration, protected PR-to-orch_recovery and authentic release/production evidence are required. If CI fails, repair in isolated branch.

### Reproducible checks
`node --test test/ai-family-consent-issuer-nonce.test.mjs test/ai-family-consent-broker.test.mjs test/ai-family-signed-consent.test.mjs` where applicable; `npm test` and repository governance checks must also pass.

author: tagspace
body:
Closes #748

**What changes, and why**: `MASON_UI_SOCKET=<path>` makes `mason serve` serve its web page on that Unix socket as well as on its loopback port. A process on the same machine, such as a supervisor or a local reverse proxy, can then reach the page without a published port or a `docker exec` per request. The code is in `src/cli/ui-socket.ts`. The decisions:

- **Who can connect**: the socket is made with mode 0600. The umask is set to 0177 around the bind, which is synchronous, so the socket has that mode from the moment it exists; it is then chmod-ed and checked with `lstat`. The folder must be a real folder (not a symlink), owned by Mason's uid, with no group or other write. Otherwise the start is refused, and the refusal gives the way out (`mkdir -m 700 …`, `chmod go-w …`).
- **What is at the path**: nothing there is fine. A socket owned by Mason's uid that refuses a connection (one a crashed run left) is unlinked and replaced, and the start says so. Everything else is refused and left untouched: a regular file, a folder, a symlink (even a dangling one), another uid's socket, a socket some process still answers on, or a probe that cannot tell (fail closed).
- **Removed on exit**: the socket is removed when the run stops (the `stopping` hook), when the run ends any other way (serve's `finally`), and on a SIGTERM or SIGINT that arrives before the run has installed its own stop (while it is still connecting). Before this change such a signal ended the process by its default action, and that runs no cleanup.
- **Trust**: the socket server passes every request to the run's own request handler (`run.emit("request")`). So a request on the socket goes through exactly the guard a request through `mason ui --bridge` meets: the Host header, the run's token or a tunnel's ticket and cookie, and the Origin. It shares the same open tunnels. Arriving on the socket grants nothing. A proxy opens a tunnel with the run's token (`POST /api/ui/tunnel`), as the bridge does. Until the run is attached, the socket answers 503 "starting" and names nothing.
- **Without the setting nothing changes**: no listener and no signal handler are added. `ServeSettings.ui.socket` is `null`.
- `mason start` refuses `MASON_UI_SOCKET` through `startSettingRefusal`, as it refuses `MASON_PG_DATABASE`, because it ignores no setting silently. Windows and paths longer than `sun_path` allows are refused on serve's one settings report. The setting is listed in `mason serve --help`, `deploy/mason-data/README.md` and `docs/WEB-UI.md`. The rules files' "loopback alone" lines now name the exception.

**The test that fails without it**: `tests/cli-ui-socket.test.ts`. `node scripts/fails-without.ts 30cabdd tests/cli-ui-socket.test.ts` → `PROVED: 4 test(s) that pass on the working tree fail with src at 30cabdd`. The four tests:
- the page and `/api/state` over the socket, with the guard enforced: no credential gives 403, a foreign or missing Host gives 421, Bearer works on the server's own Host, the tunnel's ticket trades once for a cookie that is not the run's token, the page and state are served with the cookie, a foreign Origin is refused, Bearer under a tunnel's Host is refused, and the tunnel's cookie stops working once the tunnel closes. Also 503 before the run is attached, mode 0600, and the socket removed on close;
- a stale socket (left by a listener killed with -9) is replaced; a live socket, a file, a folder, a symlink and a dangling symlink are refused and left as they were; a folder that is missing, a symlink, mode 0777 or 0770, or another uid's is refused, each with its whole text;
- the setting: unset or empty gives `socket: null`, a relative path is resolved, a too-long path and Windows are refused, the `--help` line is there, and `mason start` refuses the setting;
- `mason serve` as a process: the socket exists (0600, answering 503) while the database hangs, a SIGTERM removes it, and a regular file at the path is refused with exit 1 and left as it was.

`tests/serve.test.ts`'s settings `deepEqual` gains `socket: null`.

**Left out**: #747's read-only rules don't exist yet, so nothing was built for them. A SIGTERM on a fully started run (the database answering) is not exercised end to end here: that path is the run's stop calling the `stopping` hook, which closes the socket. A proxy still has to rewrite Host and Origin to a tunnel's loopback names, as the bridge's browser does; nothing new was added for that.

- [ ] CI is green on the last commit
- [x] generated text regenerated with `UPDATE_FIXTURE=1 npm run check`, not edited (if it changed): none changed
- [x] an error a person meets says the way out

## Goal
Resolve the six Upgrade Force defects/risks observed on XeniaCharis without changing that downstream repository.

## What changes
- Git object-aware remote verification: EOL conversions via built-in Git clean semantics; custom filters and mismatched attributes fail closed; independent PR/native/deployment evidence.
- Preflight Windows long paths and ignored contents; post-removal check of worktree registration, directory and branch; PARTIAL_CLOSEOUT; SHA-guarded local branch retirement.

- Bounded non-executing tool discovery for uv/auditors and explicit advisory/deployed-runtime coverage limits.
- One SHA pinned per invocation; later upstream drift is reported rather than causing repeated release loops.
- Reconciled VERSION/README/CHANGELOG/evolution, core standards, agent/skill/native routes and manifest.

**Dataset**: [PXD011001](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/pride/archive/projects/PXD011001)

author: jamalrizki
body:
Bug fix. Not part of an `idea` issue.

## What and why
**Bug:** `chord_chart` read only the start of the `key` argument. "Autumn Leaves in **B-flat**" came back in **B minor**: the letter was read and "-flat" was dropped without any error. It also read "Germany" as G and "C dorian" as C. `find_tunes` already checked the whole string, but it turned "B-flat" down as a key it couldn't read.

**Now:** both tools share one parser that has to match the whole string. "B-flat", "B flat", "B♭", "Bb", "Bbm", "B-flat minor" and "B natural" all work. "C-" still means C minor. Anything else gets the usual "not a key I understand" error, which doesn't echo the caller's text, so the model asks again instead of handing back a wrong key.

**Tool-use concept:** tool arguments are untrusted input. A parser that reads a prefix and ignores the rest fails *silently*. The model gets a valid-looking chart in the wrong key and can't tell. Rejecting what it can't fully read turns that into an error the model can act on.

## What changed
- `worker/src/tools.js`: `KEY_ARG_RE` accepts `-flat` / `-sharp` / `natural` and must match the whole string. `parseKeyArg` now also returns the key name (exported for tests). `chordChart` uses it for the caller's `key`. The library's own keys still go through `parseKey`.
- `worker/test/key-names.test.js` (new, 5 tests): all the B-flat spellings, other hyphenated keys, `key` + `instrument`, refused junk with no echo, `find_tunes` with "B-flat", and the parser itself.
- `docs.html`: one sentence under "Any key, transposed in code."

## Verified
- From worker/: `npm test` → **84/84 passing** (was 79).
- On main, a probe of `{tune: "Autumn Leaves", key: "B-flat"}` returned "B minor". On this branch it returns "Bb minor", first chord Ebm7.

## Size impact
No tool definition or system prompt changes: **0 characters**.

## Heads-up
A key with extra words, such as "C dorian" or "Eb for alto", is now an error and no longer quietly becomes C or Eb. The model gets "Use a note name like F, Bb, or F#." and retries. The mode word in "Bb minor" is accepted, and the tune keeps its own mode, as before.

## After merging
1. From worker/: `npm test`
2. From worker/: `npm run deploy`

Independent of open PR #30. They touch different functions.

---

## Why

A user on the easydomoticz forum moved from Tempo to EDF Zen Fixe. Since then, every counter update logs:

```
Error: Sonoff: get_corresponding_color - unknown op_tarifaire H PLEINE-CREUSE
```

The earlier fix for https://easydomoticz.com/forum/viewtopic.php?t=14468 only accepts `H PLEINE/CREUSE` (with a slash). With the dash, `_normalize_tarif` returns the value unchanged and `_known_op_tarifaire` rejects it.

The user tried a local patch that accepts both spellings. The Error stopped, but standard mode then logged:

```
Status: Z4D requests LTARF (0xff66) as not inline HEURE  PLEINE to HP../HP..
```

`_is_hchp_standard_tarif` only matches `HCHP 22h-6h`, so the LTARF label of a normalized `HC` tariff is never translated to `HP..`/`HC..`. Even when it is translated, `_normalize_hchp_color` does not know the double-space form, though `Modules/zlinky.py` `OP_TARIFAIRE_MAP` already lists it. The comparison always fails, and LTARF is read again on every counter update.

---

## Scope

- `DevicesModules/custom_zlinky.py`: `_normalize_tarif`, `_is_hchp_standard_tarif`, `_normalize_hchp_color`
- `Modules/linky.py`: `linky_tarif_color_ntarf` (NTARF → HC/HP matrix)
- Device: LiXee ZLinky_TIC, in standard and historic mode. Any radio.
- Target: `stable9`. No settings, no persistent data change.

---

## Details

- `_normalize_tarif`: `H PLEINE/CREUSE` and `H PLEINE-CREUSE` both normalize to `HC`.
- `_is_hchp_standard_tarif`: true for `HCHP 22h-6h` **and** for the normalized `HC` tariffs (`HEURES PLEINES`, `H PLEINE/CREUSE`, `H PLEINE-CREUSE`). In standard mode their LTARF label is now passed through `_normalize_hchp_color`. That function returns unknown labels unchanged, so tariffs that already sent `HP..`/`HC..` behave as before.
- `_normalize_hchp_color`: collapses repeated whitespace before matching (`HEURE  PLEINE` → `HP..`, `HEURE  CREUSE` → `HC..`) and returns a non-string value (e.g. `None`) untouched.
- `linky_tarif_color_ntarf`: `H PLEINE-CREUSE` uses the HC/HP NTARF matrix, like `H PLEINE/CREUSE`.

Tempo, EJP, BASE and `HC SEM ET HC WE` are unchanged.

---

## Validation

- `pytest .` → 3105 passed, 4 skipped (Python 3.12 venv)
- `flake8 . --builtins=Devices,Parameters,Connection --select=E9,F63,F7,F82` → 0
- `bandit` on the changed files: nothing in production code (only B101 `assert` in the new test, as in every test file)
- The new tests fail on `origin/stable9` (6 failures) and pass with this change.
- **Not verified on a meter.** No Zen Fixe Linky here. The labels come from the user's log, and the user's local patch confirmed that the OPTARIF part removes the Error.

---

## Unit Test Added

`tests/DevicesModules/test_custom_zlinky_hchp_labels.py` (14 cases):

- `H PLEINE/CREUSE`, `H PLEINE-CREUSE` and `HEURES PLEINES` normalize to `HC`, are known tariffs, and map counters `0100`/`0102` to `HC..`/`HP..`
- `_normalize_hchp_color` handles the singular, plural and double-space labels, plus `HP..`, `HC..` and `None`
- A Tempo `BBR(` tariff is not treated as HC/HP
- Standard mode, `H PLEINE-CREUSE` with LTARF `HEURE  PLEINE` on the `HP..` counter: no `ReadAttributeRequest_ff66` is sent

Plugin dependencies are stubbed with `patch.dict(sys.modules)`, so the stubs do not leak into other tests.

Refs #4636. The expander now reads a project's config files past values only the build machine knows, and past a `try` that rescues an application environment read, so the keys beside them, such as a generated Phoenix project's `dev_routes`, keep the values the config gives them. - A read of the machine or the run is an unknown value, and a native given an unknown value gives one. - An arm tested on an unknown value may be taken, the arms join, and a run over unknown values ends. - A `Mix.Project` path or config read from a config file is an unknown value. - A corpus's root is content, so its config files are read. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) ## Summary by CodeRabbit - **New Features** - Configuration analysis now accounts for uncertain values across branches, exceptions, and other control-flow paths while preserving values that remain consistent. - Environment and machine-dependent reads are treated as uncertain without necessarily obscuring neighboring configuration values. - Project paths and conditional imports are handled more accurately, including generated Phoenix configuration values such as `dev_routes`. - **Bug Fixes** - Corrected expansion behavior for certain pattern matches and application-environment reads. - Improved compatibility with `IO.warn` across Elixir versions and handling of uncertain bitstring values. - Improved evaluation of native calls, including argument validation and error handling.

Confidence Score: 3/5

Do not merge until possible clauses and reductions stop missing config writes from struct code.

Findings

1.  **Possible clauses drop known arguments** ▶ 2.  **Reductions skip later config writes** ▶

 Config reads now keep known keys beside machine-dependent values. - Config files keep known settings beside machine-dependent values. author: dudeplayz
body:
## Worum es geht

In den dunklen Themes **Nacht** und **Tiefsee** haben mehrzeilige Textfelder keine eigene Hintergrundfarbe. Der Browser malt sie deshalb im Standard-Grau (`rgb(59, 59, 59)`, wegen `color-scheme: dark`). Optionale Felder wie „Einleitung über den Positionen“ oder „Hinweis auf der Rechnung“ wirken dadurch wie deaktiviert. In den hellen Themes fällt das nicht auf.

## Prüfung

Bevor ich etwas geändert habe, habe ich alle Seiten aus `seiten.spec.ts` in beiden dunklen Themes durchsucht, mit einem temporären Playwright-Lauf (nicht committet). Gemeldet wurde jedes sichtbare `input`, `select`, `textarea` und `button`, dessen Hintergrund nicht `--surface` ist. Betroffen sind **nur Textfelder**, auf neun Seiten: Rechnung neu, Beleg, Dauerbeleg neu und bearbeiten, Anlage neu, Finanzamt, Einstellungen, E-Mail-Vorlagen. Alle anderen Funde sind gewollt: die Theme-Auswahl in der Navigation, `visually-hidden` Dateiauswahlen und das transparente Feld im Suchrahmen.

## Änderung

`textarea` bekommt `background-color: var(--surface)`, wie `.field input`, `.field select` und `.line-row` schon. Deaktivierte Textfelder behalten damit dieselbe Fläche wie deaktivierte Eingaben.

## Tests

Neu in `e2e/barrierefreiheit.spec.ts`: „Eingabefelder auf der Theme-Fläche im Theme nacht/tiefsee“ auf sechs Formularseiten. Vor dem Fix rot mit allen betroffenen Textfeldern, danach grün; die bestehenden Kontrastprüfungen für Nacht und Tiefsee (axe) bleiben grün. Lint grün.
