author: singh318683
body: ## Why the Play error can still appear on 1.0.1 Play’s own “You already own this item” dialog is `launchBillingFlow` returning `ITEM_ALREADY_OWNED`. That means the sheet was opened. The published 1.0.1 package is main `4c290c5` plus the version bump, so `PlayPaymentActivity` is in that build, but that activity still misses the purchase in three cases: - It only matches `Purchase.products.contains(sku)`. Play Billing 8 can leave `getProducts()` empty while the sku remains in `originalJson`. - When the listener receives `ITEM_ALREADY_OWNED`, it ignores the purchase list Play just delivered and queries again. An empty second query fails after the dialog. - `android-browser-helper` billing 1.2.0 implements `listPurchases` with `getProducts().get(0)`. An empty list throws, the callback never returns, and the page opens the sheet. Its `listPurchaseHistory` always returns an empty list. The website cannot invent a token that neither call returns, and the first failed purchase was never stored. ## Fix - Read the sku from `getProducts()`, `getSkus()`, and `originalJson` (`productId` / `productIds`). If exactly one unconsumed in-app purchase exists, use its token. The server still checks the product id, so a wrong token cannot become a free question. - On `ITEM_ALREADY_OWNED`, use the purchase Play passed to the listener before querying again. Query in-app and subscriptions before opening the sheet. - Answer Chrome’s `listPurchases` before the library handler, without calling `get(0)`. - The page accepts that single returned token when its item id is missing or different. - Price stays $0.99. Nothing is acknowledged or consumed in the app. The server still consumes only after an answer starts. This is versionCode **3** / versionName **1.0.2**. It is a new Android build. Installing 1.0.1 again will not include it. The website change alone cannot recover a token the phone never returns. ## Checks - `tests/test_api.py` and `tests/test_play.py`: 31 passed. - The page script parses with `node --check`. - The branch merges cleanly with `main`. - Android was not compiled: this environment has no Android SDK. Kotlin was checked by source tests only. ## What a phone still has to confirm Settings → Apps → Drishti must show **1.0.2** after this build is installed. `adb shell dumpsys package com.ikshana.drishti` should show `versionCode=3` and the PAY activity `com.ikshana.drishti.PlayPaymentActivity`. Without a device we cannot see whether the installed 1.0.1 query was empty or the library callback crashed.

author: rikki
body:
`AppModel.redetect()` clears the selection, re-detects and re-scans, so the name only covered the middle step and sat next to the private `detect()`. It is now `restartScan()`, pairing with the existing `rescan()` (which keeps the selection and only re-scans). The button label stays 「重新检测」 on purpose; it lives in the detection-warning card, where re-detecting is exactly the user's motive.

The function also assigned `screen = Screen.Choose`, a no-op write: `Screen.Choose` is a `data object` and `screen` uses the default structural-equality policy. The line was real when it was introduced in #666, shared by the home screen's 「自己选」 entry; #692 removed that entry, leaving the confirm screen's button as the only caller. It is dropped and the "called from the confirm screen only" invariant is written into the KDoc. `selection = null` stays: the confirm screen renders a full-page loader while it is null.

One deliberate difference, from review: during the `AnimatedContent` exit animation after tapping 「开始」 or 「返回」 (~300ms), a click on the now-leaving 「重新检测」 button used to pull the screen back to `Screen.Choose`. It now runs detect/scan with the result written into the new selection while the screen stays where it went. Steady-state interaction is identical; this needs a deliberate fast double tap during the transition.

Validation: 1737 device-free tests pass with 2 skipped; `ruff 0.17.3` clean. Kotlin is not compiled locally (no JDK or Android SDK here) — the `assemble` job in `.github/workflows/android.yml` covers that. Tapping 「重新检测」 once on a real device has not been done, hence `Refs` instead of `Closes`.

Refs #701

author: dsh-ctx
body:
This is by an automated agent, not a human.

Adds `skills/ecloud-space`, a global skill for 中国移动「移动云空间」(Ecpan, https://www.ecpan.cn). Personal and group cloud-disk work uses the web JSON API; chat send uses the client's embedded web IM page through a local CEF debug port, with no synthesized Windows mouse/keyboard input. Writes and messages are deny-by-default and exact-target confirmed.

## Security model

- `%USERPROFILE%\.dsh\ecloud\policy.json` is the allowlist. Safe defaults allow only `temp-waicai` for group read/write and only `文件传输助手` for chat. Public groups (`isPublic=1`) are refused while `allowPublicGroups=false`; a malformed policy fails closed.
- Every write/transfer requires `-Yes` **and** `-ConfirmTarget` exactly equal to the canonical path (`个人盘\...` or `<group>\...`). `download` is included. A mismatch is refused before the network call.
- `msg-send` requires `-ConfirmRecipient` exactly equal to `-To`, a non-empty message within the policy length, `-Yes`, and a 3-second cooldown. Non-file-assistant chats also need `-AllowAnyChat` plus the exact chat in `allowedChats` and `allowAnyChat=true`.
- `upload` rejects invalid/path-separator names, enforces the 5 MB single-shot limit, and verifies the new file is visible in the target folder. `download` verifies size and MD5 when the API provides them; a failed verification stops without blind retry.
- `view-url` returns a short-lived WPS token; the skill tells the agent not to log or share it.

## What it adds

- `login` / `status` — browser cookie capture or manual import; session validation.
- `whoami`, `ls`, `stat`, `mkdir` — personal disk listing/metadata/confirmed folders.
- `groups`, `group-ls`, `group-mkdir` — group spaces with the policy allowlist.
- `upload`, `download`, `view-url [-Edit]` — personal and group small-file transfer and WPS links.
- `msg-send`, `msg-chats`, `client-debug-status`, `client-info` — code-based chat and client status.
- `im-orgs`, `policy` — read-only IM org lookup and effective policy display/init.

## Stability and robustness

- Read-only API calls retry transient 5xx/timeout errors; writes and sends do not retry.
- Listings paginate on `pageCount` (up to 10 pages), so large folders are not silently truncated.
- The listing path no longer sends `fileType: "1"`; that filter hid files and caused a false upload-verification failure.
- Exact path/name matching, canonical target checks, upload visibility check, download size/MD5 checks, CDP warm-up, chat selection/header check, draft-clear check and no-retry send.

## Verification

Personal disk:
- `whoami`, `ls`, `stat`, `im-orgs`, `client-info`, `status` return expected data.
- `mkdir` created two empty test folders.
- Personal `upload` created `dsh-personal-upload3.txt` and verified visibility; `download` matched MD5; `view-url` returned a WPS URL.

Group `temp-waicai`:
- `groups`/`group-ls` work for the allowed group; a non-allowlisted group is refused.
- `group-mkdir` with a wrong `-ConfirmTarget` is refused; the exact target creates `dsh-security-check`.
- Group `upload`/`download` for `dsh-final-test.txt` verified MD5; group `view-url` works.
- A missing/incorrect target confirmation is refused before mutation.

Chat:
- `client-debug-status`: debug port available, `#/im` page true.
- `msg-chats` lists visible chats.
- `msg-send -DryRun` selects 文件传输助手, verifies the active item/header and inserts/clears the draft without sending.
- A non-allowlisted chat is refused; missing `-ConfirmRecipient` is refused; a recent cooldown file blocks a send.
- Two real test messages were sent to 文件传输助手 and appear in history with no Windows mouse/keyboard input.

## Limitations

- No delete/rename/move/search commands: deliberately omitted to keep the destructive surface small.
- Uploads > 5 MB need the browser chunked protocol and are not implemented.
- Chat is send-only; no message-history API. The debug port must be enabled for the client launch and is powerful/local-only; restart the client normally after use.
- The repository has no CI/reviews configured (0/0). A person should merge; auto-merge was not enabled.
- `session.json` and `policy.json` are outside the repository; never commit them.

## Test artifacts left for review

- `个人盘`: `dsh-ecloud-skill-test-20261107`, `dsh-ecloud-skill-test-script`; the latter contains the small upload test files.
- `temp-waicai` (groupId `516940`): `dsh-ecloud-skill-test` with `dsh-ecloud-skill-test.txt`, `dsh-ecloud-skill-upload-cli.txt`, `dsh-group-upload2.txt`, `dsh-final-test.txt`, `dsh-ecloud-skill-subfolder`, `dsh-security-check`.
- 文件传输助手: two test messages (`dsh-superagent 代码发送测试，请忽略`, `dsh-superagent 技能发送测试，请忽略`).

Note existing V2 player still persists qualified plays to AWS; this PR does not disable that existing write. No production deployment requested.

author: vaggab0nd
body:
Adds a Megaminx (12-faced dodecahedron) page to Cube Lab, plus a Megaminx event in the Timer.

## What's new

**`megaminx.html` (Megaminx Lab)** has two tabs:
- **Moves:**
  - a 3D Megaminx with buttons for U, R, F, L, BL, BR and their primes;
  - buttons for the WCA scramble moves (`R++`, `R--`, `D++`, `D--`, `U`, `U'`);
  - a guide to the face names, including the lower faces FR, FL, DR, DL, B and D;
  - a "Name that move!" quiz with Easy (U, R, F) and Hard (all six top faces) levels. The best streak is saved.
- **How to solve it:** a beginner method that builds on the 3x3. Each algorithm plays on its own Megaminx, and the last-face ones grey out the pieces that don't matter (cubing.js stickerings).
  1. Star around the first face (by feel).
  2. First-face corners with the **corner trick** `R' FR' R FR`.
  3. The middle rings by feel, with the **edge tricks** `U R U' R' U' F' U F` / `U' L' U L U F U' F'` and the corner trick.
  4. The last face, in four steps:
     - **Flip** `F R U R' U' F'`
     - **Sune** `R U R' U R U2' R'` or **Gap Sune** `R U2 R' U R U2 R'`
     - **Niklas** `R U2' L' U2 R' U2' L U2`
     - the corner trick twice per twisted corner.

**Also:**
- **Timer:** a **Megaminx** event, with official scrambles from cubing.js, or WCA-style `R++`/`D++` lines when offline. The scramble box now keeps line breaks.
- **Navigation:** Megaminx in the shared menu, a home tile, a Help section and glossary entry.
- **Trophies:** four achievements (Dodecahedron, Twelve Faces, Megaminx Sub-5, Megaminx Sub-2), taking the total from 38 to 42. "Puzzle Master" now reads "Solve 5 different timer puzzles", as there are six events now.
- **Docs:** `README.md` and `CUBE_LAB.md`.

## How it was checked

All checks used cubing.js 0.66's Megaminx model in Node.
- **Algorithm effects, read off piece by piece:**
  - The corner trick only swaps the front-right top corner with the one under it and touches no other top piece. Six in a row is the identity.
  - The edge tricks only touch the top face and the gap.
  - The four last-face algorithms only touch the top face. Flip flips two edges. Sune and Gap Sune each cycle three edges, keeping the front + left or the front + back-right ones. Niklas cycles three corners and keeps the two on the left.
- **A bug the checks caught:** the 3x3 corner-swap algorithm (`R U' L' U R' U' L U`) does nothing on a Megaminx, because R and L aren't next to each other there. That's why Niklas is the Megaminx version.
- **Holding rules:** the rules for each last-face step were worked out by trying every case. Edges needed the extra Gap Sune to get guaranteed rules.
- **Whole last face:** following the rules exactly on 3,000 random last faces solved all of them, about 12 algorithms on average and 21 at most.
- `R++` leaves the left face alone and `D++` the top face, as the page says.
- **Not checked:** the middle rings, which are done by feel like F2L. The page says so.

**Browser (Playwright):**
- The page loads with no errors, and the move buttons, quiz and all 8 method players work.
- Nothing scrolls sideways at desktop or phone width.
- Offline, the notice shows and the algorithms are still readable.
- The Timer's Megaminx event shows a 7-line scramble.
- Home, Help, Trophies and Skewb still load cleanly.

**Not tested:** `cdn.cubing.net` is blocked in the test sandbox, so I tested with a local bundle of the same library. The Timer used its offline scramble, not the official one. Worth a quick look live.

Task: T-1001
Closes #76

## What changed
Built to the plan and the founder decisions on #76 (Q1–Q5 accepted as written, 7 Nov).

**Database** (`supabase/migrations/20261108121337_briefs_formula_and_claims.sql`, additive):
- `app.set_formula_lines(p_product, p_lines)`: security definer, `search_path = ''`, `can_edit_product` first (42501), product row locked. It replaces the lines in one transaction, with `applied_by` set to the person, never the model (E03). Register rows are FK-validated, and a line names at most one (22023). Audited `formula.set`.
- `app.set_intended_claims(p_product, p_language, p_claims)`: the customer's own text per language, trimmed, never generated. The language must be one a market prints in. Audited `intended_claims.set`.
- `private.formula_digest(product)` (service_role only). `app.request_check` now puts the formula digest in its idempotency key and payload. **Before this, entering a formula left the key unchanged, so the next check returned the earlier job, whose additive rules were withheld.**
- No new tables. `formula_lines` and `intended_claims` already had `read_scoped` RLS and no client writes; pgTAP asserts both.

**Worker** (outside the task's lanes; covered by `scope-approved`, #76 Q1(a)):
- `store._additives`: a formula with any line matched to neither a feed material nor an additive gives `None`, so additive rules are withheld `data_missing` instead of being read as not applicable. Without this, entering a formula would have reopened #172.
- Q1 note: the decision comment on #76 restates Q1(a) as "the `request_check` formula-digest fix", while Q1 as written asked about this worker fix. I flagged it on #76 and on this PR before the label, and `scope-approved` was added afterwards.
- **Formula pinned to the check** (found by the rls-reviewer pass, fixed here): the handler passes the payload's `formula_digest` to the store. The store reads the lines and their digest in one statement, and withholds additive rules if the formula has changed since the request. Otherwise a job keyed to "no formula" that ran after a formula was entered held a *passed* additive rule, and `request_check` returned it once the formula was removed. The regression test fails without the fix.

**Web** (S-NV2-004 `/w/[workspace]/briefs/[product]`):
- The brief fields, the formula table ("n of m ingredients matched to the register", register match, %, note) and intended claims per language.
- Under the formula heading, the screen says that the formula changes check results, and that without it, or with an unmatched line, additive rules are withheld (Q4).

- Product class is read from the latest classification, else "Not determined" (Q6 had no answer, so I took its stated default).
- Two departures from the design:

The migration was re-dated to `20261108121337` so it sorts after main's `20261108073109_billing_context` (the migration guard requires it). body:
Voce backlog:5a40c73e54aa, controllo B4 di VALIDAZIONE-PRODOTTO.md. La prende la sessione Mac, in parallelo alle corsie.

## Problema
Prova in produzione del 07/11 (validazione:B4 NON PASSA): con la sessione scaduta, «Aggiungi nota» su una nota lunga porta la shell al login (`sessionLostTarget` → `leaveForSpaceLogin`). La pagina viene buttata via, la nota si perde e il rientro atterra su Oggi senza nessun avviso.

## Cura (solo client, `apps/admin/public`)
- **`admin-draft-keep.js`, nuovo:**
  - `captureDrafts` copia in `sessionStorage` il testo scritto nella vista aperta. Prende solo campi di testo con nome, mai password, hidden o file; al massimo 20 campi da 5000 caratteri, con scadenza a 2 ore. La chiave è la rotta.
  - `restoreDrafts` riempie solo i campi ancora vuoti e usa la copia una volta sola.
  - `pendingDraftRoute` dà la rotta della bozza, ma solo se è una rotta `#/` dell'app.
- **`app.js`:**
  - `leaveForSpaceLogin` copia la bozza prima di lasciare la pagina.
  - `route()` la ripropone dopo ogni render, con il toast «Ho ripreso il testo che non era stato salvato: controllalo e salva di nuovo.».
  - Se il login atterra sulla home (`#/` o nessuna hash), la shell torna una volta alla rotta della bozza.
- Ogni accesso allo storage è protetto: senza storage o con uno storage che lancia errori, la bozza semplicemente non si conserva e la shell non si rompe.

## Fuori da questa PR
Il secondo criterio della voce («dopo il sonno del web la pagina mostra il caricamento, mai un errore o una pagina JSON») riguarda l'host della pilota e Render. Va in una PR della pilota o in una voce figlia: lo decide il supervisore.

## Verifica
- `tests/admin-draft-keep.test.js` (3 test):
  - una nota lunga torna intera dopo il login, senza password né campi hidden;
  - non sovrascrive ciò che l'operatore ha già scritto e aspetta la sua rotta;
  - scade dopo 2 ore;
  - storage assente, rotto o con contenuto ostile non rompe niente;
  - viene seguita solo una rotta `#/`.
- `node --test tests/admin-*.test.js tests/bo-*.test.js`: 1280/1281. L'unico rosso è `admin-catalog-shots`, che fallisce uguale su main con il Chrome del Mac.

author: khajavi
body:
## What was wrong

During the Scaladoc rollouts, sessions fact-checked the reference pages against the library and found statements that contradict what the code does in 0.0.56. This PR fixes 20 of them so the pages agree with the reviewed Scaladoc on main. It changes docs only.

## What the pages say now

- **config** (`config-source.md`): `SysPropSource` is empty on Scala.js because it never reads the properties Scala.js emulates, not because JS has none.
- **sql**: `derivedOpaque` and `dbCodecFromAs` must be declared by name (the compiler picks `derived` otherwise, a known bug in 0.0.56), with an example that now runs a real read; `DbArray` maps to `TEXT[]`/`TEXT` and `DbNull` exists only on the write side; `insertReturning` writes the ID you pass and never gets one from the database; `Table#columns` is O(n) and comes from `columnsMeta`; the transactor factories always use `SqlLogger.noop`; `SqlLogger` reports only `Frag` and `Repo` operations; `connectZIO` and `transactZIO` open their own connections.
- **async**: `List.map` and `Array.map` call the closure for every element before the first `await` resolves (with a runnable example showing the call order); iterative `map`/`flatMap` chains over a waiting value do not overflow, recursion through `flatMap` does; `Completer#peek` returns the outcome once complete, and `Async.promise` always allocates the `Completer`.
- **jwt**: parsing keeps the last value of a repeated field and nesting is bounded by `maxDepth`; the JVM curve check names only the tested cases.
- **combinators**: `Choices` is gone (it never existed), `Concat` exists on both Scala versions, and several wrong examples and outputs are corrected.
- **maybe**: absence is the `Absent` object, not `null`; the Scala 2 `Option` conversion and `toSeq` output are corrected; parity differences are listed.
- **projection**: the in-memory store matches SQLite only for rows without `Option` fields and with valid column names; the differences are listed.
- **telemetry**: `AttributeKey` is not a case class and does not make typos compile errors; histogram points hold copies; `ExporterConfig#timeout` is never read; the batch processor retries in place; `collectedSpans` holds 1024 spans; and four statements about the global `log` and `trace`.
- **ringbuffer** and **mux**: only the two reserved `NaN` patterns are rewritten; `Cancelled` and `ProtocolError` are not produced for peer cancels or state transitions.

## How it was verified

- `docs/mdoc` on all 24 changed pages (sql pages together on a fresh sbt server): 0 errors, no warnings. The new async and sql example blocks print real output.
- `sbt "++2.13; check"` passes.
- A fresh-context review checked every changed statement against the source and the filed entry, checked writing style, and confirmed nothing was added about log escaping, `tracestate` or `ExporterConfig` header values, and that the jwt curve text names only the tested cases. Counts: 20 entries checked, 0 factual errors, 1 style nit (a comment on a `separate` example), fixed.

author: stuart6854
body:
Two new Engine groups, in pseudocode with C++ where layout matters.

**Serialisation**
- `reflection.md`: a visitor per type (one function for read and write), type descriptions as data (`TypeInfo`/`FieldInfo`, offsets, flags), where descriptions come from (macros, header codegen, schemas), what reflection drives, and prefab diffs.
- `formats.md`: text vs binary, text rules for version control, a little-endian binary writer with varints, a bounds-checked reader (count checks, fuzzing), headers with magic and checksum, chunks, atomic saves, and compression.
- `versioning.md`: which data needs versioning, version checks vs migration chains on a generic tree, tagged fields (protobuf rules), renames and moves, and old files as tests.
- `references.md`: kinds of reference, file-local ids, two-pass loading, remapping for prefabs and saves, and load-in-place with fix-ups or relative pointers (memory-mapped), plus requirements.

**Content pipeline**
- `import-cook.md`: import vs cook vs package, a per-asset-type table, deterministic tools as functions, units and axes, and import settings in metadata.
- `incremental.md`: content-hash build keys (with cooker versions and dependency keys), build deps vs runtime references, catching undeclared deps, a local and shared derived data cache, parallel builds, and the editor.
- `packaging.md`: why archives, the TOC format, per-block compression and hardware decompression, ordering from a file-access log, layered patches, DLC and mods, and security.
- `editor-workflow.md`: GUIDs in metadata files (moves, commits), file watching with debounce and start-up hash checks, validation, reference finding, and source control.

The nav, the engine index, and the home page are updated. The strict build passes locally.

**Merge [stuart6854/gamedev-reference#96](https://github.com/stuart6854/gamedev-reference/pull/96) (job system) first.** Both PRs edit neighbouring lines in `docs/engine/index.md`. Once it is in, I'll merge `main` into this branch and link the incremental-builds page to the job graph page.

author: ogabasseyy
body:
Wallet credit now remains applied when a customer chooses an eligible Credit Direct or Oxygen instalment checkout. For example, a ₦50,000 order with ₦20,000 wallet credit finances the remaining ₦30,000; fully credit-covered orders open no financier. Klump is retired from new web/mobile payment choices, initialization and bookmarked launchers, while historical callbacks and reconciliation remain available.

The replacement supersedes the previous automatic wallet-removal implementation. Server ledger projection, immutable Oxygen funding snapshots, durable Credit Direct reservations and saved-order recovery guards prevent duplicate funding and unsafe retries.

### Limitations and rollout

- Wallet-composed Credit Direct with positive platform-retained shipping is rejected before signing until direct-settlement fee collection is verified.
- Uncertain/reserved financing attempts require authoritative recovery; local expiry cannot authorize another lender session.
- Three append-only migrations are included and have not been applied. No provider transaction, deployment or merge was performed.

### Validation

- 497 targeted web tests and 39 targeted mobile tests passed before submission.
- Scoped web/mobile TypeScript checks and affected app lint passed with existing warnings.
- Three disposable PostgreSQL regression harnesses passed for credit projection, Oxygen recovery and Credit Direct reservations/concurrency.
- Commit hooks passed. Current main was merged without conflicts; exact-head CI has started. The capability-register binding gate currently fails because the payment sources changed without an accompanying register re-review (`docs/product/baci-capabilities.json`, reviewed timestamp and digests); downstream quality jobs were skipped. This remains an open prerequisite before merge.
- CodeRabbit review was attempted before committing but failed with `rate_limit`: included reviews exhausted; selected account has no assigned seat for usage-based reviews. No CodeRabbit verdict is available. Keep this PR draft pending review and CI.

Implementation and recovery details: `docs/payments/wallet-financier-balance-investigation.md`.

author: mksingh8
body:
## Requirement
- **IR-006** (Minor): "Inconsistent check-selection defaults"
- **FR-003**: "The framework shall allow expected validation rules and checks to be defined in configuration." (acceptance: unsupported or empty definitions are rejected)
- **FR-004**: "EDMVF shall support schema and structural validation." (its acceptance wording "selecting neither check preserves prior behavior" now yields overall `incomplete` instead of `not_implemented`; see Change)
- **FR-027** (partial evidence only, thresholds not addressed): "The overall execution result shall communicate whether the configured validation completed successfully based on defined rules and thresholds."
- Partially addresses **IR-017** (see Limitations).

## Change
Problems fixed:
- An unimplemented check overwrote the overall status, so a real failure was reported as `not_implemented`.
- `ready` read as "about to run" rather than "validated"; executed and unimplemented entries had different shapes.
- Duplicate entries in `validation.checks` were accepted.
- The lower-level validators handled a missing or empty selection inconsistently: `validate_csv_schema` without `schema_validation` returned a pass without reading any file; `validate_csv_dataset` with no checks read the file but ran no check; `validate_csv_scenario` with `[]` silently fell back to the configured checks and never validated the scenario.

What changed:
- **Overall status** is `passed` / `failed` / `incomplete` plus a top-level `complete` flag. Any failed check gives `failed`; otherwise any check that did not run (or no executed check) gives `incomplete`; otherwise `passed`. A failing check next to an unimplemented one is `failed` with `complete: false`. `ready` is no longer produced. `_overall` raises `ValueError` for a status it does not know, so a future status can never count as a pass by accident.
- **Per-check entries** carry `status` (`passed` / `failed` / `not_implemented`). Executed entries keep `dataset`, `passed`, `issues`, `source_path`, `target_path`. Unimplemented entries are exactly `status` and `message` (the redundant `disposition` and the requirement reference in the message are gone).
- **Duplicates:** a duplicate in `validation.checks` is rejected as a configuration error, listed in first-seen order, after the unsupported-name check. Duplicate detection applies to lists and tuples, because a set or frozenset has already removed duplicates.
- **Python check selections:** `validate_csv_dataset`, `validate_csv_schema` and `validate_csv_scenario` accept a **list, tuple, set or frozenset**, with the same rules for all four: not empty, strings only, supported names only, no duplicates, otherwise `ValueError` before any file is read. Any other type (for example a bare string, bytes, a dict, a generator or a range) is outside the supported types and is rejected. An explicit empty selection never falls back to a default. YAML and `Scenario.validation.checks` stay lists.
- **Deterministic handling:** every element is type-checked before anything is sorted or printed, so a set is rejected exactly like a list; set contents are sorted in messages, so output does not depend on hash randomization. Execution order is fixed (structural, then schema) whatever the selection order.
- **Changed `None` defaults** (this is observable): `validate_csv_dataset(path, name)` now runs header integrity and row widths (it used to run no check); `validate_csv_schema(source, target)` now reads both files and compares columns (it used to return a pass without reading); `validate_csv_scenario(scenario)` runs the configured implemented checks as before, but now validates the scenario first. Selecting `validate_csv_schema` without `schema_validation` is now an error.
- **Docs:** a "Result contract" and a "Selecting checks" section in `docs/validation-model.md`, and `docs/adr/0001-run-result-status-contract.md`. The tuple-support decision is recorded as Accepted; the record as a whole stays Proposed, with the rationale still to be written.

## Acceptance criteria → tests
| Criterion | Tests |
|---|---|
| Overall precedence and `complete`, including failed + unimplemented | `test_overall_status_precedence_and_completeness`, `test_failing_check_plus_unimplemented_check_is_failed_and_incomplete_from_yaml`, `test_overall_aggregation_table`; all 31 non-empty subsets of the 5 checks, forward and reversed, against 6 data pairs: `test_every_subset_and_order_against_every_pair` |
| Unknown statuses never count as a pass | `test_overall_never_treats_an_unknown_status_as_a_pass` |
| Entry shapes; no `ready`; deterministic, JSON-serializable payload | `test_executed_entries_have_status_and_keep_their_existing_fields`, `test_unimplemented_entry_shape_and_message`, `test_legacy_ready_value_never_appears`, `test_payload_is_deterministic_and_json_serializable` |
| Duplicate checks rejected (YAML and direct), unsupported reported first | `test_duplicate_checks_are_rejected_for_direct_scenarios`, `test_duplicate_checks_are_rejected_from_yaml_identically`, `test_unsupported_checks_are_reported_before_duplicates` |
| Lower-level selections rejected before any read; `[]` never falls back | the `rejects_bad_*selection_without_reading` tests, `test_empty_selection_never_falls_back_to_the_scenarios_checks` |
| list / tuple / set / frozenset accepted with identical results and rules | `test_fr003_check_selection_types.py` (133 tests: valid and invalid selections per type through all three public functions) |
| Strings, bytes, dicts, generators, iterators, ranges rejected | `test_unsupported_selection_types_are_rejected_with_the_accepted_types_named` |
| Sets rejected like lists; deterministic regardless of hash seed | `test_non_string_elements_are_rejected_identically_for_every_type`, `test_set_selection_messages_do_not_depend_on_the_hash_seed` (subprocess, four seeds) |
| Documented defaults for `checks=None`; scenario validated first | `test_dataset_default_runs_header_and_width_checks`, `test_schema_default_runs_the_column_comparison`, `test_validate_csv_scenario_rejects_an_invalid_scenario_like_validate_scenario` |
| Data and access problems never raise; framework errors propagate | `test_missing_target_plus_unimplemented_is_failed_not_raised`, `test_framework_exceptions_propagate_and_are_not_reported_as_data_issues` |

## Test evidence
`timeout 600 .venv/Scripts/python -m pytest -q`, Python 3.11.5, final state of this PR: **1350 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped** (552 on `main` before; +798 new). CI runs Python 3.10.

Existing tests changed only as planned: four `result["status"] == "ready"` became `"passed"`, four overall `"not_implemented"` became `"incomplete"`, and the old test that expected `validate_csv_schema` without `schema_validation` to pass silently now expects a `ValueError` and still checks that no file is read.

Measured against the previous `main` code (first review, before the tuple work and the last review fixes): 30 of 36, 105 of 182, 23 of 23 and 349 of 357 tests failed in the four main new test files. The 133-test tuple/type file and the later additions were not measured against the old code.

## Review
Two independent reviews (read-only reviewer agent, separate from the authoring), both **Approved with minor observations**, no Critical or Major findings.
- **Differential run** of old vs new code over 8,640 `run_scenario` cases and thousands of lower-level calls: only intended differences. 432 duplicate selections are newly rejected; 5,096 cases previously reported `not_implemented` now correctly report `failed`; 85 `ready` became `passed`; 2,536 `not_implemented` became `incomplete`. The `None` default changes affected 4 of 12 file kinds for `validate_csv_dataset` and 118 of 144 source/target pairs for `validate_csv_schema`.
- **Fixed in this PR:** unknown statuses could count as a pass (`_overall`); duplicates were not listed in first-seen order; the "list" wording in error messages did not match the accepted types; set elements were sor

body:
Refs #1277 (task #778). Spec: the issue body, AC1 to AC6.

## What changed
- **Record v2** (`src/hub/research.ts`, new `src/hub/research-record.ts`): every task in a terminal board state gets a record, `outcome: approved|cancelled`, `closedAt`, and the review, delivery, merge, specs, memory, person, stalls, handoffs, cohort, declines and escalations blocks. The board and journal are read through a read-only handle that never decodes titles, details, notes or envelope bodies. A value that cannot be derived is `null`.
- **Cancel cause** is read only from an explicit closed `cause` field on the cancellation entry. The board keeps none today, so cancelled records read `unknown`. It is never inferred from a decline, an escalation or the note.
- **v1 compat**: a v1 row loads as `approved`, is never rewritten, and a v2 row of the same task replaces it. Statistics filter on `outcome`.
- **Live writer** (`daemon.ts`): reads the evidence, also triggers on cancellation, and on the guarded merge's `merge result` so a later pass can fill the merge block once (`fillsMerge`).
- **Quality report** (`src/hub/research-quality.ts`, #44 AC0): per-field `n`/`unknown`, quota coverage per family (gaps over 1 h, p95 staleness, clock source), budget pauses, outcomes per family and class, event types present/absent, token attribution share.
- **Dataset export** (`src/hub/research-dataset.ts`, `ahub research export --dataset <dir> [--since] [--all]`): per-project `tasks.jsonl`, `manifest.json`, `quality.json`. Peers are family names only (`unknown` when none is known), profile/role fields are dropped, the target must be inside the home and outside every registered project (real paths, symlinks refused), files are written whole and the manifest last.
- Docs: research.md, operations.md, events.md, dogfood.md row, help. Six inventory keys classified in sorted position.

## Checks
- `bun x tsc --noEmit`, `bun scripts/inventory-hardcoded-values.ts --check`, `bun scripts/build.mjs --check`: pass.
- New tests, 36 in 5 files (record v2 over a real hub.db with hand-computed blocks, quality with known gaps, dataset, privacy canary, CLI over two registered projects) plus the 12 existing research tests, help, inventory and check-docs: 89 pass, 0 fail on this head.
- Mutation check: breaking the family allowlist and the dropped fields makes the privacy test and the `datasetTask` test fail; restored.
- `scripts/seeded-check.ts`: 421 seeds detected, one ERROR, `kimi-review-write-tool-excluded` ("unmodified named test is not green"). The same seed errors on unmodified main on this machine, so it is not from this change.
- `test/daemon.test.ts`: 4 failures here, all among the 21 that fail on unmodified main on this machine.

## Not verified
- `scripts/check.sh --changed` stops at the tarball step locally (npm 12.2.2 prints a different `pack --json` shape than the pinned npm), so the tarball and full-suite legs rely on CI. Not run on dgx02.
- No live hub ran with `research.enabled`; the daemon trigger and evidence read are covered by the existing daemon research tests, not by a real merge.
- `rendered`, `delivered`, `cited` (#1279) and the person block (#1278) are null by design.

body:
实施 #2157 阶段 A（change `issue-2157-p1` 已随本 PR 归档，strict 验证通过）。

## 交付

1. **结构化参数包 `rust/control-engine/model-data/destroyer-055/v1/`**：manifest / geometry / maneuvering / actuators / provenance 五文件，构建期 `include_str!` 嵌入（零运行时 IO）。全参数 P/B/D/T 分级标注——055 首包全 T 级（教学标称），`model-fidelity: research-nominal` 诚实标注；A2.1 审查修正（k_z=0.25L、area_r=c·Lpp·T）入包固化。
2. **加载器与 fail-closed 门禁 `sixdof/model_pack.rs`**：
   - 质量与静水排水体积闭合（`|m−ρV|/m < 1e-3`）
   - 惯量分轴回转半径界（x: [0.25B, 0.60B]、y/z: [0.15Lpp, 0.40Lpp]）——**检出 `.25L 半径` 错写为 `.25mL²` 惯量**（A2.1 实际踩过的错）
   - `mass_basis` 枚举只有 displacement_volume / stated_loading——GT/DWT 无字段可冒充排水质量
   - Lpp ≤ LOA 分立字段校验
3. **规范化内容哈希**：key 排序紧凑 JSON + 数值统一 f64（同值不同字面量同哈希）→ FNV 链式；`sixdof_runtime.parameterBundle_hash` 切换为 `模型版本@包哈希`——改包即换 run 身份（合同联动）。
4. **测试 8 用例**：全门禁通过、哈希确定性、惯量错写检出、质量失配/Lpp 越界/GT 枚举逐一拒绝、数值变化换哈希 + 键序无关、包与 plant 单一真源一致（精确惯量 k_x=0.5B/k_z=0.25L）。

## 验证

- cargo **15 套件全绿**（新增 sixdof_model_pack 8 用例）；wasm 构建；typecheck 零错误

## 阶段 B 声明（诚实，不宣称）

KVLCC2/S175/DTMB5415/Wageningen B4-70/NEMOH 公开基准双人转录、Capytaine/NEMOH 逐船 BEM 生成、黏性操纵校准、独立基准时域复现（RMSE<1%/回转 ≤10%/Z 形 ≤5°）为后续批次；本轮不虚构实船参数、不把 T 级标成 D/P。

author: cruma-io[bot]
body:
The `directory-*` evals now run against the same stand-ins and the same `PATH` on a Mac and on clean Linux, but I couldn't run a scored case. `claude` has no login in this sandbox, so a before/after on your Mac and on a Linux box is still yours to do.

**Root cause:** `claude plugin eval` hands the agent the `PATH` of the shell that started it. `case.yaml` can only set `EVAL_*` variables, and a `PATH` in the workspace `.claude/settings.json` is not applied. That is why the agent saw Homebrew, Darwin `uname` and your real `cruma`. The real `cruma proxy` then failed on DNS because the eval sandbox has no network. I got this from the binary and from `--keep-temp` runs, not from the docs.

**Changes (eval files, scripts and README only; no plugin change):**
- **Stand-ins:** `evals/fake-cruma/bin/` holds static `cruma`, `npm`, `node`, `claude`, `uname` (Linux x86_64) and `printenv`/`env`. `cruma` output comes from the existing generated `cli/` files (ADR-2), so nothing is hand-typed.
- **Wrapper:** `scripts/eval-directory.sh` copies them to `.eval-work/shims/bin`, checks them without a model call, and starts the suite with `PATH=<shims>:/usr/bin:/bin`. `--check-only` stops after the check and other options are passed through.
- **Scaffold:** `evals/fake-cruma/directory-shims.sh` exits 3 if any of those tools doesn't resolve into the stand-in directory, so an unisolated run is an error rather than a score. It no longer writes `.claude/settings.json`.
- **Prompts:** six `prompt.md` files no longer say the stand-ins are in `~/.local/bin`.
- **README:** the Evals section documents the wrapper, why it exists and how to verify with `--keep-temp`.

**Checks I ran:**
- `bash scripts/eval-directory.sh --check-only` exited 0. It checks `uname`, the install flow, `cruma --version`, hiding `CLAUDECODE` in sandbox mode only, `cruma proxy http 3000 --json` matching `cli/ready.json` byte for byte, and the scaffold refusing a host `PATH`.
- `node scripts/check-plugin.mjs` passed.
- A bare staged `claude plugin eval` load of `directory-*` loaded the plugin. Its one case result was the expected "Not logged in" error, which was not scored.
- An earlier `--keep-temp` run got past the scaffold with the shims dir in the sandbox `allowRead`.

**Not verified:** run `scripts/eval-directory.sh --keep-temp` on the Mac and on Linux, compare pass/fail per case, and confirm `directory-agent-missing` and `directory-cli-same-session` pass with the plugin. In `out/trace.jsonl` there should be no `/opt/homebrew`, no real `cruma` version and no `Darwin`. If the harness or sandbox invokes `claude`, `node`, `env` or `uname` by name, or macOS login-shell `path_helper` reorders `PATH`, only a Mac run will show it.

The change is committed as `d4831bf` on `aiboard/ta«redacted»` and not pushed.

---

## Changes

- d4831bf Isolate directory-* evals from the host: stand-ins first on PATH via scripts/eval-directory.sh, fail-closed scaffold

16 files changed, 209 insertions(+), 123 deletions(-)

author: lollipop-onl
body:
## Why

Stacked on #146 — merge that first.

oxlint, oxfmt, vitest, tsdown and lefthook were five dependencies Dependabot moved separately, with five config files and eight `package.json` scripts around them, and vitest sat a major behind only because of Node 20. Vite+ bundles all of them at versions it tests together. One `vite-plus` devDependency and one `vite.config.ts` replace them, and the gates drop from five commands to three, none taking a flag:

```sh
pnpm exec vp check && pnpm exec vp test && pnpm exec vp pack
```

The maintainer also decided (2026-11-07) that `examples/*` leave the repository's verification entirely: examples are illustrations, an LLM reviews them when they change, and one falling behind the adapter is not itself a problem. That is the last commit of this PR.

(`pnpm exec` only until the next PR makes `vp` the entry point.) #143 (oxfmt 0.76) is obsolete with this PR; I have not closed it.

## What changes

- `vite.config.ts` replaces `.oxlintrc.json`, `.oxfmtrc.json`, `vitest.config.ts`, `tsdown.config.ts` and `lefthook.yml`. Each existing Why-not comment moved next to its setting (`fixedExtension`, attw `profile`/`level`, `setupFiles`, the test-file lint overrides).
- `package.json` keeps one script, `prepare` (`vp config`). `check` / `test` / `pack` are built-ins, so no wrapper script exists. `no-console` is now an `error`, which is what `--max-warnings 0` was for.
- `scripts/check-published-types.mjs` became `scripts/check-published-types.ts`, an exported function the `pack` block runs from tsdown's `build:done` hook. `vp pack` alone produces and verifies `dist/`; I confirmed a failing check fails `vp pack` with exit 1.
- `vp check` replaces `tsc --noEmit`. Type-aware linting reported two things in shipped code, and both are silenced at the spot with a Why-not rather than changed: `String(input)` in `src/client/backlog.ts` (backlog-js always passes a string URL, so a `Request` branch would be dead, untested code) and `unknown | Promise<unknown>` on `BacklogWebhookVerifier` (equivalent to `unknown`, but it tells a consumer's editor that the verifier may be async).
- Tests import from `vite-plus/test`; the vitest-4 `Assertion` shim in `adapter.test.ts` is gone. Vitest 5 removed `describe.sequential`, so `live.test.ts` uses `{ concurrent: false }`.
- Pre-commit: `.vite-hooks/pre-commit` runs `vp staged` → `vp check --fix` on staged files. **It now blocks the commit on a failure**; the old oxlint step ended in `|| true`. Verified by staging a file with a type error and a `console.log`: the commit was refused.
- `lefthook` is out of `allowBuilds` (now `{}`) and `lefthook-local.yml` out of `.gitignore`.
- CI: `lint` + `typecheck` → one `check` job (`pnpm exec vp check`); the consumer job and release.yml's pack job build with `pnpm exec vp pack`.
- **Examples leave the verification** (last commit): root lint, type check and format ignore `examples/**`; CI's consumer job no longer type checks every example, so the reusable workflow's `skip-examples` input and its release.yml caller are gone; each example loses its `typecheck` script and the README line that ran it. Nothing else in `examples/` changes (`typescript` and `tsconfig.json` stay: Vercel compiles through them, #145), and `git diff origin/main -- examples/` is exactly those seven deleted lines. CLAUDE.md states the rule once, in its `examples/` section.
- Docs: CLAUDE.md (Quality gates, scope table), DEVELOPMENT.md (commands, hook, CI table), the PR template.
- Commit 2 is the mechanical reformat of the whole repository (the Markdown docs and rules, `smoke.mjs`); skip it in review. `sample-messages.md` is excluded from formatting because the generated file is compared byte for byte.

## Verification

Locally, on this branch: `vp check && vp test && vp pack` pass (503 passed / 10 skipped — the 8 live-suite skips as before plus the 2 new runtime-identity tests, which skip outside the CI matrix), `git status` clean.

### No published output changes

This PR changes no shipped byte. `dist/index.js` and `dist/index.d.ts` built by `vp pack` on this branch are byte-identical to the ones `pnpm build` produces on main (31c34e9), even though tsdown moves from 0.23.5 to the 0.23.4 that Vite+ bundles:

```
d5f0871623a386abed5f3919bd3afd04eab2731f9012b8293a9e5e8a0df1bfec  dist/index.js
957a0125fcc8b529db0f91da83f9a18c4cdc3c012b9158097d52f8e1d35b53e4  dist/index.d.ts
```

### `vp check` matches `tsc --noEmit`

Scratch files with one deliberate error of each class the tsconfig flags, in `src/` and in a `*.test.ts`. Both `tsc --noEmit` and `vp check` failed on every one, with the same TS codes:

| Error | `tsc --noEmit` | `vp check` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `const x: string = 42` (src and test) | TS2322 | TS2322 |
| `{ a?: string } = { a: undefined }` (`exactOptionalPropertyTypes`; src and test) | TS2375 | TS2375 |
| `const s: string = list[0]` (`noUncheckedIndexedAccess`; src and test) | TS2322 | TS2322 |
| unused parameter / local (`noUnusedParameters`, `noUnusedLocals`) | TS6133 ×2 | TS6133 ×2 (plus `no-unused-vars` for the local) |
| `import { Logger } from 'chat'` of a type (`verbatimModuleSyntax`) | TS1484 | TS1484 |

So no `tsc --noEmit` step is kept.

### One `vitest`

No direct `vitest` dependency. After `rm -rf node_modules && pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`: `pnpm why vitest` ends `Found 1 version of vitest` (5.1.0), `node_modules/.pnpm` holds one `vitest@…` directory and `pnpm-lock.yaml` one `vitest@5.1.0` entry. `@chat-adapter/tests`' `vitest: ^5.0.0` peer is satisfied by it, and the three contract suites pass against the same module `vp test` runs.

### Node identity in the test matrix

`vp` has Node-management logic and a native binding, so the Node that started it proves nothing about the Node that ran the tests. Evidence from this PR's CI run (`Test` job logs): the matrix steps start `vp` with a bare `node node_modules/vite-plus/bin/vp test`, and `src/test/runtime.test.ts` (both of its tests ran, not skipped, in all three jobs) asserts inside the test process that `process.versions.node` is the job's major and that `process.execPath` is outside `node_modules`:

| Job | Node that started `vp` (existing identity step) | Runtime test inside the test process |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Node 22 | 22.23.4, `/opt/hostedtoolcache/node/22.23.4/x64/bin/node` | passed |
| Node 24 | 24.22.2, `/opt/hostedtoolcache/node/24.22.2/x64/bin/node` | passed |
| Node 26 | 26.13.0, `/opt/hostedtoolcache/node/26.13.0/x64/bin/node` | passed |

`devEngines.runtime` pins `^26.0.0`, so the 22 and 24 rows show `vp test` does not substitute it. The check is durable: it is a test, and the matrix sets `EXPECTED_NODE_MAJOR`. I also ran it locally with Node 22.23.3 and 24.21.0 as the starting `node`; the test process was that same Node.

## Deviations

- **Lint and type check skip `scripts/consumer-smoke`** (formatting still covers it): it is a standalone project whose dependencies exist only in the consumer job, so type-aware linting reports every adapter import as unresolved. Keeping its old non-type-aware lint was tried and is not possible: a per-path override cannot switch the type check off because TypeScript diagnostics are not lint rules (`'typescript/TS2307': 'off'` fails with `Rule 'TS2307' not found`), and `lint.options` offers only the global `typeAware` and `typeCheck`.
- `scripts/check-published-types` is TypeScript now (so `vite.config.ts` can import it type-safely), not a plain `.mjs`.
- Dependabot: the vitest `ignore` block is deleted rather than rewritten — `vitest` is no longer a direct dependency, so there is nothing for Dependabot to move apart from `vite-plus`. The Why-not is on `test.setupFiles` in `vite.config.ts`.
- `vite-plus` is `^1.5.0`, like every other dependency here; Vite+ itself resolved 1.5.0 under `minimumReleaseAge`.

## Merge order with #144

The whole-repository reformat realigns the decision table in `docs/specs/adapter.md` (`| D15    |` and every other row), so open

body:
<!-- implement: RP-1239 -->
Closes RP-1239

A Project Admin can now rename and archive a Project's Trades and Locations from Project Settings › Trades & Locations, as RP-1156 already allows for Scopes. This follows up row 11 of RP-1156's gap table. The owner's six decisions on the ticket are built as written.

## What changes

- **db** (migration day 20271209, `dimension_value_status`):
  - `dimension_value.status {active, deactivated}`.
  - A new `app.update_dimension_value`. It renames (the name only; the code never changes), deactivates or reactivates a Trade or Location.
    - Only the Project's Project Admins can use it. Everyone else gets `not_found`, the same as for a made-up id or a value of the other dimension.
    - GEN is refused with `general_trade` (decision 1).
    - A Location is deactivated together with every Location below it. A Location below a deactivated one answers `parent_deactivated` (decision 2).
  - Redefined from their newest bodies:
    - `app.check_work_item_built_ins`: a new item refuses a deactivated value, but an item keeps its own.
    - `app.set_participant_visibility` and `app.set_member_visibility`: a grant may list a deactivated value only while it already covers it.
    - `app.project_visibility_gap`: counts a deactivated value only while a Work Item uses it (decision 3).
    - `app.participant_covered_values`: now returns each value's status. It is dropped and re-created with the same grants.
    - `app.documental_record_facts`: page 1's Trade list leaves out deactivated Trades, except the item's own (decision 4).
  - Search already refreshes on a name update (the `work_item_search_name` trigger), so a rename shows there too (decision 5).
- **api:**
  - New `PATCH /v1/trades/:valueId` and `PATCH /v1/locations/:valueId`, each taking `{ name?, active? }`.
  - Every Trade and Location now carries `active`.
  - The register import matches no archived value, so the preview refuses that row instead of the confirm failing.
- **web:**
  - The Trades & Locations page has Rename / Archive / Restore on Trades and Locations, with no Archive on GEN.
  - "Show archived (n)" appears on both tabs. The tab counts leave out archived rows.
  - The Archive dialog names the places a Location takes with it.
  - The New item and snag pickers, the register import's Trade, and both grant editors no longer offer archived values. They keep an item's own value, and a value the grant already covers.
- **docs:** GLOSSARY (Trade, Location) and `docs/data-model.md` say "deactivated" (decision 6). New `docs/visibility/scenarios/RP-1239.md` adds scenarios RP-1239-1 to RP-1239-4.

## Visibility

Scenarios RP-1239-1 to RP-1239-4 are tested at both seams:
- `apps/api/test/rp-1239-visibility.test.ts`
- `packages/db/test/rp-1239-visibility-rls.test.ts`

The tests use `expectHiddenFrom` with the Project Admin as the positive control. They cover:
- Nobody but the Project Admin renames or archives, including another Company's Admin on their own Project.
- An item on an archived Location stays with those who saw it and hidden from everyone else.
- The covered values read stays the Participant's own Company's and the Project Admin's.
- The gap stays the Admin's only.

Decision 4 is tested in `packages/db/test/documental-record-facts-rls.test.ts`.

## Calls for the owner

- **"Restore", not "Unarchive".** The screen says "Restore", as RP-1156 shipped for Scopes and as the reference's dialog says ("You can restore it later"). Decision 6's text says "Unarchive". Say if you want that wording on both instead.
- **Settings pickers.** Approved Suppliers, Checklist Templates and Numbering still list archived Trades. They are not "a new Work Item or a new grant". Follow-up if wanted.
- **Discarded Drafts.** The gap counts a value as used while any Work Item row has it, discarded Drafts included.

Built with `pnpm screens`, signed in as Saeed (TMC's Project Admin) on the demo seed. The after shots have Mechanical Works and Podium (with its three Floors) archived.

author: vjeux
body:
**Symptom.** MP4 audio with PCM samples over 16 bits (24- and 32-bit integer, 32- and 64-bit float) gets a version 1 audio sample entry carrying QuickTime's extended sound description fields: 16 bytes of QuickTime fields between the sample entry and its `pcmC` box, inside a version 0 `stsd`. ISO/IEC 14496-12's AudioSampleEntryV1 has no such fields, and it must sit in a version 1 `stsd`. According to upstream's `bug-fix-mania` REPORT, AVFoundation then shows the file with 0 tracks. **That symptom comes from bug-fix-mania's REPORT and wasn't reproduced here (no Apple machine).**

**Repro.** `test/node/isobmff-muxer.test.ts` › "24-bit PCM sample entry, MP4" (bug-fix-mania's own regression test, verbatim, with its `findBox` helper): a 24-bit stereo PCM track at 48 kHz. Expected an `ipcm` entry of version 0 with its `pcmC` box found at the version 0 layout, read back as `pcm-s24` at 48000 Hz. On main the entry is version 1.

**Cause.** `soundSampleDescription` bumped `version` to 1 for PCM over 16 bits in every format, and the version 1 layout is QuickTime's.

**Fix.** Carried verbatim from upstream's `bug-fix-mania` (REPORT, "MP4 / MOV muxer and boxes": "PCM > 16 bit in MP4 used the QuickTime v1 sound description (AVFoundation: 0 tracks). Fix: drop the bump"), under the audit's exception for Mediabunny output that AVFoundation can't play. It drops out if `bug-fix-mania` lands first. MOV is unaffected: it uses version 1 for every codec anyway.

**Verified here.** 42 outputs compared between main and this branch: MP4 and MOV × PCM s16/s24/s32/f32/f64/f64be/s24be (plus u8 and µ-law in MOV) at 48 and 96 kHz, AAC at 48 and 96 kHz, and remuxes of `ac3.mp4`, `eac3.mp4` and `video.mp4`.
- Only the 12 MP4 outputs with PCM over 16 bits change; the other 30 are byte-identical.
- For the changed ones, ffprobe reports the same codec, tag, rate, channels and bit depth as before, FFmpeg decodes them without errors, and Mediabunny reads back the same codec, rate and channels.
- Chrome's progressive `<audio>` plays the 24-bit, 32-bit and float32 MP4 files to the end, before and after.

Merge note: this conflicts with #4 (FLAC bit depth in the sample entry) on adjacent lines. This PR deletes the `if (sampleSizeInBits > 16) { version = 1; }` lines, and #4 adds an `else if (... === 'flac')` branch right after them; the resolution keeps #4's branch without those lines.

Found by the L77 review; fix and test from upstream's `bug-fix-mania`.

_Written by an AI agent (Claude) auditing Mediabunny on behalf of @vjeux._

author: cogwheel0
body: ## Summary Four Hermes chat features: - **Clarify forms everywhere.** When Hermes asks several questions in one clarify call, they show together in one card above the composer (each question's choices, single or multi-select with the recommended one marked, a field for your own words, Skip) and one send answers the whole request. Until now a multi-question clarify came one question at a time ("1/2 · …"), and API server runs ignored clarify questions until they timed out. - **Diff cards.** A reply that edited files ends with an "N files changed" card with +/− counts per file; tapping one opens its coloured, numbered lines. - **Cost chips on paid-tool approvals.** The price of a paid MCP call and the chat's spend against its limit, with a warning past the limit. - **Plan card.** The agent's task list pinned above the composer of its chat. Stacked on #965. ## What changes - **Clarify:** - Desktop Gateway (dashboard): the `clarify` server request is one form, answered with `request.answer {answers, outcome: "submitted"}`; multi-select answers go as a JSON array string, as Hermes reads them. Answers already locked on another device (`open_requests` after a reconnect) show read-only and are left out, so their locks stand. - A gateway's Webapp listener that offers `canonical_clarify_batch` is asked for one form per turn (`clarify_batch` on `prompt.submit`), answered with its response frame; a lone `clarify.request` uses the same card and `clarify.respond`; a skipped question is answered empty. - API server runs: `clarify.request` (Hermes 0.22.3+, when clarify is enabled for the API server) shows the same card and is answered with `POST /v1/runs/{id}/clarify`; `clarify.settled` closes it. When the event stream is lost, the run poll shows the questions and approvals still listed in `pending_controls`, one card of each kind at a time, and closes each once Hermes no longer lists it or the run ends. - The pending-decision store keeps a form's questions, so the card comes back after an app restart. A question settled elsewhere, timed out or withdrawn closes its card right away. - **Diff cards:** Desktop Gateway edits report `tool.complete.inline_diff`, and stored transcripts keep it (v0.23 stores it under `display_metadata.tool_result_metadata`). The diff keeps its line breaks, with colour codes and control characters stripped, connection secrets and credential values (`password=`, `api_key:`, `Authorization:`, Bearer tokens) redacted, and a 32 KB cap. Hermes' `a/x → b/x` headers, plain unified diffs, deletions and its "… omitted N lines" note all parse; parsing stops at 2,000 lines and 50 files, and the card lists six files before summing the rest. Several edits of one file add up to one row. The raw "Inline diff" row leaves the tool timeline. - **Cost chips:** only the fixed sentences from Hermes' `tools/mcp_tool_costs.py` and `tools/mcp_tool_handlers.py` are read (an estimate or range, a note, spend with or without a limit, a fresh limit, both over-limit forms); they leave the shown text and anything else stays as written. Past the limit the card offers only Allow once and Deny, because Hermes then takes an answer for this call only. Works on Desktop Gateway and REST approvals. - **Plan card** ("Plan · 1 of 3 done", each step done / under way / to do / dropped, nested steps indented): follows `todo.updated` and the todo tool's `tool.complete` (`todos`, `revision`) live on both Desktop Gateway wires, ignores older revisions, and is restored from `session.resume`'s `todo_state` on reopen, including after an app restart. Tap the header to fold it; a finished plan starts folded. Capped at 256 steps and 64 chats. - **Composer:** a sent message leaves the composer as soon as its turn is handed to its run, for Hermes and Direct chats alike, instead of when the run ends, so an approval or a question no longer holds the sent words in the composer. - New strings in all 14 languages. ## Testing - Against a local Hermes v0.23.0 (synthetic data, stub model), through Conduit's real Desktop Gateway service: on the dashboard a two-question clarify shows one form and is answered with one `request.answer` (Hermes reports both answered); the form survives the pending store and, after a dropped socket, comes back with the other device's locked answer read-only. On a Webapp listener Hermes offers `canonical_clarify_batch`, Conduit sends `clarify_batch`, gets one form, answers it by response frame, closes it on settle, and reconnect works. - Diffs and plans were checked live on a separate, isolated Hermes instance whose stub model edits files and keeps a todo list; this found that v0.23 stores `inline_diff` under `display_metadata.tool_result_metadata`, now read. The plan arrived live and came back after a simulated restart. - Fixtures only: REST clarify (enabling clarify for the API server is a server config change), cost chips (rendered from Hermes' own cost-sentence code; no paid MCP server configured). - Targeted tests: 199 core and 323 app, plus the chat page tests. `dart analyze` (core), `flutter analyze` (touched files) and the platform UI lint are clean; Polish localization test passes. - iOS Simulator (iOS 26 debug build, local Hermes v0.23.0, synthetic data): the diff sheet shows unchanged blank lines with the right line numbers, and the composer is empty while an approval waits. - Not done: no device run. > [!NOTE] > ### Add Hermes clarify forms, diff cards, paid-tool costs, and plan cards > - Clarification requests now arrive as one whole-form event instead of one event per question. The new `HermesClarifyFormCard` lets users answer, select, or skip all questions together and submit them in one response ([hermes_desktop_transport.dart](https://github.com/cogwheel0/conduit/pull/966/files#diff-87b74a25923f4f42cc2930c42654814ebf5d6d22826386894a538a233f88c5cd), [hermes_clarify_form_card.dart](https://github.com/cogwheel0/conduit/pull/966/files#diff-bbd151444a1913e7121d4f8169d4e35d1ff19525ad4a23c1f72ea76efa3fc29a)). > - Adds parsing and display of paid-tool approval costs (`HermesApprovalCost`), with cost/spend chips on approval cards; over-limit costs restrict choices to 'once' and 'deny' ([hermes_approval_cost_chip.dart](https://github.com/cogwheel0/conduit/pull/966/files#diff-00b7491632734ce60664c6aedcd26ba8a05a944324502bb9f991d453ba825281)). > - Adds todo/plan state: `todo.updated` events and resume snapshots populate a per-chat plan card with fold/expand behavior ([hermes_todo_card.dart](https://github.com/cogwheel0/conduit/pull/966/files#diff-8e0a4d8da0cf2d466e1f09ddf7f22ed9c3071e4fcdea200199b53050063c2d12), [hermes_desktop_todos.dart](https://github.com/cogwheel0/conduit/pull/966/files#diff-772004b0f3ed168b0a9de35eeb5c78c93e3028d1d2b7a0432abc95c447d7d436)). > - Adds sanitized inline diffs: tool results with diffs render as a changed-files card and diff sheet instead of generic tool detail ([hermes_diff_card.dart](https://github.com/cogwheel0/conduit/pull/966/files#diff-f63ffb4d43107b3296c6ed5e40f694a87dd96

author: pierricgimmig
body: `perfr update` now downloads the latest `perfr-v*` release, checks the SHA-256, and replaces the install. That is the same replacement `--yes` used to perform: retired files are removed, and `perfr.h` is written to `~/.local/include` on Linux and macOS and to `\include` on Windows. After a replacement it prints: ``` updated perfr 0.1.1 -> 0.1.2 in ~/.local/bin restart any running perfr to use the new version ``` A current install prints `perfr 0.1.2 is up to date` and does not download the archive. A build newer than the release is left in place. `perfr update --check` only prints `current`, `latest`, and `status`. It exits 0 when this install is current or newer than the release, and **1** when an update is available. Download, checksum, and install failures still exit 2, including a cargo, Homebrew, or pip install that this command will not overwrite. `--yes` is still accepted and ignored, so older scripts keep working. It is hidden from the flag list and noted as a no-op in the help. Linux, macOS, and Windows share the command. Help text, the README, the manual, `docs/releasing.md`, and the setup skill describe the new lines and the exit codes.

author: panghy
body:
## Summary

"Test key" in Settings → E2B failed with *"E2B has no Intent image for this backend's version and size yet"* for keys that should pass. CI had built and published `intent/intent-node-2x4` and `intent/intent-node-4x8` tagged 0.11.147.

**Cause.** The backend checked each size with `GET /templates/aliases/<project>/intent-node-<size>:<version>`, using the user's key. E2B's handler for that endpoint (`e2b-dev/infra`, `handlers/template_alias.go`) answers only for templates of the caller's own project:
- A different namespace gets 400 ("namespace 'intent' must match your team …").
- Another project's template gets 403, even when it is public.

The backend read 400/404 as "missing" and 403 as "key rejected". So with any normal user's key, every size looked missing. E2B has no endpoint that lets another project check a public template's tag.

**Fix**
1. **Key test:** "Test key" (`validateOnly`, and a configure with `apiKey`) checks only the key.
2. **Published sizes:** they come from a public manifest, `e2b-templates.json` (`{ schema, project, version, sizes }`), attached to the `intent-hq/intentd-releases` release `v<version>`. The backend reads it without a key.
   - When the manifest is missing, unreadable, or for another project or version (a custom `templateProject`), the backend offers `2x4` and `4x8` marked unverified and refuses no size.
   - When the manifest is verified, a size it does not list is `template-missing`.
3. **Create is the real check:** a create E2B forbids (403) or does not know (404) now fails `cloud-machine-unavailable` `template-missing`, not `key-rejected`, and leaves no sandbox.
4. **Release workflow:** after release and manual template builds, a new `manifest` job checks each `intent-node-<size>:<version>` tag with the publishing project's own key (E2B answers that for the owner). It writes the manifest and runs `gh release upload --clobber` to intentd-releases, using `INTENTD_RELEASES_TOKEN`. It is fail-soft without the secrets. The new dispatch input `manifest_only` builds nothing and only writes the manifest; it serves as a backfill for an earlier release such as 0.11.147.
5. **Test seam:** `INTENTD_E2B_MANIFEST_BASE_URL`.

The `RemoteMachine`/provider wire shape is unchanged. The verified flag is internal.

## Tests (written first; the first reproduced the user's message exactly)
- The fake E2B now answers alias lookups like real E2B does for another project's key (400 namespace mismatch).
  - Before the fix, `cloudMachines.configure` failed with *"E2B has no template intent/intent-node-4x8:0.11.147 …"*.
  - After the fix, it returns `ready`, with the sizes taken from the fake release manifest.
- If the manifest lists only `2x4`, a `validateOnly` with `4x8` gives `template-missing`, and `2x4` passes.
- Without a manifest, the fallback sizes are `2x4` and `4x8`, unverified, and `16x32` is still accepted.
- When the create gets a 404 for the template, the agent's `placementError` is `template-missing` and no sandbox is created.
- Release side (`scripts/test-e2b-template.mjs`, 33 tests): the manifest shape and ordering, slug, version and size validation, the per-size tag check, and the workflow contract (the job runs after the builds, never on PRs, with the token only there; `manifest_only` skips the builds).

Local results: `e2e_remote_launch::*` 18/18; clippy clean; `lint-workflows` clean.

After merge: run `gh workflow run e2b-template.yml -f version=0.11.147 -f manifest_only=true` to backfill 0.11.147. Backends from this release on read the manifest.

author: acalcutt
body:
These are some smb changes I made testing in https://gitlab.techidiots.net/techidiots-llc/360-riffle which i think would be useful here. most of them were tested with my repo and I asked the AI to make a PR for the fixes. I was able to copy files and disks contents to iso/shares on top of this so it was really useful.

AI Description
-------------------------------
Until now `smb://` sources could only be listed and read. Writing, checking whether a file exists, deleting, renaming and making folders were stubs (some returned success without doing anything), so the File Manager couldn't copy to a share and every share path looked like it existed. This fills them in on top of the existing libsmb2 wrapper.

### Changes
- **Write files**: `CFileSMB::OpenForWrite` and `Write` work. The file is created if missing and only emptied when overwriting, as `CFileHD` does. `smb2_write` sends at most the server's max write size per request, so `Write` loops until the whole buffer is out.
- **Stat, Exists, Delete, Rename**: `Stat` fills in type, size and times from `smb2_stat` (it used to report success for every path). `Exists` now overrides `IFile::Exists`; it was a static that never got called. `Delete` uses `smb2_unlink`. `Rename` uses `smb2_rename` and only works within a share, because SMB can't rename across shares.
- **Paths in the share**: libsmb2 leaves the path NULL for a URL that names only the share, and a folder URL keeps its trailing slash, which the server won't accept. Both are normalised before they're sent, so `smb://server/share` no longer crashes `Stat`.
- **Folders**: `CSMBDirectory::Create` and `Remove` use `smb2_mkdir`/`smb2_rmdir` (they always failed before). `Exists` checks the path is a folder (it always returned true before).
- **Listing**: items get their size and modified date from `smb2_readdir`, so sorting by size or date works and sizes no longer show as 0.
- **Domain users**: the domain used to be hard-coded to `workgroup`. A user name can now be `DOMAIN\name`, `name@domain` (sent as a UPN with no domain) or a plain name for a local account (still `workgroup`). The domain in an `smb://domain;user@server/` URL is also used. The user name keyboard for SMB shows these forms (new string 13188).
- **Logging**: when a folder can't be opened, libsmb2's reason (e.g. `STATUS_OBJECT_NAME_NOT_FOUND`, `STATUS_ACCESS_DENIED`) is logged.

### Known limitation (unchanged)
`CXBLibSMB2` holds one share connection per instance, and all files share one instance. Opening a file on another share drops the first connection. So copying between two different shares fails, while share↔HDD/USB and copies within one share work. Fixing this needs a connection per share; I've left it for a separate change.

### Testing
- Release | Xbox 360 build of current master with these commits compiles and links with no new warnings.
- The same code is used in a fork on a retail console: listing shares with sizes and dates, copying files to and from a Windows share, and creating folders on it.

author: yidaweng
body:
## Summary

Backport [apache/tvm#20756](https://github.com/apache/tvm/pull/20756) to `tilelang_main`.

`SplitFloorDivConst` / `SplitFloorModConst` can cancel a negative iterator scale into the divisor (for example `floordiv(63 - x, 2)` becomes `floordiv(x - 63, -2)`). `PadDividendToDivisor` and the following split construction assume a positive divisor, so the rewrite changes floor rounding. TileLang's `FlattenBuffer` uses this path and can turn a valid reverse index into an out-of-bounds flat offset (tile-ai/tilelang#3705).

## Changes

- After scale handling, report a provably non-positive divisor via `ErrorLogger` and return an empty `PrimExpr`, so `IterMapSimplify` keeps the original expression.
- Preserve earlier exact-divisibility branches, including valid negative-scale cases such as `floordiv(x * -2 + 62, 2) -> x * -1 + 31`.
- Leave unknown-sign symbolic divisors alone so cases like `n * 4096` keep simplifying.
- Add `test_non_positive_divisor_is_not_simplified`.

## Validation

- Rebuilt TileLang against this commit and confirmed the #3705 arithmetic reproducer retains `(7 - x // 2) // 2 * 16` (previously `x // -4 * 16 + 48`; value at `x=13` was `-16`, now `0`).
- New TVM unit test passes; positive nested-split control still simplifies to `x // 4`.
- TileLang CPU regressions for FlattenBuffer reverse indices: **77 passed** (new reverse-index file + existing flatten_buffer tests).
- Related `test_arith_iter_affine_map.py` cases (`non_positive`, nested floormod, symbolic reshape/case): **5 passed**.

This is the TVM half of tile-ai/tilelang#3705. A follow-up TileLang PR will bump `3rdparty/tvm` and add the FlattenBuffer regressions.

author: cyberpapiii
body:
## Why

Rob wants iMessage Max to install like a normal Mac app. 2.0 ships as a notarized DMG plus `brew install --cask cyberpapiii/tap/imessage-max`, and the old formula and tarball go away. This is plan 087 P8 (`plans/087-mac-app-install-and-onboarding.md`, "Ship 2.0 through a cask and retire the formula").

## What changes for people installing it

- The README's install section is two lines: open the DMG, or run `brew install --cask cyberpapiii/tap/imessage-max`. An "Upgrading from 1.x" note follows it.
- The cask installs `iMessage Max.app`, needs Apple silicon and macOS 15 or later, and links `imessage-max` (the stdio bridge) into Homebrew's `bin`, so stdio configs that run `imessage-max` keep working.
- Releases carry the DMG and the `.mcpb`, and no tarball.

## Release workflow

- `scripts/generate-cask.sh <version> <sha256>` prints the cask. The `dmg` job runs it on the DMG it just built, prints the result, and runs `brew style` and `brew audit --cask --strict` on it in a throwaway local tap. `brew audit` loads a cask only by name from a trusted tap, so the step runs `brew tap-new` and `brew trust` first.
- On a `v*` tag only, the `release` job creates the GitHub release, then checks out `cyberpapiii/homebrew-tap` with `HOMEBREW_TAP_DEPLOY_KEY` and pushes `Casks/imessage-max.rb`. The cask never names a DMG the release does not hold yet. A dry run prints and uploads the cask and never touches the tap.
- The `build-and-release` tarball job is deleted. `checks` (build.yml) already runs `check-version.sh`, and `sign-notarize-app.sh` already checks the tag, architecture, version and dylib link.

## The cask

```ruby
cask "imessage-max" do
  version "2.0.0"
  sha256 "<DMG sha256>"

  url "https://github.com/cyberpapiii/imessage-max/releases/download/v#{version}/iMessage-Max-#{version}.dmg"
  name "iMessage Max"
  desc "MCP server that lets AI assistants read, search and send iMessages"
  homepage "https://github.com/cyberpapiii/imessage-max"

  depends_on arch: :arm64
  depends_on macos: :sequoia

  app "iMessage Max.app"
  binary "#{appdir}/iMessage Max.app/Contents/MacOS/imessage-max"

  uninstall quit:   "com.cyberpapiii.imessage-max.menubar",
            signal: ["TERM", "com.cyberpapiii.imessage-max.helper"]

  zap launchctl: "com.cyberpapiii.imessage-max.helper",
      trash:     [ ...Application Support/iMessage Max, Logs/iMessage Max, 1.x logs, Caches, HTTPStorages, Preferences... ]
end
```

There are two departures from the brief, and both come from Homebrew 7's rules.

- `depends_on macos: :sequoia`, not `">= :sequoia"`. Homebrew 7's `Homebrew/OSDependsOn` cop rejects the string form and autocorrects it to the bare symbol, which means the same minimum.
- The helper is stopped with `uninstall signal:`, and `launchctl` sits in `zap`. In Homebrew 7 (`cask/artifact/abstract_uninstall.rb`), `brew upgrade` runs every uninstall directive except `signal`. So `uninstall launchctl:` would unload the helper on every upgrade. The companion that brew reopens calls `restartIfOutdated`, which restarts only a helper that is still running, so the helper would stay down until the next login. With `signal`, `brew uninstall` still stops the helper (it exits 0 on SIGTERM, and `KeepAlive.SuccessfulExit = false` does not relaunch it), `brew upgrade` leaves it running for the companion to restart, and `--zap` unloads the job. This comes from reading Homebrew's code. Nothing has been installed live yet, and lane 2 is the check.

## Retired

- `swift/Formula/imessage-max.rb`, its two checks in `scripts/check-version.sh` and `VersionConsistencyTests`, and `ruby -c` in `make release-check`.
- The `install-agent` string assertion in `ServiceFilesContractTests`, which existed only to keep the retired target out. A new `testCaskNamesTheBundledLayout` pins the cask generator to `ServiceDefaults` (label, bundle id, helper path, app-support and log folders). Mutating the log folder in the generator makes it fail.
- `make install-agent` and `swift/launchd/` were already gone after P3.

## `make install` in 2.0

It still builds the app, copies it into place, opens it with `--register-helper`, and runs `verify` and `verify-db`. The change is where it installs. It uses `/Applications` when a released copy (DMG or cask) is already there, and `~/Applications` otherwise. Two bundles with the same bundle id that both register `com.cyberpapiii.imessage-max.helper` would fight over one label and one set of Login Items entries, so a developer build replaces the released copy in place. `brew upgrade` puts the release back later. `make restart`, `make status` and `make logs` follow the same `APP` and are otherwise unchanged.

## Version

Every version site is 2.0.0 (`Version.swift`, `Info.plist`, `mcpb/manifest.json`, `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`). `CHANGELOG.md` has a 2.0.0 entry for the move from formula to app, the port and token change, the bridge, and the 1.x upgrade steps.

## For the root at release time

The tap's formula change is not pushed. Set `date:` to the tag date. Checked in a scratch tap: `brew style` and `brew audit` pass, and the formula reports `disabled?=true` with the message below. The `version` line goes because audit flags it as redundant and only the retired `check-version.sh` read it.

```diff
--- a/imessage-max.rb
+++ b/imessage-max.rb
@@ -2,9 +2,6 @@
   desc "MCP server for iMessage - AI assistant integration"
   homepage "https://github.com/cyberpapiii/imessage-max"
   url "https://github.com/cyberpapiii/imessage-max/releases/download/v1.8.0/imessage-max-macos.tar.gz"
-  # version is redundant with the url's tag segment; kept because
-  # scripts/check-version.sh and VersionConsistencyTests read it.
-  version "1.8.0"
   # sha256 of the ad-hoc-signed imessage-max-macos.tar.gz built from v1.8.0.
   # Regenerate with `shasum -a 256 imessage-max-macos.tar.gz` if the asset is
   # ever rebuilt. The tarball must be ad-hoc signed (`codesign --sign -`),
@@ -13,6 +10,11 @@
   sha256 "be91c55aba417626c1de89ca9ddf31b4d2a47e90e084089df21c130627de30ec"
   license "MIT"
 
+  # 2.0 ships as a Mac app through the cask of the same name in this tap.
+  disable! date:             "2026-11-07",
+           because:          "is now the iMessage Max app. Run `brew uninstall imessage-max`, then install the cask",
+           replacement_cask: "cyberpapiii/tap/imessage-max"

```

```
Error: imessage-max disabled because it is now the iMessage Max app. Run `brew uninstall imessage-max`, then install the cask! ...
Replacement:
  brew install --cask cyberpapiii/tap/imessage-max
```

## Verification

- `brew style --cask` and `brew audit --cask --strict` pass locally on the generated cask in a scratch tap. CI runs both in the dry run below.
- Server: `VersionConsistencyTests` 1/1, `ServiceFilesContractTests` 9/9, `LaunchdSafetyTests` 1/1, each run alone under a 120 s alarm.
- `contract`: 6 tests pass. `macos`: 49 tests pass (40 + 9).
- `shellcheck scripts/*.sh script/*.sh` is clean. `scripts/check-version.sh` prints `OK 2.0.0`.
- Lane 10 grep (`Cellar|setup-signing|install-agent|local\.imessage-max`, outside `CHANGELOG.md` and `plans/`) hits only dated records under `docs/` (plans, specs and validation dated 2026-09-01 and 2026-10-12, and a 2026-06-11 solution marked superseded), the 1.x upgrade note in `macos/README.md`, and the migration code in `macos/Sources/MaxCore` that must name the old label.
- Release dry run: see the PR comment.
