author: habibuoy
body:
## Summary

The frontend will run on a different origin, so browsers need CORS headers before they can call the API.

- **Allowed origins:** the default CORS policy allows the origins listed in `Cors:AllowedOrigins`. Each origin is trimmed and trailing slashes are ignored, so `https://app.example.com/` works. With no origins listed, no cross-origin request is allowed.
- **Requests:** any header and method is allowed. Credentials aren't, because the JWT travels in the `Authorization` header rather than a cookie.
- **`Location` header:** this is exposed so the frontend can read the id of a resource it just created. Create endpoints return `201` with only `Location`.
- **Middleware order:** `UseCors()` runs before authentication, so a 401 still carries `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` and the frontend can tell "logged out" apart from a network error.
- **Development:** `appsettings.Development.json` allows `http://localhost:3000`, the default Next.js dev server.
- **Deploying:** set `Cors__AllowedOrigins__0=https://your-frontend`.

## Tests

`CorsTests` covers:
- A preflight from an allowed origin allows the method and the `Authorization` header.
- An origin configured with a trailing slash matches.
- Other origins and an empty list get no CORS headers.
- A 401 is readable by the browser.
- `Location` is exposed.

`dotnet test Backend.sln`: 939 unit and 58 integration tests passed.

This builds on #5, so merge that first. GitHub will then retarget this PR to `main`, or you can change the base manually.

author: andydoane
body:
## N2 — Native-only AVAudioSession lifecycle and deliberate gesture recovery

**Base:** `experiment/native-ios-audio` at merge `6303ce79edb2fc6de9be4b5f056bbd776731b9fc` ([PR #20](https://github.com/andydoane/biblozoo/pull/20), N1 isolation). The owner merged/tested N1 and reports it behaved as described, including intentionally silent unmigrated Web output. **This PR does not re-enable Web Audio, HTML sound fallback or old Zoo Escape audio-repair triggers.** It is only for `com.andydoane.biblozoo.audiotest`; stable `ios-prep`, web/PWA/Android, profiles, rewards and original installed BibloZoo are untouched. **Leave unmerged for owner review.**

### Rationale / previous evidence
Prior PR #18 physical iPhone Native Classic failed with `pending=YES began=1 ended=0` already at `selected-native` and `interruption-pending` while the DEV native clip had worked independently in other tests. That did **not prove** WebKit caused the interruption. N1 removed WebKit audible output; N2 now makes native session state and explicit retry behavior observable and safer, rather than clearing the latch on foreground or falling back to Web.

### Code changes
- **Native output session owner:** `ios/App/App/BibloZooNativeSoundPlugin.swift` remains the same allowlisted three-sound AVAudioPlayer plugin and adds `activateFromGesture({purpose:"dev"|"feeding"})`. This is the **only active output-session activation entrypoint** in the experimental app. It does nothing when no native interruption/reset exists.
- **Conservative eligibility:** A genuine `.began` without `.ended` remains blocked with `interruption-pending`. Merely coming to foreground **no longer clears pending**. After a complete inactive/background→active transition **and a new explicit DEV/Got It!/Resume tap**, the native plugin may ask the OS to `setActive(true)` with a **four-second cooldown and max two attempts per foreground**. OS rejection preserves pending; acceptance only permits new native preload and is **not proof of audible playback**. `AVAudioSessionInterruptionWasSuspendedKey=true` is logged as historical rather than a new active `.began`.
- **Route/media lifecycle:** Old players are stopped/disposed on leaving foreground, route changes and media-services loss/reset, with no automatic replay. A reset requires explicit fresh gesture. No `setCategory`, `setMode`, `setActive(false)`, background entitlement, or microphone policy change. If a reset changes category, this intentionally fails `category-not-soloambient` pending a deliberate future policy review.
- **Disable competing Web-clock activation:** `SceneDelegate.swift` keeps the legacy `BibloZooAudioSessionRecovery` bridge registered but immediately rejects `reactivateAfterClockStall` with `legacy-web-recovery-disabled` for the `.audiotest` bundle, before its old `setActive` path. Read-only historic diagnostics remain available.
- **DEV and Feeding integration:** `native-sound-smoke-test.js` DEV button and `feeding-native-audio-pilot.js` Native Classic prepare now call the explicit Swift native gesture method **before** fixed-ID preload. Any blocked activation is reported, no star/chomp is sent and there is no Web fallback. Resume requires new gesture; a refused result preserves the safe paused/error path.
- **Bounded, read-only event history:** `getDebugState` adds a last-28-events in-memory trace (monotonic seq, elapsed ms, app state, foreground epoch, pending, numeric reason) plus activation/reset counters. DEV Inspect prints last eight events. No personal, verse, profile, mic or recording content; inspection never plays audio or activates the session.
- **Tests:** Updated native DEV JS VM/Swift source policy tests and Native Feeding adapter lifecycle tests including refusal before preload, genuine pending, OS result, timeouts, stale work and no Web fallback.
- **Handoff in same PR:** Updated mandatory `docs/PROJECT-HANDOFF.md` current HEAD, merged N1 owner report, N2 implementation, risks, next gate; updated `docs/TESTING.md` and `docs/AUDIO-RECOVERY.md`; added [N2 design and device checklist](https://github.com/andydoane/biblozoo/blob/experiment/n2-native-session-lifecycle/docs/N2-NATIVE-SESSION-LIFECYCLE.md).

### Validation (different evidence levels)
- [x] Verified PR #20 merged; N1 owner reports intended behavior after iPhone test.
- [x] **Node regression checks passed** including N2 DEV bridge and Native Feeding tests, existing sound/Feeding/Zoo escape/Flashcards/Read My Verse regressions.
- [x] **Production web build passed**, including N1 guard in 33 packaged HTML entrypoints.
- [x] **Final PR HEAD `116fce7e` passed both GitHub Actions jobs**: [run #42389247840](https://github.com/andydoane/biblozoo/actions/runs/42389247840), including native DEV/Feeding, N1 isolation, broader Node regressions and production web build. This does **not** compile Swift or confirm speaker output.
- [ ] **Xcode Swift compile/signing:** not run in Linux CI.
- [ ] **Physical iPhone audible acceptance:** not performed for N2. Neither `setActive(true)` acceptance nor the Node/Swift source checks prove hardware audibility.

### Owner after merge — physical iPhone test
In GitHub Desktop choose `biblozoo-native-audio` worktree → Fetch/Pull `experiment/native-ios-audio` (keep original BibloZoo installed and unmodified). Run:
```sh
node scripts/validate_native_sound_smoke_test.js
node scripts/validate_native_feeding_preview_c2.js
npm run build
node scripts/validate_native_only_ios_output.js
npx cap sync ios
npx cap open ios
```
In Xcode verify **BibloZoo Audio Test** / `.audiotest` bundle ID before running on the physical iPhone.

1. Before any DEV sound tap, use **Inspect native state**; capture `app=`, `pending=`, `last=`, `foregroundEpoch=`, activation/result, and last-eight-event `trace=`.
2. Tap **Play star**, **Play chomp** (and optional pet unlock). Record which are **actually heard**. Inspect again and copy exact state/trace, not just `accepted`.
3. Classic Feeding Preview → Drag → **Got It!**. Confirm **Native ONLY** with intentionally silent pegs, and human-heard star/chomp or explicit `interruption-pending`/other failure. Check scores/Back and no Web sound or Zoo Escape audio repair.
4. Switch apps and return while Classic is active. It should freeze and require deliberate **Resume** or Back. Tap Resume and record native `activation-os-accepted` vs `activation-os-rejected` and actual sounds. If genuinely pending without a completed return, another tap must **not** clear it. Do not spam retry; minimum four seconds between attempted activations.
5. Check no late sound/reward, unexpected recording start, lost progress, or altered original stable BibloZoo. Route/silent switch/headphones test if convenient.

**Next:** If the interruption still sticks or the Swift build fails, make a **focused N2 follow-up using the captured trace**; do not bypass genuine interruptions or add Web fallback. Only after device-confirmed native foundation proceed to N3 overlapping voices/tones. Zoo Escape/ZOO BREAK future randomized surprises remain deferred until N8.

**Merge control:** PR left **open, unmerged**. Owner reviews/merges.

author: rlopc
body:
## What and why

Adopts GitHub Actions workflow lockfiles (GA 2026-10-28), generated with `gh actions-lock` v0.4.1:

- `.github/workflows/actions.lock` records each action's commit plus its owner and repository ids, so a retagged release or a re-registered repository with the same name is caught before it runs. GitHub's secure-use reference says the lockfile supersedes SHA pinning and satisfies the "require SHA pinning" policy, which is enabled on this repository.
- The tool rewrites `uses:` from SHA to the exact version tag; the locked commits are the same SHAs as before. These three actions have no transitive action dependencies, so nothing new is pinned today.
- Dependabot regenerates the lockfile entry in the same PR when it bumps an action.
- `actions.lock` added to the push path filter and the `changes` job, since it decides which code the docconv jobs run.

The "Require lockfile" policy is not enabled yet.

author: federicohermo
body:
## Para qué

En la build v10.1.3, final 4, la placa de cinco líneas dejaba su primera línea sobre el fondo claro, arriba de la franja oscura. Además, cada cambio de placa fundía toda la pantalla.

## Qué cambia

- La franja de lectura es más alta (de 360–780 a 190–950 en el marco de 1080) y su parte oscura es el 60 % del alto. El texto más largo de todos los finales, con su botón, queda dentro. El PR #915 la sigue estirando de lado a lado.
- `RecorridoDelEpilogo` decide qué se funde. Entre dos placas con el mismo fondo funde el texto y el botón (`opacidad_del_texto()`), y `negro()` queda en 0. Con la primera placa, con la salida de la última hacia la pantalla de final y con un cambio de fondo, funde la pantalla entera, como antes.
- `BR-SHF-072` lo dice: una viñeta nueva y la existente acotada a la primera placa y a la salida de la última. Es decisión del usuario.
- El auxiliar `AvanceDelEpilogo` distingue ahora «placa leída» por `negro() == 0` y texto opaco.

## Criterios

- AC-SHF-138 → `recorrido_del_epilogo_test` (3 casos nuevos) y `pantalla_de_epilogo_test` (2 casos nuevos) → verde
- AC-SHF-134 → `pantalla_de_epilogo_test::test_el_texto_de_toda_placa_queda_dentro_de_la_parte_oscura` (toda placa de todos los finales, leída del dominio) → verde

Corrí sólo las suites de la pantalla de epílogo, del recorrido y `epilogo_en_el_almacen_test`: 28 casos, 0 fallos. Sin renders ni build web.

author: astevegreen
body:
The same fix as terminal-dusk#532 and blockchain-technology-course#39, in `scripts/lib/agy.mjs`.

## What changed
- `postApi`'s child script passed `createConnection` together with `agent: false`. With `agent: false`, `node:https` ignores `createConnection`, so the request went straight to Google and skipped the proxy's CONNECT tunnel. The cloud proxy cut the idle tunnel after about 7 seconds, and the child crashed (`node:events:497`) before any real review could answer.
- The agent option is now left out, so the request really goes through the tunnel.
- The raw tunnel socket has an `'error'` listener, so a cut tunnel comes back as a reason instead of a crash.
- The child exits once its answer is written, so a connection the proxy leaves open can't keep it running.
- When the child does crash, the reason shown is the stack's `Error: …` line.

## Verified
- New `scripts/__tests__/agyApiTunnel.test.ts` (3 tests): the request travels inside the tunnel, and a cut tunnel comes back as a reason; a crash shows its error line; the child exits even though the proxy leaves the connection open. All 3 failed before the fix. After it, all 23 tests in `agyApi` and `agyApiTunnel` pass.
- `npm run gate-stamp -- run lint test tooling` passed: 4,288 unit tests and 63 tooling tests.
- Live, through the cloud session's real proxy: a 35-second Gemini request returned HTTP 200. The old code failed at about 7 seconds.

## Not yet run
- **Pushed past the pre-push hook, with the owner's yes in chat: "yes, push the YODC branch past the hook".** The hook's Firefox and WebKit end-to-end tests can't start in a cloud session (only Chromium is installed: "Executable doesn't exist"). All its Chromium tests passed.
- **The rail second look** (`node scripts/second-look.mjs --rails-only`) answered `retry`: it needs agy on the PC.

This stays a draft until both run on the PC.

author: bolichen97
body:
## Problem / Motivation

**Goal:** `prove.py`, `pre_push_gate.py` and `regen_shared.py` start `git` the same safe way as the other prepare-pr runners: a `git.cmd` launcher works, and a `git` copy in the checkout never runs.

Depends on #32313 (it adds the shared `scripts/_tool_argv.py` this builds on); this branch is stacked on it.

The prepare-pr runners resolve `gh`/`git` through `scripts/_tool_argv.py`, but three spawn sites in the same directory still hand a bare `git` to `subprocess.run`: `prove._git_argv` (used by `_git` and both `git apply` calls), `pre_push_gate.git_argv` (every git call the gate runner makes) and `regen_shared.run`. On Windows, CreateProcess appends only `.exe` when it searches PATH, so a `git.cmd` launcher is reported missing, and it searches the current directory first. These scripts run inside the checkout they judge, so a `git.exe` committed there would run instead of the real one.

## Why it matters

`prove.py` and the pre-push gate run on contributors' machines against branches they did not write. A planted `git.exe` would run with the contributor's credentials, and a shim-installed git breaks the proof and the gate with a misleading "not found".

## Not a goal

- `pre_push_gate.run`'s profile gate command lines (`gate_map.json` argv): whether they get the batch guard is the open question in #28427; they launch unchanged.
- `regen_shared.run_entry`'s generator launch, which already resolves through `shutil.which`.
- Changing git's environment or its config pins.

## What changed (motivation → approach → change)

Symptom: a bare `git` misses `git.cmd` and is searched in the checkout first → root cause: three spawn sites left the lookup to the OS → change: each one goes through `_tool_argv.resolve`, the rule every other runner here already uses.

| Site | Shape | How it resolves |
|---|---|---|
| `prove._git_argv` | argv builder | `_tool_argv.resolve`; a refusal raises `OSError`, which `main` reports as exit 2 |
| `pre_push_gate.git_argv` | argv builder | the same; `main` turns the `OSError` into exit 2 |
| `regen_shared.run` | runner | `_tool_argv.resolve`; a refusal is returned as `(rc, stdout, stderr)` like the other runners |

`prove.py`'s "git not found on PATH" check asks `_tool_argv.which`, so it agrees with the launch. The commit and tree ids a proof names are asked for as `HEAD` and `<commit>:` instead of `HEAD^{commit}` and `^{tree}`: `^` is a cmd.exe metacharacter, so with a `git.cmd` launcher the guard would refuse every run. Each script loads `_tool_argv.py` inline at import, by path and without writing bytecode, as `green_age.py` does.

## Backwards compatibility

Compatible: on POSIX the lookup finds the same git the OS would; a missing git still ends each script with exit 2, now before any spawn; a `git.cmd` that could not start before now starts.

Removes nothing: finding git through the current directory or a relative PATH entry was never intended, and every builder and runner keeps its signature and return shape.

## Tests

- `test/test_prepare_pr_tool_argv.py`: `prove._git_argv` and `pre_push_gate.git_argv` pick the git on an absolute PATH entry over one in the cwd reachable through `.`, and raise when only the cwd has one; with a `git.cmd` launcher, `prove.pin_commit` and `pre_push_gate.head_tree` still launch it; `regen_shared.run` joins the runners that return a refusal without spawning and spawn the resolved argv.
- `test/test_prepare_pr_prove_line.py`: the pinned argv starts with the resolved git; the class sweep reads the new builder line.
- `test/test_prepare_pr_regen_shared.py`: the `npm.CMD` launch test stubs only the `npm` lookup, so git still resolves.

Determinism: the 16 new or changed test ids passed 20 runs at `-n0`, 10 runs at `-n 4 --dist loadgroup --max-worker-restart=2` beside `test_prepare_pr_pre_push_gate.py` and `test_prepare_pr_diff_signals_proof.py`, and one run in an order shuffled with seed 28427.

Proof: PROVEN test/test_prepare_pr_prove_line.py::test_every_git_subprocess_in_prove_goes_through_the_pinned_argv, test/test_prepare_pr_tool_argv.py::test_every_git_argv_builder_launches_the_git_on_an_absolute_path_entry[prove.py-_git_argv], test/test_prepare_pr_tool_argv.py::test_every_git_argv_builder_launches_the_git_on_an_absolute_path_entry[pre_push_gate.py-git_argv] (head 8b0f7354fb45)

## Manual verification

N/A — unit coverage is sufficient: the lookup is a pure function of PATH and the cwd, tested with planted executables, and each call site is pinned. A real Windows `git.cmd` launch is not reproducible from Linux; the Windows CI lane runs the same tests.

## Related Issues

Closes #28427

Part of #10937

## Sibling sweep

Swept: git grep -nE "subprocess\.(run|Popen)\(" -- src/kiro_crew/builtin_skills/kirocrew-dev/kirocrew-prepare-pr/scripts/
Sibling: src/kiro_crew/builtin_skills/kirocrew-dev/kirocrew-prepare-pr/scripts/prove.py -- changed here
Sibling: src/kiro_crew/builtin_skills/kirocrew-dev/kirocrew-prepare-pr/scripts/pre_push_gate.py -- changed here
Sibling: src/kiro_crew/builtin_skills/kirocrew-dev/kirocrew-prepare-pr/scripts/regen_shared.py -- changed here
Sibling: src/kiro_crew/builtin_skills/kirocrew-dev/kirocrew-prepare-pr/scripts/_review_pushes.py -- not affected -- its own gh runner serves only the CLI the GPT lane runs on a Linux CI runner; pr_findings passes its resolved run
Sibling: src/kiro_crew/builtin_skills/kirocrew-dev/kirocrew-prepare-pr/scripts/diff_signals.py -- not affected -- its bash and sys.executable launches use absolute paths

## Pattern harvest

Rule candidate: semgrep
Pattern: subprocess.run/Popen whose argv[0] is a bare string literal command name (e.g. "gh", "git") in a skill script, instead of a resolved path

## Checklist

- [x] At most two commits (one is the norm), with a Conventional Commits title (`feat|fix|docs|style|refactor|perf|test|chore|ci|build|revert: ...`)
- [x] Existing tests pass and new tests added for new functionality
- [x] Self-review completed; code follows project style guidelines

- [x] No secrets, credentials, or internal references in the diff

body:
This PR fixes one gate that newly fails in smart-trust#152. `check:artefact-verification` reports `NEW artefact check with no verification declaration: smart-base:processes:render:check`.

body:
## Summary

Formación capa 2, tarjeta 2: **pase de urgencia** (especificación §6.3, §7 y §8; plan `PLAN-capa2.md`, D4). El mentor actual de un pupilo puede levantar «Tu turno primero» en un asunto concreto y por un tiempo limitado. El candado de salida no cambia: lo que el pupilo escribe durante el pase sigue sellado como borrador de pasante y no sale sin aprobación.

## What changed

- **Backend: regla del turno.** `lib/trainingPass.ts` y `resolveTurnTraining` deciden el requisito del turno en chat, proyecto y tabular. `resolveTrainingStage`, que decide el sello, no cambia. Word no tiene asunto, así que no consulta pases. Una prueba de contrato lee las fuentes y verifica qué regla usa cada lugar (D4).
- **Backend: pases.** `POST/GET/DELETE /orgs/:orgId/training/pupils/:userId/passes`. Solo el mentor actual da, lista y revoca pases. La migración `20261107_61_litt_training_urgency_pass_grant.sql` (la función de concesión) también está en `schema.sql`.
  - Duración: mínimo 30 minutos, 8 horas por omisión y tope de 72 horas.
  - Máximo 5 pases vigentes por pupilo.
  - Motivo de lista cerrada: `plazo`, `audiencia`, `cliente_urgente`, `otro`.
- **Auditoría.** `training.urgency_pass_*` registra quién dio el pase, el código de motivo y hasta cuándo, sin texto libre. La nota libre va solo en la fila del pase.
- **`GET /training/stage`.** Ahora devuelve `attempt_required` y `urgency_pass`.
- **Frontend.**
  - `useTrainingStage` y `TrainingAttemptFieldUI` (`packages/ui`) siguen `attempt_required` y muestran «pase de urgencia vigente hasta …».
  - El compositor del asistente refleja el pase del proyecto.
  - Los códigos nuevos están en `CODE_KINDS` y se muestran con `describeError`/`notifyError`.
- **Docs.** `docs/training.md`, sección «Urgency pass».

## Why

Ante un plazo o una audiencia, el pupilo necesita trabajar sin escribir primero su intento. La supervisión no se debilita: el pase es del mentor, por asunto y temporal, y el borrador sigue sin salir sin aprobación.

## Testing

Integra `main` con la tarjeta 3 (#73): pases y trabajos comparten `send`/`mentorOf` en `trainingSupervision.routes.ts`. Los pases se montan en `/orgs/:orgId/training/pupils/:userId/passes` (misma URL pública), y `GET /training/me/supervision` devuelve revisiones y pases. Todo lo de abajo se corrió sobre ese merge.


Con Node 22.23.4, una suite a la vez:

- **Backend.**
  - `npm run build` y `npm run typecheck:test`: OK.
  - `npm test`: 6046 pruebas pasan. Las únicas 2 que fallan son las ambientales de LibreOffice (`isolated.test.ts` y `processLimits.test.ts`).
  - Control negativo (`trainingUrgencyPass.lock.test.ts`):
    - sin pase, el pupilo debe escribir primero;
    - con pase, no;
    - con el pase vencido, vuelve a tener que escribir primero;
    - el documento escrito durante el pase sigue sellado (`training_approval_required`) hasta que se aprueba.
- **Postgres opt-in** (`MIKE_TEST_POSTGRES_CONTAINER=littsqltest-db-1`).
  - Pasan `trainingUrgencyPass`, `trainingSupervision`, `trainingOutputLock`, `training` y `littPrivateMatterLists`.
  - La prueba del pase demuestra que nadie que no sea el mentor actual puede crear un pase. Con una función que también deja dar pases al owner, la prueba falla.
  - Fallan cuatro suites ajenas a este cambio: `orgLifecycle`, `memberDeparture`, `orgDepartureRetention` y `tabularActivity`. Necesitan el `auth.uid()` de Supabase, que este contenedor no tiene.
  - Los 31 `performance.*.sql` pasan en secuencia sobre `schema.sql` fresco, como en CI.
- **Frontend.**
  - typecheck: OK.
  - lint: 0 errores. Ninguno de los avisos cae en archivos de este cambio.
  - test:coverage: 4366 pruebas pasan. Fallan 2 que no son de este cambio, por tiempo agotado con la máquina cargada (otro worker corría su suite al mismo tiempo): `PlaybooksWorkspace.test.tsx` y `RouterSettingsSection.test.tsx`. Corridas solas pasan (89/89).
- **word-addin.** typecheck: OK.
- **Diff.** `git diff --check`: OK. El grep de azul sobre las líneas agregadas da 0.

author: milamer
body:
Closes #2.

## What changes

- `a[foo]` parses like `a.foo`. Both forms refer to the same key, so objects merge and duplicates are detected as with dots (`a.foo` + `a[foo]` → `DuplicateKeyError('a[foo]')`).
- Digits in brackets (`a[0]`) stay an ordered array and `a[]` stays a push. Bracket keys combine with both: `a[foo][0].bar`, `a[foo][]`, `a[0][foo]`, `a[foo].bar`.
- **The text in brackets is used as the key as it is**, like qs: `a[b.c]` → key `b.c`, `a[b[c]]` → key `b[c]`. Brackets are matched by nesting. No new error class.
- Bracket keys go through the same `isForbiddenKey` check as dot keys: `a[__proto__]`, `a[constructor]` and `a[toString]` throw `ForbiddenKeyError('a[…]')`. (`a[__proto__[x]]` is the ordinary key `__proto__[x]`.)
- `extractPathParts` is a hand-written scanner instead of a regex (no cast, no `oxlint-disable`): one stack pass to find `[` that no `]` closes, then one scanning loop. It runs in linear time in the path length.
- **Misplaced and unbalanced brackets no longer throw** (`0d0b2d8`, see below).
- Docs: README "Name" and "Object" sections, `parseFormData` JSDoc (`[key]` bullet, example, path description).
- `.size-limit.json`: ESM limit 1 kB → 1.2 kB. Main is 930 B; this PR makes it 1.02 kB (umd.min 1.08 → 1.19 kB of 1.5 kB).

### How brackets are parsed

- A `[` outside brackets starts a bracket part, which ends at the `]` that balances it (nesting like qs). Its text is the key as it is, unless it's an array index (digits) or a push (empty).
- A `[` that no `]` closes stays in the key: its bracket key ends at the last `]` (`a[[0]` → key `[0`, `a[b[c]` → key `b[c`). With no `]` after it, it's part of the key around it (`a[0` → key `a[0`, `x.y[` → key `y[`, `[0` → key `[0`).
- A bracket part after `.` or at the start is a normal part: `[foo]` → `foo`, `a.[b]` → `a.b`, `a[b].[c]` → `a.b.c`.
- Text after `]` is the next key: `a[0]b` → `a[0].b`, `a[b]c[d]` → `a.b.c.d`.
- A `]` that doesn't close a bracket part is part of the key: `a]b`, `0]`, `a[b]]` → `{a: {b: {']': 'v'}}}`.
- Empty keys are skipped as before (`a..b`, `a.`, `.a`).

A broken path now parses the same way whether or not an earlier field already made its parent an object; it only throws on a real type conflict.

## Compatibility with 1.0.1

Checked with a differential fuzz against the published 1.0.1 (random paths built from `a`, `foo`, digits, `.`, `[`, `]`, `[]`, `[foo]`, `[b.c]`, `[b[c]]`, `[.]`, `[.0]`, `[[0].b]`, `__proto__`, `toString`, `\n`).

**Inputs that parse in 1.0.1 and change** (release notes):

1. **Bracket text starting with `.`** 1.0.1 skipped a `.` or `[` right after `[`, so these were array paths. They are now keys. This is the only change to a 1.0.1 result that didn't already contain a broken key:

   | Path | 1.0.1 | now |
   |---|---|---|
   | `a[.]` | `{a: ['v']}` | `{a: {'.': 'v'}}` |
   | `a[.0]`, `a[..0]` | `{a: ['v']}` | `{a: {'.0': 'v'}}`, `{a: {'..0': 'v'}}` |

2. **Results with a stray `]` in a key.** 1.0.1 produced keys like `b]` when it split bracket text into path parts:
   - `a[[0].b]` → `{a: {'[0].b': 'v'}}` (was `{a: [{'b]': 'v'}]}`)
   - several fields, where an earlier one already made `a` an object: `a.x`, `a[foo]` → `{a: {x, foo}}` (was the key `foo]`); `a.x`, `a[b.c]` → key `b.c`; `a.x`, `a[__proto__]` / `a[toString]` → `ForbiddenKeyError` (was the key `__proto__]` / `toString]`); `a.foo`, `a[foo]` → `DuplicateKeyError` (now the same key)

   Over 2M single-field paths, every changed result that didn't contain such a broken key was of the form `x[.]` or `x[.<digits>]`.

3. **Unclosed `[` keeps the `[` in the key** (1.0.1 dropped it). The 1.0.1 results look plausible, so this is the change most likely to be noticed:

   | Path | 1.0.1 | now |
   |---|---|---|
   | `a[[0]`, `a[.[0]` | `{a: ['v']}` | `{a: {'[0': 'v'}}`, `{a: {'.[0': 'v'}}` |
   | `[0` | `{0: 'v'}` | `{'[0': 'v'}` |
   | `x.y[` | `{x: {y: 'v'}}` | `{x: {'y[': 'v'}}` |
   | `a[b][` | `{a: {b: 'v'}}` | `{a: {b: {'[': 'v'}}}` |
   | `a.z`, `a[0` | `{a: {z, 0}}` | `{a: {z}, 'a[0': 'v'}` |

4. **Brackets after `.` or at the start, and text after `]`.** 1.0.1 left a `]` in the key (`[foo]` → `{'foo]': 'v'}`, `a.[b]` → `{a: {'b]': 'v'}}`). They're now normal parts. With an earlier `a.z`, `a[b]]` was the key `b]]` and is now `{b: {']': 'v'}}`. One input that parsed becomes an error: `a.z`, `a[0]b` was the key `0]b` and is now `DuplicateKeyError('a[0]')`, because `a` is an object and `a[0]` needs an array.

**Inputs that threw in 1.0.1 and now parse:** every bracket key, including `a[.b]`, `a[[x]]`, `a[[0]]`, and the misplaced bracket shapes above that threw (`a[0`, `a[0]b`, `a[b]c]`, `a.[0]`, `0]`, …).

## Tests

- `bracket keys` block in `src/__tests__/index.ts`: equivalence with dots, combinations, prefixes, merging, duplicates in both directions, literal keys, keys starting with `.` or `[`, unclosed `[`, bracket parts after `.` or at the start, text after `]`, stray `]`, the same broken path with and without an earlier field, and four 200 000 character paths that must parse in under 500 ms. These fail with the first regex version of this PR (2–4 s) and with a per-`[` bracket scan (17–22 s).
- `does not pollute via a[%s]` now expects `ForbiddenKeyError`, and the `Object.prototype` names table also covers `a[name]` and `a[name].b`.
- `src/__tests__/properties.ts`: the round-trip property picks `.key` or `[key]` per nested key, and a new property checks that `a[key]` with dots in `key` (also at the start) gives that literal key. Checked that both fail when the scanner is broken (parent of a bracket key stays an array, or the key stops at the first `]`).

`npm run validate` passes with 100% coverage.

author: lionelzhaowy
body:
The completion path currently accepts an ID from every context. It does not check whether that context currently enables the source. A disabled context can therefore release the shared gateway and cause a held source to become pending again.

Gate completion with the writing context's current IE bit. Reject zero and out-of-range IDs before indexing IE. Keep enabled cross-context completion legal. Do not add an owner table or change the external PLIC interface. Update the official template, default generated RTL, and vendor patch series.

This follows [PLIC 1.0.0 Interrupt Completion](https://github.com/riscv/riscv-plic-spec/blob/f8ec1b7e9b1a92c34af8e0ab7eb33838813785a3/riscv-plic.adoc#interrupt-completion). Related upstream discussion: [lowRISC/opentitan#31690](https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/issues/31690).

Official validation base: `cd3153de2783abd3d03d0595e6c4b32413c62f14`. The official IP generator produced a 58-source/two-target instance. The same real-module test and locked dependency inputs ran before and after the patch.

| Input | Checks | Original errors | Patched errors |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Disabled-context completion | 745 | 54 | 0 |
| Affected regression | 223045 | 7251 | 0 |

The regression completed 176 vectors at 155.18 us. It includes all 57 legal sources, both contexts, enabled peer completion, disabling after claim, duplicate/invalid IDs, held-level gateways, and resets. It excludes the independent live-claim repair.

VCS W-2024.09-SP1 compiled and elaborated both versions with lint. Final lint categories and counts match the baseline. Complete-module Design Compiler GTECH `compile -no_map` checks passed with 896 flip-flops, zero latches/loops/multiple drivers/unexplained references/post-compile blackboxes. Generic writer and unconstrained-endpoint warnings remain. This is not technology mapping or timing signoff.

Public test, dependency versions, commands, and scope are in `test/PLIC_CONTRACT.md`. Every functional run used a 50 ms HDL deadline and a 90-second wall-clock limit. The complete vendor patch series reproduced the exact modified template from pinned lowRISC source.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex assisted implementation, tests, and validation. A separate AI review checked the patch and actual evidence. This was not a human review.

The public test top is `tb_plic_contract`. Select a listed profile with `+PLIC_PROFILE=<profile>`.

author: bhavyam2468
body:
## Summary

A ground-up polish pass that makes Atrium fully customizable through direct manipulation, in the spirit of token-studio but purpose-built for a launcher. Everything is pure Kotlin, zero new dependencies.

### Typography & immersion
- **Variable fonts** — 4 OFL families bundled (`res/font/`: Inter, Space Grotesk, Fraunces, JetBrains Mono) with live weight axes via `FontVariation`; the clock and the UI can each speak their own type, weight, size and tracking.
- **KWGT-grade clock, zero nerds** — 5 time formats, 9 date formats (incl. hidden), 3 arrangements (stacked both ways, or one line with a choice of separators), uppercase toggle, free 2-D placement — all exposed as touch, never as pattern strings to type.
- **Motion** — staggered intro, focus blur on launch/return, spring-tuned search open/close, keyboard-synchronized insets.

### Design studio (`DesignSheet.kt`)
The launcher mirrored on a card, where **everything is a handle**:
- **Tap** cycles representations (time/date formats, row styles, search bar styles, background mode).
- **Drag** moves the clock on a 3×3 snap grid with magnet haptics and guide rails; drags the clock-pins gap, row spacing, side insets, wallpaper dim.
- **Two fingers** scale size and weight simultaneously on clock, pins, rows, bar, background brightness.
- **Hold** (420 ms) opens a focused option sheet — only the settings relevant to that element, previewed live.
- **Double-tap** resets an element; ⟲ is a two-stage reset-everything.
- Undo/redo (80 steps), preset shuffle, Home ↔ Search mode switch, an Aa chip (tap typeface / drag weight / hold sheet), accent cycler, and a self-narrating chip bar — no manual required.

### Theming engine (`Theme.kt`)
~45 persisted design tokens with coerce-on-read, batch writes, deferred disk writes during gestures, snapshots, and 6 presets. Alignments, anchors, insets, gaps, pins, rows, icon shape/size/monochrome, search bar, accents, text brightness, wallpaper with dim scrim, tinted text — everything is live everywhere.

### Settings that scale (`SettingsModel.kt` / `SettingsUi.kt` / `SettingsColumnView.kt`)
Hub → area → page tree designed for hundreds of options: fuzzy search across titles, descriptions and tags; a "recently adjusted" hub; drag-to-adjust rows with haptic step ticks; option sheets with live previews (typefaces render in their own face, formats show themselves).

### Shared DNA (`HomeComposer.kt`)
Common builders mean the studio replica and the real home screen can never drift apart.

## Notes
- `versionName` 0.2, README rewritten.
- Verified by end-to-end manual review (no JDK/SDK in this environment): brace balance checks, full re-reads of all 13 sources, and a mid-review bug hunt that fixed 8 issues before commit.

author: guillaumelauzier
body:
## Objective

Package 6 of 6 of the Email audit (finding 11). The estimate a member approves describes the exact generation or revision about to run, and the Worker enforces the accepted maximum. Draft, Regenerate and Shorter each show a current estimate for their own operation before they are charged. Changed inputs, sources, settings, model or price need a refreshed estimate instead of silently running a different operation.

Part of #4666

The issue stays open for what this PR does not do (see Risks and `D4666.md`): durable edits and version navigation (#4660), and a live charged run.

## Implementation

**An estimate answers one operation** (`services/mail/draftQuote.ts`).
- **Fingerprint:** a hash of everything the model will be given: the task, the token ceiling and every message (recipient, purpose, tone, length, the ticked sources with their text, the live blocks) and, for a revision, the exact subject and body being revised plus the instruction.
- **Quote:** `estimate: true` now answers `{ hold_microusd, model, kind, quote, expires_at }`. The quote is signed, not stored. It holds the member, the fingerprint, the model, the maximum hold and a 10-minute expiry, so a client cannot raise its maximum or move it to another member or operation.

**A run must bring it** (`routes/mail_drafts.ts`). Before the router reserves anything, the Worker prices the operation as it stands now and accepts the quote only if it is the member's, unexpired, for this fingerprint and model, and no cheaper than the hold the router would reserve now. Otherwise it answers `409 estimate_required` with the reason (`missing`, `invalid`, `expired`, `changed`, `repriced`) and a fresh estimate, and starts no model call, reserves no spend and stores nothing. The charge cannot exceed the accepted maximum, because the hold is checked against it.

**Revising what the member sees.** `POST /drafts/:uid/revise` takes an optional `base: { subject, body }`: the text in the member's editor. The estimate and the run then name that same text, not an older saved draft behind it. Absent, it is the saved draft.

**Other callers.** The MCP tool `mail_draft` runs `runDraft` directly and is unchanged. Only the HTTP routes the composer uses require a quote.

**The page** (`estimateGate.js`, `useOperationEstimate.js`).
- The gate is derived from the operation on screen at render time, so the moment the request or the editor text changes, the old answer is no answer. A late answer for another operation is ignored.
- Draft and Regenerate share the request's estimate. Shorter has its own, of the text in the editor, read after a short pause.
- Each button is shut while its own estimate is loading, unreadable or expired, with a retry. A missing or zero price is unreadable, never free.
- A press sends the quote of its own estimate. A refused run swaps in the fresh estimate, says why, and runs nothing.
- Both surfaces use it: the Email composer (`ComposeSheet`) and the record's Ask (`EmailDraftIntent`).

## Files changed

- `cloudflare-worker/src/services/mail/draftQuote.ts` (new): fingerprint, signed quote, the check.
- `cloudflare-worker/src/routes/mail_drafts.ts`: every press prices the operation; a run needs a valid quote; the revise `base`.
- `frontend/src/pages/email/estimateGate.js` (new), `useOperationEstimate.js` (new): the gate and the hook.
- `frontend/src/pages/email/ComposeSheet.jsx`, `EmailDraftIntent.jsx`, `emailModel.js`; `frontend/src/lib/api/mail.js` (contract comment).
- Tests:
  - new: `mail_drafts_d1341` (4 cases, plus the existing cases now press through an estimate first), `email_estimate_binding_4666.test.mjs` (6);
  - updated: three frontend stubs (`email_ask_4017`, `email_page_d1344`, `messages_retirement_d1345`) now return a quote.
- `documentation/architecture/decisions/D4666.md` (new), `services/mail/README.md`.

## Testing

Each test file was run on its own, so a run's temp databases did not exhaust this container's disk.
- **Worker, all pass:** `mail_drafts_d1341` 14 (4 new), `mail_mcp_tools_d1343` 5, `mail_people_d1348` 8, `mail_accounts_d1340` 10.
- **Frontend, all pass:** `email_estimate_binding_4666` 6, `email_ask_4017` 5, `email_page_d1344` 6, `messages_retirement_d1345` 7, `email_sheet_4017` 6, `eadwyn_composer_d652` 12, `eadwyn_composer_foot` 4.
- **New assertions:**
  - No quote, a forged quote, another recipient setting, other sources, another member and moved source contents each start no run and store nothing.
  - Shorter's estimate differs from the draft's and cannot be swapped.
  - The instruction and the member's base text are part of the operation.
  - The quote verifies only when it is the member's, unexpired, unforged, for this model and no cheaper than the hold.
  - Mounted: Shorter waits for and names the edited text, is shut the moment the text changes, and a late answer for old text never opens it. A refused run takes the fresh estimate. A failed estimate shuts the buttons with a retry. A zero hold is never read as free.
- **Mutations caught (5):** the approval check skipped; the fingerprint not compared; the maximum not enforced; an answer for another operation accepted; Shorter pressable without its estimate.
- **Guards pass:** `tsc` (apart from `src/agents/sdkRuntime.ts`, which needs the uninstalled `agents` package), eslint on the touched frontend files, `check-api-drift`, `check-sql-prepare`, `check-refusal-bodies`, `check-timestamp-comparisons`, `check-folder-docs`, `check-decision-ids`, `check-dark-mode`, `check-unused-imports`, `check-frontend-logging`, `check-secret-logging`, and the auth inventory.
- **Not run here:** the full `npm run test:drift` and the build. CI runs them. No live charged run was made.

## Risks

**Ships:** the Worker and the frontend build. No migration, binding or secret (the quote is signed with the existing `JWT_SECRET`). Roll back by reverting the commit.

- **A draft or revision over HTTP now needs a quote.** The two composer surfaces send it. Any other direct HTTP caller of `POST /api/mail/drafts` or `/revise` would get `409 estimate_required`; I found none in the repo. The MCP tool is unaffected.
- **The router has no per-run ceiling input.** The ceiling is enforced by refusing before the run when the hold it would reserve exceeds the accepted maximum. A price change between that check and the router's own reservation is not closed by this PR.
- **Shorter now makes an extra estimate request** after a pause on each edit. It runs nothing and charges nothing.
- **Shared files.** `ComposeSheet.jsx` is also edited by AxalNetwork/StudioOS#4881 (#4665, the send path); the changes are in different regions. Durable edits and version integrity stay with #4660.
- **Security.** No secret in the diff. The quote carries no content beyond a hash, and no raw text is returned. Mailbox ownership and the support-session refusal are unchanged.

## Dependencies

Part of #4666. Coordinates with #4660 (durable edits and versions) and AxalNetwork/StudioOS#4881 (package 1). Blocks nothing.

body:
## Summary

PR B of the visualization work package: strengthens the `rule-presentation/v1` contract and separates **syntactic validity** from **repository-backed publication eligibility**.

**Stacked PR:** base branch `feat/public-visualizations` (PR A, #23). It must be reviewed/merged first or retargeted to `main` after PR A. This PR does not publish a real reviewed rule.

**Baseline:** `main` at `4a3e7b1`; branch base commit `e792144`; head `37b1c8e`.

## What changed

### Unknown / conditional effective periods

- `effective_period` now accepts `status`: `known`, `unknown`, `conditional`, `retrospective` or `unresolved`.
- Unknown/unresolved periods require `from`/`to` to be null; no date is fabricated.
- Conditional periods require a recorded condition; dates are still ordered.
- The renderer displays unknown/conditional/retrospective labels instead of an empty or invented date.
- Existing synthetic fixture remains valid; it is a known period.

### Partial translations

- Localized objects may omit individual languages; at least one language expression is required.
- The renderer falls back to the first available expression, marks it with `lang`/`dir`, and shows a visible translation-fallback notice.
- It never generates a translation or presents one as official.
- The complete text equivalent may also be partial; at least one language must have one explanation per ladder step, and any present translation must be complete.

### Readable graph labels

- Rule dependency nodes now show a wrapped short label alongside the node ID, with the full label retained in the accessible node list.

### Graph / ladder mappings

The schema now supports `outcomes` and optional `mappings`:

- node-to-step mappings;
- branch true/false targets;
- test expectations.

Validation rejects unknown node/step/outcome references, unmapped nodes, duplicate branches, contradictory true/false targets, unreachable intermediate steps, unknown expected outcomes and duplicate tests. This is a **structural** check; it is not a proof of semantic equivalence and does not replace manual review or engine execution tests.

### Publication gate

`validate_publication(data, root)` is separate from `validate_presentation` and runs only for non-synthetic artifacts. It:

- resolves the policy record, source, provision, legal version and reviewed interpretation in `regions/mena/`;
- requires the research record itself to be reviewed;
- checks the interpretation is resolved with reviewer/date;
- checks the provision references the named source;
- requires an encoding artifact path and verifies its SHA-256 and engine version;
- requires passing test evidence;
- rejects artifact/test paths that escape the repository root.

Synthetic artefacts are explicitly exempt. The gate is **not** legal verification and is **not called by the public build**, because no real reviewed presentation exists.

## Files modified

- `regions/mena/schemas/rule-presentation.schema.json`
- `framework/rule_presentation.py`
- `regions/mena/data/visualizations/synthetic-procurement.json`
- `tests/test_rule_presentation.py`
- `docs/RULE-PRESENTATION.md`
- `docs/VISUALIZATION-MILESTONE.md`
- i18n keys for translation fallback and effective-period statuses
- generated synthetic demo pages

No research record, candidate source, source check, legal-effect status or real instrument changed. No real publication-gate invocation exists in the build.

## Backward compatibility

- Existing known `effective_period` with `from`/`to` remains valid.
- Existing fully translated synthetic fixture remains valid; mappings/outcomes were added to exercise the new checks.
- Existing synthetic authoring does not need a publication artifact path.
- Real reviewed artifacts will need `provenance.artifact_path`, `tests_path` and resolved repository evidence.

## Tests

```text
framework/validate.py                    -> pass
tests/                                   -> 315 tests OK (38 rule-presentation tests)
research-toolkit/tests                   -> 15 OK
registry / instruments / import / manifest -> current (68 files)
build.py                                 -> 154 pages
check_html.py                            -> 154 pages pass
npm run test:a11y                        -> 464 passed
git diff --check                         -> clean
```

New negative tests include unknown effective date, conditional period, partial translation fallback, mapping references/branches/tests, publication gate bypasses, wrong artifact checksum, failed test evidence, unresolved record and wrong source.

## Accessibility

The public synthetic demo is the only rendered rule presentation. Its layout is unchanged except for fallback/period text; the full 464-check Playwright/axe suite passed. Manual screen-reader, real 400% zoom and native Arabic/French review remain outstanding.

## Legal limitations

- Structural validation is not legal verification.
- The publication gate proves repository evidence resolves; it cannot prove the interpretation is legally correct.
- No real reviewed rule is published; all current candidate interpretations remain unresolved.
- No engine execution occurs in the public site.

## Rollback

Revert `c3ccc26` and `37b1c8e`; the PR is stacked on #23 and should not be merged independently. No data migration or legal-record change is involved.

body:
## O que muda

Em «Rever talão», ao editar uma linha (ou a data/total do resumo), o teclado deixava pouco espaço porque a barra de navegação e o rodapé ficavam no ecrã.

- Enquanto uma linha ou o campo de data/total está aberto, a barra de navegação e as ações do rodapé (Confirmar talão, Guardar e rever depois, Eliminar talão) ficam escondidas. A barra «Desfazer» fica.
- Esconde-se pelo estado aberto, não pelo foco: com o foco, tocar em «Guardar» mudava o layout e o toque falhava.
- «Sair sem guardar?» e a pergunta de eliminar continuam a usar o rodapé, para não prender a pessoa.
- A data em falta que abre sozinha não esconde o rodapé; «Nome da loja» também não.
- «Dividir linha» e «Remover linha» aparecem logo no painel, sem «Mais opções». Os campos de «Mais opções» continuam recolhidos.
- `useHideNav(active = true)`: as chamadas existentes não mudam.

## Fora de âmbito

Editar um talão já confirmado: o backend recusa (409 `invalid_state`) e o Douglas já foi avisado.

## Consequências

- Com a barra escondida, no computador a grelha lateral some e a página salta à esquerda (como nos ecrãs inteiros).
- Depois de «Adicionar linha» é preciso «Guardar» ou «Cancelar» no painel antes de usar o rodapé.

## Verificação

- lint, typecheck e Vitest (614) passam.
- e2e mock: 190/190 antes do `/simplify`; os 12 testes do ecrã de revisão repetidos no código final.
- `e2e/stack/journey.spec.ts` foi ajustado mas não foi corrido (precisa da stack completa).

body:
## Was
Beim Ziehen einer Figur lief der Weg über brennende Felder, obwohl es einen gleich teuren Weg ohne Feuer gab. `reachable()` (`src/core/rules/movement.ts`) zählt jetzt je Knoten die betretenen Gefahrenfelder (`hazard`, `isHazard` = Terrain `burning`, das einzige Feld, das beim Betreten schadet). Bei gleichen Bewegungskosten gewinnt der Weg mit weniger Gefahrenfeldern.

- Reichweite, erreichbare Felder und Kosten bleiben unverändert. Ist der Weg durchs Feuer kürzer, bleibt es bei ihm.
- Vorschau (`pathTo(reachNow(...))`) und Bewegung (`doMove` → `reachable`/`pathTo`, bzw. der mitgeschickte Pfad auf Nebelkarten) nutzen dieselbe Funktion, zeigen also denselben Weg.

## KI und Replays
Die KI nutzt dieselbe Suche, meidet Feuer bei Gleichstand also auch. Ihre Entscheidungen bleiben trotzdem gleich: Die Sortierung der offenen Liste lässt `hazard` bewusst weg, die Felder werden in derselben Reihenfolge gefunden wie vorher (die KI löst eigene Gleichstände über diese Reihenfolge), und ein später gefundener Weg mit weniger Feuer wird neu eingereiht. Ein erster Entwurf mit `hazard` in der Sortierung hatte die Sim-Werte leicht verschoben, deshalb diese Lösung.

Geändert wird nur der gelaufene Pfad, also der Pfad im `moved`-Event, der Animation und Sichtbarkeit im Nebel steuert. Der Spielzustand bleibt gleich: Feuerschaden, Beute und Trigger hängen nur am Zielfeld.

- `pnpm sim --campaign act1 --runs 50`: Ausgabe identisch zu `main`, abgesehen von der Laufzeit.
- Keine Replay-Fixtures oder Sim-Erwartungen betroffen. Alle bestehenden Tests sind unverändert grün.

## Tests
`tests/unit/path-hazard.test.ts`: zwei gleich teure Wege, Feuer auf jeweils einem (beide Richtungen), damit wird der Weg ohne Feuer gewählt, und die Bewegung läuft denselben Weg wie die Vorschau. Ist nur der Weg durchs Feuer kürzer, wird er genommen. Erreichbare Felder und Kosten sind mit und ohne Feuer gleich.

`pnpm check` grün (1592 Tests).

body:
Baseline Profile の生成と起動時間の計測を、公式の Baseline Profile Gradle プラグイン（`androidx.baselineprofile` 1.5.0）の手順に合わせます。

これまでは独自の build type（`minified`・`nonMinified`）とコピー用のタスク（`copyBaselineProfile`）で生成していました。公式の手順と違うため、初めて触る人には分かりにくい状態でした。

## 変更点

- `app` にプラグインを適用し、`:benchmark` を生成側にしました。生成は `./gradlew :app:generateBaselineProfile` で行います（API 33 以上の端末かエミュレータが必要です）
- 生成したプロファイルは `app/src/release/generated/baselineProfiles/` に置き、リポジトリで管理します。ビルドのたびには生成しません（`automaticGenerationDuringBuild = false`）。再現可能なビルドを保つためです
- 独自の build type をやめ、プラグインが作る `benchmarkRelease`（R8 あり・debug 鍵で署名）と `nonMinifiedRelease`（R8 なし）を使います。`:release-test` と起動時間の計測は `benchmarkRelease` が対象です
- プロファイルを API 37 のエミュレータで生成し直しました
- CONTRIBUTING・AGENTS.md・`docs/`・CI の計器テストのジョブを、新しい手順に合わせて更新しました

## 確認したこと

- `./gradlew --no-build-cache clean check :app:assembleDebug :app:assembleRelease assembleAndroidTest`（単体テスト 779 件）
- `:release-test:assembleBenchmarkRelease :benchmark:assembleBenchmarkRelease :benchmark:assembleNonMinifiedRelease`
- 計器テスト（API 26・37 のエミュレータ）: app 18 件・data 9 件・release-test 3 件
- `:app:generateBaselineProfile`（API 37）
- release の APK に `assets/dexopt/baseline.prof` が含まれること
- 起動時間の計測（`:benchmark:connectedBenchmarkReleaseAndroidTest`、API 26・37）

## 参考

body: ## Summary Two Hermes chat features: - **Context & usage**, from a Hermes chat's overflow menu: how full the model's context window is, what fills it, the chat's token, cache and cost totals, the plan's allowances, and **Compact now**. - **Error cards:** a failed Hermes turn shows a card that says what broke, whether the chat is blocked or can go on, when a limit resets, and offers one fix. Stacked on #966 (#965 → #966 → this). ## What changes - **Context & usage sheet:** - Context window used / total and percent, and what fills it (system prompt, tools, subagents, conversation); the chat's token, cache and cost totals; the plan's allowances: per-window gauges with reset times, the account's plan and top-up balances, a rate limit, and how much the chat's model draws on the plan. - Compact now summarizes older messages on the server, optionally keeping a topic in focus, shows request size and message count before and after when Hermes reports them, and reloads the transcript. When Hermes declines (the summary would be longer), the sheet says the chat was kept as it is. - Desktop Gateway (legacy wire) reads `session.usage`, `session.context_breakdown`, `usage.bars` and the current provider's `model.options` row, and compacts with `session.compress`. A gateway's Webapp listener reads `session.stats` and compacts with a fenced `session.mutate compress`; it reports before/after only in a summary line, which is read for the numbers. The last turn's usage fills in a window the reads don't report. API server chats show the session's token and cost totals; they have no context window or Compact. - **Error cards:** - What broke (the provider, its credentials, credits, a plan or rate limit, a chat too long for the model, a cut-off reply, the chat's working folder, Hermes itself…), blocked vs. degraded, reset time, failing provider and model, and Hermes' own sentence. - One action, chosen the way Hermes Desktop chooses its main fix and second option, keeping the first Conduit can do: Retry, Continue a cut-off reply, Compact (opens Context & usage), Switch to the model a plan still serves and retry, Use credits, Open the provider's settings or billing page, or New chat. A send that may already be queued offers nothing, so it can't run twice. - Desktop Gateway turns read `message.complete`'s `error_surface`, `billing` and `partial` on both wires; a classified failure's copy is no longer shown as the answer unless Hermes marks it partial. API server refusals map where they fit (deleted session, conflicting or draining request, too many requests with Retry-After); other failures keep their text, and a later error without a card drops the old one. - New strings in all 14 languages. ## Testing - Against a local Hermes v0.23.0 (synthetic data, stub model), through Conduit's real service: on the dashboard, window, breakdown, totals, `usage.bars` and `model.options` read correctly; Compact on a 3-turn chat is declined and shown as kept; on a 16-turn chat it goes from 34 to 12 messages and the chat reloads. On a Webapp listener the same through `session.stats` and the fenced compress. On the API server, session token and cost totals show (the API server updates them only for `/v1/runs` turns). - Error cards, against a separate isolated Hermes whose stub model fails on purpose: 401 gives a blocking auth card with Retry and the provider and model; 429 a degraded card with Retry and a reset time; a context overflow (with automatic compression off) a blocking card with Compact. - New tests: 54 core and 17 widget; related suites pass. `dart analyze` (core), `flutter analyze` (touched files) and the platform UI lint are clean; Polish localization test passes. - Not done: no simulator or device run. > [!NOTE] > ### Add Hermes error cards and the Context & usage sheet > - Adds `HermesErrorCard` in [hermes_error_card.dart](https://github.com/cogwheel0/conduit/pull/967/files#diff-4be270b1c45e9280336fe3a02f20d41929a7d21a9a8eec61327283077322fccd). Assistant messages with a classified Hermes error render this card instead of the plain banner; the card offers actions like retry, continue, compact, model switch, use credits, and new chat, filtered by service type and conversation state. > - Adds the `HermesContextUsageSheet` in [hermes_context_usage_sheet.dart](https://github.com/cogwheel0/conduit/pull/967/files#diff-38ae8b385b3359f1a5514d1bc0c5d390dddb5087d4011c540c0e12a74e9f9e31), opened from the chat overflow menu for native Hermes conversations. It shows context-window contents, token and cost totals, plan allowances, and a Compact action that requests desktop session compaction with a focus topic. > - Adds the `HermesErrorSurface` model in [hermes_error_surface.dart](https://github.com/cogwheel0/conduit/pull/967/files#diff-427bc1737dd59d88105e420284779e0a3c6612be1792306d7bf9ba7c886dadc7) and the `HermesContextReport` model in [hermes_context_usage.dart](https://github.com/cogwheel0/conduit/pull/967/files#diff-baa19026dc1ba8ad3704911645438b018a0d1b8ed0861b1be7b485c8650c3a77). Both parse and validate gateway data with bounded sizes, and derive error kinds, severity, and recovery actions. > - Extends `HermesDesktopApiService` in [hermes_desktop_api_service.dart](https://github.com/cogwheel0/conduit/pull/967/files#diff-134a50cb3ede1fa214a6e2a73d12d69210aa0aada9f9ebd5cd376e290999e011) with context-report, compaction, and keep-going-on-credits methods, including pending-compaction tracking with a 15-minute deadline. > - Updates all 14 localization `.arb` files with strings for the new UI. > - Behavioral Change: desktop turn runtime no longer emits non-partial failure text as final output; it is reported as an error with a surface. `hermesDesktopTranscriptChangesProvider` now emits `HermesTranscriptChange` wrapper objects instead of bare ID strings. > > > > Macroscope summarized 7c14efa. > >

author: seo-rii
body:
### Description

Adds **WireGuard proxy (experimental)** for YouTube and YouTube Music through the existing Network proxy hooks, preserving the working app-local transport.

Users import a supported WireGuard `.conf`, explicitly enable routing and restart. Intercepted requests use an authenticated loopback proxy backed by `wireguard-go` and a userspace TCP/IP stack. Each app keeps an AndroidKeyStore-encrypted profile. Both patches are default-selected in JVM and Android DEX metadata; **routing remains off by default**.

The shared settings now reuse Morphe themes, toolbar and preference rows. Profile errors distinguish file access/text, unsupported configuration, native loading and secure storage; only fixed, sanitized native validation reasons are displayed. The parser accepts case-insensitive `PersistentKeepalive = off` and bare numeric `Address`/`AllowedIPs` as single-host routes.

### Scope and maintenance

This remains a draft test PR in my personal fork before an official upstream submission. The separate custom-distribution backport retains its v2.1.0 base and is not merged into this dev-based PR.

Supported scope: `arm64-v8a`/`x86_64`, ordinary APK installation, one peer, numeric endpoints and explicitly covered DNS. It does not require Android `VpnService`, root or a separate WireGuard app. Intercepted requests have no direct fallback on failure. **Only hooked requests are covered; this is not a system-wide VPN or complete kill switch.**

The contribution includes the Music Requester routing prerequisite, pinned Go/NDK source builds, dependency notices and CI/bundle checks. The shared transport and dependency module pins are preserved. Dependency advisories and same-app multiprocess-storage limitations remain documented.

[Design](https://github.com/seo-rii/morphe-patches/blob/feat/wireguard-upstream/docs/wireguard/design.md) · [Security and dependencies](https://github.com/seo-rii/morphe-patches/blob/feat/wireguard-upstream/docs/wireguard/security.md) · [Validation record](https://github.com/seo-rii/morphe-patches/blob/f5a31ba865b0f548993da585df94849c9ac5dcc6/docs/wireguard/validation.md)

Related context: [MorpheApp #2827](https://github.com/MorpheApp/morphe-patches/issues/2827) concerns SOCKS5/proxy expansion. This contribution does not implement SOCKS5 or close that request.

### Current verification

- [Fork CI](https://github.com/seo-rii/morphe-patches/actions/runs/42475845801) **passed** at `f5a31ba865b0f548993da585df94849c9ac5dcc6`.
- Local full source build: 1,481 Java/Kotlin cases, 1,476 passed and 5 existing Jam APK-dependent skips; no failures/errors. The total includes 24 new import-workflow boundary cases.
- Go race/vet: 26 top-level tests; host JNI: 42 checks; Python verification tools: 33 tests. Standard-syntax regressions failed before the parser fix. These checks use public synthetic inputs, not personal profiles.
- Both native ABIs, JVM/Android default flags, exact JNI signatures and exception constructor, resources and dependency notices passed inspection. The real Morphe loader found 203 patches and both app-specific WireGuard dependencies.

Final local source-built bundle SHA-256: `58c1728705754ff117aac037addbf420ee887fa4b1101731a51ac1e0242f8675`.

| Target | WireGuard-focused | Complete defaults |
| --- | --- | --- |
| YouTube 21.30.216 | `--validate` and final APK inspection passed | Passed |
| Music 9.30.53 | `--validate` and final APK inspection passed | Passed |

The signed originals were verified against existing Google signer allowlists. Universal YouTube used an explicitly labeled unsigned arm64-only fixture with retained content verified against the original; Music used its original arm64 APK. No compatibility force flag was used. All four patched outputs were unsigned host-validation artifacts.

The validation record preserves earlier artifact cohorts, including the older YouTube 20.51.39 default-selection Captions ambiguity reproduced with WireGuard disabled. Earlier minimum/experimental cases were not rerun for this new bundle.

### Still unverified

Actual Android target-app UI/picker/import and AndroidKeyStore integration, server handshake, playback, DNS/leak behavior, network transitions and concurrent app/process behavior remain unverified for this artifact. The reporting user's import error has not been reproduced on their device. The maintainer's successful v2.1.1 device use is a separate historical report. Earlier Android shell-JNI checks do not establish target-app acceptance.

author: meywd
body:
`load-small` now compares the relay with its base commit **on the same runner**. Main's `load-small` has been red since #808, and #832 failed it at +34.6 %. Neither is a relay regression; this fixes the gate.

## What the evidence says

#808 replaced sampled `docker stats` CPU with the relay containers' cgroup CPU time, the median of five rounds. Within a run that is steady: each run's rounds agree within about 1 %. But it still compared against **main's last run**, and another run is another machine. The same relay code measured, CPU-seconds per Mbit (median of 5 rounds):

| run | commit | figure |
|---|---|---|
| main | `2917a4967` (#808 merged) | 0.000875 |
| main | `ec0dfe5ce` | 0.000451 |
| main | `6be172b2d` | 0.000610 (failed vs 0.000451) |
| main | `d97ee875e` | 0.000634 (failed vs 0.000451) |
| #808 | `f38ed69cc` | 0.000604 |
| #832 | `e6d031799` | 0.000607 (failed vs 0.000451) |

That is a 1.9× spread on code that doesn't change between those runs. The figure depends on the CPU the job lands on. My earlier local experiment (#808: main's and the PR's relay alternating on one machine) agreed within 1 %, because it was one machine.

## The fix

- **Same machine.** The `load-small` job builds the base commit's relay image: the pull request's `base.sha`, or `github.event.before` on a push (the previous commit if there is none). It runs `load-small` with that relay, then with this commit's, on the same runner. Both use this commit's scenario code, with 3 one-minute rounds each. It then compares the two. The 20 % threshold is unchanged.
- **Fails closed.** A base relay that can't run this commit's cluster fails the job. So does a missing baseline: `maktaba-loadtest compare` now errors instead of treating it as "the first run".
- **Removed:** the download of main's artifact baseline, and the `actions: read` permission it needed.
- **Docs:** `docs/cloud-sizing.md` now explains both lessons (sampling, and another run is another machine), plus `docs/cloud-rehearsal.md` C12 and the contributor guide in en and ar.

## Tests

- `TestCompareFailsClosed`: a missing baseline errors, 25 % worse fails, 10 % passes.
- `actionlint` is clean.
- This PR's own cloud rehearsal runs the new `load-small` steps; the description will be updated with its two figures.

author: daetojecactus
body:
Closes #73

## What changed
`pnpm preview` now shows what the action engine made of the day: the main action of every line and, on request, why it was chosen. It still only reads GitLab and sends nothing.

- **The main action under every line:** an issue with its merge requests, a merge request without an issue, a push without a merge request. Preview loads the trait index for the role of the employee (`TraitService.loadIndex`) and classifies the day with `ActivityService`. The line shows the action, the state and the details, for example `main: merged · tested, after_approval, closes`. A task that is kept out of the report is marked `excluded from the report`.
- **`--trace`** (`pnpm preview <username> <date> --trace`) also prints for every line:
  - why the main action won (the only one, a higher tier, a higher weight, a later time);
  - every candidate with its tier and weight with the role bonus;
  - the parts a composite absorbed (`← code`);
  - the own facts that the accuracy rules dropped, with the rule.
  Unknown flags print the usage.
- **`PreviewRenderer`:** printing the day moved out of `PreviewService` into its own class, so it is tested without the database and GitLab. `PreviewModule` imports `TraitModule` and `ReportModule`.

## How it was checked

author: claudio-michel[bot]
body: ## Why The model proxy gave a capped Claude Code run's wrap-up note to the first paid request on the session's model once the note was due. With no small model set (serve sets none), Claude Code sends its title and summary calls on the session's model too, so such a call could take the note. The note was then counted as told, and the turn's own request went without it, so the model never saw it. ## What - **Only the turn's own request takes the note** (`@parcha/agentrun-kernel`, `run-adapters/src/host/proxy.ts`). The proxy asks for the note only for a request its policy counts as the turn's answer request (`ProviderPolicy.answers`), the same test it already uses for a content-filter stop. On Claude Code that is `anthropicAnswers`: does the body offer one of the session's own tools? A side call goes as its client sent it, and the note waits for the turn's request. - **A session's remote MCP tools count as its tools** (f023f2445). `anthropicAnswers` takes the session's `mcpTools` beside its own and built-in tools, as the policy's own allow-list does, so in a session whose only tools are a remote MCP server's the title call takes no note and the turn's request does. The same classifier gates the proxy's content-filter stop (`answering`, `proxy.ts:713`, read at `:740`). An MCP-only session's side call that hits the provider's content filter is now left to the client, instead of ending the turn. - **A session with no tools counts every request as the turn's.** It offers nothing to tell its requests apart by, so `anthropicAnswers` returns true for each of them, and its turn request always takes the note: a run is never left untold. In serve's non-interactive mode the CLI makes no title or summary call (`turn-requests.test.mjs` pins one main-model request per turn), so no title call can take the note there. For interactive use, see the follow-up. - Codex's policy has no `answers`, so every Codex request still counts as the turn's. OpenCode turns its title and summary agents off, so it makes no side request. - The Codex-shaped test script's words now give Codex's least by effort: 1,024 tokens for the answer plus 8,192 of reasoning at medium (9,216 in all), or 16,384 at high (17,408). The script's 10,240 was called "high". Upgrading: nothing to do; a side request no longer takes the wrap-up note. ## Prior art - OpenCode sends a session's title as a request of its own, apart from the turn's (`context.request.title`), and books its usage under `source: "title"`, never as the turn's: [packages/core/src/session/title.ts#L67-L72](https://github.com/sst/opencode/blob/fdce6365bcdf2af0fdac65d46dc1806a75d10b02/packages/core/src/session/title.ts#L67-L72). ## Evidence - **Red** (4896ebf97, test only): `wrapup-note.test.mjs`, "a title or summary call on the session's own model … takes no note". The real `anthropicPolicy` (no small model, one session tool) runs behind `startModelProxy` with a recording provider. The CLI's title call (session model, a short prompt, no tools) is sent first, then the turn's request. On main, the title call carries the note and the turn's request does not: `+ actual - expected` gives `[true, false]` against `[false, true]`. - **Fix** (c720b796d): the note gate in the proxy adds `policy.answers ? policy.answers(body) : true`. - The real pinned CLI, driven with no small model, makes one main-model request per turn and no title or summary call (`turn-requests.test.mjs`, on main). So in serve's non-interactive mode the fix guards against a later CLI version that starts making such calls. ## Gate | Tests | Pass | Fail | |---|---|---| | run-adapters-claude-agent: claude | 9 | 0 | | run-adapters: adapters | 331 | 0 | | serve: serve-cap-before | 10 | 0 | | serve: serve-cap-expected-run | 4 | 0 | | serve: serve-cap-wrapup-run | 23 | 0 | | serve: serve-cap-wrapup | 7 | 0 | | serve: serve-opencode-wrapup-note | 1 | 0 | | serve: serve-cap-raise | 32 | 0 | | serve: serve-cap-raise-cent | 4 | 0 | | serve: serve-cap-pause | 2 | 0 | | serve: serve-harness-booking | 9 | 0 | | serve: serve-harness-cap | 2 | 0 | | serve: serve-spend-cap | 10 | 0 | | serve: serve-spend-cap-clamp | 8 | 0 | | serve: serve-cap-unknown | 48 | 0 | | serve: serve-booking-pi | 20 | 0 | | serve: serve-harness-slow-root | 14 | 0 | | serve: serve-harness-multi-tool | 6 | 0 | | serve: serve-capacity | 19 | 0 | The root build, the generated checks, export-source and typecheck pass. ## Test plan - [x] `wrapup-note.test.mjs`: the title call takes no note and the turn's request does (new; red at 4896ebf97) - [x] `wrapup-note.test.mjs`: a session with no tools, `answers` true for its turn request, which carries the note (new pin) - [x] `wrapup-note.test.mjs`, "through the proxy, a turn's first request ([user, system]) is admitted at its bound with the note in it": its body now offers the session's tool (test data only). It had none, through a policy whose session has one. The real CLI offers the session's tools on every turn request, turn-start included. A probe of the pinned CLI's request bodies (two turns per session, no small model, the same scripted provider as `turn-requests.test.mjs`) is the source of that fact: a tool session's two turn requests both offer `mcp__hands__lookup`, and a tool-less session's offer `[]`. So without the tool, the gate rightly read that body as a side call. - [x] `wrapup-note.test.mjs`, "a session whose only tools are a remote MCP server's tells its requests apart by them": with `mcpTools` only, `anthropicAnswers` counts a body offering the remote tool as the turn's and a body offering none as a side call (new; red at 6976996b7, "a body offering no tool is a side call") - [x] `wrapup-note.test.mjs`, "a session whose only tools are a remote MCP server's: its title call takes no note, and the turn's request, which offers the remote tool, takes it": through the proxy (new; red at 6976996b7, the title call carried the note) - [x] `turn-requests.test.mjs` (real CLI), `proxy-note.test.mjs` and the serve wrap-up and cap files, unchanged and passing - [ ] CI 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

Theme defects found by rendering the app windows offscreen in the dark and light themes.

Version 2026.11.07.0128 with a CHANGELOG entry. The release is not tagged yet. It needs the steps in RELEASING.md, including the Graph audit.

Pester ran on a lab machine: 17 passed, 0 failed (the new tests plus the button and XAML tests). Before the fixes, the new tests gave 7 passed and 9 failed. The Workbench, Installer Drop dialog and main window were rendered offscreen in both themes and checked by eye. No window ran on the dev PC.

author: alballaa
body:
## What

1. **Open handlers check the real file and its type.** `hub:open-file`, `hub:open-order-file` and `hub:open-product-doc` now go through `SafeFilePath.realFileWithin` with a new `ATTACHMENT_EXTS` allowlist (documents, pictures, print files, zip). An executable or script (`.exe .bat .cmd .ps1 .hta .lnk .js .vbs .command .app .desktop …`) in those folders is no longer handed to `shell.openPath`.
   - **Receipts:** the paperclip never opened a receipt picked outside userData/temp. Receipts are now copied into `userData/receipts/` (new `hub:pick-receipt`; `hub:read-receipt-qr` copies the picture on success) and stored as `receipts/<name>`, relative to userData, so the book does not carry the Windows user folder. `hub:open-file` resolves relative paths against userData. Old absolute receipt paths fall back to `hub:open-path` (Documents/Downloads/Desktop, pictures/PDF only).
2. **Electron fuses** via `build.electronFuses` (electron-builder 26.15.3 supports it natively, flips after afterPack and before signing). Bed Ready spreads `build`, so it gets them too, and its flavor afterPack is untouched. Set: RunAsNode off, NODE_OPTIONS off, embedded asar integrity on, only-load-from-asar on, cookie encryption on, `resetAdHocDarwinSignature`. **EnableNodeCliInspectArguments stays on**: `scripts/verify-release.mjs` (the release launch gate) uses Playwright `electron.launch`, which always passes `--inspect=0`, so turning it off would fail every release. Verified with a local `--dir --mac --arm64` pack: the fuses read back as set, `ElectronAsarIntegrity` is in Info.plist, and `verify-release.mjs --app` passes against the fused build.
3. **Restore no longer sends decrypted secrets to the renderer.** New `restoreSnapshotToDisk` (lib/store-io.js) writes the restored store on the main side: it refuses non-Khayt files, normalises, keeps machine-local slicer settings, puts back the current secret only where the backup holds the mask, keeps main-owned keys, applies the API-token role guard, and encrypts. It returns the masked copy. The window's follow-up save then merges its masks against the backup's own secrets. Used by restore-backup, restore points and off-site restore.
   - **Also fixes a live bug:** all three handlers called `decryptStoreSecrets`, which main.js stopped importing when store-io.js was extracted (May). Every restore threw a ReferenceError and showed "restore failed".
4. **Legacy `settings.sallaWebhookSecret` / `zidWebhookSecret`** (plaintext, not on the secret list) are deleted once `lanApi` holds a value, in both `migrateLanApiSecrets` and the renderer's `migrateLanApiSettings`.

## Tests
- New: `test/restore-keeps-the-backups-secrets.test.js` (9), `test/electron-fuses.test.js` (5), 3 new cases in `test/safe-file-path.test.js`. Also a restore step in `scripts/e2e-smoke.mjs`: a real IPC restore, the reply is masked, the backup's secret is decrypted from disk, and it survives the window's save.
- `npm run lint`, `npm run check:globals`, 99 related test files (988 pass; the only failure is the known local `receipt-qr-desktop`, where `jsqr` is missing), `node scripts/e2e-smoke.mjs` ok.

author: desure85
body:
## Что и почему

SC-02c: `tasks_list` и `knowledge_list` читают страницу из SQLite-индекса (запись в #297, каркас в #296). Файлы остаются источником истины.

- Индексный путь только для проекта, признанного полным: `projects.synced_at` и `meta.dirty = 0` и число строк равно `projects.file_count`. Иначе (пустой индекс, dirty, `STORAGE_INDEX=off`, ошибка) прежний файловый путь без изменений.
- Наполнение: при первом обращении к неполному проекту фоновый `fillProject` (один промис на проект, пачками по 2000, запрос не ждёт, старт не блокируется; форма как у `warmup.ts`).
- `file_count` поддерживается инкрементально в транзакциях upsert/delete (иначе после любой записи проект выпадал бы из индекса).
- Фильтры status/tag/priority/parentId/type/updatedSince, `countOnly`, точный `total` (`totalExact: true`, намеренное изменение контракта, закреплено тестом), курсор SC-01 совместим в обе стороны, самолечение строк страницы по mtime, частичные индексы для count (схема v2: старый индекс пересоздаётся пустым и наполняется заново).
- Запись решения: `docs/dev-cycle/decisions/2026-11-07-1830-sc-02c.md`.

## Проверено мной

- `build`, `test:types`, `lint:md`, `backlog:check`; индексные тесты 45/45 (scale-index 23, metadata-index 9, write 13) под Node 24.
- ПОПРАВКА (после merge): моя проба эквивалентности на копии /data («16 сравнений, различий 0») была пустой: скрипт читал не то поле ответа (`items` вместо `data`) и сравнивал пустые списки, поэтому в этом PR она ничего не доказывала. Корректная проба после merge (постранично, с фильтрами, на копиях данных и на живом ядре) показала расхождение, причина в СТАРОМ дефекте файлового пути SC-01 (курсор при содержательном фильтре), а не в индексе: индексный путь отдаёт все 209 активных задач `pending` проекта mcp, файловый только 145-150. Отдельная задача заведена.
- Нашла пробел при приёмке: `file_count` не менялся при create, проект выпадал из индекса и наполнялся заново после каждой записи. Исполнитель исправил (инкремент), повторная проба: после create `file_count` 462→463, `synced_at` не меняется, наполнение не перезапускается.
- Мои мутации: убрала `+1` при вставке документа → RED (`expected 3 to be 4`); убрала `−1` при удалении документа → RED; откат → 23/23.

## По отчёту исполнителя (не перепроверено)

Полный `npm test` 281 файл / 3273 теста; остальные мутации revert-check (гейт, фильтры, курсор, самолечение, dirty, частичный индекс); замер на синтетике 100k: `tasks_list` 1176 → 16 мс, `knowledge_list` 1232 → 21 мс, ответ ~32 КБ (порог < 300 мс и < 1 МиБ выполнен); после 300 записей между чтениями 15 мс, наполнение не перезапускалось; наполнение 200k строк за 35 с, БД 143 МБ.

## Ограничения (известны)

- Файл, добавленный в обход сервера, гейтом не виден: сверка с каталогом на каждом чтении была бы той же O(N). Зона SC-02d (`doctor`, `reindex --verify`).
- После неудачной записи в индекс (`dirty=1`) проект читается файлами до `rebuild()`/`reindex` (SC-02d).
- После merge на живом ядре индекс заполнится по проектам при первых обращениях (фон), до этого чтения идут файловым путём. Откат: `STORAGE_INDEX=off`.
- Не проверено: два процесса на одном `DATA_DIR`; legacy-раскладка на 100k не бенчмаркалась (покрыта тестами).

author: vytor-oliveira
body:
Closes #15

Reportado por @anndrelzz.

## O que mudou

- **Uma transação só.** O claim do status e todos os decrementos entram no
  mesmo `prisma.$transaction`: ou tudo vale, ou nada vale. A compensação
  manual no `catch` deixou de existir, porque não há mais o que desfazer.
- **Repositórios participam da transação de quem chama.** `updateStatus` e
  `decrementStock` aceitam um `TransactionClient` opcional, com o `prisma`
  de sempre como padrão. A leitura pós-claim usa o mesmo cliente — ler pelo
  de fora enxergaria o estado de antes das escritas não commitadas.
- **Alerta de estoque mínimo depois do commit.** Saiu de dentro do
  `decrementStock` e virou `notifyLowStock`. Dentro da transação o decremento
  ainda pode voltar atrás, e avisar sobre estoque desfeito é alarme falso.
