_Requested by **Daniel** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01SsqKtLk4Va9P3DsUSWyDXu?thread=cmsg_01SsqKtLk4Va9P3DsUSWyDXuMpLFD7f2jVA8uTcNDTorFc)_

## Why

`GET /setup` makes about 22 queries, and the API has 5 database connections, so every re-read queued the page's own reads behind it. The app re-read Setup in several places:

- on each navigation while Ahoy was not ready,
- on opening Team settings or its Setup section,
- after a change to My Copilot token.

Daniel asked for it to be read only when the app starts, and nothing more.

## What changes

- `App` reads Setup once, when the person is let in. The navigation re-read is gone.
- The Setup section and Team settings no longer read it on opening.
- `CopilotTokenStore` no longer reads it after a save, removal or test. Instead it updates the token's step from its own answer (`copilotSetupStep`, worded like ahoy-hosted's `copilotStep`), so the Team settings label matches the page.
- The Setup section's **Check again** and **Try again** are the only other reads.
- The banner and the section therefore show the start's answer until a reload or one of those presses.

## Checks

`npm run build`, `typecheck`, `lint`, `test` (218 files, 3765 tests) and `format` all pass. They ran on Node 22.23.4 rather than 24, with `@acme-fedev/auth` stubbed in `node_modules` because the private registry cannot be reached from the cloud session. Nothing was run in a browser.

A code review was run, and its findings are fixed in 0e55c20. Two findings were left as asked: a fix made in another section, or a failed start read, shows only after a reload or Check again.

This pairs with ahoy-hosted's `perf/fewer-db-round-trips` but needs nothing from it.

body: ## Summary BSC patron tiers reuse the existing `PatronTier1` / `PatronTier2` / `PatronTier3` bits and the perk-tier checks those bits already feed. The definitions live in `src/lib/bsc/patronTiers.ts`. Early Supporter bit 199 is unchanged. | Tier | Price | Bit | What you get | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Pup | $3 | PatronTier1 | 🐾 on the name, +10% of the 30 minute base trip length | | Good Boy | $7 | PatronTier2 | Pup benefits, +20% trip length, the Good Boy bank background, daily cooldown at 75%, monthly cosmetic box | | Top Dog | $15 | PatronTier3 | Good Boy benefits, custom bank background color, 🐶 cosmetic pet, the Top Dog Discord role for early access | No tier grants coins, tradeable items, XP lamps, or drop-rate boosts. The monthly box is a cosmetic mark (🎀), not loot. The dog is an emoji on the name, not an item. ### How tiers are assigned 1. Discord roles. Set `PATRON_ROLE_PUP`, `PATRON_ROLE_GOODBOY`, `PATRON_ROLE_TOPDOG`, and `SUPPORT_SERVER_ID`. Member updates and an hourly sync set or clear the matching bit. The highest role wins. If the role envs are unset, the sync does not wipe anyone. 2. Owner override. `/admin patron` is owner-only. `manual` defaults to true, and role sync skips that player until `manual:false`. 3. Optional Patreon API v2. If `PATREON_CREATOR_TOKEN` and `PATREON_CAMPAIGN_ID` are set, the hourly sync also reads active patrons and maps `PATREON_TIER_*_ID` through the member's linked Discord id. Manual overrides still win. The old campaign fetch shape is the model. It does not call the old oldschoolgg or GitHub sponsor sync. The old robochimp `patreonTask.run()` and the GitHub sponsor webhook no longer grant tiers. Setup steps are in `docs/RELEASE.md`. This branch sits on the playtest release branch. ## Env vars ``` SUPPORT_SERVER_ID= PATRON_ROLE_PUP= PATRON_ROLE_GOODBOY= PATRON_ROLE_TOPDOG= PATREON_CREATOR_TOKEN= PATREON_CAMPAIGN_ID= PATREON_TIER_PUP_ID= PATREON_TIER_GOODBOY_ID= PATREON_TIER_TOPDOG_ID= ``` The public page is still `PATREON_URL` (default `https://patreon.com/bscbot`). Enable the Server Members intent in the Discord developer portal so member updates arrive. ## QC Create the three Patreon tiers, connect each one to a Discord role with Patreon's Discord integration, put the role ids in the env, and restart the bot. ``` /admin patron user:@Player tier:1 ``` Owner only. The player gets the Pup bit, 🐾, and a longer max trip. A later role sync does not remove it. ``` /admin patron user:@Player tier:2 ``` Daily cooldown is 75% of normal. `/bank` backgrounds include Good Boy. ``` /claim name:Supporter cosmetic ``` Good Boy or Top Dog only. The reply is a cosmetic mark and no items. A second claim in the same month is refused. ``` /admin patron user:@Player tier:3 ``` The name shows 🐶. Custom bank color works: ``` /config user bg_color color:#4e42f5 ``` A player without Top Dog is refused. ``` /admin patron user:@Player tier:0 ``` Clears the patron bits and keeps the manual lock. ``` /admin patron user:@Player tier:0 manual:false ``` The next role sync may grant the tier again if they still have a patron role. Give a test account only the Pup role and remove it. Within the member update, or within the hour, the bit follows the role.

## What and why

Breach (#1824) found that the shipped Orca AI helm never burns in any mode: the burn was only set when a person held the helm, so an AI Orca flew everywhere at cruise. This gives the AI helm a default burn, Breach's rule without its course-specific hard turns and walls:

author: sadeekfarhan21
body:
Found while testing shared-plan links: Down the Hatch's share code changed from c27154d2 to d03755c8 within the day, so every link to it (spot pages, plan pages, the new in-app plan links) went dead.

Cause: `dedupeEvents` merges a re-found spot into the stored one but kept the newest row's id, and the run then deleted the old row. A standing deal's slug includes the placeholder start the scrape gave it, so each re-find minted a new id → new `short` → broken links.

Fix: the merged spot keeps the earliest-discovered id (and still takes the newer/higher-confidence details). Test added; one existing expectation updated (a and b merge under b, the first found).

author: petrickmsilva-alt
body:
## Objetivo

Executar a **Fase 0 — Architecture Discovery & Blueprint** do programa Brobond ERP 3.0: auditar o estado real do repositório e produzir a arquitetura-alvo **baseada em evidência de código**, sem refatoração funcional e sem alteração de banco.

## Escopo

Auditoria + documentação. **Não** altera runtime, **não** cria migration, **não** toca produção.

## Arquivos alterados

Novos, em `docs/architecture/`:

- `README.md` — índice arquitetural
- `CURRENT-STATE.md` — auditoria do estado atual (números reais de `npm run architecture:audit`)
- `DOMAIN-MAP.md` — mapa de domínios (12 alvo + adicionais, com estado/evidência)
- `DEPENDENCY-MAP.md` — dependências e riscos de acoplamento
- `SOURCE-OF-TRUTH.md` — matriz de autoridade das entidades críticas
- `CONTEXT-MAP.md` — bounded contexts e contratos entre domínios
- `TARGET-ARCHITECTURE.md` — arquitetura-alvo (Modular Monolith) + diagramas C4 (Mermaid)
- `DATA-ARCHITECTURE.md`, `INTEGRATION-ARCHITECTURE.md`, `SECURITY-ARCHITECTURE.md`
- `API-CONTRACTS.md`, `EVENT-CATALOG.md`
- `ROADMAP.md`, `RISK-REGISTER.md`, `MASTER-BACKLOG.md`
- `NATIVE-STORE-DECOMMISSION.md` — plano de retirada da loja pública nativa `/loja`
- `ADR/ADR-0001..0014` — 14 ADRs + índice

## Decisões registradas (aprovadas pelo Diretor)

- **ADR-0001** Modular Monolith (sem microserviços)
- **ADR-0007** descontinuação da loja pública nativa `/loja` (RETAIL WooCommerce passa a ser a única loja pública)
- **ADR-0005/0006** identidade comercial e RETAIL/WHOLESALE
- Fonte canônica SQL-first, multi-tenant por `empresa_id`, operacional×analítico, eventos/outbox, migrations, RBAC — formalizados em ADRs

## Achados principais (evidência)

- O ERP **já é**, na prática, um Modular Monolith com multi-tenancy real e fonte SQL-first (212 tabelas, 184 com `empresa_id`; 174 recursos; 474 rotas; 89,7% de cobertura de tenant).
- **Nenhum risco P0/P1** identificado no escopo auditado.
- Auditoria da loja nativa: identificadas superfície pública (`/loja/*` + `/api/loja/*`), serviços **compartilhados** a preservar (motor de pedidos, frete, Payment Engine, reserva) e a área administrativa a revisar.

## Testes executados

| Verificação | Comando | Resultado |
|---|---|---|
| Typecheck | `npm run typecheck` | ✅ OK (domain+server+client) |
| Testes server | `npm --workspace server test` | ✅ 2183 pass · 0 fail · 88 skip |
| Testes client | `npm --workspace client test` | ✅ 1165 pass · 0 fail |
| Lint | `npm run lint` | ✅ 0 errors (615 warnings baseline) |
| Inventário arquitetural | `npm run architecture:audit` | ✅ OK |
| Auditoria de menu | `npm run audit:menu` | ✅ OK |
| Auditoria de UX | `npm run audit:ux` | ✅ OK |

**BLOQUEADO no sandbox (coberto pelo CI):** `test:pg`, `smoke:pg`, `prisma validate` (sem PostgreSQL local / download de engine). Não marcados como aprovados.

## Riscos

Documentação pura — reverter o PR não afeta runtime. Riscos do programa em `docs/architecture/RISK-REGISTER.md`.

## Pendências

Ver `docs/architecture/MASTER-BACKLOG.md`. Decisões que exigem o Diretor (não tomadas unilateralmente): destino de SEO das URLs antigas de `/loja` (301×410) e destino administrativo de `LojaConfigPage`/`estadoLoja`.

## Rollback

Revert do PR (nenhum efeito em runtime).

## Situação operacional

Sem alteração em produção, sem deploy, sem alteração de configuração externa, sem ativação de conectores, sem cutover.

author: kenzi
body:
Spec silnika §13.8.2 (wyzwalacz `page`) i §13.8.1 pkt 3 (przypadki zgodności), PR silnika #1903, merge d5e3480cd. Zlecenie: architekt-it, 2026-11-08.

## Wyzwalacz `page`
- Filtry w `when`: `paths` (`include` / `exclude`, prefiks z granicą segmentu, `exclude` wygrywa, `"/"` = tylko strona główna), `lang` (klucze `langPrefixes` koperty: najdłuższy prefiks, wpis `/` jako ostatnia opcja, bez dopasowania = język nieznany), `device` (`mobile` = `(hover: none)`), `minPageViews`, `minSeconds`, `minScrollPct`, `chance` (FNV-1a 32-bit na UTF-8 `visitorId␟scenarioId␟nodeId`, `% 100 < chance`).
- Raz na odsłonę. Po innym wyzwalaczu liczy się odsłona **otwarta** po nim (`pageAt > arm.at`), nawet gdy próg czasu mija na tej samej odsłonie.
- Działa na zamknięte: nieznane pole (także w `paths`), zła wartość, `lang` bez `langPrefixes` albo złe `langPrefixes` = węzeł invalid + `console.warn`. To odstępstwo od reguły 8, celowe: filtr odbiorców nigdy nie jest „miękki”.
- Sprawdzany przy otwarciu strony w tym samym passie co `return_visit` (jeden popup naraz). Progi czasu i przewinięcia idą przez mechanizm `engagement`. Nasłuch tylko wtedy, gdy któryś `page` ma próg.

## ma-cases
- `tests/fixtures/ma-cases/<NNN>-<slug>.json` + `index.json`, 27 przypadków `page`. Runner `symuluj()` w `tests/ma.test.js` puszcza je na prawdziwym ma.js i blokuje bramkę.
- Oczekiwania nie pochodzą z kodu: język i ścieżka z tabeli w recenzji #1903, kubełki `chance` z niezależnego FNV w Pythonie.
- Mutacje ma.js: brak granicy segmentu, język nieznany jako pl, chance bez separatora, ignorowane device i minPageViews, page na tej samej odsłonie co X. Każdą łapie co najmniej jeden przypadek. Na ma.js z main pada 25 z 27. Dwie mutacje są nieobserwowalne: zdjęcie końcowego `/` daje to samo dzięki prefiksowi z granicą, a podwójne odpalenie blokuje `once_per_visit` i `eng.signalled`.
- `t` porównujemy do pełnej sekundy w dół (timer progu odpala ok. 20 ms po progu).
- Runner odrzuca `visitor.profile` ≠ null i `visitor.lead`, żeby żaden przypadek nie przeszedł w połowie.

## Testy
- `npm test` 1024/1024, `release:check v1.9.0-ma.44` zielony na 745282f.
- Dist: zmienia się tylko `ma.min.js`. magicznylukecin.pl (`@main`) nie używa `d2-ma`.

Merge i tag: decyzja Piotra (zgoda nocna obejmowała tylko PR-y po sygnale 2destate).

Stage 5 of moving the review into the Rust CLI. `craft init --propose` lists the profile and discovered external systems; the `review-init` skill asks the reviewer for each integration point (system, git URL, deployed tag or commit) and `craft init --write` stores them in `~/.craft/projects/<id>/review.toml`, outside the repo. `craft review start` fetches each point shallowly into `~/.craft/sources` at its revision (branches refused, cache reused offline, a 240 s overall budget, git's repo-locating environment cleared) and gives the external-sources block to the lifecycle, compatibility and race lenses and the verifiers; what could not be prepared is named in the report and the review goes on. Also fixes the stage-4 subdirectory case of the deferral and scope checks.

Dropped Low findings:
- The `review-init` skill description does not say the source reading is not yet observed live.

author: chrisrogers37
body:
Build PR 3 of #1053's compaction at task close (the build is posted at https://github.com/Claudfather/Claudlobby/issues/1053#issuecomment-6711475779): the host-wide slot, one compaction at a time. It is passive: nothing takes the slot yet. The build's executor (PR 4) is to take it just before it types `/compact`, and to release it once the compaction is proven or has ended.

## What changes

A new stdlib runtime script, `claudlobby/_runtime_scripts/compaction-slot.py` (Python 3.9):

| Call | Outcome | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| `take --fleet F --bot B`, no live lease, load1 under 40 | `granted`: a lease that names the bot, the time it was taken and an end 10 minutes later, with its lease ID | 0 |
| `take` while a lease is live, whoever holds it | `refused`, `held`, naming the holder and its end | 75 |
| `take` while load1 is 40 or more | `refused`, `load`, with the reading | 75 |
| `take` when the load cannot be read | `refused`, `load_unreadable` | 75 |
| `release --fleet F --bot B --lease ID`, that lease live | `released` | 0 |
| `release` of an ended lease, or a lease ID, fleet or bot that is not the current lease's | `not_held`; nothing changes | 0 |
| `status [--json]` | `free` or `held`, the live lease or the last one and how it ended (`released`, `expired`, `reset`), and load1 beside the line | 0 |

- **A refusal writes nothing.** The holder named in a `held` refusal can be the caller itself, so a bot can see that its own compaction is still in flight.
- **A lease is a record, not a held lock.** The executor's process is short-lived, so the lease is `state/compaction-slot/lease.json` in the data root, replaced whole: a temporary file, then a rename. So a holder that died leaves its lease to end at its 10 minutes, and a host reset ends it at once, since its boot ID no longer matches.
- **Each take and release decides under a non-blocking flock** on `state/compaction-slot/lock`, held for one decision and waited for at most 2 s. So of two racing takes one is granted.
- **A record that cannot be read holds nothing.** `status` names it, and the next take replaces it, so a damaged file never wedges the slot.
- **The load line is 40,** the heavy slot's own stop line (`heavy-slot.py`'s `RENDER_LINES`). The load is `/proc/loadavg` where it exists, else `os.getloadavg()` (macOS).
- **A release names its lease ID,** so a late release never ends a later lease.
- **Not built: the stop file.** The plan had a `disabled` file in that directory as an operator's stop for every compaction. It is left out, with its test and its `disabled` reading, under the ruling that framework changes get no on/off switches.

**Files:**
- `claudlobby/_runtime_scripts/compaction-slot.py` (new, mode 755).
- `tests/test_compaction_slot.py` (new).
- `CLAUDE.md` and its copy `AGENTS.md`: the script's index line, which `tests/test_instruction_budget.py` requires of every script in that folder.
- `claudlobby/_runtime_scripts/CLAUDE.md` and its copy `AGENTS.md`: the script's row in the script table.
- `changelog.d/feat-1053-compaction-slot.md`.

## Verified

- **Tests:** `tests/test_compaction_slot.py` (new, 11 tests). Each runs the script by its path, as the executor is to run it, so its execute bit and shebang are pinned too. Each has its own slot directory, a stand-in `/proc` for the load, a boot ID and a clock, through the script's test seams.
  - A second take is refused while a lease lives, for another bot and for the holder itself, and granted once the lease is released.
  - A lease whose holder died (the process that took it has exited) is still held at 599.9 s and ends at 600 s.
  - A host reset (another boot ID) ends a live lease.
  - load1 40.00 from the stand-in `/proc` refuses and writes nothing; 39.90 grants.
  - A load that cannot be read refuses.
  - Two racing takes grant one: six takers start while the test holds the slot's lock, so they meet at it. One is granted, and five are refused as `held`.
  - A take waits for the slot's lock and, held past its 2 s wait, refuses as `lock_busy` and writes nothing.
  - A late release never ends a later lease, the same bot's or another's, and a release of an expired lease is `not_held`.
  - A record that cannot be read (not JSON, a list, a partial lease) holds nothing, and the next take replaces it.
  - `status` reads `free`, load1 and the line, and makes nothing.
  - With no data root and no seam, the script refuses at exit 2; with `CLAUDLOBBY_ROOT`, the lease is at `state/compaction-slot/lease.json`.
- **Mutants:** each changes one line of the script, in its own tree and venv, and each fails at least one test: no live-lease check fails 3 (the second take, the holder that died, the race); `>` in place of `>=` at the load line fails the load test; a lease that ignores its boot ID fails the host reset; a release that ignores its lease ID fails the late release; no flock fails the lock wait. The race test caught that last mutant in one of the two runs: with no lock to meet at, the six takers seldom overlap, so the lock-wait test is the one that pins the lock. The unchanged tree passes all 11. Two runs, each in one lease of the heavy-job slot: at `6fe511ea` and at this head, whose script differs only in reading the boot ID before the lock.
- **Local run.** Each tree was a fresh export with its own venv, run through the host's heavy-job slot and capped: `ulimit -v` 4 GiB, `ulimit -f` 256 MiB per file, a 15-minute limit. The covering set: the new file and the 12 files that check every script in the folder or the instruction files (`test_instruction_budget.py`, `test_changelog_fragments.py`, `test_bash_parse.py`, `test_cadence_retirement.py`, `test_event_type_registry.py`, `test_report_addresses.py`, `test_send_keys_ratchet.py`, `test_validate_harness_reads.py`, `test_boundary_invariants.py`, `test_claude_version.py`, `test_known_values.py`, `test_fleet_claude_bin.py`).
  - At main (`47d16dfb`), the 12 files: 337 passed, exit 0.
  - At this head (`a092415e`), the new file and the 12: 348 passed, exit 0.
- **No live test:** the script is passive. Nothing in the framework calls it before PR 4, so no bot's behavior changes when it ships.

## Held files

Every open PR's file list was read at 22:24:21-22:25:10Z (83 open PRs), and again before this PR opened, at 23:15:12-23:16:02Z (84 open PRs, with one new holder, #2793). The second read's positive controls: `claudlobby/compact_request.py` maps to #2788 alone, and the newest PR's first file to #2793. Each read took every page, included renamed files' old names, and was positive-controlled. Four of this PR's files are held:

| File | Holders | This PR's lines | The holders' lines |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CLAUDE.md` | #1846, #1969, #1971, #1982, #2041, #2102, #2299, #2364, #2793 | one line after `keepalive.sh` in "Bot lifecycle and supervision" (line 57) | #2102: the "What that is for" paragraph (line 7). #2364: the top paragraphs (lines 1-14) and `plane-otel.sh` after `plane-view.sh` in "Observable plane". #2299: the first lines of "GitHub identity and tool-call guards". #2793: the "Every PR body" heading and paragraph (lines 253-255). #1846, #1969, #1971, #1982 and #2041 change text main no longer has (its old `lib/` tables and the earlier test notes). |
| `AGENTS.md` | #2102, #2299, #2364, #2793 | the same line (the byte copy) | the same as in `CLAUDE.md` |
| `claudlobby/_runtime_scripts/CLAUDE.md` | #2299, #2360, #2364, #2647 | one row after `heavy-slot.py` (line 107) | #2299: a row after `git-credential-github-app`. #2364: a row after `plane-view.sh`. #2360: the `plane-lookup.py` row. #2647: the `start-bot.sh`, `runtime-admission.sh` and `lib-common.sh` rows. |
| `claudlobby/_runtime_scripts/AGENTS.md` | #2299, #2360, #2364, #2647 | the same row (the byte copy) | the same as in that `CLAUDE.md` |

author: elseform-tech
body:
## Summary
Step 1 of the approved plan `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-07-agent-cli-integrations-design.md`. The agent can run the `themis` CLI in its shell to manage integrations, and the app server limits what that shell can reach.

**Ships together with step 2 (#309, stacked on this branch).** Without step 2, an "Allow in this chat" on one `themis` command could cover dangerous ones. Merge #309 into this branch first, then this PR into `main`.

### How it works
- **Credential:** one random 256-bit token per run, minted on the run's first shell, background or git command. Subagents get their own.
  - Passed as `THEMIS_AGENT_TOKEN` and `THEMIS_AGENT_PORT`.
  - Revoked for the chat in `finish_run`.
  - Masked as `[redacted]` in shell and `background_task` output, hidden from Debug output, never logged.
- **How the server tells agent from person:** the person's token, compared in constant time, means the person; an issued token means an agent; anything else is `unauthorized`, using the shared constant from #307.
- **Allow-list, deny by default** (`crates/desktop/src/server/agent.rs`):
  - status and diagnostics;
  - read-only settings;
  - integrations through the store, as the agent's: no consent is recorded, and MCP secrets and sign-in stay the person's;
  - the agent's own chat only (`threadId` required).
  - Everything else is refused: approvals, its own permissions and mode, settings writes, secrets, the person's terminal, projects, other chats, review decisions, browser controls, server and app lifecycle, and memory.
  - Refusals log `server`/`agent_call_refused` with metadata only.
- **`server.json` is hidden from every agent command, YOLO included.** It holds the person's token; if an agent could read it, the guard would be pointless. AGENTS.md now lists it among the walls YOLO keeps. This is an owner decision and a deliberate departure from the spec.
- **PATH:** `<app-data>/agent-cli/themis` links to the app's own executable and goes first on the run's PATH. Agents can't write the app data, so they can't swap the link. On Windows no link is made; the environment variables are still set.

### Threat model and limits (also in `docs/configuration.md`)
- With no sandbox (Windows, `sandbox.enabled: false`, Linux without bubblewrap or Landlock), an agent can read `server.json`. That's the same situation as the existing app-data write wall.
- A person-approved "Run outside the sandbox" could expose the person's token.
- With `sandbox.network: "block"`, the agent's `themis` can't reach the server.
- A background task still running after its run ends loses CLI access (owner decision).

## Tests
- `agent_cli_e2e`: every refused area is refused for an agent token and works for the person. A forged token gets `unauthorized`. A real scripted run finds `themis` on PATH, runs `themis plugin list`, sees the token as `[redacted]`, has `approve_action` refused, and can't read `server.json` under Seatbelt. After the run, the token is `unauthorized`.
- The guard was confirmed failing with the check disabled, then passing.
- Unit tests: token lifecycle, the allow-list, a property test over arbitrary method, chat and action, and a scale test showing the guard check stays flat from 100 to 8,000 issued tokens.

## Merge with main
Merged `origin/main` (#305–#307). The `server.rs` conflict was resolved to the guard, using #307's `UNAUTHORIZED` constant. `run_until` went over 100 lines after the merge, so its three housekeeping loops moved into `spawn_housekeeping` (a pure move).

## Checks (the combined stack, at the tip of #309)
- `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` (macOS): ok.
- Ratchets: ok.
- `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast`: 1762 passed, 0 failed, 8 ignored; no servers left running.

## Not verified
The real desktop app and its live-check row, and Linux and Windows outside CI.

## TSUMGI #230 — client source alignment after approved production 12K cutover

**Scope:** source-only dotnix config/tests/docs, Draft, nonclosing. No Merge or Nix/home-manager switch performed by this PR.

The user explicitly approved the reversible Sirius 8K→12K production cutover. Sirius Qwen3.8-27B now serves native `n_ctx=12288` in the production Worker; Control/Gateway advertises **10,240 input / 2,048 output / 12,288 total** tokens; actual Gateway 10,143-token request, Chat/Tool Call/Streaming and 10,275-token limit rejection passed with >2GiB free VRAM per GPU. Bonsai production remains **8K**.

**Reason:** dotnix `packages/opencode/default.nix` launcher republishes source-owned `packages/opencode/config/opencode.json` into the normal global config directory each time OpenCode is invoked. A manual edit of `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` to 12K was overwritten by the original source `8192`. This PR aligns the **canonical source** rather than fighting the generated output.

**Changes:**
- Only provider `tsumgi` model `qwen3.8-27b` `limit.context: 8192 → 12288` (output stays 2048).
- Preserve Bonsai `8192/2048`, other model providers, global OpenAI plan/build Agent, permissions, tool settings, and all endpoints.
- Update source contract test to assert independent Qwen vs Bonsai limits.
- Update operator docs with verified November 8 production limits and launcher regeneration behavior.

**Validation on Adam:**
- `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_opencode*.py' -q`: **37 PASS**.
- `tools/check-repository.sh`: PASS (OpenCode tests, package-registry tests, Nix all-systems no-build).
- Exact changed source `OPENCODE_CONFIG=<source>/opencode.json opencode debug config` reported Qwen context **12288** / output 2048, Bonsai context 8192 / output 2048, and global `plan` still `openai/gpt-6.1-sol`.
- Real `opencode run --pure --agent tsumgi-qwen --model tsumgi/qwen3.8-27b` with this explicit source override completed **exit 0** and expected marker. This qualifies an explicit source override, **not yet the installed global dotnix baseline**.

**Pending:** independent PR review, CI exact-head, separate approval to Ready/Merge and deploy/rebuild the dotnix-managed OpenCode package. Until then, the installed normal OpenCode launcher continues to re-sync the old 8K global config. Do not change global Agents, the Bonsai budget, or TSUMGI production deployment via this PR.

Refs: [TSUMGI #230](https://github.com/upiscium/TSUMGI/issues/230), [TSUMGI #230 production log](https://github.com/upiscium/TSUMGI/issues/230#issuecomment-6714127399), [dotnix #68](https://github.com/upiscium/dotnix/issues/68).

author: kharkevich
vic-lsh
body:
## Problem

The desktop app is getting one Cost dashboard across all runs. The backend owns every cost number (totals, splits, pricing, buckets); the app only displays them. `WatchRunCost` (#4047) serves one run, so a dashboard built on it would have to open a stream per run and then sum totals, rank runs, merge the splits by type of agent and model, and re-bucket a series itself. That is exactly the arithmetic the app must not do, and a second implementation of it would drift from the run view.

## Solution

`rpc WatchHostCost(WatchHostCostRequest) returns (stream WatchHostCostResponse)` on `OrchestratorService`. It covers every run the host holds, live and ended, and sends the whole view when it opens and again each time any run's cost changes.

A `HostCost` holds:

- the total and its tokens by kind, `run_count`, `turns` and `unpriced_turns` (a cost with an unpriced turn behind it is a lower bound, exactly as in `RunCost`; a cost nobody reported is absent, never zero);
- `runs`: the most costly runs, most first, each with run id, name (the run's task, cut to 256 bytes at a character boundary), status, cost, tokens, turns, unpriced turns and cost limit; at most 32, a run with no priced turn after the priced ones; the rest are added up in `other_runs`;
- `roles` and `models` summed across runs, and `series` over time in buckets sized to the span (the same ladder and the same `SpendSeries` type as a run), and `last_hour_usd`;
- an optional `since` in the request: only turns that finished at or after it, in the runs that did not end before it; the series starts at `since`. An instant after the host's clock is refused with `InvalidArgument`.

Additive change only; `buf breaking` (FILE) passes. `protocol_version` is unchanged: an older host answers `Unimplemented`, which the feed shows as that stream failing alone.

The app side is a typed `HostCostFeed` in `clients/apps/desktop` core, held per window under `model.data.hostCosts`, with the fake daemon serving published views. No UI.

### Design

- **Data and types.** No new stored data: the view is derived from turns in the store and run facts in core state. New wire messages: `HostCost`, `HostRunCost`, `OtherRunsCost`, `WatchHostCostRequest/Response`; `RoleCost`, `ModelCost`, `SpendSeries`, `SpendBucket`, `ModelSpend`, `ModelRef` and `Usage` are reused unchanged. `run_count == len(runs) + other_runs.runs` and `unpriced_turns <= turns` are CEL rules, held by Go, Python and the JS evaluator (the corpus test runs the JS one). In TypeScript the window is a closed template type, `'all' | 'since:<ms>'`, which is also its key in the model.
- **Owner.** The math stays in `orchestrator/internal/cost` (pure). The contract is stated in `internal/wire`, the stream in `internal/daemon`, the display shape in the desktop `state` folder, the stream in desktop `core`.
- **Interface.** `cost.Host` (`NewHost`, `Run`, `Agent`, `Add`, `Live`, `View`) and `cost.HostView`; `wire.HostCostMessage`; `Service.WatchHostCostFrom` / `WatchHostCost`; `client.WatchHostCost`; desktop `HostCostFeed`, `HostCostView`, `readHostCost`, `applyHostCost`.
- **Same math, not a fork.** `View` now embeds a `cost.Breakdown` (total, turns, roles, models, series, last hour) that `Ledger` computes once (`breakdown`), and `HostView` embeds the same. A `Host` holds one `Ledger` of every counted run's turns (an agent now says which run it belongs to), so the splits, buckets and rate are the run view's code over more turns. A run's line in the list is the total of that run's own turns in the same order the run's view adds them. `wire` states the lists of both messages through one `breakdownOut`. In the desktop `state`, the host view reuses the run view's readers (`usageView`, `roleView`, `modelCostView`, `seriesView`).
- **Direction.** No new import edge: `cost -> core`, `wire -> cost` and `daemon -> cost` already existed (archcheck unchanged); no Python module changed, so no `tach.toml` edge.
- **Stream.** Follows `WatchRunCost`: a snapshot at a `Cut`, then the events of every run (`Interest{Everything, Ticks}`); one whole view per poll when a turn ended, an agent appeared or a run's status or end moved; a refresh every `CostRefresh` while a counted run is live, and none once nothing is live (the view is then as of the latest end, so it never changes).
- **Drift left, not fixed.** (1) Like `WatchRunCost` and the `WatchRuns` snapshot, opening reads the turns inside the engine's `Cut`, where nothing commits; for the host that is every counted run's turns (a `since` skips runs that ended before it and reads only turns that overlap it). A host-wide ledger the engine maintains and streams share would remove the per-stream read; not done here, and worth doing if opening is slow on a big host. (2) A run that never opened is counted like any other (it cost nothing); excluding it would need removing its lead from the ledger when the run ends.

### Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  store[(store: turns)] -- read once at open --> feed
  hub[hub: events of every run] --> feed
  feed[hostCostFeed] -- Run / Agent / Add --> host[cost.Host: one Ledger of the counted runs' turns]
  host -- View now --> view[cost.HostView = Breakdown + runs + others]
  view --> wire[wire.HostCostMessage] --> rpc[WatchHostCost]
  rpc --> app[desktop HostCostFeed -> model.data.hostCosts by window]
```

## Verification

Property tests over generated hosts hold the host view to what `WatchRunCost` serves for each run, through the pure projection, the daemon service and the whole-daemon simulation. I mutated the projection and the stream (window filter, cap, sort, run count, as-of rule, run/agent/turn events, refresh, window read boundary, future-since check) and each mutation failed a named test.

### Correctness properties

- The host total equals the sum over runs of each run's own total (cost, tokens by kind, turns, unpriced turns); no cost when no run has a priced turn; true for generated sets of runs and turns, including unpriced turns, runs with no turns (and runs whose session never opened) and more runs than the list holds.
- Each run's line in the list equals that run's own view; the list is the head of the most-costly-first order of all runs; `runs` plus `other_runs` lose nobody (`run_count`, turns, cost and tokens add up).
- The splits by type and by model are the sums of the runs' splits, in a run view's order; the buckets hold every priced turn once and add up to the total.
- The view does not depend on the order runs, agents and turns arrive in, nor on a turn told twice.
- A window counts exactly the turns that ended at or after `since` (a turn that ended at that instant is in), in the runs that did not end before it, and equals the host of the world cut to the window.
- The view is as of the host's clock while a counted run is live and fixed once none is; the stream sends nothing for events that cost nothing, one view for the events of a poll, and a view that a new client would be given (up to the log sequence) after any script of turns, runs starting and stopping, clock moves and lag.

### Testing

- `./support/repoctl/repoctl doctor --fix && eval "$(./support/repoctl/repoctl doctor --env)"`
- `./scripts/check_proto.sh`: pass (generate and diff of Go, TS, Python bindings; `buf lint`; `buf breaking` FILE against origin/main; 1183 pytest)
- `./scripts/check_format.sh`, `./scripts/check_lint.sh`: pass
- `cd orchestrator && go vet ./... && go test -count=1 ./...`: pass except `internal/localfs` (fails the same way at origin/main on macOS; it is a Linux statfs check) and `gatewayroot` (macOS `TMPDIR` makes the socket path over 100 bytes; passes with `TMPDIR=/tmp`)
- `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/hub ./internal/daemon/... ./internal/client ./internal/mcp ./internal/search`: pass
- Go tests added: `internal/cost/host_test.go` (pure properties over 400 generated hosts), `internal/wire/host_cost_test.go` (contract, limits, corpus), `internal/daemon/host_cost_test.go` (sum

body:
Gets the website sync ready for the agents launch: it reads only what landlords gave us, the team approves every change while we launch, and a unit can have its own page.

## What changes

**Only sources we were given**
- The sync reads only a URL a landlord uploaded or gave us, pages on that same site (subdomains included) and unit pages. A Zillow or Apartments.com page we were given allows only that building's pages on the portal.
- The crawler refuses every other page. A given URL that now redirects to another site fails the read and alerts the team, rather than being followed.
- Source search (Zillow, Apartments.com, the web) and "Read found pages" are off (`FOUND_SOURCES_ENABLED`).
- In the Agent tab, landlords see only pages from their own sites and links they sent.

**Launch review** (`WEBSITE_SYNC_TEAM_REVIEW`, on unless set to off)
- Every website change a sync finds waits in a new section of the admin Agents tab: "Website changes waiting for the team". Nothing reaches students until the team applies it, and landlords don't see this queue. Their Agent tab says the team checks changes during launch.
- Agent knowledge from a sync: new facts are added, but changing or removing a fact the agent already has waits for the team.
- Applying a change that puts a lease live checks the landlord's payment method and agreement, even when the team applies it.
- A change the team rejected isn't raised again while the website says the same thing.

**A page per unit**
- In the Agent tab, a unit can have its own page. The sync reads that page alone and trusts it for that unit.
- A unit page that disappears withdraws the unit's leases; they come back if the page does. Units are never renamed or deleted.

**Own pages on company sites**
- When a landlord gives a company-wide page, the 4am run finds each listing's own page on that site and attaches it, recorded as `source_attached`.
- A listing that matches no page, or more than one, is left alone.

**Daily agents digest**
- New "Website sync, by listing" section. For each listing it shows whether the run was held and why, pages read, what is waiting by type, failures, pages the sync was not allowed to open, and own pages attached.

## Migrations (applied to dev, NOT to prod)
Apply both to prod before this reaches main:
- `202611060001_listing_unit_pages.sql`
- `202611070001_sync_launch_review.sql`

## Test plan
- [x] Dev syncs of Ceylon (own site) and The Mark (Zillow): every change was held for the team with nothing applied, off-site pages were refused, and listing data was unchanged.
- [x] Knowledge: new facts were added, while a changed pet fee and a smoking rule waited for the team. The admin approved one and rejected the other; the landlord was refused on both.
- [x] Admin applying a new lease for a landlord without a payment method or agreement was blocked with the gate message.
- [x] Sub-pages: macapartments.com matched all 12 MAC buildings to their own pages (out of 124 on the site); a made-up building matched nothing.
- [x] Digest renders the new section; admin queue and landlord Agent tab checked in the browser.
- [ ] On staging: Admin > Agents shows "Source search is off" and the team queue. View as a landlord: the Agent tab shows the launch note and no held changes.

## Objective
Complete the two specific remaining recruiter-proof gaps without adding a separate product or paid model service.

### A. Real-data evaluation (CI-first)
- Original NLBSE-2023 held-out archive verified by fixed SHA256, original label distribution checked.
- Precommitted 96-case diagnostic: 24 source-labeled cases per class, stable SHA-based selection independent of result, excluding repeated issue IDs.
- Existing Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct GGUF Q4_K_M model and pinned llama.cpp container run actual CPU inference; no mock responses.
- Frozen zero-shot JSON prompt, baseline on identical truncated text, per-class precision/recall, accuracy, macro-F1, full confusion and paired within-class bootstrap interval; model output hashes, case hashes and timings.
- One-shot GitHub Actions job only on this owner-created PR's initial `opened` event. No raw issue texts or free-form model responses in CI report; no third-party paid APIs, no secrets, no write-token.

### B. Browser interaction (beta)
- Browser-only WebLLM inference, no hosted server/secrets/running costs, separate `docs/live.html` and `docs/live.js`.
- Qwen2.5 1.5B (same base model, different quantization/runtime) plus 0.5B mobile option (different capacity).
- The browser performs *model inference only*; n8n/API/SQLite/approval remain verified separately in historical real Docker CI. No replay, no simulated fallback.
- Front-page link clearly marked Beta; must verify real browser inference and mobile behavior before claiming DoD B.

### Release gates
- Confirm exact HEAD SHA, green deterministic tests and genuine LLM CI report.
- Review static CSP/third-party dependency and WebGPU functionality. If incompatible, document precise blocker rather than claiming success.

author: sugalabubaker
body:
The voxel raster takes a cluster per subgroup instead of per workgroup (ADR-0061's amendment of 2026-11-07), the first item of its "What is left". Most voxel clusters are small: the city's cells' proxies average 85 voxels, and a third have 32 or fewer. Before, both of a workgroup's subgroups loaded each cluster's records and computed its transforms, and a small cluster left the second subgroup nothing but an empty flush.

## What changes

**RHI (2e4978f).**
- `NphGpuComputePipelineDesc.subgroup_size` lets a compute pipeline ask its subgroups' size: a power of two from the new `NphGpuLimits.subgroup_size_min` to `subgroup_size_max`. Every subgroup is then that size and full.
- The device now requires subgroup size control, full compute subgroups, and compute among the stages a size can be asked of. Vulkan 1.3 makes every device have all three.
- New quirk `NPH_GPU_QUIRK_SUBGROUP_BARRIER_WAITS_FOR_WORKGROUP` for lavapipe (Mesa 25.2.8). There, a subgroup barrier waits for the workgroup's other subgroups. If one has returned, a subgroup that passes barriers in a loop never goes on, and what it would write after is lost.
- Two new gpu tests:
  - `compute_pipelines_take_the_subgroup_size_asked` checks sizes, counts and lanes, and the refusals.
  - `a_subgroup_barrier_waits_for_its_subgroup_alone` passes on the RTX. On lavapipe, eight lanes wrote before the loop and none after, so it logs the quirk there.

**Renderer (61cf13e).**
- The voxel raster asks for subgroups of 32 (else the device's nearest size), two per workgroup. Each subgroup takes its own cluster from its records to its last flush, with its own copy of the bricks and its own queue, and waits for no other.
- A phase with fewer than `NphRendererDesc.voxel_share_clusters` clusters (1,024) leaves most of the GPU idle. There a second pipeline (`k_share`) gives each cluster a workgroup, whose two subgroups take alternate batches.
- `vis args` gives one of the two dispatches the phase's workgroups and the other none (the new `NphVisArgs.voxel_share_args`), so neither pipeline carries the other's code.
- On the quirk's device, a workgroup is one subgroup.

## Cost (RTX 3060 Ti, 4K; two builds interleaved, main eb53e34 against this; ms)

| Scene | Before | After | Voxel raster, phases 0 + 1 |
|---|---|---|---|
| City rooftop | 10.143 | 9.977 | 1.426 + 0.196 → 1.284 + 0.182 |
| City crossing | 6.923 | 6.915 | 0.115 + 0.016 → 0.107 + 0.016 |
| City park and streets (5 views) | 6.827–8.096 | 6.836–8.097 | unchanged (frames −0.007 to +0.009) |
| Landscape forest | 58.10 | 55.26 | 17.29 + 1.75 → 14.74 + 1.54 |
| Landscape (5 other views) | 50.56–62.10 | 47.83–59.74 | phase 0 −1.95 to −2.56 |
| `foliage_4k_production` | 6.443 | 6.223 | 1.786 + 0.348 → 1.613 + 0.322 |

**DRAM** (GPU traces of the two builds, four frames each; MB per frame, phases 0 + 1). The pass moves about the same data as before:

| Voxel raster | Main | #160 |
|---|---|---|
| City rooftop | 87.5 + 18.5 | 92.4 + 19.0 |
| Landscape forest | 1,118.4 + 64.8 | 1,126.5 + 56.0 |
| City street (phase 0) | 1.2 | 1.9 |

The frames' totals are within the traces' spread (rooftop 2,369 against 2,365 MB), and the other passes differ by up to 10 MB between traces.

**Image:** the city's and the landscape's views drawn as their instances (`--debug-view=instances`) match the old build pixel for pixel. The crossing's 401 differing pixels differ just as much between two runs of the old build.

## Tests

- `VoxelAloneGpu.voxel_clusters_draw_where_their_rays_meet_them` runs the rays test with every phase's clusters a subgroup each (`voxel_share_clusters` 1). In `VoxelGpu`, the tests' small phases share them.
- Both pass against the CPU twin on the RTX 3060 Ti and on lavapipe, along with the rest of the voxel suite.
- render_tests: 345 pass on the RTX.
- gpu_tests: 104 pass on the RTX; on lavapipe, 97 pass and 7 are skipped.
- Shaders pass glslang 14 and spirv-val.

## Measured and not kept (in the ADR)

- **A table of each voxel's brick and cell, filled once per cluster:** phase 0 went 1.416 → 1.607 ms. The fill costs the same whatever the cluster's size, and it took 80 registers.
- **Splitting a workgroup's subgroups into halves:** 96, then 80, then 72 registers. It fails on lavapipe because of the barrier quirk.
- **The shared mode in the same pipeline:** +0.022 ms with a runtime stride, +0.031 ms with a call per mode.

## Found along the way

`foliage_shadows_sun_4k_production`, which has no budget, measured 15.6 ms in one A/B and 23.4 ms in another, with either build. This is the shadow map's resolution bias controller. With the sun turning every frame, both bias 0 and bias 1 are stable states, and which one a run settles in depends on its history. Given the same frames, the two builds' shadow maps are identical frame by frame. It's a follow-up for the shadow map, not caused by this change.

body:
This PR corrects the ground-truth reading order of ten pages in `MPDocBench/MPDocBench.json`. On each page, one or a few elements carry an `order` that contradicts the page:
- a date, credit or "编著" line is numbered outside its block;
- a cover or article title is numbered after its first content;
- a coupon heading is separated from its bullets;
- a chart grid is read by column although its captions run across each row;
- two elements are numbered as if they sat on another page.

Each correction moves the misplaced elements to where the page places them. The elements in between shift by the same amount, so their relative order is unchanged. Only `layout_dets[].order` changes (149 lines). The reading-order metric reads this field and nothing else. This PR is independent of the other `fix-gt-*` PRs.

The ten pages come from an audit of every place where a parser's reading order disagrees with the ground truth, across all 420 documents. Most disagreements were the parser's errors, ambiguous layouts (grids, floating boxes, side-by-side blocks), or matching artifacts, and none of those are changed here. Only pages where the ground-truth order cannot be defended are corrected.

Each evidence image shows the page twice, numbered by `order`: as annotated (left) and after this PR (right). The moved elements are in red.

author: fhchu
body:
Snapshots are about 100 bytes against the 1,100-byte datagram budget, so a frame too big for a datagram can only come from a bug. The old fallback sent it on the stream, which hid the bug. Now it's an error on both sides:

- **Relay:** logs an error with the frame's size and the limit, then drops the frame. Other `SendDatagram` failures end the session.
- **Browser:** `console.error`, then drops the frame. The stream-framing fallback and its `LENGTH_SIZE` constant are removed.

Both sides log every dropped frame; the old relay warning logged only once.

Not run in a real browser: the suite can't reach the JS. `notes/` (Relay.md, Networking.md) still describes the fallback, to update after merge.

author: ofirgall
body:
## Summary
- On every launch, including restarts, kv sets `KOALA_ENV_KVIM_CONF` to `<env config dir>/.kvim.conf` (for example `~/.config/kvim-envs/<env>/.kvim.conf`). It's set even when the file doesn't exist, and kv never creates the file. `-c/--cfg` still affects only the user layer.
- New `kv env config [NAME] [--path]`:
  - It creates the env conf with `{}` if it's missing, then opens it in KoalaVim running in that env through the normal launcher.
  - `--path` only prints the path.

body:
## Summary
- `Topics:Keywords` maps a topic name to the words and phrases that suggest it, replacing the built-in wellness topics. `Topics:Enabled` set to false tags posts with their hashtags only. A topic name that can't be a tag, or a topic with no keywords, stops startup.
- Staff can choose topics through `/admin/topics` (ranking admins). Each save adds a new `TopicSetEntity` version, and the newest one is used. Staff can list and read earlier versions, start from a ready-made set in `TopicLibrary` (wellness, climbing, running, cycling, gardening), and preview the topics some text would get (rate-limited like the ranking preview).
- `TopicRules` picks the staff set first, then `Topics:Keywords`, then the built-in set. It reloads at most once a minute, and straight away on the instance that saved. `TopicMatcher` does the matching and validation.
- `PostService`, the dev tag backfill and the simulator now get their topics from `TopicRules`. Posts that are already tagged keep their tags.
- New error codes: `topics.invalid`, `topics.unknown_library`, `topics.version_not_found`.
- Rider inspection cleanups in the touched files: collection expressions, a `switch` in validation, an early return in the reload lock, `Ok(...)` in `GetVersion`, and dropping `public partial class Program;` from the API (ASP0027).


## Also in this PR
- **The `TopicSets` migration** (`20261107232736_Init`), so the API starts and every test suite runs.
- **Engagement on feed posts:** `likes`, `comments`, `reposts`, `liked` and `reposted` on Following, For You, Favourites and tag feeds (`AttachEngagementAsync`). For a repost they're on the post it shares. On `/admin/feed` and `/ranking/preview`, `liked` and `reposted` are the staff member's, so `IHomeFeedService.PeekAsync` and `ForYouService.PreviewAsync` take the staff member's external ID. New `EngagementTests`.
- **Acting as a member from the admin panel:** feed cards can like, repost, comment and reply, report, edit and delete, and follow or favourite the author, through the member endpoints. There's a Favourites tab on your own feed.
- **`docker-compose.dev.yml`:** the infrastructure without the API and worker, for running those on your machine.

## Docs
- `docs/configuration.md`: which topics apply and in what order, the limits, and choosing topics through the API. It links to the docs site.
- `docs/errors.md`, `docs/auth.md`, `docs/runbooks.md`: the new codes, the ranking admin role covering topics, and saving topics in the audit log.
- Docs site, once deployed: a new Topics section in the [API reference](https://docs.feedfabric.dev/api/#topics-ranking-admin), plus updates to [Error codes](https://docs.feedfabric.dev/api/errors/), [Tags and mentions](https://docs.feedfabric.dev/how-it-works/posting/#tags-and-mentions) and [Operating](https://docs.feedfabric.dev/operating/).

## Still to do before merge
- No tests yet for `TopicMatcher`, `TopicStore` (versioning, unknown library) or the `/admin/topics` endpoints.
- The admin panel has no Topics page yet; for now, topics are chosen through the API.

## Testing
- `dotnet build`: no errors. One existing warning, NU1510 on `Microsoft.Extensions.Hosting` in the worker.
- `dotnet test`: 176 passed, 2 skipped, 0 failed across the Application, Api and Worker suites.
- `npm run build` in `web/admin` succeeds.
- The docs site builds (`npm run build` in `web/docs`), and the new anchors resolve.

author: smaug123
body:
A follow-up to #2161. `ModuleHandle.ResolveMethod` stopped the run on a MethodSpec whose arguments violate the method's constraints. It now raises `VerificationException` in the guest, with CoreCLR's message.

CoreCLR checks the constraints as it instantiates the method (`SatisfiesMethodConstraintsForInstantiation`, genmeth.cpp:309-372). It stops at the first parameter, in declaration order, that refuses its argument, and throws `IDS_EE_METHOD_CONSTRAINTS_VIOLATION`:

> Method Holder`1[System.Int32].Struct: type argument 'System.String' violates the constraint of type parameter 'V'.

The message names the declaring type as the MemberRef's parent instantiates it, the method, the argument and the parameter, and no particular constraint. `RuntimeModule.ResolveMethod` catches only `BadImageFormatException`, so the guest sees `VerificationException` itself. I measured every kind of constraint (struct, class, `new()`, interface, base class, self-referential, `allows ref struct`), and arguments that are generic, nested or arrays. All of them give this one shape, with each type spelled as `TypeString::AppendType` spells it.

## Changes

- `NativeRuntimeTypeHelpers.validateConstraintsOn` returned a PawPrint diagnostic string, whose docstring warned it must not reach a guest. It now returns a `GenericConstraintViolation`: the refusing parameter and the argument bound to it, which is what CoreCLR reports. Its two reflection callers, `MakeGenericType` and `MakeGenericMethod`, used the result only as a predicate, so they are unchanged apart from the type.
  - That drops the diagnostic's naming of *which* constraint failed. Nothing read it apart from the TODO this PR removes.
- The MethodSpec arm formats the message from that record and raises it. It names the declaring type through a local helper moved out of the MemberRef arm, which both arms now use. The helper now takes the type from `lookupTypeDefn`, which loads its base chain: a MethodSpec over a MethodDef can be the first thing to touch the type, and classifying the type needs that chain. The helper then substitutes the declaring type's concrete arguments, so `resolveMemberReference` no longer returns the parent's `TypeDefn` arguments.
- `NativeRuntimeTypeHelpers.methodConstraintsViolationMessage` spells the resource. `UnsafeAccessorDispatch`, which already raised the same message, now uses it as well.
- `TestGenericConstraintSatisfaction` read the violated index out of PawPrint's message with a regex. It now reads the record's parameter.

## Tests

`TestModuleResolveMethodSpec` used to have one case PawPrint refused. Its expected answers can now carry the exception's message, and its contexts any list of types. It gains these cases, each pinned against the real runtime:
- a `struct` constraint and a `class` constraint, each with an argument that violates it and one that does not;
- a second parameter that violates while the first is satisfied, which names `B`;
- two parameters that both violate, which names the first, `A`;
- a method on `Holder<int>`, whose message names ``Holder`1[System.Int32]``;
- `where V : T`, read in the caller's type context, violated with `t=string` and satisfied with `t=object`;
- a violation on `OnXml : System.Xml.XmlDocument`, run alone, so that it is the first thing to touch `System.Private.Xml`. Codex found that this crashed, before the helper loaded the base chain.

The refusal test is gone: nothing in this fixture is refused any more.

- Red first: PawPrint stopped the run at the old TODO.
- Mutation check. Each of these mutants fails the fixture:
  - rendering types without their namespace;
  - substituting the wrong arguments into the declaring type;
  - reporting the last violation rather than the first;
  - always naming the first parameter.

Suites, run locally at the tip: default 5343 passed, 15 skipped, 0 failed; `TestCategory=Guest|TestCategory=GuestSolo|TestCategory=GuestPure|TestCategory=GuestImpure` 1605 passed, 0 failed.

Codex review found two things, both fixed here: the first-touch crash above, and that the parameter's name was spelled raw. The message now renders the parameter through the same type-name renderer as the other two, as CoreCLR renders all three through `AppendType`. A second Codex review at the tip found nothing actionable.

## Not changed

- `MakeGenericType` and `MakeGenericMethod` still raise a message-less `ArgumentException` with no inner exception for a violation. CoreCLR raises `TypeLoadException` or `VerificationException`, and CoreLib's `ValidateGenericArguments` (RuntimeType.CoreCLR.cs:2022) rewraps it with `Argument_GenConstraintViolation`. That rewrap calls the `RuntimeTypeHandle.SatisfiesConstraints` FCall, which PawPrint does not implement.
- That renderer escapes no names (CoreCLR's `TypeNameBuilder::EscapeName`), anywhere it is used. CoreCLR spells a parameter named `+` as `'\+'`; PawPrint spells it `'+'`. Fixing that is a separate change to the renderer.
- Malformed MethodSpec blobs remain untested.

Stack #199, 1/5: **#194** → #195 → #196 → #197 → #198.

## `boxery help`, rendered from the command table
`boxery --help` was 95 hand-written lines: one ungrouped list, signatures that pushed descriptions onto ragged second lines, several commands on one line, and multi-line explanations (`patch` took four). Now each entry in `controller/cli.mjs`'s `COMMANDS` carries its help next to its handler (`{ help, run }`; aliases are `{ alias }`), and `controller/usage.mjs` renders from it:

- **`boxery COMMAND --help`** (also `-h`, `help COMMAND`, `COMMAND SUB --help`): usage lines, details, options, commented examples, see-also and a docs link. The long explanations moved here.
- **Before setup:** all of the above works with no host configured. `boxery run --help` used to fail with "no host configured".
- **Unknown command:** `boxery: unknown command: sshh (did you mean ssh?); see: boxery help`, exit 2. It used to print the whole usage on stdout and exit 1.
- **Terminal only:** bold headers only when stdout is a terminal, and `NO_COLOR` turns them off.

The design follows `pi --help` (sections, one-line descriptions, `# comment` examples, per-command help) and `herdr --help` (grouped commands, a footer for agents).

`PRE_HOST` now comes from the table, and `test/parity.test.mjs` reads aliases from it rather than keeping its own list.

Part of #1014. 24th batch: the base mending, explosions, fire, furnaces and hoppers hooks.

## What

Reviews 12 hooks against Fabric API 26.3: `mending_repair`, `explosion_prime`, `fire_odds`, `smoke_source`, `firework_explode`, `fluid_level_change`, `framerate_limit`, `furnace_burn`, `furnace_extract`, `furnace_smelt`, `furnace_start_smelt`, `hopper_inventory_search`.

No keys added. All 12 are recorded as gaps in a new `docs/fabric-ledger.md` section:
- `mending_repair`: no Fabric event exposes the selected Mending stack and mutable repair amount.
- `explosion_prime`: no Fabric event observes this explosion-start notification.
- `fire_odds`: `FlammableBlockRegistry` registers block/tag data rather than providing a per-state query event.
- `smoke_source`: no Fabric event exposes the campfire smoke-source query.
- `firework_explode`: no Fabric event reports completed rocket explosion effects.
- `fluid_level_change`: `FluidFlowEvents.ALLOW` observes spread attempts and neighbor updates with a fluid state, rather than the old/new level decision and explicit level pair.
- `framerate_limit`: no Fabric event exposes the final mutable window framerate limit.
- `furnace_burn`, `furnace_extract`, `furnace_smelt`, `furnace_start_smelt`: no Fabric event reports these fuel, extraction and cooking moments with the hook arguments.
- `hopper_inventory_search`: no Fabric event reports the selected container or entity target; transfer storage lookups have a different contract.

Docs only: no hook metadata, dispatch, host, adapter or gameplay change, so no tick-time effect. Suggested label: `skip-release`.

## Other projects' code

Fabric API (https://github.com/FabricMC/fabric at `2065040b236a0d5ac011bd6a45625dc49579b222`, Apache-2.0) was read to compare event contracts and is cited by file and line in the ledger. No code was copied.

## Checks

author: andromarces
body:
Records the macOS live probe of the ADR 0086 read-only access filter, in `adr/0086-leave-out-a-read-only-access-whose-modification-time-predates-the-turn-window.md`.

The probe ran a worker turn in a linked work tree of a disposable repository. It restored `file1.txt` by `git checkout` and `file2.txt` by a Vim `:w`, then rewrote `file3.txt` at the same size and restored it. It read `file4.txt` with `cat`. The envelope field `mainWorkTreeChangedInTurn` held `["file1.txt","file2.txt","file3.txt"]`, and the envelope carried no `mainWorkTreeChanged` key. Every file ended equal to its start state.

The record states macOS 27.3 (build 26C5035r), Node v27.0.0-alpha.0.0.0, opencode v0.0.0-dev-973, and agent-loop head e57daf0e2247dd67dc5e297fe6e17ad653398501.

author: rim-world
body:
## Summary

Add an opt-in Rio profile for Windows MSI installations:

- Keep KnownTerminals.rio on NotifyProtocol.Bell as the safe default.
- Add a separate RIO_OSC9 profile with the same Kitty graphics, true color, and hyperlink capabilities, but NotifyProtocol.Osc9.
- Return RIO_OSC9 only when both conditions are true:
  - process.platform === "win32"
  - RIO_AUMID_REGISTERED === "1"
- Leave Linux, macOS, portable Rio, other terminals (for example, otty and WezTerm), and old MSI installations on their existing behavior.
- Add the missing TUI changelog entry requested during review.

The companion Rio MSI change registers the Start Menu shortcut AUMID and sets RIO_AUMID_REGISTERED=1; see the companion-change section below.

## Screenshot

![Rio window running omp with a completion toast on Windows 11 26H2](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Rim-World/oh-my-pi/evidence/rio-toast-omp-2026-11-08/rio-toast-omp-2026-11-08.png)

This is a real-machine screenshot from the Rio + oh-my-pi end-to-end test on Windows 11 26H2. The Rio window shows the omp TUI , and the lower-right toast is the completion notification. It was captured after installing the test MSI built from this branch and running the modified oh-my-pi source.

## Problem

The installed oh-my-pi 18.18.0 maps Rio to NotifyProtocol.Bell. On Windows 11 26H2, that path only triggers Rio's bell and background-tab indicator; it does not call Rio's desktop notifier. A user running omp in Rio therefore saw no task-completion toast, while other terminals (for example, otty and WezTerm) showed one.

The second layer is in Rio's Windows installer: rio-notifier uses ToastNotificationManager::CreateToastNotifierWithId("Rio"), and the shipped MSI shortcut did not carry System.AppUserModel.ID = Rio. Without the AUMID registration, a submitted toast may not become a visible banner.

The fix therefore needs both sides:

- Rio MSI: register the AUMID and advertise that fact.
- oh-my-pi: use OSC 9 for Rio only when that advertisement is present.

## Companion change (required)

This PR is one half of a two-repository fix. The other half is the Rio MSI change that registers the shortcut AUMID and sets RIO_AUMID_REGISTERED=1.

Companion PR: https://github.com/raphamorim/rio/pull/2029

The companion change is required because this PR only activates when the installed MSI sets the flag. Without the Rio change, current MSI installations do not set RIO_AUMID_REGISTERED, so this PR keeps Rio on BEL.

If the companion change is not accepted:

- This PR does not fix the original omp notification issue, because no current MSI sets the capability flag.
- This PR does not introduce a new issue. Windows without the flag remains BEL; Linux and macOS remain unchanged; portable Rio remains BEL; other terminals (for example, otty and WezTerm) remain unchanged.

Neither PR alone fixes the user-visible issue. This PR is safe to land before the Rio change because the new behavior is dormant until the flag exists.

## Changes

### packages/tui/src/terminal-capabilities.ts

- Add:
  ```ts
  const RIO_OSC9 = new TerminalInfo(
    "rio",
    ImageProtocol.Kitty,
    true,
    true,
    NotifyProtocol.Osc9,
  );
  ```
- In getTerminalInfo, route Rio as follows:
  ```ts
  if (terminalId === "warp") return getWarpTerminalInfo(platform, env);
  if (terminalId === "rio") {
    return platform === "win32" && env.RIO_AUMID_REGISTERED === "1"
      ? RIO_OSC9
      : KNOWN_TERMINALS.rio;
  }
  return KNOWN_TERMINALS[terminalId];
  ```
- Update the Rio comment to describe the capability flag rather than treating the old AUMID limitation as permanent.

### packages/tui/test/terminal-capabilities.test.ts

Add coverage for:

- Windows + RIO_AUMID_REGISTERED="1" → NotifyProtocol.Osc9
- Windows + missing flag → NotifyProtocol.Bell
- Windows + RIO_AUMID_REGISTERED="0" → NotifyProtocol.Bell
- Linux + flag → NotifyProtocol.Bell
- macOS + flag → NotifyProtocol.Bell
- The RIO_OSC9 variant preserves Kitty graphics, true color, and hyperlinks
- Existing other-terminal behavior (for example, otty and WezTerm) remains unchanged

### packages/tui/CHANGELOG.md

- Add the Unreleased Fixed entry with this PR link and contributor credit, as requested during review.

## Relationship to oh-my-pi PR #12922

PR #12922 is the prior reference change for Rio notification behavior: https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/pull/12922

### What is the same

- Rio remains on BEL by default.
- This PR does not globally switch Rio to OSC 9.
- The Linux D-Bus/notify-send fallback is preserved.
- The Windows AUMID limitation is still treated as real; the fix does not assume that OSC 9 works without registration.
- No version-number sniffing or runtime shortcut probing is introduced.

### What is different

- #12922 kept Rio on BEL because the MSI did not register an AUMID. This PR makes OSC 9 possible only after the MSI provides an explicit capability signal, RIO_AUMID_REGISTERED=1.
- The switch is Windows-only. Linux and macOS stay on the existing BEL path, so the reason #12922 rejected a global switch is preserved.
- The new behavior is opt-in per installation: MSI installs can use OSC 9; portable Rio without the MSI remains BEL.
- This PR ships with an actual MSI/Windows notification test and a visible toast screenshot, rather than treating the AUMID condition as permanently blocking.
- The earlier PR's "happy to revisit if Rio starts registering an AppUserModelID" condition is now met on the Windows/MSI path.

This PR can be folded into #12922, landed after the corresponding Rio MSI change, or kept as a follow-up if maintainers prefer to keep the original PR focused on the BEL recommendation.

## Test environment

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| OS | Windows 11 26H2 (build 10.0.26300.9818) |
| Installed Rio | official 0.5.29 MSI; test MSI used ProductVersion=0.5.30 |
| Rio binary in test MSI | 0.5.29 binary; only installer metadata changed |
| oh-my-pi source | v18.18.0 baseline, branch fix/rio-aumid-notify |
| Runtime | Bun 1.4.4 |
| Shell | PowerShell 7.6.9 and Windows PowerShell 5.1 |
| Notification path | modified oh-my-pi → OSC 9 → Rio → rio-notifier → Windows Toast |
| WPN record | Order=1621, handler Rio, payload matched the smoke test |

## Validation performed

### Unit and type checks

- bun test packages/tui/test/terminal-capabilities.test.ts
  - 77 passed, 7 skipped, 0 failed
  - 270 assertions
- bun run check:types
  - 1,406 files; no type errors

### Process-level smoke test

- No flag: {"id":"rio","notify":"\u0007"} (BEL)
- Flag 1: {"id":"rio","notify":"\u001b]9;"} (OSC 9)

### Rio end-to-end test

- Installed Rio 0.5.29, then the x64 test MSI from the companion Rio change.
- Confirmed the Start Menu shortcut AUMID was Rio.
- Confirmed RIO_AUMID_REGISTERED=1 in the machine environment.
- Ran the modified oh-my-pi source in Rio and sent a notification.
- Visible Windows toast appeared with header Rio; WPN recorded Order=1621, handler Rio, matching payload.
- The screenshot above is the captured visible result.

### Installer checks performed by the companion Rio change

- Upgrade install: official 0.5.29 → test 0.5.30, exit code 0.
- Fresh install: exit code 0.
- Uninstall: exit code 0; AUMID, environment variable, shortcut, and PATH entry removed.
- Official 0.5.29 restored afterward.

## Compatibility

| Environment | Flag | Behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Windows + new MSI | 1 | OSC 9 |
| Windows + old MSI | absent | BEL |
| Windows portable, no MSI | absent | BEL |
| Windows portable, MSI installed | 1 | OSC 9 |
| Linux | not checked | BEL + existing notify-send fallback |
| macOS | not checked | existing behavior |
| Other terminals (e.g. otty, WezTerm) | n/a | unchanged |

The environment is read once at process start. After installing or upgrading the MSI, Rio and the terminal that launches it
